articles.title: “Es el mayor emprendedor de nuestro tiempo”: David Ellison celebra la entrada de Elon Musk en Skydance
articles.text:
Elon Musk se convirtió en accionista de Skydance, el gigante audiovisual surgido de la fusión entre Paramount y Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), según confirmó su presidente y consejero delegado, David Ellison, durante la cumbre DealBook 2026 del diario The New York Times, celebrada en Nueva York.
La inversión, que según el digital Semafor rondaría los 1.000 millones de dólares (unos 910 millones de euros), convierte al empresario sudafricano en socio de una compañía que reúne a estudios y cadenas como CBS, CNN, HBO, Max, Nickelodeon y Paramount+.
Cuánto invirtió Elon Musk en Skydance y qué dijo David Ellison
David Ellison no precisó la cifra exacta aportada por Musk a Skydance, aunque el digital Semafor había adelantado a finales de octubre de 2026 que la cantidad se aproximaría a los 1.000 millones de dólares.
Se trata de una suma idéntica a la que Larry Ellison, cofundador de Oracle y padre de David, destinó en 2022 a la compra de Twitter, la red social que Musk rebautizó posteriormente como X.
Durante su intervención en la cumbre del Times, el consejero delegado de Skydance definió la llegada de Musk al accionariado como un gesto de reconocimiento hacia su gestión. “Contar con su voto de confianza y tenerlo como accionista es un honor y un privilegio. Y si en el futuro surgiera alguna oportunidad de colaborar con él estaríamos encantados, pero, por el momento, no hay nada”, afirmó.
Elon Musk habría invertido cerca de 1.000 millones de dólares en Skydance, la empresa resultante de la fusión entre Paramount y Warner Bros. Discovery. La operación lo convierte en accionista de un conglomerado que controla estudios y cadenas como CBS, CNN, HBO y Paramount+, aunque por ahora no existen planes de colaboración conjunta entre ambas partes.
Ellison fue más allá en sus elogios hacia el empresario, al que describió con comparaciones históricas. Según declaraciones citadas por la revista Variety, el directivo señaló que Musk es “el mayor emprendedor de nuestro tiempo”, alguien que además “no invierte en muchas empresas”.
La admiración expresada por Ellison se extendió a los proyectos tecnológicos de Musk fuera del ámbito audiovisual. “Siento una enorme admiración y respeto por Elon. No sé si lo han visto recientemente, pero contemplar Starship (de su compañía SpaceX) es sencillamente una maravilla… En realidad, es a la vez el (Nikola) Tesla y el (Thomas Alva) Edison de nuestra época…”, agregó el presidente de Skydance.
Qué estudios y cadenas integran el nuevo gigante Skydance
La compañía que ahora cuenta con Musk entre sus accionistas nació de la unificación de titanes históricos del entretenimiento. Skydance reúne bajo un mismo techo a Paramount Pictures, Warner Bros. Pictures, CBS, CNN, HBO, Max, Nickelodeon y Paramount+.
Esta concentración de marcas plantea interrogantes sobre el tratamiento editorial de contenidos vinculados al propio Musk dentro del grupo. Uno de los casos más sensibles es el del documental “Musk”, dirigido por Alex Gibney, un retrato del magnate que no esconde sus sombras y que le valió al director amenazas de denuncias por parte del equipo legal del empresario sudafricano.
Ante la consulta sobre si la nueva relación accionarial modificaría los planes de emisión de ese documental, Ellison fue categórico. El directivo apuntó que la entrada de Musk en el capital de Skydance no altera los planes de HBO Max de emitir en esa plataforma la producción de Gibney, pese a la polémica que generó entre el equipo legal del empresario.
Finalmente, es pertinente señalar que Skydance es la productora encargada de crear muchas de las grandes películas y series de acción que seguramente ya disfrutas. En términos sencillos, son el motor creativo y financiero que hace realidad superproducciones llenas de adrenalina, como Top Gun: Maverick, la saga de Misión: Imposible o la serie Reacher.
Básicamente, cuando ves una historia moderna con acrobacias increíbles, efectos visuales espectaculares y puro entretenimiento que te mantiene pegado al asiento, el equipo de Skydance suele estar detrás de las cámaras trabajando para llevar toda esa emoción directamente a tu pantalla.

articles.title: Ubisoft Merges "For Honor" and "The Crew" Team with Casual Game Division
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
Ubisoft Merges "For Honor" and "The Crew" Team with Casual Game Division
Ubisoft started a massive organizational overhaul in January 2026, rearranging its various studios into five Creative Houses, each of which would be responsible for the funding, creative direction and development, and branding of the games under its purview. In Ubisoft's recent H1 financial report, the gaming giant says that it has officially concluded that restructuring effort—which has led to significant layoffs over the course of the year—with the combination of Creative House 3 and Creative House 5 into a single entity.
Creative House 2, which includes iconic franchises like The Division, Ghost Recon and Splinter Cell alongside March of Giants, has been named Massive Entertainment. Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms. With the appointment of an external General Manager for Creative House 4, who will join in January, all Creative House leadership positions are now filled.
As per the previous announcement, Ubisoft's Creative House 3 was responsible for a number of live-service franchises, including The Crew, For Honor, Riders Republic, Brawlhalla, and Skull & Bones. Meanwhile, Creative House 5's scope was to be focused on casual and mobile games, including Just Dance, Idle Miner Tycoon, Ketchapp, Invincible: Guarding the Globe, Uno, and Hasbro. All of these properties will now be under the leadership of Julian Bares. It's unclear if this will have any impact on the development direction of either Creative House, but Ubisoft says that the merger was performed to leverage synergies between the teams. 
Ubisoft has also spun off Motherbrain, the team behind Teammates, the playable generative AI experience, with a focus on "developing proprietary technology for new forms of gameplay," like "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds."
Sources:
				Ubisoft, 				via Insider Gaming

articles.title: GTA 6 a pesé plus lourd que Netflix et YouTube réunis sur le réseau de Bouygues Telecom
articles.text:
Plus gourmand que les géants Netflix et YouTube réunis, le téléchargement de GTA 6 a mobilisé jusqu'à 40 % du trafic chez Bouygues Telecom, ces dernières heures. L'opérateur a battu son record de trafic, sans encombre pour ses abonnés.
Le téléchargement de GTA 6 a pesé jusqu'à 40 % du trafic total du réseau Bouygues Telecom en journée, loin devant Netflix et YouTube, qui en représentent d'ordinaire environ 20 % chacun, apprend-on ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026. Mercredi soir, à quelques heures de la sortie du jeu, l'opérateur avait même enregistré son pic de trafic le plus élevé de l'année. Bouygues Telecom assure pourtant que cette activité, conforme à ses prévisions, s'est déroulée sans mauvaise conséquence pour ses clients.
« Un pic jamais atteint », Bouygues Telecom raconte la déferlante GTA 6 sur son réseau
Bouygues Telecom a enregistré « un pic de trafic jamais atteint » sur son réseau, supérieur de 10 % à celui des journées habituellement les plus chargées, à commencer par le dimanche. Le sommet a été atteint mercredi soir vers 21h30, à quelques heures du déblocage, porté par les retardataires qui téléchargeaient encore le jeu et ses jusqu'à 212 Go. Sans livrer de chiffre précis, Jérôme Latrille, le directeur technique et plan réseau de Bouygues Telecom, confirme « qu'il s'agit du pic de trafic le plus élevé de l'année ».
Depuis l'ouverture du préchargement de GTA VI le 10 novembre, Bouygues Telecom a aligné plusieurs pics historiques, le 10, le 12, date de l'arrivée des boîtes contenant un code de téléchargement, puis le 18. « Ces dix derniers jours ont été particulièrement chargés en journée du fait du téléchargement du jeu », résume le responsable. Et ce flot de connectivité a débordé sur la fin de soirée, et ce sont ces débordements qui ont fait tomber les records.
Rapporté à l'ensemble du réseau, c'est encore autre chose. En journée, le téléchargement de GTA 6 a représenté jusqu'à 40 % du trafic total, et jusqu'à 25 % encore mercredi soir, « soit davantage que Netflix et YouTube réunis ». Les deux plateformes, d'ordinaire les plus gourmandes, pèsent chacune environ 20 %. Sur une semaine entière, l'opérateur dit avoir écoulé 20 % de trafic de plus que lors de ses semaines habituellement les plus chargées de l'année.
Pourquoi le réseau de Bouygues Telecom n'a pas flanché
L'opérateur a traversé tranquillement cette phase mouvementée. « Ce pic exceptionnel, aussi spectaculaire soit-il, est conforme à nos prévisions et s'est déroulé sans encombre pour nos clients », assure Jérôme Latrille. Bouygues Telecom suit depuis des années l'essor des téléchargements de jeux vidéo, un usage en très forte croissance, et l'opérateur l'intègre à ses projections pour dimensionner son réseau. Jeudi matin, le trafic revenait déjà progressivement à la normale. L'essentiel des téléchargements a eu lieu pendant le préchargement et la nuit de la sortie, et l'opérateur n' pas constaté « à ce stade de prolongement de ce pic exceptionnel ».
Le préchargement mis en place par Rockstar Games aura servi de soupape, en étalant une grande partie de la demande avant la sortie. C'est grâce à ces téléchargements anticipés, selon Bouygues, que le pic de mercredi soir est resté « dans la fourchette que nous avions envisagée ». Les opérateurs français planchent aussi ensemble, au sein de l'AF2M, sur un guide de bonnes pratiques destiné aux éditeurs de services et aux CDN, ces réseaux qui distribuent les contenus au plus près des internautes. L'idée est de leur suggérer des optimisations, sans aucun impact pour les utilisateurs, afin d'aplanir ces pics. PlayStation et Rockstar en auraient déjà appliqué certaines, comme « diluer le trafic sur une période de pré-chargement assez longue et éviter les heures de grande écoute pour les mises à disposition finales ».
Bouygues Telecom n'est en tout cas pas le seul opérateur à avoir pris ses précautions. Free a renforcé sa bande passante, mobilisé des équipes dédiées et gelé son réseau les 18 et 19 novembre, tandis qu'Orange a vu son trafic doubler, sans incident. Le vrai couac est venu d'ailleurs, avec la panne du PlayStation Network mercredi soir, résorbée vers 20h30. Bouygues espère que les travaux de l'AF2M permettront aux opérateurs de nouer « un dialogue structuré avec les éditeurs de jeux vidéo », pour réduire encore l'intensité de ces pics « dans les années à venir ». GTA 6 ne sera sans doute pas le dernier poids lourd à débarquer.

articles.title: US Air Force shifts its air defense strategy toward sensors and AI
articles.text:
US Air Force announces new focus on sensors and autonomous warfare — with drone-killing kit top of the list
US Air Force rips up its air defense playbook to bet big on modern defense systems
- US Air Force puts sensors and AI at the heart of modernization
- New strategy shifts attention from interception toward earlier detection and coordinated responses
- Autonomous systems are becoming central to the Air Force's future combat planning
The US Air Force has introduced a new modernization plan that focuses on advanced sensors, artificial intelligence and autonomous systems to counter increasingly advanced aerial threats.
Its new Force Design 2026 changes how the service plans to defend against air attacks and prepare for future wars.
The approach prioritizes finding and tracking threats early and coordinating responses, rather than depending mainly on weapons that intercept and destroy incoming aircraft or drones.
New strategy prioritizes sensors, AI, and networked warfare
The updated framework identifies sensors, interconnected networks and artificial intelligence as technologies increasingly influencing modern air defense operations.
These capabilities could help military forces identify incoming threats, coordinate defensive responses and manage multiple unmanned aircraft operating simultaneously.
Air Force officials also acknowledge that technological developments are creating difficulties for traditional approaches to generating military airpower.
Systems previously considered effective may encounter limitations when confronting increasingly sophisticated weapons and interconnected defensive networks.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“New technologies are enabling fantastic capabilities that were unimaginable just a few years ago, but those same technologies threaten some of the ways we have historically generated airpower,” said Lt. Gen. Chris Niemi, deputy chief of staff for Force Modernization and chief modernization officer.
The strategy also emphasizes combining autonomous capabilities, advanced detection equipment and command systems with existing aircraft.
Such integration would allow different military platforms to coordinate operations, particularly when conventional communications and navigation systems become unavailable.
This approach places software, information sharing and automated coordination closer to the center of future air combat operations.
Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach described the revised framework as a significant departure from the service's previous modernization approach.
Force Design 2026 replaces the Air Force's previous modernization framework
The new strategy succeeds the One Force Design framework introduced in October 2024 under former Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin.
That earlier document established modernization priorities intended to guide capability development and future operational planning across the service.
Its approach divided counter-drone responsibilities into three categories covering short-range, long-range and intercontinental aerial threats.
These classifications provided a structure for considering defensive capabilities against unmanned aircraft operating across different distances.
The revised framework changes the emphasis toward integrating detection technologies, autonomous platforms and command infrastructure.
An Air Force spokesperson explained that the latest framework provides continuing guidance for identifying operational weaknesses, developing capabilities and determining modernization priorities.
However, much of the information remains classified and all we know is that the Air Force wants coordinated systems capable of operating under increasingly difficult battlefield conditions.
Wilsbach said the service needed to reconsider established approaches as emerging technologies changed the character of aerial warfare.
This suggests that future investments will increasingly account for threats capable of challenging traditional aircraft operations and existing defensive arrangements.

articles.title: CISA Warns of 4 Exploited Flaws Linked to Ransomware, Cryptomining, and LLMjacking Attacks
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Wednesday added four vulnerabilities impacting Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM), BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
The vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-90436 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An unsafe reflection vulnerability in Apache Axis that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code.
- CVE-2026-90817 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A code injection vulnerability in REDCap that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.
- CVE-2026-40217 (CVSS score: 8.8) - An unprotected alternate channel vulnerability in LiteLLM that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via bytecode rewriting at the /guardrails/test_custom_code URI.
- CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in Synology DSM that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.
"An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing," CISA said about CVE-2026-90817. "Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash."
The addition of CVE-2026-90436 to the KEV catalog follows reports that the flaw is exploited in conjunction with the 4EverAble2Shell vulnerabilities affecting N-able N-central to deploy cryptocurrency miners on vulnerable servers.
Rapid7, in its own analysis of the flaw, said it detected exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center in a customer environment by taking advantage of the fact that the corporate workspace platform uses the Axis library as part of its XML-RPC and SOAP APIs.
"To be vulnerable, the Confluence instance must have the 'Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP)' enabled," Atlassian said. "Please note that this setting was turned off by default for new installations starting in Confluence 3.0. This feature was fully removed in Confluence 10.0."
In the activity documented by Rapid7, threat actors are said to have weaponized the flaw to run shell commands and scripts fetched from temporary Pinggy and Cloudflare Tunnel domains, followed by enumerating the compromised environment. The incident was flagged on November 13, 2026.
"Just over three minutes after the first observed execution, the attackers were authenticating to MySQL with Confluence's own database credentials, querying page bodies, application links, and attachments with names associated with credentials, tokens, VPN configurations, and private keys," Rapid7 said.
"The attacker's scripts, likely AI-generated, then targeted files in Confluence's default location for uploaded page attachments (/var/atlassian/application-data/confluence/attachments/v4/), parsed Office documents, searched for credentials, and hunted for payment card numbers, using Luhn checks to filter out false positives."
In addition, the attackers have been found to map various internal services, use a Confluence application credential to query the internal Atlassian Crowd API for users and group memberships, and attempt to carry out a Kerberos-based credential harvesting technique called AS-REP Roasting.
Although these efforts were unsuccessful, the threat actor managed to acquire a service account credential and queried a production cloud data warehouse. About 12 hours after the first exploit request, the attacker signed in to Microsoft 365 as an integration service account using legacy authentication from "192.238.253[.]176."
CVE-2026-90436, which affects Axis 1.x versions, remains unpatched as Axis 1 has reached end-of-life (EoL) status. It's recommended to migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Alternatively, users can use a build of Axis with the patch from a July 12, 2026, commit applied.
As for CVE-2026-90817, Safe Security said in a report published late last month that it observed an unknown threat abusing the flaw to "stage a transient web shell, followed by an in-memory loader that retrieved XMRig disguised as image files, masqueraded the miner as syslog-ng, and established persistence through cron and an added SSH key."
The exploitation of CVE-2026-40217 stems from a Google Threat Intelligence Group report this week in which threat actors have leveraged the vulnerability to elevate limited-access inference keys into full administrative credentials and establish persistence as part of LLMjacking attacks aimed at financial services, retail, transportation, and technology organizations in North America, South America, and the Asia Pacific region.
Rounding off the list is CVE-2024-10441, which Synology disclosed earlier this month as being exploited in ransomware attacks targeting Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices. The attacks have been found to result in the deployment of C3RB3R ransomware.
In light of active exploitation, federal agencies have been recommended to apply fixes or necessary mitigations for DSM, REDCap, and Axis flaws by November 21, 2026, and for the LiteLLM flaw by December 2, 2026.

articles.title: Descargar WhatsApp Plus APK original para Android: por qué pone en peligro la cuenta bancaria
articles.text:
Descargar WhatsApp Plus APK original para Android puede poner en riesgo la cuenta bancaria y otros datos personales. Aunque estas versiones prometen funciones adicionales, WhatsApp advierte que las aplicaciones modificadas son desarrolladas por terceros y no es posible validar sus prácticas de seguridad y privacidad.
El uso de una aplicación no oficial puede exponer al usuario a malware capaz de robar información y dañar el teléfono.
Si el dispositivo almacena contraseñas, datos de acceso o archivos vinculados con servicios bancarios, esa exposición también puede comprometer la seguridad de la cuenta bancaria.
WhatsApp señala que las versiones no oficiales infringen sus Condiciones del servicio. La plataforma no avala estas aplicaciones porque no puede garantizar que los mensajes, la ubicación, los archivos compartidos y otros datos personales permanezcan privados y seguros.
Cuáles son los riesgos para la privacidad y el acceso a la cuenta
Las aplicaciones no oficiales pueden recopilar o exponer información del teléfono sin que el usuario conozca el alcance de esas prácticas. “Tu privacidad y seguridad están en riesgo”, advierte WhatsApp sobre este tipo de herramientas desarrolladas por terceros.
Además de la posible exposición de datos, la cuenta puede sufrir restricciones. WhatsApp indica que el uso de aplicaciones no autorizadas puede derivar en un bloqueo temporal o permanente, así como en limitaciones para vincular otros dispositivos.
Entre los ejemplos de aplicaciones no oficiales, WhatsApp menciona GB WhatsApp, FM WhatsApp, TeleMessage y TM WhatsApp.
Si aparece un mensaje que exige usar la aplicación oficial para iniciar sesión o informa el cierre de sesión por utilizar una versión no autorizada, la recomendación es eliminarla del dispositivo.
Para recuperar el acceso de forma segura, WhatsApp aconseja desinstalar la aplicación no oficial, descargar WhatsApp o WhatsApp Business desde su sitio web y volver a registrar el número de teléfono.
La plataforma también advierte que no puede garantizar la transferencia correcta de una copia de seguridad creada desde una aplicación modificada.
Qué nuevas funciones hay en WhatsApp
WhatsApp incorporó cuatro funciones para los chats grupales que buscan facilitar la organización de conversaciones con muchos mensajes y ayudar a los usuarios a recuperar información pendiente.
La principal novedad permite fijar mensajes sin un límite de tiempo predeterminado. De este modo, datos como direcciones, enlaces, horarios o anuncios pueden quedar visibles en la parte superior del grupo mientras sus integrantes lo consideren necesario.
WhatsApp también amplió la opción para compartir el historial reciente con nuevos participantes.
La herramienta ya permitía enviar mensajes anteriores al sumar a una persona al grupo, pero ahora se puede hacerlo después de su ingreso al tocar su nombre dentro del chat. Los mensajes compartidos mantienen el cifrado de extremo a extremo.
Otra de las funciones es el estado para grupos. Los integrantes pueden publicar actualizaciones destinadas solo a los miembros de una conversación específica, sin enviarlas al resto de sus contactos.
Al igual que los estados tradicionales de WhatsApp, estas publicaciones desaparecen después de 24 horas. Los usuarios del grupo pueden verlas, reaccionar y añadir sus propias actualizaciones. La opción apunta a separar comunicaciones informales de los mensajes habituales del chat.
La cuarta novedad es un filtro para identificar conversaciones no leídas en las que el usuario fue mencionado o recibió una respuesta directa.
Incluye las menciones generales con la etiqueta @all. La herramienta permite encontrar con mayor rapidez los intercambios que requieren atención, sin revisar uno por uno todos los grupos pendientes.
La disponibilidad puede ser gradual, por lo que algunos usuarios podrían no ver inmediatamente las herramientas aun después de actualizar la aplicación. Para comprobar si ya están habilitadas, es necesario contar con la versión más reciente de WhatsApp para Android o iPhone.

articles.title: GTA 6 : après les consoles, à quand espérer la sortie de la version PC ?
articles.text:
GTA 6 : après les consoles, à quand espérer la sortie de la version PC ?
Deux ans, un an ou six mois : les allergiques aux 30 FPS ou celles et ceux qui ne jurent que par le PC rongent leur frein en attendant l'arrivée de GTA 6 sur Steam. Un marché qui a bien changé depuis la sortie de Red Dead Redemption 2, l'avant-dernier jeu de Rockstar.
À peine Grand Theft Auto 6 arrivé sur les consoles PS5 et Xbox Series que (presque) tous les regards se portent sur la version PC. Comme à son habitude, Rockstar Games s’est gardé de toute officialisation en ce sens : à l’époque de GTA 5, il aura fallu attendre la confirmation des versions PS4/Xbox One pour avoir des nouvelles du portage PC – avant deux retards successifs qui ont repoussé sa sortie au 14 avril 2015, soit près de 2 ans après la parution des galettes originales PS3 et 360. Pour Red Dead Redemption 2, l’attente fut beaucoup plus courte, puisque la version PC a été annoncée un an après les débuts du jeu sur PS4/Xbox One, pour une arrivée le mois d’après. Un délai considérablement réduit, qui pourrait l’être encore davantage pour GTA 6.
Les temps ont changé, et si l’appétence du grand public pour les consoles n’a pas faibli – la PlayStation 5 est la 8e console la plus vendue de tous les temps –, le marché du PC a connu une explosion en popularité. Si l’on s’en tient au pic d’utilisateurs connectés en simultané sur Steam (la seule métrique vraiment viable à l’heure actuelle), on passe du simple au double : 16 607 492 en novembre 2018 contre 43 505 724 au cours du mois d’octobre dernier. S’offrir une version PC pour son titre AAA, c’est aussi s’offrir une source de revenus non négligeable – inquiétudes liées au piratage mises à part, même si les solutions anti-crack comme Denuvo sont bien plus robustes qu’auparavant. Le cas Grand Theft Auto est d’ailleurs particulier, puisqu’il s’agit de l’un des rares jeux pour lesquels les joueurs et les joueuses console sont prêts à repasser à la caisse pour profiter des versions PC. En l’absence de chiffres officiels, les trackers de ventes numériques ont estimé à environ 400 000 les exemplaires PC de Red Dead Redemption 2 vendus un mois après son lancement sur l’Epic Games Store et le Rockstar Launcher – puis un boost à 1 million après son arrivée sur Steam le mois suivant.
Et au vu du tremblement de terre provoqué par GTA 6, nul doute que les joueurs PC patienteront encore moins longtemps – 6 mois dans le meilleur des cas, assez long pour donner envie aux fans de double-dip et assez court pour titiller la curiosité des sceptiques qui n’auraient pas encore oublié tout ce pataquès sur console. Quoi qu’il en soit, il nous tarde de découvrir l’optimisation du jeu pour cette éventuelle édition PC : les CPU des consoles actuelles souffrent de l’importante densité des systèmes de NPC et d’interactions du jeu, et gageons que les PC profiteront des solutions de reconstruction et de génération d’images disponibles via le DLSS 4.5 de Nvidia ou le FSR 4 d’AMD.
Gare aux marchands de rêve toutefois – nombreux seront les escrocs à proclamer avoir vibecodé une « recompilation » de GTA 6 sur PC : cette pratique qui consiste à transposer les binaires d’un jeu console en un code compilable et exécutable sur un autre hardware, et qui fait rage sur la scène rétro depuis quelques mois. Des exemples se sont déjà fait connaître sur X, et on ne saurait trop vous conseiller de les ignorer poliment pour votre hygiène numérique.

articles.title: ASUS Agent Computer : ce PC RTX 5060 Ti 16 Go peut-il réduire la facture des agents IA cloud ?
articles.text:
Les agents IA ne se contentent plus de répondre : ils planifient, appellent des outils et vérifient leur travail, en consommant des tokens à chaque étape.
ASUS propose d'en reprendre le contrôle avec l'Agent Computer, un PC capable de les faire tourner en local. Clubic a reçu le Gravity IA, assemblé par Materiel.net autour d'une ASUS PRIME GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 Go, pour évaluer ce que cet investissement peut faire gagner face au cloud.
Quand l'IA passe du chatbot à l'agent, le compteur de tokens s'emballe
Là où un chatbot se contente de répondre à une requête, un agent reçoit un objectif, le découpe en étapes, mobilise des outils et contrôle le résultat, une évolution que porte la campagne ASUS Agent Computer – Powering Every AI Choice. Sur une API facturée au token, un agent qui tourne en continu multiplie toutefois les appels et finit par transformer une dépense ponctuelle en coût récurrent, un enjeu que détaille le microsite ASUS Agent Computer.
Facture cloud contre PC local : le calcul qui change la donne
Sans prétendre que le local coûte toujours moins cher, Clubic a mis cette dépense récurrente en regard du prix du Gravity IA, affiché à 2 949,95 € chez Materiel.net.
| Dépense cloud | Coût annuel | PC rentabilisé en | Écart potentiel sur 5 ans* | 
| 250 € / mois | 3 000 € | environ 12 mois | environ 12 000 € | 
| 500 € / mois | 6 000 € | environ 6 mois | environ 27 000 € | 
*Hors électricité et licence Windows. Montants indicatifs, qui dépendent de l'usage et de la tarification des services cloud.
Il faut y ajouter une licence Windows, le PC étant livré avec une version d'essai, ainsi que l'électricité : à titre illustratif, avec une consommation moyenne hypothétique de 300 W pendant huit heures par jour et un tarif d'environ 0,20 € le kWh, la facture représenterait environ 175 € par an. Une fois le matériel acquis, chaque nouvelle requête exécutée en local coûte surtout de l'électricité et du temps machine, sans pour autant devenir gratuite.
Face à un abonnement chatbot d'une vingtaine d'euros par mois, l'achat ne se rentabilise pas dans un délai raisonnable, alors que le calcul devient très favorable pour ceux qui font tourner des agents ou consomment de l'API au quotidien.
Gravity IA : bien plus qu'une carte graphique
La configuration reçue par Clubic repose sur une ASUS PRIME GeForce RTX 5060 Ti OC 16 Go, dont les Tensor Cores et l'écosystème CUDA accélèrent l'inférence locale. Ses 16 Go de VRAM permettent d'exploiter la combinaison recommandée par NVIDIA pour cette catégorie de carte : OpenClaw associé à LM Studio ou Ollama et à un modèle comme Qwen 3.5 9B ou gpt-oss 20b.
Un Agent Computer ne se résume pas pour autant à sa carte graphique, et le Gravity IA en fait la démonstration. Si les 16 Go de VRAM de la RTX 5060 Ti déterminent la taille et le type de modèles qui tournent confortablement sur le GPU, les 32 Go de DDR5-6000 absorbent la charge des applications, le contexte et, le cas échéant, la part du modèle déchargée en mémoire système. Le SSD NVMe de 2 To conserve en local les modèles, les jeux de données, les index RAG et les fichiers de travail, tandis que la carte mère ASUS PRIME B860-PLUS WIFI, associée à un Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, sert de socle à la plateforme comme à ses évolutions. L'alimentation 750 W 80+ Gold et le ventirad be quiet! Dark Rock 5 garantissent quant à eux la stabilité lors des charges prolongées, celles qu'imposent des agents capables de travailler pendant des heures.
Sans rivaliser avec une station de travail à 32 Go de VRAM ou plus, cet ensemble équilibré forme une plateforme d'IA locale et agentique grand public, taillée pour le RAG, le code assisté et les agents personnels, bien plus qu'un simple PC équipé d'une RTX.
Assemblé et testé en France par Materiel.net, le Gravity IA fait partie de la sélection ASUS Ai Agent Computer et se commande sur sa fiche produit ou depuis l'espace ASUS Agent Computer de Materiel.net.
Local, cloud ou hybride : à chaque tâche son terrain
L'Agent Computer ne se pose pas en remplaçant du cloud : le local convient aux tâches récurrentes et aux documents sensibles, le cloud aux modèles les plus avancés et aux besoins ponctuels très lourds, et l'approche hybride combine les deux. L'exécution locale peut ainsi réduire l'exposition de documents sensibles à des services tiers et offrir davantage de contrôle sur leur traitement.
Pour ceux qui débutent, ASUS propose Zenni Claw, une approche plus guidée de l'IA agentique. En simplifiant la prise en main et en s'appuyant sur des skills et des workflows prédéfinis, l'outil cherche à réduire la complexité de configuration, afin de permettre aux utilisateurs de passer plus facilement du simple assistant conversationnel à des workflows agentiques capables d'exécuter des tâches. Selon le cas d'usage, ces tâches s'exécutent en local, dans le cloud ou en combinant les deux.
DLSS 5 : la même RTX, l'autre visage de l'IA
Le GPU qui fait tourner modèles et agents en local sert aussi une tout autre démonstration de l'IA, celle du rendu neuronal. Réservé aux GeForce RTX 50 Series, DLSS 5 inaugure le 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, une étape de rendu par IA qui enrichit l'éclairage et les matériaux à partir de l'image finale produite par le moteur du jeu, tout en préservant l'intention artistique de la scène d'origine. La technologie fonctionne de concert avec la Ray Reconstruction et le Multi Frame Generation, qui multiplie le nombre d'images affichées.
Avec sa mise à jour Eagle's Shadow, War Thunder profite ainsi de reflets plus marqués, d'ombres affinées et d'un microcontraste renforcé, que les combats se déroulent dans les airs, au sol ou en mer. Where Winds Meet suivra le 23 novembre, en complément des technologies DLSS déjà prises en charge par le jeu. Sur une même RTX 5060 Ti cohabitent donc deux visages de l'IA : l'inférence locale et les agents d'un côté, le rendu neuronal et les technologies DLSS de l'autre.
« Votre PC. Votre Agent. » : ASUS lance son challenge
ASUS invite enfin les passionnés à rejoindre l'ASUS Agent Computer Challenge, une compétition française de projets d'IA agentique et locale répartie en trois catégories (AI Entry, Developer, Advanced / High-End). Le jury, qui compte Pierre Bittner comme relecteur technique, privilégiera la pertinence et la faisabilité des projets plutôt que leur audience sur les réseaux sociaux, et les candidatures sont ouvertes jusqu'au 6 décembre 2026. Clubic publiera de son côté un test complet du Gravity IA le 23 novembre.

articles.title: Valve Ditches Steam Machine Reservations but Warns of Price Hikes and Shortages
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
Valve Ditches Steam Machine Reservations but Warns of Price Hikes and Shortages
Valve officially released the Steam Machine in mid-2026 with a reservation program and limitations on per-customer sales in order to minimize the impact of the ongoing RAM crisis and ensure that as many people as possible got a fair shout at buying a living room console-PC hybrid. Now, nearly five months after the console's initial launch, Valve has dropped the Steam Machine's reservation program and started selling the device to the public. At the time of the announcement, Valve had stock of the 512 GB Steam Machine, but it has not yet cleared out the existing reservation queue of the 2 TB unit. However, the announcement that the Steam Machine's general availability also comes with a warning that supply and pricing aren't guaranteed.
We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2 TB model in particular will be especially constrained.
We anticipate having more information to share come January.
This change means that the Steam Machine will now be available to add to cart directly, but it also means that once the currently available production run has been sold through, the Steam Machine will be marked "out of stock" until more units have been produced and are ready to ship. The 2 TB Steam Machine has been marked as "out of stock" already, since there are more people on the waitlist than there are units available. Valve also clarified in the announcement that "no one on the waitlist is guaranteed a unit," suggesting that the 2 TB Steam Machine may switch to regular sales before the waitlist is cleared.

articles.title: I used the Geekom IT13 mini PC for everything from Office to video editing
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Opening the box, the IT13 with its dull blue finish looks like any other mid-range mini PC. However, on lifting it from the box, the metal build and weight start to highlight its potential. Windows 11 Pro ran smoothly, and most apps ran without issue. However, while it performed well in benchmarks, real-world use highlights its business focus.
Reasons to buy
- + Compact design
- + Hybrid CPU architecture
- + Integrated NPU
Reasons to avoid
- - GPU lacks power for games
- - Struggles with complex video edits
- - Not suitable for larger LLMs
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
GEEKOM IT13: 30-second review
My initial impressions of the Geekom IT13 2026 Edition were mixed, shaped mainly by preconceived ideas about these small machines over the years. Essentially, the IT13 2026 Edition has a smaller-than-average form factor, and its casing is finished in a dull blue; these traits are usually apparent on machines at the cheaper end of the market. However, at just over $1,000 / £1,000 at the time of this review, this mini PC is priced at least at the mid-to-upper end.
Taking the small box out, the metal rather than plastic casing gives a good measure of quality, and a closer look at the box shows a decent selection of ports, including a 2.5GbE LAN port, two USB4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot on the side.
While the ports on the back are close together, the layout is well thought through, making it easy to connect accessories. One point on the port layout is that there are two USB Type-A ports on the front. While these can be useful, most PC accessories I have looked at in the last couple of years have been USB-C, so having at least one of these newer ports would have been handy.
Powering up, and reflecting the machine's business focus, the final steps of the Windows 11 Pro setup need to be completed. This takes around five minutes, not including updates.
Initial impressions from the software and benchmarks suggest that, while nothing in the specifications really stands out as particularly interesting, performance throughout is solid. Microsoft Office apps run as you would hope, and Windows 11 Pro handles them with ease.
Switching up the demands on the system and running through the Adobe Creative Suite shows that both Lightroom and Photoshop run with surprising ease, and it’s only when Adobe Bridge starts rendering thumbnails that the limits of the internal RAM cause a slowdown.
Video editing with 4K footage from a Canon EOS R50 V, I was impressed with how well it handled with plenty of speed as I scrubbed through the timeline with few slowdowns. Switching to 4K video shot on the Sony A7 IV in S-Log and starting to apply grading highlighted the limits.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
At each point throughout the test, the small machine impressed in every type of use, showing that this machine has been designed for general performance, and for this it ranks among the best mini PCs I've tested. Its small size makes it easy to position in any workplace. With its metal chassis and robust credentials, it’s equally suited for a rig or as a portable workstation, especially in the studio.
The small size, the current cost of memory, and the latest-generation CPU all contribute to the machine's price. While on paper that CPU might seem less powerful than many older CPUs, the hybrid design and how it allocates resources does go some way to justify the price.
GEEKOM IT13: Price and availability
- How much does it cost? From £1,099
- When is it out? Available now
- Where can you get it? Directly from Geekom.com
The Geekom IT13 is widely available through many online retailers including Amazon.com and Geekom.com in the US. In the UK, you'll find it at Amazon.co.uk and Geekom's UK site.
At the time of writing there is only one variant of the machine which includes a 1TB SSD and 32GB of RAM.
At present Geekom are presenting the following offers on the price with a 15% discount using the code TRDT3U7F this is valid until the 31st December 2026.
- Value: 3.5 / 5
GEEKOM IT13: Specs
CPU: Intel Core Ultra 7 356H, Panther Lake, 16 cores (4 Performance, 8 Efficient, 4 Low Power Efficient), 16 threads, up to 4.7GHz
Graphics: Intel Xe3 integrated graphics, 4 Xe cores; Intel AI Boost NPU, up to 50 TOPS
RAM: 32GB dual-channel DDR4, expandable to 64GB
Storage: 1TB M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 ×4 NVMe SSD (up to 2TB), M.2 2242 SATA SSD slot (up to 1TB), 2.5-inch SATA drive bay (up to 2TB); 5TB total supported capacity
Left Ports: SD card reader
Connectivity: 2 × USB4, 3 × USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A, 1 × USB 2.0 Type-A, 2 × HDMI 2.0, 2.5GbE Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4
Audio: 3.5mm headphone/microphone jack, audio output via HDMI and USB
Camera: None
Size: 117 × 112 × 49.2mm
Weight:  652g
OS Installed: Windows 11 Pro
Accessories: Power adapter, power cable, HDMI cable, VESA mounting bracket and screws
GEEKOM IT13: Design
The first thing to note about the IT13 is its size: at 117 × 112 × 49.2mm and 652g, it’s one of the smallest mini PCs I’ve looked at in a while. A couple of years ago, we started to see quite a few of these compact form-factor options, but most had cooling issues and the potential for thermal throttling; more recent models have improved cooling and size. The latest processors also draw considerably less power than their predecessors.
The Geekom IT13 is a welcome return to the compact mini PCs we were seeing a couple of years ago, but now with the far more energy-efficient Intel Core Ultra 7 356H, which is a hybrid CPU that works far more efficiently and thus cooler than many older processors.
While the box is small, Geekom is pitching this as a general mini PC equally suited to the office, studio, or home, with power that meets most people’s needs.
Sure enough, the performance impressed throughout the test, and while there are limitations, the assortment of ports and upgrade options certainly appealed.
Starting on the exterior, the front has two USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A ports alongside a 3.5mm headphone jack and the power button. On the side is an SD card reader slot, and around the back are another USB 3.2 Gen 2 port and a USB 2.0 port (both Type-A), plus two USB4 ports, a 2.5GbE LAN port, two HDMI ports, and the DC input.
Unlike many of the new mini PCs I’ve looked at recently, this one offers plenty of upgrade potential. Access to the insides is gained by unscrewing the four bolts in the base, then prying the plastic top cover off and removing a further four screws.
As the case is removed, the two antenna wires need to be carefully unhooked from the casing. As these wires are incredibly delicate, you need to take this step slowly to avoid damage.
Inside the machine, it’s packed with 32GB of dual-channel DDR4 RAM, all neatly laid out with the 1TB M.2 2280 PCIe Gen 4 ×4 SSD, which can be upgraded to 2TB. Checking closely, there’s the smaller slot for the M.2 2242 SATA SSD, and this can be up to 1TB. Then, if you need to boost the internal storage further, there’s space for a 2.5-inch SATA HDD.
- Design: 4 / 5
GEEKOM IT13: Features
The power of mini PCs has leapt forward this year, especially with the advent of NPUs and the greater resource demands created by AI features in mainstream apps. The boost in AI use has created resource constraints for many older machines and their CPUs.
Older PCs took a blunt-instrument approach, and as long as they had enough resources, these small mini PCs could achieve a surprising amount; hybrid cores have been around since 2020 in the Lakefield processors, and have been steadily improving performance since.
The Intel Core Ultra 7 356H is based on Intel’s Panther Lake architecture and features 16 cores and 16 threads. These comprise four Performance-cores, eight Efficient-cores and four Low Power Efficient-cores. This hybrid architecture lets the processor distribute workloads based on their performance and requirements.
The processor also includes an Intel NPU, and this is rated at up to 50 TOPS. The NPU is only called on by apps that have been specifically optimised for use, and when used, it frees up resources from the CPU or GPU. The NPU will also support compatible local language models alongside Windows AI features; however, at present cloud-based AI processing is still the most common resource for integrated AI.
Essentially, while the overall specifications of the newer Panther Lake processors on paper may seem less impressive than those of older CPUs, resource allocation is far better.
The integrated GPU is Intel Xe3 Graphics for U7-356H, which offers good all-round performance, though it does draw on RAM alongside the CPU. However, for most creative applications, including those from the Adobe Suite, the power available is more than sufficient for most uses.
While many mini PCs use soldered LPDDR5X RAM, Geekom has opted for standard DDR4, letting you expand the 32GB of RAM that comes with the machine up to 64GB. This is ideal for creative applications and gaming, while 32GB will more than suffice for most office-based work.
Unusually, there are three storage slots, and the machine ships with a 1TB M.2 NVMe Gen 4 SSD. Alongside this, there’s room for a compact M.2 SATA SSD and a 2.5-inch SATA SSD, which are crammed into the small body, boosting the storage from the 1TB that ships with the machine all the way up to a very respectable 5TB, although only one of those will be the ultra-fast M.2 NVMe.
One surprise in the feature list was that it has two HDMI 2.0 ports and two USB4 ports, supporting up to four 4K monitors or one 8K display. This is ideal if you have large amounts of data you need to see on screen, and four 4K monitors are perfect for creative applications, although you’re normally limited to two or three.
Obviously, this is an incredibly small machine, which in the past has created heat distribution issues. However, to manage the heat, the IceBlast 2.0 silent cooling system has been integrated, which uses copper heat pipes to pull heat away from the electronics and push it out through vents dotted around the body.
One of the more surprising features is the reinforced metal internal frame, which Geekom claims can withstand up to 440lb (approximately 200kg) of pressure.
The network connectivity is good for an office environment with a single 2.5GbE Ethernet port and Wi-Fi 6E.
One big point about this machine that I really like is that GEEKOM gives you flexibility. So while you have a very powerful CPU, GPU, and NPU combination that can’t be upgraded, the RAM and storage offer far greater flexibility. With the USB4 ports at the back, you can connect to eGPUs and ultra-fast storage if needed.
As a final point on the feature set, this nice, small machine will already save you plenty of desk space, and it also includes a VESA mount. So if you want to mount it on the back of your monitor, that’s possible; and if you’re mounting it in a vehicle or on a rack or rig, the small size makes it nice and easy.
- Features: 4.5 / 5
GEEKOM IT13: Performance
CrystalDiskMark Read: 6,067.3 MB/s
CrystalDiskMark Write: 5,630.81 MB/s
Geekbench 6 CPU Multi: 15,150
Geekbench 6 CPU Single: 2,780
Geekbench 6 GPU: 23,903
Geekbench 7 CPU Multi: 16,394
Geekbench 7 CPU Single: 2,504
Geekbench 7 GPU: 21,903
PCMark Overall: 8,333
Cinebench R23 CPU Multi: 16,610
Cinebench R23 CPU Single: 2,051
Cinebench 2026 CPU Multi: 4,023
Cinebench 2026 CPU Single: 492
Fire Strike Overall: 6,198
Fire Strike Graphics: 6,670
Fire Strike Physics: 29,342
Fire Strike Combined: 2,285
Time Spy Overall: 3,210
Time Spy Graphics: 2,834
Time Spy CPU: 12,999
Wild Life Overall: 18,634
Steel Nomad Overall: 501
Sky Diver: Not tested
Windows Experience Overall: 8.4
Procyon: 1,303
Alongside standard mini PC uses for productivity, creative work, and browsing the internet, the IT13 features an integrated NPU that can boost local AI workloads with compatible apps, although at present many applications rely heavily on cloud-based AI processing. However, with the NPU present, I was keen to check out the AI performance alongside the more usual tasks.
As ever, I started the benchmarks by testing SSD speed, and it delivered impressive results, with transfer rates up to 6,067MB/s. It’s a reasonably fast PCIe 4.0 SSD, although the fastest drives using this interface can exceed 7,000MB/s. The speed of the SSD was highlighted throughout the test, especially as I started with video and photography applications where data was accessed quickly from the local drive to enable fast renders and exports.
As I ran through the Microsoft Office applications, I noted fast loading and use. I launched a large image-heavy PowerPoint presentation alongside Adobe Photoshop and a few browser windows. I noted that as enhancements were made, the amount of RAM I was using in the task monitor was getting close to the upper limit, and whilst the machine still ran well, I could start to feel a slight slowdown when switching from one application to another. Most notably, this was within Adobe Bridge, where thumbnail images started to render slowly.
The upshot is that for most Microsoft Office applications, the computer with 32GB of standard RAM and a 1TB SSD is more than sufficient for the vast majority of people. Even if you’re into video editing or photography, it has more than enough power, not just for lightweight apps but to fully run Adobe Photoshop and Lightroom. Where it will start to slow is when you just leave all applications open with large video and image projects.
When I opened Premiere Pro, an application known for pushing the limits of many mini PCs, I was impressed by how quickly it handled the data. However, the 1TB SSD is rather limited due to the size of the 4K footage that I’d captured on the Canon EOS R50 V. Plugging an external SSD into the USB4 port, whilst slower than the speed of the internal SSD, was still more than enough to provide data and video footage to Premiere Pro. Again, editing standard 4K footage, even with that limit of 32GB of RAM, was exceptionally good.
As I pushed the machine and quickly loaded 4K S-Log footage shot on the Sony A7 IV, I noticed a slowdown as the colour grading started. A 4K five-minute edit was well within this machine's limits, but as the complexity of the edit and grading increased, the timeline took longer to render, and the editing workflow felt sluggish.
Switching over to Blender, I was surprised by how fluidly it could create complex models quickly. The only real slowdown came when rendering those models, especially after I imported them with full texture mapping, and it was obviously due to the limitations of the internal GPU.
Finally, after getting through a good amount of work, I settled down to a bit of gaming; I loaded up Cyberpunk 2077 and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. The gameplay was quite different between the two games, with Indiana Jones running perfectly well at low settings. Overall, the gameplay was good, and I only saw a little graphical glitching during real action.
Switching from Indy to Cyberpunk 2077, I instantly realised that the graphics needed lowering, with resolution and effects dropped, including disabling ray tracing. Again, gameplay was possible, but I noted the frame rate was around 19 or 20 fps, which made it a bit jittery and, for me, not ideal for a relaxing gaming session. However, if needs must, you can still get through.
Finally, I wanted to test out the AI potential by running Lemonade. I ran several lightweight LLMs. I started with Qwen3.8-Distilled-2B-NPU2, a relatively lightweight LLM that I installed directly in Lemonade, though I discovered it wasn’t using the NPU, but was relying on the CPU and NPU.
I then ran a series of tests to explore this model's limitations, since it’s relatively small. The first point was just general conversation. Could it hold a conversation, and how accurate was it? Its actual knowledge was pretty good, though compared with online chat, you can tell its limits.
However, when you tie that chat in with, say, summarising a document, it really comes into its own, and it’s good at giving short summaries for emails and text, although I did have to copy everything into the chat window.
Likewise, giving it some data and asking it to summarise that data as a couple of paragraphs again worked well. It’s very technical and straightforward copy, but sufficient enough for when you do need to write a short extract quickly.
Likewise, I asked it to write a simple Python script to copy content from one folder to another, and again, it worked well. It’s very regimented, and I noticed that when I tried to update the code, it would just add to it, so there’s quite a bit of clean-up needed. However, it’s a starting point, and for a place to experiment, especially with Python, HTML and other basic coding, it’s actually surprisingly proficient, although you do have to copy and paste the code from the chat window into something like Visual Studio.
For anything more complex, like analysing images or even creating them, this is well beyond the limits of this particular model. However, other models can work and give you a basic idea of how these local LLMs can be used.
I then installed OpenVINO and ran a few more tests, this time focusing on a model that utilised the local NPU rather than the CPU and GPU. Here, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct proved to be the perfect option. This approach did mean that Python needed to be installed, and while the NPU kicked into action, the process isn’t as straightforward as you would hope, requiring some knowledge of LLM use. However, it does show the potential.
By the end of the test, the Geekom IT13 proved to be a powerful mini PC, well beyond what I had imagined, but the price at over £1000 does initially seem expensive. However, a quick comparison of other mini PCs with this level of CPU and memory quickly showed that this cost is actually well balanced.
- Performance: 4.5 / 5
GEEKOM IT13: Final verdict
The IT13 is an interesting mini PC. It’s small, compact and offers plenty of advanced connectivity options, including two USB4 ports at the back that enable connections to ultra-fast SSDs as well as eGPUs.
Throughout the test, I couldn’t help feeling that while the price is well balanced given the CPU and the potential for expansion and features, it still feels expensive for what is essentially a very solid workplace machine. But then that is the cost of hardware at present.
There’s no doubt that its Windows performance is exceptional. If you’re looking for a straightforward office machine that won’t slow down, even with the entire Microsoft Office suite open alongside browsers and music, it’s an ideal option. The way the cores work also means that when you need that extra power for handling images, it’s there, and when idle, it consumes far less power.
Using Photoshop, Lightroom, and even Premiere Pro, this small machine handled all of them as long as you’re not pushing it beyond general office-based use. So, for example, in an office environment, you’re more likely to shoot straight 4K without advanced codecs and are also unlikely to go into advanced effects or colour grading; in that case, this machine can handle pretty much any standard 4K edit you want to throw at it.
However, as you get more advanced with video enhancements, you can start to see where the integrated GPU struggles. The struggle is also reflected when gaming, and whilst I was impressed overall by the smoothness of gameplay in Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, with a game like Cyberpunk 2077, you can start to see where it falls.
This new mini PC, then, is a great option for any office looking for a compact machine that can do more than a bog-standard office PC. It can handle all Microsoft Office applications in one go; it can handle Adobe Creative Suite, and what surprised me most was its potential for installing and testing out local LLMs, even if just to give you an idea of how they work.
I do find it a bit overpriced for what it can do, since older machines can run traditional apps just as well. However, you’re paying that added premium for one of the latest CPUs and the AI-potential boost through the integrated NPU.
Should I buy the GEEKOM IT13?
| Value | Unfortunately, component costs mean the machine is expensive | 3.5 | 
| Design | Overall, build quality is decent, and the machine feels robust. Just be careful for wires when opening it up. | 4 | 
| Features | With plenty of ports, decent connectivity and plenty of upgrade options, this is a feature-packed mini PC. | 4.5 | 
| Performance | Decent performance across the board, making this a good high-end office machine, although GPU performance is limited. | 4.5 | 
| Overall | An excellent choice for an office machine with a little more power than most, and its integrated NPU can be useful for AI-enhanced applications. | 4.5 | 
Buy it if...
You need a powerful office machine.
Throughout the test, application speed showed how this small machine packs plenty of power for productivity and creative work.
You need something small and portable.
While the shell of the case might be plastic, the interior is metal, and it all feels good and robust, perfect for use out in the field.
Don't buy it if...
You need GPU performance.
While the integrated Intel graphics are impressive for most productivity tasks, you'll hit the limit for more advanced creative work.
You’re limited on budget.
Older machines can be just as powerful for a lot less money.
For more professional-grade desktops, we've tested the best business computers.
Alastair is a photographer, filmmaker and tech writer who has been working in the publishing industry since the late 1990s. For more than 25 years he has covered photography, video and technology across Future's photography, technology and gaming brands. He runs a photography and video production company and lectures in TV and film. He can usually be found testing mini PCs or prototyping and prop building with the aid of 3D printing.

articles.title: Black Friday : le téléviseur Philips Ambilight QLED 4K de 65 pouces à 649 € au lieu de 899 € chez E.Leclerc
articles.text:
Black Friday : le téléviseur Philips Ambilight QLED 4K de 65 pouces à 649 € au lieu de 899 € chez E.Leclerc
Du 20 au 30 novembre, E.Leclerc retire 250 € du Philips Ambilight 65PQS8701, qui passe sous la barre des 650 € dans sa version à 65 pouces.
Au-delà de la remise, ce modèle a un argument bien rare : ce fameux halo lumineux qui prolonge l’image sur le mur, et qui change complètement la façon dont on regarde un film, ou dont on joue à un jeu vidéo.
Ambilight, pour une immersion totale
C’est la signature de Philips depuis des années, et elle reste d’ailleurs exclusive à la marque : ce nom est employé pour désigner des LED intégrées à l’arrière du châssis, qui projettent sur le mur un halo de couleurs capable de suivre en temps réel ce qui se passe à l’écran. Sur ce modèle précis, le dispositif couvre trois côtés, ce qui donne une enveloppe lumineuse large plutôt qu’un simple liseré.
Vous savez, il est finalement assez difficile de décrire l’effet à l’écrit : en réalité, il faut le voir pour mieux le comprendre, mais tentons quand même l’expérience. L’ambilight fait que l’image ne s’arrête plus au cadre. Par exemple, un plan de nuit pourra permettre d’assombrir la pièce, tandis qu’une pelouse de stade pourra la teindre en vert, là où un jeu lui permettra de réagir à chaque explosion. En prime, pensez à votre santé : le confort visuel y gagne aussi, puisque l’écart de luminosité entre un écran très lumineux et un mur noir se réduit nettement. C’est justement cet écart qui a tendance habituellement à fatiguer les yeux lors d’une séance nocturne.
En parallèle, la fonction AmbiScape permet de synchroniser vos éclairages connectés compatibles avec l’action, ce qui donne à toute la pièce des allures de prolongement de l’image, avec une immersion encore plus approfondie. S’y ajoutent plusieurs modes dédiés, dont un mode jeu, un mode musique et un éclairage tamisé, ainsi qu’une adaptation automatique à la couleur de votre mur.
Une image QLED 4K épaulée par le processeur P5
La dalle 4K de 3 840 x 2 160 pixels s’appuie sur une couche de points quantiques (d’où l’appellation QLED, vous voilà au courant) qui élargit le volume de couleurs affichable et donne des teintes plus franches qu’un simple rétroéclairage LED classique. Sur 164 cm de diagonale, cette définition prend tout son sens dès deux mètres cinquante de recul.
Le vrai travail se joue toutefois en coulisses, avec le processeur P5 Perfect Picture Engine, à savoir l’élément le plus souvent sous-estimé d’un téléviseur. Cette puce permet de traiter simultanément les couleurs, le contraste, la netteté et la fluidité des mouvements, et surtout, elle remet à niveau les contenus qui ne sont pas en 4K (ce qui reste le cas de la majorité de ce que l’on regarde). Sachez qu’un bon processeur se mesure justement là, à savoir sur une source médiocre et pas sur une démo soignée.
Côté HDR, le téléviseur prend en charge le HDR10, le HDR10+ et le HLG, ce qui couvre le streaming comme la diffusion en direct, et les amateurs de réglages noteront la compatibilité avec la calibration Calman.
Dolby Atmos, DTS:X et un moteur sonore qui s’adapte
Le téléviseur est compatible le Dolby Atmos et le DTS:X, ces deux formats ayant pour objectif principal de placer les sons en hauteur et autour de l’auditeur. Le moteur IntelliSound analyse de son côté ce que vous regardez pour ajuster les réglages, en distinguant un film, un concert ou un journal où seule la voix a de l’importance. Bien entendu, des styles prédéfinis et un égaliseur restent accessibles si vous préférez garder la main, avec un renforcement des dialogues et un mode nuit.
Soyons précis sur une chose néanmoins : la configuration audio reste un système deux voies de 20 W, ce qui est largement suffisant au quotidien, mais qui ne remplacera pas une barre de son si vous cherchez un certain impact dans les basses. De fait, le téléviseur est prêt pour l’emploi, avec une sortie eARC sur son premier port HDMI et une télécommande unique capable de piloter l’ensemble.
Titan OS et le reste du quotidien
Pour lier le tout, ce téléviseur profite d’une interface Titan OS, qui a tendance à viser la simplicité, avec un accès direct aux principales applications de streaming, de Netflix à Prime Video en passant par Disney+ ou YouTube. Le téléviseur est par ailleurs compatible Matter, et fonctionne avec Google Home, Amazon Alexa et Apple Home, ce qui permet de l’allumer ou de baisser les lumières à la voix depuis l’assistant que vous utilisez déjà (si c’est le cas, évidemment).
Considérez aussi un petit détail pratique : le châssis, épais de 56 mm et pesant 18,4 kg sans son pied, accepte une fixation murale VESA 300 x 300. Ce sera bienvenu pour tirer au mieux parti de la fonction Ambilight, puisque le halo a besoin d’un mur proche pour s’exprimer au mieux.
Pour le jeu
Quant aux joueurs, qui accordent de l’importance à des données parfois un peu différentes, sachez que le téléviseur prend en charge le VRR, qui synchronise l’affichage avec la console pour éliminer les déchirures d’image, et l’ALLM, qui bascule automatiquement en mode faible latence dès qu’une partie démarre. Une barre de jeu permet en outre d’accéder aux réglages sans quitter l’écran, et vous pouvez compter sur trois entrées HDMI, dont la première assure également la sortie audio eARC vers une barre de son (comme vu précédemment).
L’offre
Actuellement, le Philips Ambilight 65PQS8701 passe à 649 € au lieu de 899 €, soit 250 € de remise, du 20 au 30 novembre chez E.Leclerc. À ce tarif, un 65 pouces QLED 4K doté d’Ambilight sur trois côtés se situe nettement en dessous de ce que coûte habituellement cette combinaison plutôt gagnante, si vous voulez notre avis. Les prix pouvant évoluer pendant l’opération, c’est celui affiché sur la fiche produit qui fait foi au moment de l’achat.

articles.title: Qué tan efectivo es cargar el celular en modo avión para llegar al 100%
articles.text:
Cargar el celular en modo avión puede acelerar el proceso para llegar al 100%. Según la empresa española Yup Charge, activar esta función durante la carga puede reducir hasta un 25% el tiempo necesario, porque el dispositivo deja de destinar energía a mantener activas las conexiones de WiFi, datos móviles y Bluetooth.
Cuando el teléfono opera en modo normal, sus radios de comunicación trabajan de forma continua en segundo plano y consumen energía que compite con la que entra por el cargador.
Al desactivar esas funciones con el modo avión, una mayor parte de la corriente disponible se destina a reponer la batería. El resultado es una carga más rápida, sin necesidad de comprar accesorios adicionales.
Por qué el modo avión acelera la carga
El modo avión desactiva las antenas de radio, suspende las notificaciones y detiene la sincronización de aplicaciones. Según Yup Charge, esto permite que una mayor proporción de la corriente se dirija a las celdas de la batería, lo que explica la diferencia de velocidad.
El recurso es útil cuando se dispone de poco tiempo y se necesita que el dispositivo esté listo cuanto antes.
Sin embargo, el modo avión solo optimiza la velocidad de carga. La salud de la batería a largo plazo depende de otros hábitos.
Además, no es un opción viable si es necesario estar pendiente de un mensaje o llamada. En estos casos, lo recomendable es activar el modo de ahorro de batería presente en varios celulares, disminuir el brillo de la pantalla, desactivar el Bluetooth y limitar el uso de manera considerable.
Cómo cuidar la batería del celular
El primero consejo es usar siempre el cargador original o uno certificado y compatible con el modelo del dispositivo. Esto garantiza que la corriente suministrada sea la adecuada y evita daños internos.
Conviene evitar cargar el celular hasta el 100% de forma constante. Lo recomendable es mantener el nivel de batería entre el 20% y el 80%, ya que los ciclos completos de carga reducen su vida útil con el tiempo. Las descargas totales frecuentes también aceleran el deterioro.
Otro hábito recomendado es evitar el uso intensivo del teléfono mientras se carga. El calor generado eleva la temperatura interna y afecta tanto la velocidad de carga como el estado general de la batería.
Las temperaturas extremas, tanto el calor como el frío, son uno de los principales factores de degradación en las baterías modernas. La vida útil de una batería de celular ronda entre dos y tres años, equivalentes a entre 300 y 500 ciclos completos de carga.
Un mal manejo puede acortar ese período y provocar descargas rápidas, apagados inesperados y una reducción en el rendimiento general del teléfono, ya que muchos sistemas limitan la velocidad del procesador cuando detectan un deterioro avanzado de la batería.
Las cargas cortas y el riesgo de dejarlo conectado
Dejar el celular cargando toda la noche no es una práctica recomendada, aunque los teléfonos inteligentes modernos detienen el flujo de energía al llegar al 100%. El problema es el goteo continuo de carga posterior, que genera calor y acelera el desgaste de la batería.
Según Isidor Buchmann, de Battery University, cargar el dispositivo en intervalos cortos durante el día es una práctica más saludable.
Honor e ingenieros de Xiaomi coinciden en esa postura: las cargas cortas y frecuentes reducen el desgaste. Aunque el teléfono detiene la carga al llegar al máximo, permanecer conectado durante muchas horas genera microciclos de recarga que deterioran la batería con el tiempo.
“El calor es el principal enemigo silencioso de la batería”, advirtió Juan Pablo Cortés, director de ventas de Xiaomi Colombia.

articles.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Fixes Coming November 19
articles.text:
The maintainers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday issued an advisory announcing an upcoming security release that addresses critical flaws.
The release is scheduled for November 19, 2026, between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC.
"These releases are part of PHP's regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions," the maintainers said. "The highest severity is CRITICAL."
However, the project also noted that issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups. It did not disclose any additional specifics.
The update is expected to include CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution flaw that succeeds only if the following conditions are met -
- An application sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration, and its code switches the handler to php with ini_set() before calling session_start().
- Session upload progress is enabled, which is PHP's default.
As mitigations, users were urged to set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release and restart the PHP worker for the setting to be applied.
The development comes nearly a month after PHP released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively tracked as PHP2Shell that enable unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via specially crafted HTTP requests.
The shortcomings have since come under limited active exploitation, targeting publicly-accessible Palo Alto Networks management interfaces and Check Point Security Gateways to launch attacks against Active Directory and deliver backdoors.
In a report published on October 30, 2026, Hunt.io said it identified 616 PHP2Shell-related files, spanning shared exploit kits, cloned proof-of-concepts (PoCs), custom heap exploits, scanners, and post-exploitation tooling, across multiple hosts, even as participants in underground forums have sought exploits, discussed prerequisites, and whether circulating PoCs worked.
"Exploit developers are unlikely to create a single universal exploit that works reliably across all affected PHP deployments," CrowdStrike said.
Last month, PHP also released patches to address a critical flaw in Brotli (CVE-2026-111497 aka Node2Shell or Broccoli2Shell), an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the decoder library that could result in arbitrary code execution.
Users are advised to apply the updates as soon as they become available.

articles.title: The AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU comes with a free 850W PSU thanks to Newegg’s Black Friday sale
articles.text:
The AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU comes with a free 850W PSU thanks to Newegg’s Black Friday sale
If it’s time your AM4 PC got an upgrade, Newegg is throwing in a free PSU with this AMD Ryzen 7 processor
The AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D has made a comeback as part of AMD’s celebrations to mark the tenth anniversary of the AM4 processor socket, and Newegg is sweetening the deal by bundling a free power supply with this capable bit of silicon.
The 10th Anniversary Edition is currently listed at $349.99, with a $29 discount available if you use the promotional code on the page. And by clicking a button on the website, you’ll also receive an ASRock 850W power supply, normally valued at $84.99.
It’s an interesting opportunity for anyone looking to upgrade an existing gaming PC without replacing their entire platform.
Today’s best AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D deal
The processor is available directly from Newegg for $349, and you can enter the code on the product page to save $29. You can also claim the free ASRock PRO-850B power supply while the promotion lasts.
Why the Ryzen 7 5800X3D is still worth considering
AMD’s eight-core, 16-thread processor uses the Zen 3 architecture and features a maximum boost clock of 4.5GHz. Its biggest advantage is 96MB of L3 cache, which uses AMD’s 3D V-Cache tech to boost gaming performance in titles that can take advantage of having more data readily accessible to the processor.
As its Anniversary Edition designation indicates, this chip slots into the established AM4 socket and uses DDR4 memory. That makes the Ryzen 7 5800X3D a particularly appealing option for any PC owners who want to upgrade an older system without investing in a new motherboard and memory.
The 5800X3D remains a formidable gaming processor, although its productivity performance is less impressive by modern standards. It also lacks integrated graphics, so you’ll need a dedicated graphics card.
Read our original AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D review
Is this bundle worth buying?
The 5800X3D’s $349 asking price is difficult to justify for someone building a completely new PC. However, existing AM4 owners can avoid replacing their motherboard and DDR4 memory, making this a much more attractive upgrade.
The additional $29 discount and free 850W PSU sweeten the deal, especially if you’re also planning to upgrade your graphics card and need some extra juice.
Should you buy it?
Buy it if… you’re upgrading an existing AM4 gaming PC and want a substantial CPU performance improvement without rebuilding your system.
Skip it if… you’re building from scratch or prioritize productivity performance. A newer platform may offer a better long-term investment.
