articles.title: LibreOffice maker asks governments why they had no backup plan for the Microsoft 365 outage
articles.text:
Down with the Cloud: The outage that took down Microsoft 365 is likely to leave a mark on many of the parties involved. Even The Document Foundation, the "small" organization managing LibreOffice development, wants answers from the officials who tied entire organizations, and a good deal of taxpayer money, to a single productivity vendor.
The Document Foundation has shared a list of pointed questions aimed at organizations hit by the recent Microsoft 365 outage. TDF is hardly a neutral party: the non-profit develops the free alternative, and it says it received more than 1,000 donations in 24 hours as the outage unfolded.
In particular, the foundation behind the LibreOffice productivity suite wants to know the ins and outs of the contractual obligations that led to widespread issues across many enterprise and public organizations. Free alternatives do exist, TDF argues, so why aren't more organizations using them?
According to the sources TDF cites, the outage left some of Microsoft's most popular services unavailable or degraded in at least 70 countries for almost 24 hours. Affected organizations included parliaments, courts, police forces, local authorities, health services, and more. Microsoft said the outage stemmed from a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade (it later pointed to a latent bug dating back to July), with no cyberattack involved for once.
Now, TDF is asking public officials and administrators to explain themselves. The foundation wants to know the actual impact of the outage, and whether contingency plans were prepared for email, calendars, documents, and other critical services before the problem started on November 12.
Both SMEs and larger organizations should have had alternative communication channels in place when Outlook became unreachable. The disruption reached clinical work: in the UK, NHS services reported problems with patient referrals and prescriptions, and pharmacies warned of delays.
Legal proceedings relied on the same services, too, with a trial in Manchester halted after a judge sent jurors home. TDF is asking which clinical and court procedures depend on a single vendor's email and calendar, and which have "independent" fallbacks.
Furthermore, TDF questions how much "public" money was spent on Microsoft licenses and cloud subscriptions over the last five years. Document portability should now be a crucial requirement for data management, and TDF is asking administrators why they didn't have a tried and tested exit strategy when Microsoft's clouds disappeared into thin air during office hours.
The main idea behind TDF's pointed inquiry is that, for twenty years, it has been proposing open source and open standards to politicians and public officials, and it was only met with "smiles." LibreOffice is an open, free alternative to proprietary and subscription-based services, and TDF is now urging officials to finally listen before yet another massive outage hits the computer world.
The timing is no accident, and the argument isn't new. Over the past year, Denmark's digital ministry, the German state of Schleswig-Holstein, Austria's armed forces, and the International Criminal Court have all announced moves away from Microsoft, citing digital sovereignty. TDF's questions land in a climate where that case was already being made.
Indeed, LibreOffice is a popular alternative to Office and other commercial office platforms, and millions of people already use the suite every day. However, replacing Microsoft's solutions is no easy feat for public institutions and larger enterprises alike. Schleswig-Holstein reported misdirected emails and delays during its migration, and open source software alone wouldn't have prevented a server-side capacity failure like this one.

articles.title: 500 Global, Sanabil Investments select seven startups for accelerator's 12th cohort
articles.text:
500 Global, Sanabil Investments select seven startups for accelerator's 12th cohort
- US-based venture capital firm 500 Global and Saudi Arabia's Sanabil Investments, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), have selected seven startups from 888 applications for the 12th cohort of the Sanabil Accelerator by 500 Global.
- Running from 27 September to 9 December 2026, the hybrid accelerator supports early-stage startups operating across operational technology cybersecurity, sovereign AI, regulatory technology, construction technology, legal technology, women's health and fintech.
- The selected startups are CQR, which develops cybersecurity solutions for industrial infrastructure; Daleela, a women's health platform; Delta Flow, an AI-powered construction project management tool; Inovat, a cross-border VAT refund platform; JUSTECH, an AI-powered legal technology platform; Ossus AI, which automates compliance, risk and cybersecurity operations; and Watad, a construction procurement and financing platform.
- Participating startups receive mentorship, workshops led by industry operators, and access to regional and international networks. The cohort will present at an invitation-only Demo Day on 9 December 2026, while applications for the next cohort are open.
Press release:
500 Global, a multi-stage venture capital firm, and Sanabil Investments, a wholly owned company of the Public Investment Fund (PIF), announce the twelfth batch of the Sanabil Accelerator by 500 Global, a hybrid program supporting early-stage founders building in sectors critical to the region’s future. Running from September 27 to December 9, 2026, the cohort brings together a highly selective group of seven startups, chosen from 888 applications, with companies building across operational technology (OT) cybersecurity, sovereign AI and regulatory technology, construction technology, legal technology, women’s health, and fintech.
Batch 12 leans further into the infrastructure that underpins the region’s growth. Several companies in this cohort are building for heavily regulated or mission-critical environments: protecting the industrial control systems behind critical infrastructure, running compliance and risk operations for regulated businesses, and bringing AI into the Saudi legal system. Two companies are focused on construction, one of the region’s largest and most capital-intensive sectors, addressing project delivery and contractor cash flow. For this cohort, the team continued to prioritize companies that demonstrate strong operating discipline, clear business fundamentals, and a sharp focus on execution.
Participating founders have received targeted mentorship, operator-led workshops, access to regional and global networks, and exposure to ecosystem stakeholders ahead of Demo Day on December 9, 2026. Batch 12 has been designed around hands-on execution support tailored to each company’s stage, market, and go-to-market motion.
“Batch 12 shows how far founders in the region are willing to go in tackling hard problems,” said Abdulrahman AlJiffry, Partner at 500 Global. “This cohort is building in areas like critical infrastructure security, sovereign AI, construction, and legal services, where trust and execution matter as much as the technology itself. These are companies with the potential to become foundational to how the region operates, and we are proud to support them with the capital, mentorship, and network to help them scale from MENA to the world.”
A spokesperson for Sanabil Investments added, “The quality and ambition of the founders in Batch 12 reflect the strength of the region’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. These companies are applying technology to some of the Kingdom’s most important sectors, from critical infrastructure and regulated industries to construction, healthcare and financial services. Through the Sanabil Accelerator by 500 Global, we are proud to support ambitious founders with the networks, expertise and access they need to build scalable businesses and contribute to the Kingdom’s long-term growth and economic diversification.”
The Sanabil Accelerator by 500 Global Batch 12 companies are:

articles.title: Des milliers de satellites-miroirs pour renvoyer la lumière du Soleil : le premier va officiellement décoller
articles.text:
La startup californienne Reflect Orbital accélère sur ses satellites-miroirs, avec un premier vol désormais ciblé pour le deuxième trimestre 2027. Mais la communauté scientifique s’inquiète de ce projet au plus haut point.
Fondée en 2024, Reflect Orbital veut vendre du « soleil à la demande « grâce à des satellites équipés de miroirs capables de réfléchir la lumière solaire vers des zones précises de la Terre après la tombée de la nuit.
Après avoir obtenu l’autorisation du régulateur américain pour un premier satellite de démonstration, la jeune pousse vise le déploiement de jusqu’à 50 000 engins d’ici à 2035 afin d’alimenter les fermes solaires après le coucher du Soleil, d’éclairer des chantiers ou l’agriculture, et d’épauler des opérations de secours nocturnes. Et visiblement, son projet séduit.
Black Friday Roborock
Profitez du meilleur du nettoyage et bénéficiez de meilleures offres et services : plus de points Cadeau, réductions sur les packs, assurance transport gratuite, paiement en plusieurs fois sans frais, prix garantis pendant 30 jours
Reflect Orbital sécurise ses futurs lancements
Car ce 10 novembre, la start-up a annoncé avoir bouclé une levée de fonds de 73,5 millions de dollars, portant le total de ses financements à plus de 100 millions de dollars. Et si elle garde l’identité de la fusée confidentielle pour son premier lancement, elle a réservé deux vols auprès de l’entreprise indienne Skyroot Aerospace afin de sécuriser d’autres déploiements futurs.
Sur le terrain, Reflect Orbital a déjà mené une simulation grandeur nature le 10 octobre dernier, de 19 heures à minuit, près de Lone Pine en Californie. Des projecteurs installés en altitude ont reproduit un faisceau d’environ 0,7 lumen (un peu plus intense qu’une pleine lune) pour aider des secouristes bénévoles à s'entraîner. Car pour les équipes de secours, cette lumière peut s’avérer précieuse lors d’une catastrophe majeure comme un séisme.
Les voix s'élèvent
Les experts, eux, sont préoccupés. En effet, l’observation de ces miroirs à travers un télescope amateur comporte un risque de lésions oculaires irréversibles. Un enjeu d’autant plus majeur pour les astronomes : une multiplication massive de ces engins risque de saturer les clichés de traînées lumineuses et d’augmenter la luminosité du ciel nocturne, compliquant la détection de galaxies lointaines ou d’astéroïdes potentiellement dangereux.
Mais ce n’est pas tout. Des spécialistes du sommeil, de la chronobiologie et de l’écologie ont prévenu qu’une lumière artificielle continue pouvait dérégler l’horloge biologique humaine, perturber le repos et désorienter les espèces migratrices ainsi que les écosystèmes.
Problème, aucune instance internationale n’impose aujourd’hui de règles strictes sur la brillance ou le volume de ce type de constellations, voué à se multiplier, laissant la régulation à la traîne face aux ambitions industrielles. De son côté, Reflect Orbital assure que son service exigera des autorisations et un accord local.
Elle promet, en outre, que l’éclairage au-dessus des observatoires astronomiques sera interdit, tandis que les satellites resteront éteints tant qu’aucun client ne les sollicite.

articles.title: TechPowerUp GPU-Z v2.72.0 Released
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
TechPowerUp GPU-Z v2.72.0 Released
TechPowerUp today released the latest version of GPU-Z, the popular graphics subsystem information and diagnostic utility for gamers, PC enthusiasts, and engineers. Version 2.72.0 comes with support for the NVIDIA RTX Spark processor. Support is also added for a rare GeForce RTX 5070 variant based on the larger GB203 silicon; and the unreleased GeForce RTX 4090 Ti engineering sample. Over in the red team, support is added for the AMD BC-250 mining GPU; and the new Intel graphics solutions supported cover "Raptor Lake-H" Refresh; and Iris Pro P555.
On machines with integrated graphics, the memory now shows "iGPU" followed by committed memory share size. A tooltip that shows sensor value statistics when hovering over the sensor's number display has been added. We've added support for yet-unknown NVIDIA power rails in the Advanced view, which are now displayed as "Rail ### power draw." This feature is disabled by default. For graphics cards with unknown GPUs (such as fake ones), GPU-Z will now detect DirectX API version and feature-level support from the software instead of showing "unknown."
DOWNLOAD: TechPowerUp GPU-Z v2.72.0Clock speed and temperature monitoring has been added for certain AMD iGPU models. We've refined the Sensors tab, wherein the minimum/maximum/average readings now exclude invalid sensor readings. GPU Hotspot temperature reading has been added for AMD R9 200/300, Fury and RX 400/500 Series (Polaris, Lexa, Hawaii, Fiji, Bonaire, Tonga). OpenGL detection sometimes not working has been fixed. CUDA capabilities are now listed in the Advanced tab, which lists out several new CUDA attributes on NVIDIA GPUs.
- Added support for NVIDIA RTX Spark (some memory details still missing)
- Added tooltip that shows sensor value statistics when hovering over the sensor's number display
- On integrated GPUs, instead of "N/A", system memory is now shown as memory size: "iGPU (64 GB)"
- Unknown NVIDIA power rails are now included in sensors as 'Rail xxx Power Draw' (disabled by default)
- Unknown GPUs will now probe DirectX support from the running system instead of showing 'Unknown'
- Added support for clock and temperature monitoring on some AMD iGPUs
- Sensor min/max/avg no longer include invalid sensor readings in the calculation
- Added support for reading hotspot temperature on AMD R9 200/300, Fury and RX 400/500 Series (Polaris, Lexa, Hawaii, Fiji, Bonaire, Tonga)
- The Hot Spot thermal sensor is now named 'Hot Spot' on both AMD and NVIDIA
- Fixed OpenGL detection sometimes not working
- Fixed various typos and small errors in Advanced -> CUDA
- Added names for more DXVA GUIDs for AMD and NVIDIA
- Fixed DXVA detection for 8K support
- Added support for CUDA Capabilities 6.2, 7.x, 8.x, 9.0, 10.x and 12.x and several new CUDA attributes
- Advanced tab: don't show corrupted 'NVIDIA BIOS' section if the BIOS can't be read at all
- Added support for AMD BC-250 mining GPU
- Added support for NVIDIA RTX 5070 (GB203) and RTX 4090 Ti ES
- Added support for Intel Raptor Lake-H Refresh and Iris Pro P555 (E3-1558L v5)

articles.title: “Están pasando muchas cosas, tenemos que separarnos del ruido”, CEO de AMD Lisa Su sobre Jensen Huang
articles.text:
La directora ejecutiva de AMD, Lisa Su, se refirió a la renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO de Nvidia y evitó profundizar en la crisis interna de su principal competidor.
La ejecutiva elogió el recorrido de la compañía y de su fundador, pero señaló que la discusión debe volver a la expansión de la infraestructura para inteligencia artificial (IA).
“Nvidia es una compañía fenomenal. Jensen ha sido un líder tremendo para la industria”, afirmó Su en el evento TomorrowX Summit. Luego planteó que los acontecimientos alrededor de Huang deben evaluarse con distancia: “Están pasando muchas cosas. Tenemos que separarnos un poco del ruido”.
La líder de AMD señaló que “el ruido se resolverá solo con el tiempo” y propuso observar a largo plazo. A la par, valoró la conducción interina de Colette Kress, quien asumió el liderazgo de la firma fabricante de chips.
Por qué AMD ve una oportunidad en el mercado
La CEO afirmó que AMD atraviesa un momento de expansión vinculado a la construcción de centros de datos y sistemas de cómputo destinados a la inteligencia artificial. Según explicó, la empresa ve una “oportunidad tremenda” para formar parte de esa infraestructura junto con sus socios comerciales.
Su evitó formular previsiones concretas sobre un posible traslado de clientes desde Nvidia. En cambio, puso el foco en la hoja de ruta de AMD y en su capacidad de entrega.
Qué líderes han lanzado su apoyo al regreso de Jensen Huang a Nvidia
Elon Musk criticó la salida de Huang y comparó la decisión con apartar a una figura decisiva de un club deportivo en plena racha de triunfos. Durante la cumbre DealBook, en diálogo con el periodista Andrew Ross Sorkin, afirmó: “Tienes una racha ganadora y de repente echas a Michael Jordan de tu equipo”.
“No me parece una decisión inteligente”, añadió Musk. El CEO de Tesla y SpaceX señaló que una figura como Huang es difícil de reemplazar por su conocimiento técnico, sus relaciones con proveedores y clientes, y el vínculo que construyó con los trabajadores de Nvidia durante más de tres décadas.
Asimismo, Musk dijo que había escuchado una posición similar de parte de otras figuras del sector y del presidente Donald Trump. “Creo que el presidente ha expresado públicamente que piensa que Jensen debería haberse quedado como director ejecutivo, y todos los que conozco piensan lo mismo”, declaró.
La salida del cofundador de Nvidia generó una campaña pública que reclama su regreso. Musk firmó una carta abierta junto con Tim Sweeney, director ejecutivo de Epic Games, y Garry Tan, presidente de Y Combinator, para pedir la restitución de Huang en el cargo.
La petición superó las 165.000 firmas, incluidas más de 7.500 de empleados de Nvidia, una cifra equivalente a más del 15% de la plantilla, según la información difundida por los impulsores.
El cofundador de Uber, Travis Kalanick, también se pronunció: “Huang erró, sí, errar es humano, pero no creo que nada de lo que hizo alcance el umbral para separarlo de su compañía”.
El respaldo público contrasta con la posición comunicada por el directorio de Nvidia, que aceptó la dimisión y nombró a Kress como directora ejecutiva interina. El debate sobre una eventual restitución quedó condicionado a una decisión de la junta o a una acción de los accionistas en una futura reunión corporativa.
Por qué no es posible que la salida de Jensen Huang detenga el avance de la IA
El director ejecutivo de OpenAI, Sam Altman, afirmó que la salida de Huang no alterará el crecimiento de la industria de inteligencia artificial. Durante el evento Silicon Valley & The World, reconoció el peso del fundador de Nvidia en el desarrollo del sector, aunque descartó que el mercado dependa de una sola persona.
“Es difícil imaginar la revolución de la IA sin Jensen y la compañía que ha construido”, declaró Altman. Aun así, sostuvo que la demanda se mantiene firme: “Hay tanta demanda, y está tan claro que la IA es real y que la gente quiere usarla y que los ingresos y la demanda están creciendo con tanta fuerza, que creo que la industria estará bien”.
Altman definió a Huang como un “héroe” personal y sostuvo que “los héroes tienen defectos”. Aludió a su destitución temporal al frente de OpenAI en 2023, una experiencia que, según explicó, le permitió comprender parte de la situación que enfrenta el exCEO de Nvidia.

articles.title: FinBursa names Angelica Tigan CRO to lead US and global expansion
articles.text:
FinBursa names Angelica Tigan CRO to lead US and global expansion
- New York-based private markets technology company FinBursa has appointed Angelica Tigan as Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) to oversee global sales and partnerships, with an immediate focus on expanding its presence in the US.
- Tigan brings nearly 20 years of experience in private markets technology, having held sales leadership roles at BlackRock's Aladdin business and eFront, alongside previous positions at Intralinks and Gen II Fund Services.
- Co-founded and led by CEO Ismail Badereldine, FinBursa provides an AI-powered platform for private equity, venture capital, private credit, real estate and M&A firms, integrating investment CRM, deal management, fundraising, investor relations and virtual data rooms.
- The appointment follows the launch of FinBursa 360, which incorporates ALF, an agentic AI system designed to support investment research, due diligence, investor identification, fundraising and M&A transactions through five specialised AI agents and an orchestrator.
Press release:
FinBursa, the intelligent front office for private markets, has appointed Angelica Tigan, a former BlackRock and eFront sales leader, as Chief Revenue Officer to lead its global commercial expansion following the launch of FinBursa 360. Based in the US, Tigan will lead sales and partnerships worldwide, with an immediate focus on the US.
Tigan brings close to two decades in private markets technology, having built, led and scaled sales teams at BlackRock (Aladdin) and eFront, with previous experience at Intralinks and Gen II Fund Services.
FinBursa 360 is an all-in-one platform for private equity, private credit, real estate, venture capital and M&A advisory firms, family offices, wealth managers, placement agents and fund administrators. It brings investment CRM, deal flow and deal management, virtual data rooms (VDR), fundraising, opportunity distribution, investor relations and investor portals into one system of record.
AI built into the platform, not bolted on
ALF, FinBursa's agentic AI, runs five specialised AI agents and an orchestrator for fund managers, capital allocators and M&A advisors. Its relationship intelligence maps who knows whom across the firm and surfaces warm introductions to investors and buyers. Its research agent switches on for any deal, fundraise, sale or portfolio company, monitoring news and RSS feeds across its industry and geography for AI signals that help teams reduce risk and act on opportunities faster.
For fund managers and investors running due diligence, ALF reviews data room documents, flags contradictions, and drafts investment committee materials. For firms raising capital, it identifies best-fit investors from mandates, past commitments, recent engagement and AI signals, with shortlists and draft outreach. For sell-side M&A advisors, it helps prepare the CIM, build data rooms, shortlist buyers using AI signals, and track buyer outreach at every stage.
Ismail Badereldine, co-founder and CEO of FinBursa, said: "In the AI era, private markets firms need a connected front office, and we expect demand to grow sharply. Angelica understands what these firms value most, and knows how to turn great technology into real results for them. Her appointment will accelerate our growth in the US and globally."
Angelica Tigan, FinBursa's Chief Revenue Officer, added: "I've spent my career helping private capital firms get more from their technology, and FinBursa stands out. It's a modern, AI-native platform that connects the front office first, so AI can do far more. Firms can be up and running in days rather than months, without long implementation projects, and the return on investment is clear. I see a significant opportunity to bring this globally, particularly in the US."

articles.title: AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain — 93 large ‘AI factories’ with projected capacity of around 50 gigawatts
articles.text:
AI data center power demand will double by 2030 thanks to $4 trillion in spending, adding an entire Great Britain to energy strain — 93 large ‘AI factories’ with projected capacity of around 50 gigawatts
The real bottleneck isn't AI chips, but power grids.
The AI data center build-out is pushing electricity grids across the globe, with many regions facing demand from projects that would exceed the current peak load that each system could support. According to the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) World Energy Outlook 2026 report, a total of 120GW of capacity is currently available across all types of data centers across the globe, with another 120GW expected to be completed by the end of the decade, 75% of which would be dedicated to artificial intelligence. Aside from that, it’s also tracking 93 large “AI factories” that are either under construction or being expanded via satellite imagery. It estimates that the capacity for these sites grew from under 2GW to 17GW in just two years, and that they’re expected to hit a total of 50GW upon completion, the equivalent of adding a second Great Britain to power demand.
This massive power consumption is one of the reasons for the opposition against their construction in communities, with residents blaming them for increased utility prices. However, the IEA says that its analysis “does not yet show a clear relationship between growth in data center capacity and increases in electricity prices.” It noted that if a data center uses existing capacity and pays for its share of the cost, then it could potentially lead to lower utility bills for all customers. However, if the grid operator is required to upgrade its system to accommodate the large consumer, then it could also lead to increased monthly bills if the costs are spread across all users.
Emissions are another issue that the IEA has raised. Renewable energy dominates data centers’ power purchase agreements at nearly 50%, but actual power generation puts coal- and natural-gas power sources closer to 60%. This is likely due to the need for reliability, with the latter kicking in when the former cannot deliver the power that the data center needs. Aside from that, a few projects are deploying their own power, like Elon Musk’s Colossus 2 in Southaven, Mississippi, with about 180GW planned or under construction in the U.S. So, even though renewable energy is growing to accommodate demand, it’s also expected that coal- and natural-gas emissions from data centers will rise by 70% by 2030.
Investments in AI data centers are expected to hit $32 trillion by 2050, putting the infrastructure spending for the industry larger than railways, electrification, and the internet, combined. Despite that, the IEA says the grid remains a significant bottleneck — renewable power plants take between one and five years to complete, which is around the same time that some massive data center projects take if they do not face an extended moratorium, while transmission works can take three to five times longer. This is probably one of the reasons why some AI hyperscalers are choosing to put jet engines on their sites instead, although these are also facing shortages, especially in turbine blades.

articles.title: GTA 6 : ours déchaîné, tigre en liberté, avion qui s’écrase…les joueurs découvrent des scènes complètement folles
articles.text:
L’attente aura été longue, mais elle est désormais terminée : GTA 6 est officiellement sorti. Si certains joueurs se concentrent sur l’histoire de Lucia et Jason, d’autres se sont empressés de parcourir librement l’État de Leonida pour en découvrir ses moindres recoins. À ce titre, le nouveau titre de Rockstar est qualifié par certains de générateur d’événements tant le monde ouvert est riche et organique. En l’espace de 24 heures, les réseaux sociaux ont été inondés de clips illustrant cet aspect du jeu. En voici une petite sélection.
Des animaux dangereux, des meubles à monter et un avion qui s’écrase
Dans GTA 6, une ouverture de coffre ou de porte peut réserver de sacrées surprises. Par exemple, un joueur est tombé sur des défenseurs de la cause animale réclamant la libération d’un animal retenu dans un camion. Le joueur décide de les aider en tirant avec une arme sur le loquet de la porte arrière du camion. On découvre alors un ours blanc enfermé dans une cage. Un militant écologiste décide de le libérer et la situation tourne au drame : l’ours se met à attaquer violemment tout le monde.
 Tyler (@Tylerrr) helps libtard protestors free a bear 😭😭 pic.twitter.com/XdKaiKjI7y
— Tyler Russell Paparazzi (@TLRupdates) November 18, 2026
Un autre exemple avec ce joueur qui décide d’aider une personne dont la camionnette est enlisée. Sauf qu’au lieu de pousser le véhicule, le joueur ouvre la porte arrière, laissant s’échapper un tigre. S’ensuit une bagarre à mains nues entre Jason et le tigre.
 A PRIMEIRA PESSOA A MORRER DESSA FORMA NO GTA 6 pic.twitter.com/qDMQhR3DLK
— Cortes do Chorume (@cortesdochorume) November 18, 2026
Voler un véhicule dans GTA 6 peut faire rameuter la police, mais il semble que cela ne soit pas le seul danger. Un joueur a ainsi volé la voiture d’un homme avant d’entendre des miaulements à l’intérieur du véhicule. Un chat, visiblement contrarié par la situation, s’en est alors violemment pris à Jason.
 If you steal a car with a cat inside in GTA 6, it will growl and try to attack you
The cat will jump on Jason, forcing him to throw it out of the car pic.twitter.com/Wr6QisquSE
— Dexerto (@Dexerto) November 18, 2026
Nous restons dans le registre des animaux, mais cette fois-ci avec un événement plus sympathique pour le joueur. Jason, en pleine mer, est rejoint par un chien sauveteur… qui conduit un jet-ski. Le protagoniste monte alors derrière l’animal, qui prend ensuite le large à toute allure. Tout va bien.
 aight, game of the year 😭😭🐕 pic.twitter.com/u2sYxMZyp3
— edeninho🦚 (@edeninhooo) November 18, 2026
GTA 6 a aussi été présenté comme un simulateur de vie. Un joueur peut ainsi passer son temps, non pas à parcourir la plage ensoleillée de Vice City, mais à retaper son appartement. Peindre les murs, monter un meuble, visser des planches : les possibilités sont multiples. Un utilisateur du réseau social X explique avec humour qu’il a pris un jour de congé pour « bosser à l’intérieur de GTA ».
 > peço folga do trabalho pra jogar GTA 6
> abro GTA 
> trabalho dentro do GTA pic.twitter.com/9gFVViazot
— malcriadinho perigoso (@buldogues) November 18, 2026
Il n’y a pas que le travail dans la vie : les joueurs peuvent donc aussi se prélasser en scrollant sur leur téléphone virtuel. Un passe-temps pour ceux qui n’en auraient pas encore assez avec leur véritable téléphone.
 You Can DOOM SCROLL on Your Phone in Grand Theft Auto 6 😭
Social Posts also have Comments, with CRAZY replies. pic.twitter.com/lKIElbbLen
— DETONATED (@DETONATEDcom) November 18, 2026
Enfin, nous pouvons mentionner un événement qui illustre particulièrement bien la dimension organique du dernier titre de Rockstar. Un joueur roulait tranquillement sur une route lorsqu’il a aperçu un avion en perdition. Il s’est alors lancé dans un périple pour se rendre sur le lieu du crash et constater les dégâts.
 Plane crash world event in GTA 6 (Don’t mind the driving) pic.twitter.com/rd3ttWqokk
— ɴ (@WearingSPF3000) November 18, 2026
Il s’agit là seulement d’une petite sélection d’événements survenus dans GTA 6. En réalité, nous aurions pu encore donner une multitude d’exemples. Rappelons que le jeu vient tout juste de sortir, son monde ouvert doit encore être pleinement exploré.
Le jeu réserve probablement encore beaucoup de surprises
GTA 6 est sorti il y a un peu plus de 24 heures (si l’on tient compte de sa sortie en Nouvelle-Zélande). Vu la taille de la map et le travail accompli par Rockstar, les joueurs ont certainement encore énormément de choses à découvrir. Il est même probable que certains événements ne soient découverts que dans plusieurs mois, voire années. Il ne reste plus qu’à reprendre sa manette pour tenter de découvrir toutes les surprises de GTA 6.

articles.title: What we learned from Nvidia's first earnings call without Jensen Huang - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
What we learned from Nvidia’s first earnings call without Jensen Huang
Nvidia Corp. reported its quarterly results this week, and contrary to the prevailing narrative, the sky didn’t fall.
Revenue more than doubled year-over-year. The Vera Rubin chip platform achieved the fastest product ramp in the company’s history, and management raised its fiscal 2028 growth outlook to roughly 75%, up from 70%. By all accounts, it was a solid beat and raise.
This was Nvidia’s first earnings call without co-founder Jensen Huang, whose resignation as president and chief executive was announced on Nov. 12. Board Chair Harvey Jones told investors that the resignation followed the “disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company’s code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms.” Hours after Huang publicly said he would be willing to return, Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and would not take questions about the circumstances or the board’s ongoing investigation.
Colette Kress, the longtime chief financial officer who is now also serving as interim CEO, set the tone in her first minute: “Our ambition will not change. Our passion for innovation will not change, and our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change.”
After listening to the call, I believe Nvidia answered the short-term question and left the long-term one open. The company made a convincing case that it can execute without its founder. It has yet to show who decides where it goes next. Here are five things we learned and what they mean for those who buy, budget for or operate artificial intelligence infrastructure.
1. The machine will run without the founder
The fear going into the call was disruption. The quarter closed before Huang’s exit, so the results can’t settle that. The guidance can, and it went up. Hyperscalers brought Vera Rubin into production in about a month, half the time Grace Blackwell required. The roadmap is set through Vera Rubin Ultra next year and Feynman in 2028, and Kress said the supply agreements extend through the end of the decade.
She explained that the past month has been “Business as usual.” Kress added, “We’ve engaged with our customers, suppliers and partners. They’re all 100% behind us.” She also noted that TSMC leadership was at Nvidia’s offices this week.
I have long held that Nvidia’s moat was never the silicon. It’s the accumulated layers of systems, software and supply chain built around it. The past week was the first real test of that view, and so far, it’s holding. A yearly product cadence this complex runs on thousands of engineers and a supply chain planned years in advance.
Asked about talent retention, Kress acknowledged that “there are diverse opinions” among employees while insisting they are “committed to doing their life’s work” at Nvidia. The company’s talent can’t be overstated, and although Huang was the face of the company, the employees are what made it tick.
Earlier this week, Cisco Systems Inc. CEO Chuck Robbins appeared with Brian Sozzi. When asked whether he still trusts Nvidia, Robbins replied immediately, “Absolutely.” He added, “The industry’s bigger than one person. I don’t care how good you are. There are a lot of smart people. There are 42,000 people at Nvidia. So I’m not all that concerned.” Huang may have been the most visible Nvidia employee, but the company is full of smart, driven people. Leadership understands this, and I expect turnover to have minimal impact.
Employee retention is a top-of-mind issue for Nvidia executives. Business Insider reported this week that the company held its first all-hands meeting after Huang. The article noted that Kress announced plans to accelerate pay raises and equity grants, Jones discussed the CEO search and Buck outlined the roadmap. It’s reasonable to believe that Huang’s departure was a shock to employees, but the business goes on, and I expect things to settle down in short order.
For information technology buyers, nothing changes about what you’ve ordered or planned over the next 18 to 24 months. Don’t pause a deployment because of a leadership headline. The advice I gave in August still applies: Welcome Nvidia’s simplification and hedge the dependency.
2. The board wants a diplomat as much as a technologist
One of the more interesting comments on the call came from Jones, not Kress. In describing the CEO search, which will consider both internal and external candidates, he said the board “appreciates that we’re living in a world where advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are driving major changes in our marketplace. Our new CEO will need to navigate those waters carefully.”
That was paired with immediate action. On the morning of earnings, the board created a standing national security and export control oversight committee of three directors that will retain outside experts. Kress disclosed that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China and noted that the U.S. Commerce Department issued new export controls this week, which the company “still has some time to study.”
Huang was a product visionary who also served as the industry’s chief diplomat. The board is now signaling that fluency in Washington is a core requirement, on par with technical vision.
For IT leaders at multinationals, export policy is now a deployment variable. The new Commerce rule is intended to block remote access to advanced chips via data centers in third countries, so the location of your capacity and who can access it are now compliance questions. Bring your compliance team into AI infrastructure planning early.
3. Allocation has become a readiness test
With demand still far ahead of supply, who gets Nvidia systems matters more than what they cost. Kress laid out the criteria more clearly than I’ve heard before. First are land, power and shell, meaning whether a customer’s facility is ready to receive and use the gear in the quarter it ships. Second is capital. Third, for customers that aren’t investment-grade, is proof of off-take, or evidence that someone has committed to use the capacity.
“All are getting the same pricing,” Kress said. “That is super important for us, and we just need to assure that they are ready on their side in terms of being able to accept the compute.”
Those same factors were incorporated into the guidance. Kress said the outlook “considers data center readiness, the strength and durability of end customer demand, and our customers’ access to capital.” The reality is that the AI bottleneck has shifted from the chip to the building, the grid and the balance sheet. Nvidia is serving as the industry’s underwriter, determining who is ready.
The lesson for enterprise buyers is that readiness is the currency. If you want on-premises systems, secure power, cooling and funding before requesting allocation. If you can’t, buy capacity from a provider that has already cleared this hurdle. In my view, this also helps explain why sovereign AI is growing so quickly for Nvidia. Those projects often arrive with land and power already in place.
4. Nvidia’s checkbook is getting pickier
Over the past year, Nvidia has used its balance sheet to seed the ecosystem through guarantees, investments, and commitments to neoclouds and AI labs. Though neoclouds remain important, Kress brought a different tone to this audience. She said Nvidia will “continue to be disciplined and selective” in supporting neoclouds and that it is “rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees” as other sources of capital become available. Asked about vendor financing, she acknowledged that “a lot of things have changed over this last quarter.”
Two notable details emerged during the call. When Bernstein Research analyst Stacy Rasgon pressed on what he read as new disclosure language about neocloud commitments, Kress explained that Nvidia’s guarantees take effect only after a partner has raised its own debt and equity, built the facility and installed the compute. If the project stalls, the guarantee lapses.
“Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No,” she said. Even so, spelling it out clarifies Nvidia’s participation in neoclouds. When asked about uses of capital beyond the share buyback, which she said Nvidia still plans to complete, she put suppliers first: “The top priority is going to be our suppliers.” Prepayments to expand capacity come before customer financing, which will be reserved for “very strong customers.”
This was a critical piece of information for investors. I’ve previously compared vendor-financed neoclouds to the CLECs of the internet era, where the financing organization was left holding the bag. A CFO-led Nvidia appears to see the same risk. The result is a shakeout in which well-capitalized neoclouds with contracted demand grow stronger, while thinly funded ones struggle to secure systems. This should offer some comfort to investors that circular financing has been de-risked.
The flip side is that someone still must fund the buildout outside the hyperscalers. Kress pointed to infrastructure capital partners establishing financing platforms. Whether that money arrives as fast as Nvidia steps back is what to watch for.
My advice to IT buyers is to ask, before signing a multiyear deal with a neocloud, how it’s financed, how much capacity is committed and where it stands in Nvidia’s allocation queue. Those were niche questions a year ago. They should be standard due diligence now.
5. Agents are pulling demand well beyond the GPU
The demand story has shifted from training models to running agents, broadening what customers need from Nvidia. Citing OpenRouter data, Kress said agentic workloads now account for roughly 80% of tokens. Falling token prices are driving more usage, keeping GPU rental rates climbing.
The CPU growth story shouldn’t surprise anyone. In May, I wrote that agentic AI opens a massive new spigot for Nvidia on the CPU side. This quarter, demand outpaced supply. “Agentic AI is driving extraordinary demand for CPUs, far outstripping supply,” Kress said, noting that Nvidia’s Vera CPU is now adopted by CoreWeave, Meta, Nscale and Open AI. Agents spend much of their time calling tools, running code and moving data, which is general-purpose work. A CPU shortage amid a GPU boom shows how quickly the workload is changing.
Nvidia is also filling in the layers above and around the hardware. The agent safety platform pairs OpenShell, which limits what agents can access, with Sentry, which runs on BlueField data processing units and monitors agent behavior in silicon. In my view, the biggest barrier to deploying agents in production is control, not model quality.
The network is part of this, too. Kress said co-packaged optics is in volume production, and Lambda’s deployment, announced at this week’s SC26 conference, is the first large-scale proof point. Nvidia is a formidable networking vendor, though buyers mixing accelerators will still want to weigh a network supplier that isn’t also selling a competing chip.
For IT buyers, plan CPU capacity for agent workloads now, and insist that agent controls reside outside the model, in infrastructure you can audit.
Dark-horse CEO candidates
The question of who the new CEO will be might not be just about Nvidia but about the entire industry. If the board goes internal, Ian Buck seems to be the frontrunner. Externally, the names most bandied about are Advanced Micro Devices Inc. CEO Lisa Su, Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas and Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian, or we could see Manuvir Das make a comeback and return to the company.
Most industry watchers describe Nvidia as a chip company, a view that is about a decade out of date. Nvidia’s value comes from the full systems it has built around its silicon. Each is a stack tailored to an industry: hardware, libraries, frameworks, pretrained models, simulation and developer tools, all tuned to work together.
The next CEO must treat silicon as a key layer of an open, secure, agentic enterprise stack. Enterprises won’t buy GPUs. They’ll buy outcomes: agents that run safely on governed data across clouds, on-premises and at the edge. Whoever runs Nvidia next must sell that outcome, play well within an ecosystem Nvidia doesn’t fully control, and make security a core part of the platform. Here are three dark-horse candidates to consider:
Matt Garman. The Amazon Web Services Inc. CEO has led the world’s largest cloud through the shift to AI. He knows what it takes to turn infrastructure into consumable services at enormous scale. Garman also lives the open-stack approach: AWS offers model choice, runs its own Trainium chips alongside Nvidia’s, and sells to enterprises that want flexibility rather than lock-in. He would bring operational discipline and a deep feel for the customer. The question is whether Nvidia’s biggest customer-turned-competitor can credibly lead the supplier.
Jeetu Patel, Cisco Systems Inc.’s president and chief product officer, is the best storyteller in enterprise tech after Huang himself. He has spent the past few years rebuilding Cisco’s portfolio around secure AI infrastructure, integrating networking, security and observability into a single platform. That is exactly the “open, secure, agentic” stack Nvidia must deliver. Patel thinks in platforms, moves quickly,and has been personally using AI agents to shape his product views. He also has deep enterprise credibility, which Nvidia needs more than additional credibility with hyperscalers.
Charlie Giancarlo, CEO of Everpure (formerly Pure Storage), may be the most underrated name here. He built networking businesses at Cisco, spent time in private equity, and has repositioned Pure as a data management company. Storage revenue is growing thanks to hyperscaler wins. Giancarlo understands that agentic AI depends on data and that the data layer and the network are where enterprise AI succeeds or fails. He is a systems thinker who has led a platform transition before.
Two final points on the CEO hire: For some reason, there is a tremendous amount of industry chatter that Jensen Huang was the only person at Nvidia with key relationships with suppliers, partners, and other ecosystem providers. I know for a fact that is not true. Nvidia’s leadership, which includes Buck, Deb Shoquist (executive vice president of operations), Nico Caprez (vice president of global AI development), Gilad Shainer and Kevin Deierling (networking leadership), Kress and others, all have deep relationships with the ecosystem.
Also, I wouldn’t expect the board to make a snap decision about its next CEO. The roadmap is baked beyond Feynman, and the company can continue for a couple of years, if needed. This is an important hire; the board should take its time and ensure it’s the right person.
Final thoughts
This call confirmed what many industry watchers, including me, have long believed: The moat was built in layers, and those layers held. Supply is constrained, the roadmap is set and customers are still asking for more than Nvidia can build.
Kress closed the call by saying, “We’ve got this.” On execution, I believe her. Kress is a steady hand right now, and the discipline she brings to capital allocation should make the AI buildout healthier. The bets that created Nvidia’s position, though, were placed years before the market arrived. Post-Jensen, Nvidia will continue to perform as it did; as Robbins put it, no one is bigger than the industry.
My advice to IT buyers is to stick with current plans and closely monitor the CEO search. Since Nvidia’s roadmap is baked through Feynman and beyond, it can ride momentum for the next two years or longer.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: GTA 6 senior design director confirms the ‘tools’ players acquire in the open world through the fence systems can be used again after completing jobs — ‘Even in the cases where we do show a level of completion, these locations can be hit again and again’
articles.text:
- Grand Theft Auto 6 senior design director: content & flow, Scott Butchard explains how criminal activity can be replayed even after completing jobs
- Butchard says the fences introduce robbery mechanics that can be used throughout the whole game after finishing missions
- He says that while jobs appear completed on the map, locations can be revisite and "tackled" in different ways
Rockstar Games has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 players can hit locations repeatedly even after completing jobs.
Responding to questions sent directly to Rockstar by TechRadar Gaming, senior design director: content & flow, Scott Butchard explained that missions involving fences — places on the map where players can sell any vehicles and loot they've stolen — introduce tools that can be used throughout the entire game.
"The fences introduce you to these different robbery mechanics in the open world, initially to progress their flows and build a relationship with them," Butchard said. "However, as these begin to expire, the player is left with the tools to continue these jobs off their own backs.
"For example, car tips for Randy’s list give way to you now having the experiences of where to find the best cars to sell to him. Yasmani points you to a range of places to rob and expands your knowledge in those areas as your work with him."
But what happens after players complete these jobs, whether it be a robbery or car-theft mission? Can players expect more self-generating scenarios that incentivise them to revisit missions even when they're complete?
According to Butchard, after players check off these jobs and they appear completed on the map, their related locations can be hit repeatedly.
"Even in the cases where we do show a level of completion, these locations can be hit again and again - tackling them in different ways each time," he said.

articles.title: Apple pourrait annuler l’iMac OLED pour ces deux raisons majeures
articles.text:
Finalement, l'iMac OLED attendra encore ! Après un MacBook Pro OLED enfin disponible, la marque à la pomme pourrait lâcher ses plans pour son ordinateur fixe pour au moins quelques années.
Alors que l'entreprise californienne vient de lancer son MacBook Pro avec écran OLED après de nombreuses années d'attente, Apple envisagerait de repousser, voire d'annuler, le projet d'un iMac doté d'une dalle OLED. Deux raisons seraient à l'origine de cette réflexion : le coût des dalles et la faiblesse des ventes de certains produits déjà équipés.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
L'Apple Watch : élément déclencheur de l'OLED
Initialement, la marque à la pomme s'est intéressée à la technologie OLED avec l'Apple Watch, alors que les autres produits de la marque utilisaient tous des dalles IPS LCD. La technologie a ensuite été portée sur iPhone et iPad, avant d'atterrir sur le MacBook Pro PROLED, présenté récemment.
Le constructeur avait pour idée d'étendre cette technologie à l'ensemble de sa gamme Mac, sur plusieurs années. L'iMac OLED n'étant au final pas attendu avant 2029, voire 2030.
Cependant, nos confrères de The Elec, indique que ce calendrier pourrait être une nouvelle fois repoussé, voire carrément abandonné. Apple serait en discussion avec Samsung Display à ce sujet.
Le coût, la demande, rien n'y est
Le premier facteur et non des moindres, c'est le coût. Les iMac se vendent à des volumes nettement inférieurs à ceux des ordinateurs portables de la marque. Ainsi, il serait compliqué de maintenir un tarif intéressant si les dalles OLED, plus coûteuses, étaient adoptées.
La demande est aussi de la partie. En effet, la faiblesse des ventes de l'iPad Pro OLED aurait également pesé sur la décision. Ainsi, John Ternus, le nouveau PDG d'Apple, examinerait la viabilité commerciale d'une extension de l'OLED à d'autres produits. La marque à la pomme aurait alors déjà demandé des devis à ses fournisseurs pour un écran d'iMac destiné à être lancé courant 2029. Ces devis concerneraient des dalles LCD, et non OLED.
Source : 9To5Mac

articles.title: Fiscalía y Junta piden tres años y medio de cárcel para los dos presuntos autores de daños en Pintia, en Valladolid
articles.text:
¿Cómo se destruye en una mañana una excavación protegida tras doce años documentándola? La Fiscalía de Valladolid y la Junta de Castilla y León piden tres años y seis meses de prisión para cada uno de dos administradores que abrieron una zanja en el yacimiento de Pintia. ¿Para qué era? Para meter una tubería de 10 centímetros con la que regar ajos y remolacha. El juicio será en marzo de 2027. Ellos insisten en ser completamente inocentes y desconocer lo que tenían debajo, pese a los carteles.
Qué pasó. Pintia fue una ciudad de los vacceos, un pueblo prerromano del valle del Duero. Está en Padilla de Duero, en Peñafiel, y su poblado de Las Quintanas es Bien de Interés Cultural desde 1993. Según la acusación, el 12 de enero de 2024 se abrió con una retroexcavadora una zanja para instalar una tubería de riego de diez centímetros de diámetro, sin autorización de Cultura.
Casi toda se tapó después con una pala cargadora, salvo unos 15 metros. Quien lo descubrió fue el director del yacimiento, Carlos Sanz, durante una inspección habitual en época de lluvias. Entonces avisó al Seprona, quienes paralizaron las obras.
Cuánto se destruyó. La acusación habla de unos 260 metros de longitud, que la UVa rebaja a unos 230. Mide entre 40 y 60 centímetros de ancho y entre 1,20 y 1,50 metros de profundidad, y atraviesa las parcelas 62 y 66, en el núcleo de un poblado de 25 hectáreas.
Los primeros sondeos técnicos hablaban de unos 1.200 metros cúbicos de terreno “completamente destrozado”. Es una estimación inicial y habrá que contrastarla con el peritaje en el juicio. Sanz calificó el daño de imposible de recuperar. El consejero de Cultura de entonces, Gonzalo Santonja, dijo que se había destruido en una mañana el trabajo de doce años y comparó los yacimientos BIC con las catedrales.
Datar el tiempo. El problema no es la superficie, sino lo que había debajo. Según el relato de las acusaciones, la zanja cortó la estratigrafía, es decir, los niveles de tierra que permiten fechar con precisión cada resto. Afectó a manzanas de viviendas vacceas y romanas, seccionó un tramo de la muralla vaccea y alteró un sector artesanal extramuros. Afloraron fragmentos de vasijas, cerámicas, adobes y tejas.
Cuánto se pide. Ahora mismo hay tres cifras a tener en cuenta:
- Cárcel: 3 años y 6 meses para cada acusado por parte de Fiscalía y Junta, y 3 años por parte de la Universidad de Valladolid. Subsidiariamente, todas piden multa por el delito imprudente.
- Restauración: la Junta exige que los acusados ejecuten a su cargo las medidas para restaurar el bien en lo posible.
- Indemnización: la Fiscalía reclama 918.853,40 euros, según un peritaje de noviembre de 2024. La Junta pide 669.470,51 euros y la UVa, 235.792,12 por la pérdida de capacidad de investigación de su Centro de Estudios Vacceos.
Las aseguradoras Mapfre y Axa aparecen como responsables directas en la petición de la Fiscalía.
La versión de los acusados. La defensa pide la absolución. Dice que cultivaban ajos y remolacha desde 2017 en una finca de 3,80 hectáreas y que nunca recibieron aviso de la protección arqueológica en el contrato de arrendamiento, el Registro ni el Catastro. Alega error de tipo invencible y que el cartel existente era genérico y estaba deteriorado. La acusación sostiene que había carteles informativos desde 2003 y 2004. La defensa impugna también la tasación.
Qué dice la jurisprudencia. Los casos más conocidos son de saqueadores que sabían lo que hacían, como el de la necrópolis celtíbera de Aratikos, donde el Supremo acabó condenando a tres años. Pintia se parece más a las obras en terrenos con restos, donde la discusión es cuánto sabían los autores. Según repaso académico citado, el artículo 323 exige dolo, pero admite el eventual: basta con representarse el daño como probable y aceptarlo.
¿Error invencible? El error invencible exime al “culpable”, aunque no se admite si el yacimiento es notorio. Si era vencible, se castiga como imprudencia grave (art. 324), solo con multa de 3 a 18 meses, y el deber de cuidado aumenta según el nivel de protección del bien. El mismo trabajo cita una condena por imprudencia grave en Cantabria (2007) por excavar en un terreno catalogado. Añade que los tribunales han atenuado penas por falta de señalización. Además, el Supremo (STS 641/2019) no exige una declaración administrativa previa para que exista protección penal.
Lo que se juzga. Se juzgan dos cosas: qué sabían o podían saber los acusados, y si una zanja de tubería puede acarrear cárcel y casi un millón de euros. Lo irreparable no depende del veredicto, porque lo que se llevó la zanja no volverá a excavarse. Con un BIC desde 1993, un yacimiento en excavación y carteles, el error “invencible” lo tiene complicado; pero todo puede ser.

articles.title: Día del Hombre: los mejores memes que puedes usar para dedicar
articles.text:
Este jueves 19 de noviembre, las redes sociales se llenan de saludos y memes por el Día Internacional del Hombre. Algunas publicaciones celebran a padres, amigos y compañeros; otras ironizan sobre lo poco conocida que resulta la fecha o sobre cómo muchos se enteran de que existe cuando ven una imagen compartida en Instagram, Facebook o WhatsApp.
El humor suele apoyarse en situaciones cotidianas: el amigo que recibe una felicitación inesperada, el grupo que pregunta si de verdad “hay un día del hombre” o quien responde con un meme al saludo. También circulan bromas sobre el contraste con otras fechas conmemorativas.
Por qué se conmemora el 19 de noviembre
El Día Internacional del Hombre se celebra cada 19 de noviembre y fue impulsado en 1999 por Jerome Teelucksingh, profesor de Trinidad y Tobago. La fecha busca destacar modelos masculinos positivos, reconocer las contribuciones de los hombres y los niños y poner atención en temas como la salud física y emocional. También propone mejorar las relaciones entre hombres y mujeres y promover la igualdad. La organización de la jornada resume estos objetivos en seis ejes.
El tema internacional de 2026 es “El futuro es de todos”, según el anuncio de International Men’s Day. La consigna invita a pensar en el bienestar y el futuro de hombres y niños como un asunto que involucra a toda la sociedad. El comunicado de este año mantiene el foco en la inclusión y en la colaboración.
La fecha no tiene el mismo reconocimiento en todos los países y puede pasar inadvertida para muchas personas. Por eso, cada noviembre suelen aparecer memes que juegan con la sorpresa de descubrirla o con la pregunta de por qué no se habla tanto de ella. El formato breve y fácil de compartir ayuda a que el tema llegue a usuarios que quizá no buscarían información sobre la conmemoración.
El humor en redes y la fecha de marzo
Parte de las bromas también menciona el 19 de marzo, día asociado con San José, que en algunos países se vincula con celebraciones dedicadas a los hombres o a los padres. La coincidencia alimenta memes sobre la existencia de dos fechas. Sin embargo, no tienen el mismo origen: el Día Internacional del Hombre se conmemora el 19 de noviembre, mientras que las celebraciones de marzo responden a tradiciones locales o religiosas.
Los memes pueden ser una puerta de entrada para conversar, pero también simplifican asuntos que requieren más contexto. La salud masculina, por ejemplo, incluye tanto la prevención de enfermedades como el acceso a apoyo emocional. La jornada también anima a reconocer a hombres que cuidan de sus familias, acompañan a sus comunidades y contribuyen a su entorno, lejos de los estereotipos de celebridad o éxito.
Una fecha para compartir y reflexionar
Las felicitaciones y las imágenes humorísticas forman parte de la conversación digital de este 19 de noviembre. Junto con ellas, la efeméride propone reconocer distintas experiencias masculinas y promover vínculos basados en el respeto. El humor puede acercar la fecha a más personas, siempre que no desplace esos temas ni los convierta en motivo de burla.
Así, entre memes sobre quién recordó la fecha y mensajes de saludo, el Día Internacional del Hombre invita a mirar más allá de la publicación viral: hablar sobre bienestar, valorar modelos positivos y pensar en cómo construir un futuro en el que todas las personas puedan participar.

articles.title: Age verification laws might have resurrected adult DVD sales
articles.text:
Ripple effect: Since age verification systems became mandatory in many territories, users have found various ways to circumvent them and continue accessing social media, adult websites, and other content deemed harmful to children. While most resort to VPNs or seek help from adults, recent sales data suggest that others are turning back to physical media.
A major adult film producer and a retailer recently told Mashable that adult DVD sales have surged in regions where governments have passed laws requiring online services to implement age-verification systems. The news adds to growing evidence that these measures have had limited effectiveness.
David Eliason, who owns three adult video stores in South Dakota, reported a 20% to 22% increase in sales over the past year. South Dakota passed its age-verification law last June.
Eliason confirmed that other stores had stopped selling DVDs due to the widespread availability of online adult content, but age-verification laws could slow that trend. Lewis Adams, director of adult video distributor Pulse Distribution, also confirmed an increase in sales in states with age-verification laws, including Texas, Florida, and Tennessee.
Age-verification laws in Australia, the United Kingdom, and numerous US states require websites hosting adult content to verify visitors' ages using methods such as facial scans and ID checks. Many adult users are reluctant to share personal information with these services, some of which have suffered security breaches, and have quickly found ways to bypass the requirements.
VPN use has skyrocketed in these regions, and Utah has even attempted to restrict VPN access in response. Some users reportedly resort to mannequins or 3D models to fool facial scanners, while others switch to non-compliant websites or pirate adult videos through torrents and Discord. Some privacy advocates argue that device-level age verification is the least intrusive approach.
In a recent Youth Endowment Fund study, roughly one-third of teenage respondents reported having bypassed age checks. Of those, one-quarter admitted to accessing adult content. While requiring an ID at an adult video store is technically another form of age verification, at least DVD players don't track their users online.
In related news, Best Buy recently begun testing a return to the market. So far, only The Odyssey is available in stores, but other titles including Project Hail Mary, Interstellar, It's a Wonderful Life, Top Gun, and Obsession are available as Blu-rays and 4K Blu-rays through the retailer's website.

articles.title: ADATA XPG INVADER X MINI Chroma Series Launched
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
ADATA XPG INVADER X MINI Chroma Series Launched
XPG, the gaming brand of ADATA Technology, today announced the INVADER X MINI Chroma Series mid-tower gaming chassis, giving the popular INVADER X MINI a vibrant new look. Available in SKY, CORAL, IRIS, and AQUA, the series marks XPG's first officially launched colorful chassis. It features panoramic glass, five pre-installed ARGB fans, ATX motherboard support, GPU clearance up to 330 mm, and support for 240 mm radiators, combining distinctive style with cooling performance and build flexibility.
Building on the popular INVADER X MINI, the Chroma Series introduces four expressive colorways—SKY, CORAL, IRIS, and AQUA. From refreshing sky blue and vibrant coral to dreamy purple and aqua green, the new palette brings a fresh alternative to gaming chassis traditionally dominated by black, white, and darker tones. As XPG's first colorful chassis series, it combines bold exterior colors with glass panels and ARGB lighting, creating greater visual harmony between internal components and the overall desktop setup while giving gamers more freedom to express their personal style.Compact Design Delivers Flexible Cooling and Hardware Support
Measuring 460 x 210 x 359 mm, the INVADER X MINI Chroma Series supports ATX, Micro ATX, and Mini ITX motherboards, offering broad hardware compatibility within a compact footprint.
- 4 mm Panoramic Tempered Glass
- The panoramic glass design provides a clear view of internal hardware and ARGB lighting for a cohesive showcase build.
- Five Pre-Installed ARGB Fans
- Five 120 mm ARGB fans, including four reverse-blade fans, deliver efficient airflow while keeping lighting fully visible.
- Flexible High-Performance Hardware Support
- Supports GPUs up to 330 mm, CPU air coolers up to 166 mm, and top-mounted radiators up to 240 mm, giving builders flexibility between air and liquid cooling.
- Easy Maintenance
A tool-free removable front panel and top and bottom dust filters simplify routine cleaning and system maintenance.
Bringing More Color and Personality to Gaming Spaces
As gamers place greater emphasis on both performance and personal style, the INVADER X MINI Chroma Series combines vibrant colors, panoramic glass, and flexible hardware support to balance aesthetics with functionality. As XPG's first colorful chassis series, it gives gamers a more distinctive way to personalize their gaming setup without compromising the compact versatility of the INVADER X MINI.

articles.title: Apple may be developing its own AI agent that runs your Mac | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple appears to be working on its own AI agent to conduct computer work on behalf of users — including using apps, accessing websites, and coding, among other things.
The news was originally reported by Bloomberg, which spotted a job listing the iPhone maker recently posted for a senior engineering manager to oversee the creation of an “AI agent that can use a computer.”
“Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does,” the posting says. “It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple.”
The posting additionally notes that the agents should be able to move “fluidly between tools” and “carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.”
TechCrunch reached out to Apple for more information but did not receive a response.
Agents capable of computer work have become one of the hottest commodities in the tech industry over the past year. Major labs like Anthropic and OpenAI have launched such services, while other major tech brands — like Meta, which recently launched its Muse agent line — have also moved into the space. It makes sense that Apple — which is trying to expand its AI offerings in the new John Ternus era — would want to follow suit.
Bloomberg additionally notes that, at the same time that Apple is working on its own digital assistant, the company is making it significantly harder for third-party agents to gain total control over its computers.
The outlet notes that the version of its upcoming macOS 27.3 will deploy warnings discouraging users from granting full access to third-party agents. In October, Apple issued a notification to developers stating that the company planned to “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”
Bloomberg writes that while the iPhone maker “has eyed introducing the service as soon as the end of next year,” progress on its in-house agent “remains in the early stages.”

articles.title: Gemini 4 Neon : Google continue de dégainer de nouveaux modèles d'IA, au risque de vous embrouiller
articles.text:
Fin septembre, on avait droit à Gemini 4 Argon. Moins d’un mois plus tard, c’était Gemini 4 Carbon qui arrivait et la semaine dernière, c’était au tour de Gemini 4 Hydrogen d’apparaître. Cette fois-ci, c’est Gemini 4 Neon qui est là, avec la promesse d’un modèle intermédiaire entre performances et coûts maîtrisés.
Gemini 4 Neon : un modèle entre deux extrêmes
Comme Google l’explique dans son billet de blog qui annonce ce modèle, Gemini 4 Neon est conçu pour les travaux qui demandent à la fois du raisonnement avancé et une exécution rapide. Programmation, analyse de données, recherche scientifique, synthèse de documents, automatisation de tâches… ce Neon sait a priori tout faire. Google le positionne entre Carbon, réservé aux gros projets, et Hydrogen, plus optimisé pour les usages quotidiens.
C’est pourquoi Gemini 4 Neon vise les tâches fréquentes, mais complexes. C’est parfait pour faire de l’analyse de tableurs, de PDF, de graphiques ou de fichiers audio/vidéo. Des tâches qui peuvent être régulières en entreprise et avec une IA qui veut s’intégrer dans la routine des travailleurs. Ce modèle possède une fenêtre de contexte d’un million de tokens. Pour le moment, Gemini 4 Neon est accessible aux utilisateurs abonnés à Google AI Pro ou AI Ultra dans l’application Gemini.
Pourquoi Google multiplie les modèles d’IA
Google ne sort pas Neon par simple effet d’annonce, à l’instar d’Argon, de Carbon ou d’Hydrogen. Ces différentes versions ne changent pas beaucoup entre elles, c’est toujours Gemini 4 derrière. Mais avec Neon, l’entreprise cherche à éviter le compromis habituel entre un modèle très puissant, mais lent et coûteux, et un modèle rapide, mais limité sur les tâches complexes.
Le géant de l’IA a donc enfin créé une famille de modèles : Hydrogen remplace les usages rapides, Carbon est destiné aux projets qui demandent de la précision et Argon est juste en dessous de Carbon en termes de performances. Neon vient donc se glisser entre Hydrogen et Argon/Carbon, avec un coût moins élevé : 3 dollars par million de tokens en entrée et de 15 dollars par million en sortie. À court terme, Neon est cependant plus cher au token que Carbon (2 et 10 dollars) ; c’est normal, puisque Carbon profite d’une réduction de 95% jusqu’au 30 novembre.
Google n’est d’ailleurs pas le seul à publier un modèle dit intermédiaire. OpenAI aussi s’y est penché récemment avec GPT-6.1 Terra sorti le mois dernier. Lui aussi est dans la même niche : un niveau intermédiaire, conçu pour des tâches professionnelles et complexes. Néanmoins, le prix n’est pas le même, puisque le modèle d’OpenAI est trois fois moins cher.

articles.title: Intel continues layoffs with cuts to its IT department, hundreds of employees reportedly affected — company’s workforce reduced by 27,800 under Lip-Bu Tan
articles.text:
Intel continues layoffs with cuts to its IT department, hundreds of employees reportedly affected — company’s workforce reduced by 27,800 under Lip-Bu Tan
Hundreds of people possibly affected.
Intel has reduced its workforce by approximately 27,800 employees under Lip-Bu Tan, based on the company's reported headcount figures, but this does not seem to be enough. The company has reportedly initiated another round of layoffs, this time across its global information technology (IT) organization, as its chief executive continues to reduce expenses and simplify the company's operations, reports Business Insider.
The latest cuts in Intel's IT organization reportedly began on November 16, although Intel has not disclosed how many employees will lose their jobs, notes TrendForce citing CTech. Some employees claim that the reductions could affect a double-digit percentage of the department's workforce of around 2,607 people at 55 sites in 53 countries, so we are talking about at least 260 people if we are talking about a 10% reduction, or as much as 520 if we are talking about a 20% reduction. One has to keep in mind that these estimates have not been independently verified. Intel has neither confirmed the number of affected employees nor identified the specific teams involved. Instead, the company reiterated to Business Insider that it regularly reviews its workforce to ensure that personnel and financial resources correspond to its strategic priorities.
The latest reductions follow several rounds of layoffs throughout 2026. In July, Intel eliminated positions in its Data Center and AI Group. Between July and October, the company submitted nine Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) notices in California, which covered 222 employees, according to Business Insider. The most recent notice, filed on October 22, concerned 67 permanent job cuts at Intel's Folsom campus (which mostly specializes in R&D, hardware validation, and software development), effective October 31. As of November 17, no additional WARN notices had been reported.
Intel employed 81,100 people as of September 27, 2026, including 76,500 employees at Intel itself and another 4,600 at Mobileye and other subsidiaries. This compares with 85,100 employees at the end of 2025 and 108,900 a year earlier, which means that the company's workforce declined by 4,000 since December, 2025, and 27,800 since December, 2024. respectively.
Intel's workforce reductions began well before Lip-Bu Tan became chief executive in 2025. In 2024, his predecessor Pat Gelsinger announced plans to eliminate more than 15,000 positions, or approximately 15% of the company’s workforce. Tan has continued to reduce expenses, eliminate management layers, and discontinue lower-priority projects as Intel attempts to cut costs and reduce losses/improve profitability.

articles.title: To Do: Microsoft vai encerrar aplicativo de organização • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
To Do: Microsoft vai encerrar aplicativo de organização
Contas corporativas serão direcionadas ao Planner, enquanto usuários pessoais terão de procurar outra ferramenta a partir de junho de 2027.
Quem usa o aplicativo de organização de tarefas Microsoft To Do tem até 30 de junho de 2027 para procurar uma nova solução. A data marcará o encerramento do suporte ao serviço da companhia no Windows, macOS, Android, iOS e na versão web.
Contas corporativas e educacionais serão direcionadas ao Planner, mas usuários pessoais não terão um substituto da própria Microsoft, inclusive assinantes do Microsoft 365 Personal ou Family. Também não haverá uma migração automática das informações armazenadas no To Do.
A Microsoft afirma que disponibilizará uma ferramenta para exportar listas e tarefas antes do encerramento, mais ainda não detalhou como ela funcionará. A companhia alerta que exportar os dados não significa que eles poderão ser importados depois pelo Planner ou por outro aplicativo.
Nas contas corporativas, tarefas antigas ainda poderão aparecer no Planner durante a transição, mas membros de listas compartilhadas e suas permissões de acesso não serão transferidos.
O fim dos aplicativo no ano que vem não marca o sumiço das informações armazenadas. Segundo a Microsoft, o serviço que funciona em segundo plano, suas APIs e o sistema de sincronização serão desligados posteriormente.
Deverá haver um período de transição para que o To Do seja completamente encerrado, incluindo os dados registrados nele. A empresa, porém, ainda não informou quanto tempo esse período vai durar.
O encerramento faz parte de uma reorganização maior dos apps de produtividade da Microsoft, que pretende reunir o To Do e os planos básico e premium do Planner em “planos unificados”, segundo o Windows Latest. O movimento também deve integrar o Copilot e o Cowork aos serviços.
Ashna Patel, integrante da equipe do Planner, afirmou que a Microsoft está levando o gerenciamento pessoal de tarefas para dentro dp Planner enquanto descontinua gradualmente o To Do. O programa, no entanto, não possui aplicativos nativos para Windows ou Mac, funcionando pela web ou dentro do Microsoft Teams. Não oferece, também, acesso offline.
O fim do To Do encerra também uma trajetória iniciada a partir de outro aplicativo de tarefas. Em 2015, a Microsoft comprou a 6Wunderkinder, startup de Berlim responsável pelo Wunderlist. O negócio foi estimado entre US$ 100 milhões e US$ 200 milhões.
A equipe do serviço passou então a trabalhar no desenvolvimento do Microsoft To Do, lançado como sucessor da plataforma, e encerraram o Wunderlist em 6 de maio de 2020. Naquela transição, porém, a Microsoft ofereceu uma ferramenta para importar diretamente as listas do Wunderlist para o To Do.

articles.title: Power-efficient inference chips let enterprises own AI hardware - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI inference servers shrink to fit the air-cooled racks enterprises already run
Power-efficient inference chips are becoming the entry price for enterprises that want to run AI on hardware they own.
As AI shifts from building models to running them every day, costly graphics processing unit racks and the liquid cooling they demand keep many companies renting compute instead. That gap is opening room for challengers to the incumbent chipmakers. Axelera AI B.V. built its business at the edge with low-power chips and edge AI development tools, and it is now taking that technology into data center infrastructure, according to Manuel Botija (pictured), vice president and head of product at Axelera.
“Enterprises cannot own their own infrastructure. They’re locked out because of the cost and the power,” Botija said. “We are enabling them now to own it. It’s not that we are helping the world save power or save money — which we are — but it’s that we are unlocking use cases that were simply not possible before.”
Botija spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how power-efficient inference chips are heading for the data center and how enterprises locked out by the cost and power of GPU racks can own their own AI infrastructure instead of renting compute. (* Disclosure below.)
Power-efficient inference chips head for the data center
Axelera’s Europa chip has been shipping since September. Ahead of SC26, the company unveiled Titania, a third-generation architecture that scales the design up to a 400-watt chip. The resulting six-kilowatt server is built to perform like leading data center GPUs while fitting into the existing 20- to 30-kilowatt air-cooled racks of an ordinary enterprise data center, Botija explained.
“Having a six-kilowatt server that can perform like a data centre GPU is a pretty big deal,” he said. “It basically means that they have some storage equipment, some networking equipment, some traditional CPU equipment, and next to all of that, they can also insert some AI inference hardware acceleration without needing to go and rebuild another server room or another data center.”
For enterprises that would rather own their AI hardware than pay a recurring cloud bill, the barriers have been steep. A GPU rack costs at least $1 million, often far more, and usually requires liquid cooling, Botija noted. Axelera’s answer rests on digital in-memory computing, a technique that grew out of its founders’ research and gives the company’s power-efficient inference chips a performance-per-watt advantage.
“Now you can own your own infrastructure,” Botija said. “You can amortize those investments and … reduce your opex, and therefore be more profitable as a company.”
