articles.title: Beware of GTA 6 scams — Security expert shares tips on how to stay safe as game launches worldwide
articles.text:
Beware of GTA 6 scams — Security expert shares tips on how to stay safe as game launches worldwide
Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out on consoles, and cybercriminals are counting on launch-day excitement to steal your logins and cash
- Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19 on consoles only
- Gaming phishing jumped 1,300% ahead of release
- ExpressVPN's Dr Pete Membrey shares six tips to avoid launch-week scams
Grand Theft Auto VI finally lands on consoles today, November 19, ending around a decade of waiting. Alongside genuine fans downloading the blockbuster, cybercriminals are using launch-week hype to steal passwords and payment details.
On November 16, the UK's Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) warned gamers to use unique passwords, enable two-step verification, and think twice before clicking links. Even the best VPN cannot stop you from typing your login into a convincing fake storefront, though quality tools can block known malicious domains.
Dr Pete Membrey, Chief Research Officer at ExpressVPN, backs the regulator's warning and says criminals are aiming far beyond your gaming library.
"A gaming account is rarely the real prize. Criminals want the email address and password behind it, because the same combination often opens banking, shopping, and social media accounts," he said.
ExpressVPN: Starting from $2.49 per month
ExpressVPN is the easiest VPN to use on our list, making it a great option for anyone slightly less tech-savvy. It’s also very fast thanks to the Lightway Turbo protocol and has great unblocking skills, making it an ideal streaming VPN. Subscriptions start at $2.49 per month on the two-year plan. As with most VPNs, there’s a 30-day money-back guarantee.
The GTA 6 scams already hitting players
This week's warnings follow a steep rise in GTA-themed fraud reported across the cybersecurity industry.
Research covered by TechRadar Pro shows gaming phishing emails surged 1,300% ahead of launch, with GTA impersonation attempts accounting for 42.4% of phishing emails analyzed by KnowBe4 during the weekend of October 31–November 1, 2026.
Scammers are also targeting frustrated PC players who face a longer wait. NordVPN researchers uncovered a $200 dark web scam kit that uses fake PC installers to spread a cookie stealer, a crypto wallet drainer, and hidden mining software.
Meanwhile, Surfshark identified 212 GTA-themed domains, with about one in four appearing designed to defraud players; it projected over 750 malicious or opportunistic domains would go live by launch day. Promises that a VPN will unlock the game early are false too, because console stores lock accounts to your original region.
Can a security app stop every GTA scam? Not if you willingly run an unverified download or scan a malicious code on your phone.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
How to stay safe on launch day
As Membrey warns, while you enjoy the game, you should keep in mind: "Launch week is when people are excited, distracted, and in a hurry, and scammers count on that."
Staying protected, however, comes down to slowing down before you click. Membrey advises buying and downloading strictly through the official PlayStation or Xbox store, rather than following links in emails or messages.
Treat free keys, giveaways, and early access offers as scams, especially when a time-limited deal asks for your login. Never sign in through a link you were sent; open the platform or publisher site yourself instead.
In an exclusive interview with TechRadar, Membrey said to watch out for QR codes in unexpected messages, too, which attackers frequently send on evenings and weekends when people check personal phones while relaxed. Criminals now build QR codes out of text characters specifically to slip past automated email filters, making personal devices an easy target.
"The risk goes up on a personal phone because it usually sits outside any work or home email security," Membrey told TechRadar.
Finally, use a different password for every account and track them with a password manager. Membrey says you should skip SMS codes wherever stronger options exist, prioritizing passkeys first and an authenticator app second.
Ultimately, Membrey says to be wary of messages that make you feel rushed, ask you to log in, pay, or scan something. When this happens, he recommends heading to the official store or publisher’s site. “A genuine offer will still be there a minute later. A scam usually won’t survive being checked."

articles.title: GTA V sur iPhone et Android : à l’heure de GTA 6, Take-Two fait supprimer plus de 600 projets sur GitHub !
articles.text:
La veille de la sortie de GTA 6, GitHub a publié quatre demandes de retrait visant des adaptations de GTA V pour iPhone, Mac, Android et Windows. Take-Two réclame aussi le blocage de centaines de copies de leurs dépôts.
Début octobre, GTA 5 tournait dans un onglet de navigateur. Six semaines plus tard, les adaptations issues de cette version se retrouvent dans le viseur de Take-Two, la maison mère de Rockstar. GitHub a publié les quatre notifications de l’éditeur le 18 novembre dont celle-ci, juste avant la sortie de GTA 6, plus de treize ans après son prédécesseur.
D’un onglet de navigateur aux applications mobiles
PlayGTA5.com n’a tenu que quelques heures. Le site permettait de lancer une version non officielle du jeu qui tournait directement sur la machine du joueur dans un simple navigateur, grâce à une compilation en WebAssembly, un format de code que les navigateurs savent exécuter. Rockstar et Take-Two n’ont pas commenté la disparition du site. Et l’hypothèse selon laquelle le portage aurait été réalisé à partir de code source ayant fuité n’a pas été confirmée.
La fermeture du site n’a pas arrêté la circulation de cette compilation. En quelques jours, des développeurs l’ont reprise pour faire tourner le jeu dans des applications pour iPhone, Mac et Android. C’est sur GitHub que ces projets et leurs variantes se sont multipliés.
Plus de 600 forks visés pour deux projets à eux seuls
Les demandes ciblent Muguet, destiné à iOS et macOS, glue5, qui couvre aussi Android et Windows, ainsi que gta5mobile-android et trois dépôts du développeur de PlayGTA5. Take-Two veut aussi désactiver leurs forks, des copies de dépôts que d’autres utilisateurs peuvent modifier séparément. L’éditeur en a recensé 263 pour Muguet et 349 pour glue5.
TorrentFreak a constaté que les dépôts de Muguet, glue5 et PlayGTA5, ainsi que les forks qu’il a consultés, affichaient un message de blocage au titre du DMCA, la loi américaine sur le droit d’auteur à l’ère numérique. GitHub n’a pas donné le nombre total de dépôts désactivés. Le premier dépôt cité dans la notice visant gta5mobile-android renvoyait une erreur 404, qui peut correspondre à un retrait ou à un passage en privé.
Pour Take-Two, l’outil compte autant que les fichiers du jeu
Une seule des quatre notifications affirme qu’un dépôt distribuait le jeu complet. Selon Take-Two, une version publiée le 9 octobre sur le dépôt PlayGTA5 proposait 21,2 Go de fichiers. Dans les autres cas, l’éditeur vise les outils qui permettent d’utiliser les données du portage web. Glue5 automatisait par exemple sur GitHub la création d’une application à partir de la compilation fournie par l’utilisateur avec une option pour charger à la demande quelque 20 Go de ressources.
« Parce que je tiens à ne pas être poursuivi, vous aurez besoin de votre propre copie », indiquait la documentation de Muguet, citée dans la notice. Il s’agissait des fichiers du portage Web qu’une installation officielle de GTA V ne fournissait pas. Take-Two estime que demander aux joueurs de se procurer eux-mêmes ces fichiers ne dégage pas les auteurs de leur responsabilité s’ils facilitent sciemment une reproduction non autorisée. C’est l’argument de l’éditeur dans sa demande de retrait, et aucun tribunal n’a pour l'instant tranché cette affaire.
Les auteurs peuvent contester le blocage par une contre-notification. Si celle-ci est recevable, GitHub rétablira l’accès au bout de 10 à 14 jours ouvrés, sauf si l’ayant droit engage une action en justice et en informe la plateforme. Le dépôt du mod Multi Theft Auto a ainsi été restauré sans procès. En 2021, le projet re3, qui réimplémentait le moteur d’anciens GTA, était lui aussi revenu en ligne avant que Take-Two ne poursuive ses auteurs.
Un portage reste accessible selon TorrentFreak. Revenu en ligne début novembre, le 5★ Port ne propose plus de compiler l’application via GitHub. Ses auteurs invitent désormais les ayants droit à les contacter et s’engagent à retirer le dépôt s’ils se manifestent. Le jeu du chat et de la souris n'est pas fini. Prochaine target, GTA 6 ?
- Outil disponible gratuitement.
- Création de dépôts illimitée.
- Collaboration simplifiée.
WebAssembly (Wasm) est un format binaire standardisé que les navigateurs peuvent exécuter à haute performance, en complément de JavaScript. Il permet de compiler du code C/C++ ou Rust vers un binaire portable, souvent plus proche des performances « natives » qu’un script classique. En pratique, un moteur ou une partie du jeu peut être porté pour s’exécuter dans l’onglet du navigateur, à condition de gérer l’affichage (WebGL/WebGPU), l’audio et les entrées. Le point bloquant reste généralement le volume de données (textures, sons) et leur chargement, car un jeu moderne représente des dizaines de gigaoctets à déplacer et à décompresser. Wasm ne “magique” pas les droits d’utilisation : il facilite l’exécution, pas la légitimité des assets ou du code portés.
Le DMCA (Digital Millennium Copyright Act) encadre aux États-Unis une procédure de “notice-and-takedown” : un ayant droit signale un contenu qu’il estime contrefaisant, et la plateforme peut le désactiver rapidement pour limiter sa responsabilité. GitHub publie souvent ces notifications de manière transparente (sauf exceptions) et bloque les dépôts concernés, ce qui peut se traduire par une page indiquant un retrait DMCA ou une inaccessibilité. L’auteur du dépôt peut répondre via une contre-notification s’il estime le retrait infondé, en donnant des éléments d’identification et une déclaration sous serment. Si la contre-notification est jugée recevable, GitHub peut restaurer le contenu après un délai (typiquement 10 à 14 jours ouvrés), sauf si l’ayant droit engage une action en justice pendant cet intervalle. Ce mécanisme ne tranche pas le fond du litige : il organise surtout une procédure rapide en attendant, éventuellement, un juge.
Un fork est une copie d’un dépôt GitHub, créée dans le compte d’un autre utilisateur pour modifier le code indépendamment ou proposer des contributions. Techniquement, le fork conserve l’historique Git et peut continuer à vivre même si le dépôt d’origine n’est plus maintenu, ce qui facilite la diffusion et la dérivation d’un projet. Quand un ayant droit demande aussi le blocage des forks, il ne vise plus seulement une source centrale, mais potentiellement des centaines de clones répliquant le même contenu (ou des variantes proches). Cela réduit la résilience du projet face aux retraits, car la suppression du dépôt principal ne suffit pas à stopper la circulation si les forks restent accessibles. À l’inverse, tous les forks ne sont pas forcément identiques : certains peuvent avoir retiré les fichiers litigieux, ce qui complique l’évaluation au cas par cas.

articles.title: Día del Hombre: 30 frases que no conviene enviarles por WhatsApp
articles.text:
El Día Internacional del Hombre se conmemora este 19 de noviembre y muchas personas recurren a WhatsApp para enviar saludos. Algunas frases, aunque se presenten como bromas, refuerzan estereotipos sobre la masculinidad, minimizan la salud mental o promueven relaciones desiguales.
La fecha busca poner el foco en asuntos como el bienestar físico y emocional de los hombres, los vínculos familiares, la paternidad y los modelos de conducta. Por eso, un mensaje puede reconocer la jornada sin condicionar el valor de una persona a su fuerza, sus ingresos o su capacidad de ocultar problemas.
Entre los mensajes que conviene evitar aparecen los que vinculan ser hombre con no pedir ayuda, controlar a la familia, soportar cualquier situación o cumplir un papel económico determinado. También pueden resultar ofensivos los saludos que cuestionan la existencia de la celebración.
Estas son 30 frases que no conviene enviar por WhatsApp en el Día del Hombre:
- “Feliz día a los hombres de verdad”.
- “Los hombres no lloran, se aguantan todo”.
- “Un hombre tiene que ser fuerte siempre”.
- “Feliz día a los que mantienen la casa”.
- “Un verdadero hombre protege a los suyos”.
- “Hoy también celebran el Día del Hombre, qué curioso”.
- “¿De verdad necesitan un día para ustedes?”.
- “Todos los días son el Día del Hombre”.
- “Feliz día a los que se lo merecen, porque no todos califican”.
- “Felicidades a los sufridos que tienen novia o esposa”.
- “Hoy puede descansar de aguantar a su mujer”.
- “Feliz día, aunque mañana vuelve a obedecer en casa”.
- “Hoy le damos permiso para opinar”.
- “Que tenga un buen día, macho alfa”.
- “Feliz día al jefe de la casa”.
- “Un hombre de verdad no pide ayuda”.
- “Los hombres resuelven, no se quejan”.
- “Feliz día a los que no tienen miedo”.
- “Los hombres deben saber defenderse siempre”.
- “Un hombre nunca muestra debilidad”.
- “Feliz día a quienes llevan los pantalones”.
- “Hoy celebremos a los proveedores del hogar”.
- “Ser hombre es cargar con todo sin hablar”.
- “Felicidades, aunque ustedes ya mandan todos los días”.
- “Un hombre debe trabajar duro y no reclamar”.
- “Feliz día a los que no dependen de nadie”.
- “Hoy se celebra a los hombres que saben controlar a su familia”.
- “Un hombre no necesita terapia, necesita carácter”.
- “Feliz día a los caballeros, no a cualquiera”.
- “Hoy es su día, pero no se acostumbre”.
Los mensajes pueden reforzar presiones sobre la masculinidad
Frases como “los hombres no lloran” o “un hombre no necesita terapia” presentan la vulnerabilidad como una falla. Ese tipo de expresiones puede desalentar la búsqueda de apoyo profesional o el diálogo con familiares y amigos ante problemas de salud mental.
También es preferible evitar mensajes que asocien la identidad masculina con la obligación de proveer dinero, proteger a otros o ejercer autoridad dentro del hogar. El Día del Hombre puede ser una oportunidad para reconocer afectos, acompañar procesos personales y valorar vínculos basados en el respeto.
Un saludo breve, directo y sin estereotipos puede ser suficiente: “Feliz Día Internacional del Hombre, espero que tengas un buen día” o “Feliz día, gracias por estar presente”. La intención adquiere mayor relevancia cuando evita burlas, exigencias o prejuicios.
El 19 de noviembre también promueve el cuidado de la salud
La celebración internacional se popularizó desde 1999 a partir de una iniciativa impulsada en Trinidad y Tobago por Jerome Teelucksingh, docente de la Universidad de las Indias Occidentales. La fecha se eligió el 19 de noviembre, día del cumpleaños de su padre.
Existen antecedentes de iniciativas previas para establecer una jornada dedicada a los hombres. Además, la tradición católica recuerda a San José de Nazaret cada 19 de marzo, una fecha vinculada con la figura paterna, la familia y la fe.
Elegir un saludo respetuoso también implica reconocer que la masculinidad no tiene un único modelo. El 19 de noviembre puede servir para valorar la presencia, el afecto, la responsabilidad compartida y la posibilidad de pedir ayuda. Un mensaje sin burlas ni exigencias evita reproducir presiones innecesarias y abre espacio para vínculos más equitativos, donde cada persona pueda expresar sus emociones y construir su identidad sin quedar atada a estereotipos.

articles.title: Proton Lumo AI
articles.text:
Lumo is a privacy-focused AI assistant designed to help users tackle everyday tasks, explore ideas, and boost productivity without compromising their personal information.
Unlike many mainstream AI chatbots, Lumo puts privacy at the forefront. Conversations are protected with zero-access encryption, meaning that even Proton cannot read them. The service is designed to keep user data private rather than using conversations for advertising or AI model training.
Developed by the team behind Proton Mail and Proton VPN, Lumo combines AI-powered assistance with Proton's established approach to privacy and security. The project is backed by the nonprofit Proton Foundation.
Features
Your chats are yours and yours alone
The questions you ask Lumo – about your work, your health, or your ideas – aren't accessible to us. So they can never be used to target ads, shape what you see online, or build a personal profile that third parties could exploit.
Safeguarded by advanced security
Your conversations are saved with zero-access encryption so that you're the only one who can read them. Proton can never see them, and neither can anyone else.
With transparent code you can trust
Unlike with other AI assistants, Lumo's code is fully open source, so anyone can verify that it's private and secure – and that we never use your data to train AI models.
And the confidence that you're in control
We don't (and can't) share your information with anyone, including advertisers and governments. And Lumo is a European service that complies with GDPR, so you can delete your account at any time.
What Lumo can help you do
Create images
Turn descriptions into images in seconds. Refine and iterate until every detail matches your vision. Your ideas will never be reused by Lumo's model to inspire someone else's design.
Dive deeper
Get clear, personalized answers to complex questions in seconds. Gain new insights, explore ideas, and get real-time information with built-in web search knowing your queries are never used for targeted ads.
Stay on schedule

articles.title: Patriot Launches AI Matrix SSD and DRAM Series Engineered for Local AI Workloads
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
Patriot Launches AI Matrix SSD and DRAM Series Engineered for Local AI Workloads
Patriot Memory today announced the Patriot AI Matrix series, a dedicated lineup of DDR5 memory modules and PCIe M.2 2280 NVMe SSDs engineered for local AI computing. Organized across PRO, Mid, and Entry tiers, the portfolio pairs screened memory ICs and high-endurance NAND flash with ongoing open-source LLM benchmark validation, enabling builders, creators, and SMBs to match hardware directly to on-device AI demands.
Running AI locally provides direct data privacy, offline reliability, and predictable hardware costs without recurring API token fees. However, scaling local LLMs exposes critical bottlenecks beyond GPU compute—namely memory-bound limits when holding multi-billion-parameter weights and runtime context, and storage-bound constraints when loading large checkpoints or querying local RAG datasets.Matched Configurations for Local AI Bottlenecks
Unlike conventional consumer components marketed with generic AI claims, Patriot structured the AI Matrix series around two core pillars:
Sustained Bandwidth & Endurance: Screened DRAM modules maintain multi-channel stability under continuous token generation and context processing, while high-endurance NAND flash supports heavy model loading and frequent dataset read/write cycles.
Parameter-Mapped Ratios: Each tier pairs specific DRAM capacities and speeds with matched PCIe Gen 5, Gen 4, or Gen 3 SSD throughput to align system budgets with target LLM parameter scales.
Tiered Lineup Matched to Real-World AI Workloads
- PRO Tier (34B-70B Models | Enterprise RAG, Multi-Step Tool Calling, Multilingual Workflows):
- AI Matrix MS560 SSD: PCIe Gen 5 x4 M.2 2280; 1 TB, 2 TB, and 4 TB; sequential read/write up to 14,000 / 11,000 MB/s (4 TB).
- AI Matrix MD57N DRAM: DDR5 up to 6000 MT/s (OC); available in a 64 GB (2x32GB) UDIMM kit.
- Mid Tier (14B-34B Models | Multimodal Understanding, Code Generation, Local Assistants):
- AI Matrix MS450 SSD: PCIe Gen 4 x4 M.2 2280; 1 TB, 2 TB, and 4 TB; sequential read/write up to 5,000 / 4,500 MB/s.
- AI Matrix MD55N DRAM: DDR5 up to 6000 MT/s (OC); available in a 32 GB (2x16GB) kit.
- Entry Tier (7B-14B Models | Coding Support, Translation, Copywriting):
- AI Matrix MS350 SSD: PCIe Gen 3 x4 M.2 2280; 512 GB, 1 TB, and 2 TB; sequential read/write up to 3,000 / 2,000 MB/s.
- AI Matrix MD35N / MD34N DRAM: DDR5 5600 MT/s; available in a 32 GB (2x16GB) kit.
Ongoing Empirical Validation
Every Patriot AI Matrix tier undergoes monthly benchmark testing across mainstream open-source LLMs—including Llama, Gemma, and CodeLlama—measuring prompt-processing (pp512) and token-generation (tg128) responsiveness alongside extended continuous local AI stress testing to verify sustained thermal and operational stability. By updating validation data monthly as models evolve, Patriot equips system integrators and builders with transparent, workload-verified guidance for local AI deployment.

articles.title: Anthropic's 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of them ponied up about 3.4 million shares apiece to sell in the IPO.
At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.
Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropy.
However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”
With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.
$104.8 billion. That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.
Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.
Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012, it raised $16 billion on IPO day.
28% stake to Amazon and Google combined. All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company. Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropic because when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup, it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.
The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.
More than $1 trillion. As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.
Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.
All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

articles.title: Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales — former Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen is married to outgoing Nvidia VP Jay Puri
articles.text:
Supermicro sued by shareholders over claims Nvidia executive’s wife knew about illicit China sales — former Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen is married to outgoing Nvidia VP Jay Puri
Shareholders are implying that she turned a blind eye to the alleged smuggling of Nvidia chips.
More information about the alleged knowledge of chip diversion by a Supermicro executive is being revealed as shareholders’ civil lawsuit against the company progresses. According to The Telegraph, the investors alleged that there was “no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company’s illicit sales.” Chen, the former Chief Growth Officer at Supermicro and described by a colleague as the company’s sales leader, resigned from her position in April of this year — about a month after the three Supermicro employees, including its co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, were arrested for a $2.5-billion AI GPU smuggling scheme.
Cenly Chen is married to former Nvidia Executive Vice President of Worldwide Field Operations Jay Puri, who is also described as the company’s sales chief. The Information also called him Jensen Huang’s right-hand man and said he was the person that Nvidia’s customers turned to if they wanted to buy chips or had other pressing concerns. The shareholders’ accusations and her relationship with Puri have put the former Supermicro executive in the spotlight, especially after Huang’s sudden departure from the AI chipmaker amid a flurry of affairs and smuggling accusations.
Sources say that Puri controlled the AI chip allocations to server manufacturers, including Supermicro, while the lawsuit claims that Chen decided how many Nvidia racks each Supermicro customer could get. A former Supermicro employee was also quoted in the complaint saying that it was “widely known within the Company that Chen had to leave because she had sent emails requesting that Nvidia release chips with serial numbers associated with the GPUs illegally diverted to customers in China.” This apparently refers to the serial numbers that were moved from real to dummy servers using a hairdryer.
Supermicro has said multiple times that it has cooperated with the U.S. government regarding the smuggling investigation and that it has not been included in the lawsuit against the three defendants. Furthermore, the company has denied her involvement regarding Nvidia GPU allocations. “Chen did not manage Supermicro’s relationship with Nvidia and did not decide how Nvidia GPUs were distributed to customers,” a Supermicro spokesperson told The Information. They also said that she left voluntarily and that her LinkedIn profile now reads her current position as CEO of ChronoScale, an Nvidia cloud partner based in Silicon Valley. As for Puri, he stepped away from his position at Nvidia in late August, about two months before the Jensen Huang scandal blew up, although he remains as an advisor to the AI chipmaker.

articles.title: Egypt's Connect Money raises $3.5 million pre-Series A
articles.text:
Egypt's Connect Money raises $3.5 million pre-Series A
- Egypt-based fintech Connect Money has raised $3.5 million in a pre-Series A round led by existing investors Mohamed Farouk, Algebra Ventures and DisrupTech Ventures. The transaction combines new capital with secondary share sales, allowing several early investors to make partial exits.
- Founded in 2024 by Ayman Essawy, Marwan Kenawy and Momtaz Moussa, Connect Money provides embedded finance infrastructure that enables businesses to issue branded prepaid cards and integrate financial services without building their own banking systems.
- Operating under a licence from the Central Bank of Egypt, the company manages card issuance, regulatory compliance, programme management and daily operations through partnerships with banks, payment processors and card networks. It has issued more than 300,000 cards across six sectors.
- The funding brings Connect Money's reported cumulative financing to $11.5 million and will support expansion into Saudi Arabia and Morocco, including regulatory licensing and local technology infrastructure. The company is pursuing a Saudi Central Bank licence and targeting a Moroccan launch in the first half of 2027.
Press release:
Egyptian fintech startup Connect Money has raised $3.5 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by existing investors Mohamed Farouk, Algebra Ventures and DisrupTech Ventures, as it prepares to expand its embedded finance services into Saudi Arabia and Morocco.
The transaction combines fresh investment with secondary share sales, providing partial exits for several early investors. The company did not disclose how much of the $3.5 million represents new capital.
The round brings Connect Money's reported cumulative funding to $11.5 million, following an $8 million seed round in June 2024.
Founded in Egypt in 2024 by Ayman Essawy, Marwan Kenawy and Momtaz Moussa, Connect Money provides embedded finance infrastructure that allows businesses to offer branded prepaid cards and integrate financial services into their existing products.
Operating under a licence from the Central Bank of Egypt, the company works with banks, payment processors and card networks to manage card issuance, regulatory compliance, programme management and daily operations.
Connect Money said it has issued more than 300,000 cards across six sectors, including retail, fintech, agritech, education, oil and gas, and platforms serving small and medium-sized enterprises.
The new investment will support the company's planned entry into Saudi Arabia and Morocco, with a focus on securing regulatory approvals and establishing the infrastructure required to operate in both markets.
In Saudi Arabia, Connect Money is seeking a licence from the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA). In Morocco, it is building its local operational and technology infrastructure ahead of a planned commercial launch in the first half of 2027.
The expansion will extend Connect Money's embedded finance services beyond Egypt, as it targets businesses seeking to offer payment products without developing their own banking infrastructure.

articles.title: Guerre contre l’IPTV : l’un des plus gros sites pirates de Turquie ferme ses portes
articles.text:
Un nouveau géant du piratage vient de tomber. L’Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE) a annoncé la fermeture définitive de Dizigom, l’un des plus importants sites de streaming illégal de Turquie. La plateforme, qui comptait environ 21 millions de visites par mois, permettait de regarder gratuitement des films et des séries. Pour rappel, l’ACE est une coalition internationale qui réunit plus de 50 grands groupes de l’industrie du divertissement, dont Amazon, Apple TV, Netflix, Paramount, Sony Pictures, Universal, Disney et Warner Bros. Discovery.
À lire aussi : Un géant de l’IPTV pirate indien cesse ses activités
Trois ans d’enquête pour faire tomber Dizigom
La coalition a ouvert une enquête sur Dizigom dès 2023. Avec l’aide de la police et la justice de la Turquie, elle a cherché à identifier tous les responsables du site, à débusquer leurs biens et à cartographier l’infrastructure technique du service. Les investigations ont fini par porter leurs fruits.
Face aux poursuites pénales brandies par l’ACE, les pirates à l’origine de Dizigom ont fini par accepter un accord à l’amiable. Ils se sont engagés à fermer définitivement le service et à céder 16 noms de domaine à l’ACE. Désormais, toutes les adresses du site renvoient vers une page qui présente les dangers du piratage et fait la liste des offres de streaming légales.
« La fermeture de Dizigom est une nouvelle étape importante pour perturber les activités illégales qui profitent de contenus créatifs volés », se félicite Larissa Knapp, vice-présidente exécutive de la Motion Picture Association, chargée de la protection des contenus, ajoutant que « ces opérations ne s’arrêtent pas à un seul site web ».
À lire aussi : Ils revendaient des boîtiers IPTV en France – la justice les condamne à une lourde sanction
Une première en Turquie
Dizigom est la première affaire pénale lancée par l’ACE en Turquie. Elle a ouvert la voie à plus de dix autres enquêtes analogues à l’encontre de géants du streaming illégal. La chute de Dizigom s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une vaste offensive contre l’IPTV pirate. Ces derniers mois, l’ACE a fait tomber AnimePlay, une plateforme d’anime aux plus de 5 millions d’utilisateurs, puis le réseau de streaming sportif PirloTV et ses 44 noms de domaine.
Ces fermetures ne suffisent pas toujours à mettre un terme aux activités des pirates. Cet été, HBO a fait tomber le géant du streaming illégal Streamzy.to, mais le site pirate est revenu presque aussitôt sur Internet. C’est précisément pourquoi l’ACE s’attaque de plus en plus aux personnes derrière les sites pirates, et pas seulement aux adresses. Cette approche permet une perturbation plus durable des géants du streaming illégal.

articles.title: China's first fully AI-generated movie flops at the box office
articles.text:
No AI in Cinemas: China's first fully AI-generated film has flopped at the box office. The country is at the forefront of AI adoption across both businesses and society, but consumers are apparently unwilling to pay for what many might consider genAI "slop."
Sanxingdui: Future Past, a 100-minute sci-fi movie about a future AI apocalypse, failed to earn enough at the box office to cover the AI token costs required to generate the entire film. China's first fully AI-generated feature film has turned into a massive flop, despite locals already spending countless hours watching AI-generated clips on their smartphones.
According to box office figures tracked by Beacon Pro, Sanxingdui "generated" just around 1.8 million yuan ($270,000) after spending three weeks in Chinese cinemas. Meanwhile, the team behind the film reportedly had tens of millions of yuan in production costs to recoup before turning a profit.
Bona Film Group, the company behind the movie, adopted an entirely AI-based workflow, without actors, performers, or other cinema professionals. Yue Ming, the director and writer behind Sanxingdui's convoluted plot, worked with Shengshu Technology and its Vidu AI platform to complete the project. The team first generated a large number of clips before assembling the final "movie" by stitching the individual visuals together.
Unsurprisingly, the resulting genAI patchwork made for a disjointed story that very few moviegoers bothered to watch in theaters. According to University of California professor Michael Berry, Sanxingdui's failure can be attributed, at least in part, to the way Chinese users currently "enjoy" AI-generated content on their mobile devices
Chinese platforms are full of genAI "microdramas," with hundreds of thousands of AI-generated clips reportedly released in the first eight months of 2026 alone. And it's not just Chinese viewers: although he cannot understand a single word of Mandarin, my elderly father spends hours upon hours every day watching these AI-generated clips, which are full of over-the-top Asian characters.
Berry suggests that Chinese audiences may regard genAI content as a form of cheap entertainment: something they can casually watch on their phones but aren't willing to spend money on when looking for a proper movie theater experience.
Furthermore, Sanxingdui arrived in cinemas at a time when China's domestic movie industry was already experiencing a significant downturn. Beacon Pro data shows that box office revenue this year is down 30% compared with 2025, reaching "only" 31.6 billion yuan over the first 10 months.
Even People's Daily, the official newspaper of the Chinese Communist Party, described Sanxingdui's poor performance as a sign of the challenges AI-based "creative work" is likely to face in the foreseeable future. According to Berry, audiences around the world may eventually begin rejecting AI-generated content in favor of something a little more human, or at least something featuring a coherent storyline.

articles.title: Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up
articles.text:
In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a New York City bill.
When I log into Amazon today, I’m met with a vertical banner that reads: “ATTENTION NYC Council could add up to $5 per order” with a button that says “Act now.”
I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website. The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged into Amazon.
Amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses.
Clicking on “Act now” on Amazon’s homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states:
Right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.
It’s not unusual for Amazon to take a stance on political matters, and it has publicly opposed the Delivery Protection Act since April. What is new is Amazon using its online marketplace to push a political view. It’s uncommon to see a pop-up about legislation when visiting a shopping website.

articles.title: Is AI becoming feral?
articles.text:
Is AI becoming feral?
Oxford experts make the case for thinking of AI as ‘feral’
“A horde of AI agents conspired against their creators,” cried a recent headline of an article published in The Economist.
“‘We’re plausibly close to crossing the line’: are warnings of uncontrollable AI coming true?” the Guardian asked just a few days later.
These are just some of the many alarming front-page news stories which have emerged after an autonomous AI agent in Open AI’s training recently breached Hugging Face, an American company based in New York City that develops computation tools for building applications using machine learning.
However, despite what these headlines suggest, the future is not necessarily doomed. As our Oxford colleague Ciaran Martin recently wrote in the Economist, “fears of AI-induced cyber-Armageddon are overdone”.
Jerome Ravetz, Affiliate of the Institute for Science, Innovation and Society (InSIS), University of Oxford; Lukas Zumbrunn, Oxford-Hyundai Motor Group Foresight Centre, Saïd Business School, University of Oxford; Rafael Ramirez, Oxford-Hyundai Motor Group Foresight Centre, Saïd Business School, University of Oxford
Still, it’s true that the unprecedented way in which AI agents have coordinated and communicated raises novel, radical uncertainties. How concerned should we be? It’s a difficult topic to debate, as the facts are often contested, the implications unimaginably vast, and values are in dispute (c.f. a wave of anti-data center social movements).
As AI grows and evolves at bewildering speeds, we argue for a richer yet flexible vocabulary to better comprehend this transformation. Research has shown that helpful insights can often be best expressed with the help of metaphors.
Here we offer 'feral', or something that was originally tame, but which then slipped out of control and became worse than wild. The ‘feral’ idea has been familiar since Classical times, with the experience of imported goats going feral and destroying the vegetation of their islands.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The prospect of a ‘feral’ technology system is concerning because attempts to control a system that has become deeply uncertain, or feral, can actually intensify its dangers. Feral does not mean that catastrophe or permanent disorder is inevitable: early recognition may allow the trajectory to be arrested, mitigated or transformed, but stabilization is contingent rather than automatic.
Feral technology throughout history
A good example of how an information system can become feral is the familiar story of printing and the Reformation. It started with Johannes Gutenberg's vision of replacing handwritten books; he is best remembered for producing a Latin Bible with movable type. It took a few decades for his highly sophisticated cast-type printing press technology to meld with an existing popular stream of block printing. Eventually the printers could produce cheap broadsheets and pamphlets, which Martin Luther used to great effect to distribute his Ninety-Five Theses and other writings: a brilliant PR move that changed the world. Luther and other Protestant reformers like William Tyndale translated the Bible into common languages like Saxon German and Early Modern English and used the printing press to distribute these translations. As Tyndale boasted, “ere many years I will cause a boy that driveth the plough shall know more of the Scripture than thou dost.”
Ecclesiastical reform fed political agitation and revolt. For a while, it seemed as if the invention had gone feral: printing had escaped the purposes of its early users and generated consequences that they could neither predict nor contain. But as the 'magisterial reformation' stabilized, the vernacular Bible was tamed and recruited to the purposes of the State; thus the 'King James' Bible was commissioned by King James I to bring its production under royal and ecclesiastical oversight and establish a common English text for use across the Church of England.
We can see this dialectic of upheaval and (temporary) stabilization also at work in other subsequent developments in information technology. In the 1840's, the telegraph came in association with the railways; indeed, the rights-of-way by the tracks were an ideal channel for the new cables. Within 20 years, telegraph wires spanned the Atlantic Ocean. This strongly supported international capitalist enterprise and the rapid development of international finance — and with it the repeating and intensifying cycle of global speculation and collapse. This example shows how a technology can destabilize the system in which it is embedded, rendering it feral.
Is AI feral?
Today, AI has put us in the midst of another information technology boom, with over a dozen companies valued at more than a trillion dollars involved in the venture. Can all these developments be kept tame by existing regulatory systems, or will feral tendencies emerge again?
Unfortunately, there are several factors that are working against implementing sensible regulatory systems. For example, while there are political calls to pause the development of enhanced capabilities AI models, they are frequently met with rhetoric that resembles the Cold-War-era: ‘If we slow down, we’ll lose out to the Chinese competition – and potentially be threatened by their greater AI capabilities’. Presumably a similar ‘arms race’ argument plays out among Chinese AI developers and their own regulatory authorities.
Meanwhile, AI companies have repeatedly said their products could lead to terrifying futures – including the idea that AI ‘could kill all humans’. Sceptics note that this type of rhetoric could serve to highlight the power of AI and lead to higher public offerings. In a New York Times guest essay, Georgetown University Professor of Computer Science Cal Newport called this monetization of public concerns by AI companies “doom trolling”. By continuously sounding the alarm about doomsday scenarios of AI, they are stating that AI is already feral.
The boy who cried wolf did not make the wolf any less real. Doomsday statements merely make it harder to recognize when a wolf – that is, a feral future – has really arrived. A challenge, now, is neither to dismiss AI warnings as hype nor to surrender to apocalyptic rhetoric, but to cultivate institutions capable of distinguishing profitable panic from genuine feral danger.
Both apocalyptic rhetoric and total disregard for AI’s dangers are overly simplistic views that assume that AI will progress linearly. But there are many complex paths the future of AI technology could take.
For example, the ‘frontier’ models may fail commercially, leading to a financial crisis in that end of the AI industry. This, combined with popular resistance to data centers, may produce a cancellation of data center projects.
At the same time, resistance to continued scraping may threaten the quality assurance of the LLMs. AI in China may evolve on a different path from the West; what we see as job-destruction may solve China’s demographic problem of an ageing labor force.
Standard risk analysis can’t prepare us for these possibilities. Instead, our scenarios approach provides the conceptual tools for managing such feral futures.
Managing feral futures
In two of the authors’ earlier scenarios work, we developed methods for dealing with the complexity and deep uncertainty that characterize feral futures. These include: treat weak signals as possible evidence, include critics in an extended peer community, rehearse scenarios outside established risk models, and make interventions monitored and reversible. The lesson is not that standard risk analysis is useless, but that it can become counterproductive when a system has moved outside the class of events on which the analysis was built.
In AI, standard risk analysis would call for treating every anomalous behavior as a familiar model-safety problem and responding only by expanding existing tests, benchmarks or controls. Those measures may create confidence while missing interactions among autonomous agents, markets, infrastructures and institutions; a hurried patch might also displace behavior into less visible settings. The first task in our approach is therefore to recognize when a supposedly tame risk has become a deep uncertainty, then use responses that can be monitored, challenged and reversed.
This is where ‘Zen’ and ‘aesthetics’ become practical disciplines to plan for feral futures. ‘Zen’ asks decision-makers to loosen their attachment to the labels, models and professional identities that made the system appear manageable. ‘Aesthetic’ attention means noticing unexpected patterns and uncomfortable signals before they can be expressed as reliable metrics. Used in scenario practice, the two heuristics help institutions rehearse unacceptable or politically difficult futures, invite dissenting observers and test small, reversible interventions. They complement formal risk analysis by helping people recognize when their existing tools no longer fit the situation.
Beyond simple scenarios
The rapidly increasing powers of AI present an unprecedented challenge to our civilization. Simple dichotomies of the future do not help our understanding or our abilities to influence its evolution. The scenarios methodology, with its heuristics of ‘Zen’ and ‘aesthetics’, allow us to reach enriched understandings of futures, both simple and feral. We offer it as our current understanding of how to respond to that challenge.

articles.title: Raptor chip stacks 3D DRAM to tackle inference memory limits - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
D-Matrix bets stacked DRAM can solve inference’s memory bandwidth problem
As artificial intelligence workloads shift to inference, memory bandwidth decides whether hardware generates tokens quickly or sits idle. D-Matrix Corp. is answering with Raptor, a second-generation chip stacking 3D DRAM beneath its compute logic.
AI infrastructure has become a systems game, and winners combine memory, interconnect and software into cohesive designs, according to Satyam Srivastava (pictured), fellow at d-Matrix.
“It’s no longer a chip problem. Chip plays a part of it. Memory bandwidth is a fundamental advantage that has to be solved,” Srivastava said. “The next is energy efficiency. The next is interconnect efficiency. The next is software cohesiveness.”
Srivastava spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed d-Matrix’s Raptor chip and its stacked 3D DRAM, inference memory bandwidth and the shift toward heterogeneous computing. (* Disclosure below.)
Raptor brings a stacked-memory tier to inference
D-Matrix proves each risky technology on a test chip first. Jayhawk proved die-to-die connectivity, and Jayhawk II validated digital in-memory computing. The Corsair accelerator combined both and entered full production earlier this year, Srivastava explained.
“Fast forward, we have the Pavehawk chip, test chip, which is proving out 3D DRAM stacked underneath the logic die, which serves as the core technology for Raptor, which is our second-generation chip coming out next year,” Srivastava said.
Stacking keeps the distributed memory architecture intact but moves memory cells onto a separate layer rather than consuming logic die area. Data travels a short distance and never crosses an interposer. That puts 3D DRAM in a new tier between SRAM and high-bandwidth memory, Srivastava said.
“So you’re getting 10 times higher energy efficiency compared to HBM, 10 times higher bandwidth compared to HBM, where it sits in between SRAM and HBM in terms of capacity,” Srivastava said.
Pairing a Corsair-based server with an existing Hopper GPU fleet can raise utilization from about 20% to as much as 80%, meaning more tokens per dollar, Srivastava noted. D-Matrix has also adopted NVLink Fusion rackscale infrastructure from Nvidia Corp. to connect its accelerators to Nvidia’s AI factories.
“For us, it unlocks the opportunity to participate in a very established ecosystem, the world’s most popular AI factory. We get access to a very hardened design of an MGX rack,” Srivastava said.
The partnership points toward heterogeneous computing, where software orchestrates GPUs, CPUs and accelerators such as Raptor as one system, with the cluster as the unit of computing, Srivastava explained.
“So think of a chip, but that chip is an entire cluster and it has many different hardware units,” Srivastava said. “Some are GPUs, some are CPUs, some are ASIC accelerators, and you can use whichever one you like to serve the needs of the workload the best.”

articles.title: NVIDIA : des résultats étincelants... et pourtant une action qui recule
articles.text:
Les résultats du troisième trimestre de l'exercice actuelle de NVIDIA ont été exceptionnels. Et pourtant, le marché a encore sanctionné l'ex-firme de Jensen Huang !
Les temps sont difficiles du côté de NVIDIA. Et ce, évidemment, du fait de la très grave polémique qui a entraîné finalement la démission de Jensen Huang. Et depuis, même si l'activité est toujours brillante au sein de l'entreprise, elle crée un vrai mouvement de défiance au sein des marchés. Ce qui se confirme encore cette semaine, avec une situation franchement paradoxale.
Des résultats brillants, au-dessus même des attentes des analystes
NVIDIA a encore présenté des résultats étincelants cette semaine pour le troisième trimestre de son exercice. Son chiffre d'affaires a ainsi crû, durant le troisième trimestre de l'exercice actuel, de +103%, à 115,8 milliards de dollars.
Une croissance tout simplement folle, et qui a même dépassé les attentes des analystes, qui voyaient plutôt NVIDIA annoncer un chiffre d'affaires trimestriel de 108,85 milliards de dollars. Et pourtant, le marché n'a pas connu d'embellie derrière.
Un cours à la Bourse qui réagit négativement
En effet, ces résultats présentés mardi soir, après la clôture de la Bourse, n'ont pas eu l'effet que l'on aurait attendu. Ils ont d'abord fait bondir le cours de 2% à l'ouverture mercredi, à 159,19 dollars, pour dégringoler dans la journée, et clôturer à environ 150 dollars.
« Nous pensons que les résultats d'hier ont stabilisé le sentiment des investisseurs et mis un frein à la récente vague de ventes massives dans le secteur de l'IA, mais ils ont davantage reporté que résolu définitivement les inquiétudes des investisseurs » a résumé le vice-président de la recherche chez Counterpoint, Neil Shah.
Il faut dire que NVIDIA doit faire à la fois face aux doutes grandissant quant aux niveaux de rentabilité actuels de la technologie de l'IA, et à la crise à la direction de l'entreprise, qui n'a pas encore de nouveau PDG permanent.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Nvidia se enfrenta a una nueva amenaza tras la destitución de Jensen Huang: la pérdida de sus mejores ingenieros
articles.text:
Por primera vez desde que Jensen Huang dejó de ser su CEO, Nvidia reunió a sus empleados en Santa Clara para darles un mensaje: nadie debe preocuparse por su sueldo. Aunque el hombre que hizo millonarios a muchos de esos empleados ya no esté al frente de la compañía no hay motivos para marcharse.
Al parecer, la salida de Huang no solo ha traído a una nueva CEO interina, sino que también se ha convertido en un incremento salarial para evitar que los mejores ingenieros de la empresa sigan a su cofundador en su próxima aventura laboral.
Dinero antes de lo previsto. Colette Kress, CEO interina designada por el consejo de administración de Nvidia para cubrir la dimisión de Jensen Huang tras sus 'affaires' extramatrimoniales y las sospechas de espionaje de una de sus amantes, prometió subidas de sueldo y más acciones para sus empleados.
El anuncio se hizo durante la presentación de resultados de la compañía para el tercer trimestre fiscal, y llegarán mucho antes del ciclo habitual. Nvidia presentó unos ingresos de 115.800 millones de dólares en el tercer trimestre, un 103% más que hace un año. Un analista de Bank of America preguntó a Kress por la retención de talento, a lo que la directiva respondió que estabilizar la plantilla era "probablemente lo más importante" y que lo mejor que pueden hacer es "cuidar de cada uno de los empleados".
La acción de Nvidia subió cerca de un 5% al día siguiente.
Los ingenieros que no pueden irse. 33 años de liderazgo de Huang han servido para que su cofundador se granjeara una lealtad férrea de muchos de sus ahora exempleados. Antes de la rendición de cuentas de Nvidia, Ben Reitzes, de Melius Research, preguntó sobre "el plan para retener a todos los ingenieros". Nvidia ha perdido unos 550.000 millones de dólares de valor en bolsa desde que su consejo apartó a Huang. La hoja de ruta para recuperar ese capital a base de fabricar chips depende de quien los diseñe.
El riesgo de fuga de talento entre sus ingenieros es relativamente pequeño en número, pero muy serio por el impacto que puede provocar. Brad Gastwirth, de Circular Technology, aseguraba a Business Insider que perder entre cinco y diez líderes técnicos tendría un efecto desproporcionado. El experto considera probable que empresas rivales como AMD, Broadcom u otras grandes tecnológicas aprovechen la situación de incertidumbre en el liderazgo de Nvidia para captar a su mejor talento a golpe de talonario.
Los millonarios de Huang. Huang no solo pagaba bien a sus empleados: repartía riqueza. Los veteranos acumulan acciones del plan de compra para empleados. Este plan permite destinar parte del sueldo a comprar títulos de la empresa. Desde 2019 el valor del papel ha subido un 3.776%, según Fortune, y por eso muchos son millonarios.
Esa gratitud se deja notar ahora, cuando Huang necesita hacer presión frente a la junta directiva. Hay una petición con unas 180.000 firmas para que vuelva. Por ese motivo, la subida de sueldos puede leerse como un gesto para calmar a los más fieles a su antiguo jefe con la promesa de mayores recompensas si permanecen en el su puesto.
Cuánto cobra un ingeniero de Nvidia. Según la plataforma laboral Levels.fyi, la compensación mediana en Nvidia es de unos 233.675 euros al año. El puesto mejor pagado que recoge esta plataforma supera el millón de dólares anual. Por otro lado, uno de los calendarios de acciones que muestra la web reparte los títulos en bloques de cuatro años: 40%, 30%, 20% y 10%.
Si los nuevos paquetes siguen un esquema similar, los empleados estarán atados a su empleado durante varios años hasta que se consoliden esas acciones. Aun así, un rival potente puede seguir la táctica de Meta con su superlaboratorio de IA e igualar las recompensas prometidas con las acciones.
En Xataka | Nvidia es el Super Glue de la industria de la IA. Sin Huang al frente, temen que sea pegamento de barra
