articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX has a plan to eliminate cell phone dead zones | TechCrunch
articles.text:
CEO Elon Musk said SpaceX has completed the design of a miniature rooftop cell tower that could provide better coverage to mobile phones and eliminate dead zones inside buildings where signals from its Starlink satellites have trouble reaching.
These mini cell towers are expected to go into production in 2027, Musk said, during an interview at the DealBook Summit this week.
“We’ve got a plan that enables ubiquitous access on Earth, including via cell phone,” Musk said, noting the company is launching its Direct-to-Cell V2 satellite constellation next year, which will increase bandwidth 40-fold. “But there is a missing piece of the puzzle here which is that if you’re indoors, especially if you have a metal roof, that blocks the signal from space. So we need something that’s terrestrial that addresses situations where people are, you know, in a building with a thick roof essentially.”
The company’s efforts initially focused on buying wireless spectrum after receiving the Federal Communications Commission’s approval in 2024 to move forward with plans to offer a direct-to-phone version of its Starlink satellite internet service, in partnership with T-Mobile. SpaceX struck a $17 billion deal with EchoStar in 2025 and agreed this year to acquire a portfolio of low-band spectrum valued at $8 billion.
Combining that wireless spectrum with mini cell towers should boost signals and end the dead zone problem, he said. According to Musk, the company has completed the design of what he described as “a micro cell tower thing that you just put on your roof, like a Starlink dish.”
Musk, who has a history of missing his own production deadlines, demurred, saying the devices were “going into production, I think, next year.”
The idea isn’t new, but it wasn’t clear until this week how much progress SpaceX had made toward developing the hardware.
SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said during the company’s August earnings call that it wouldn’t use big cell towers and would instead deploy small, low-power cellular base stations.
Even with this latest progress report, SpaceX appears to be still working out the details. Musk said one approach would be to bundle the small cellular base stations together with Starlink terminals.
SpaceX’s plan to build a hybrid cellular-satellite network has fueled speculation, and even predictions, that legacy telecom companies could be in danger. But Musk doesn’t think so, because he expects an entirely new class of customers to drive demand for wireless bandwidth: AI.
“I don’t think this means, like you know, AT&T, Verizon, or others go out of business or anything,” he said, adding that maybe they’ll lose some revenue. “But I actually think that the demand for bandwidth will be tremendous in the future, and a lot, and that bandwidth will be driven primarily by superintelligence and robots, and they’re going to need a lot more bandwidth than humans.”

articles.title: Does your AI agent need an LLM to decide what to do next?
articles.text:
Does your AI agent need an LLM to decide what to do next?
Say “good morning” to an AI agent, and it might search its long-term memory before saying hello back. Somewhere in that system, a service performs a semantic lookup to determine whether your greeting requires understanding your beverage preferences. Even if you take your coffee very seriously, this seems like a lot of infrastructure for two words.
Does this request need a more capable model than conventional options? Is this retrieved memory relevant? Should the workflow pause for a human?
This inefficiency and indecision is where Mike Chambers, a senior AI DevEx engineer at AWS, sees an opportunity. In a conversation last month at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2026 in San Jose, California, Chambers explained to The New Stack Editor-in-Chief Nick Lucchesi how developers can use decider models to handle the small judgments that add up inside an agent.
Decider models (also called decision models or System One models) are specialized AI models that choose from a fixed set of options or rate inputs on a scale — returning calibrated probabilities without generating free-form text. Popularized by TypeSafe AI’s Jev, they give software and agentic workflows fast, low-latency judgments with explicit confidence scores. (AWS’s Strands Labs released its own open-source decision model, the 2-billion-parameter Strands Decider 2B, on October 1.)
An if statement with a feel for language
Chambers describes the approach as “a little bit like having an agentic-powered ‘if’ statement inside of your code.”
Developers have used classifiers for years. What makes this generation of decider models interesting, Chambers told The New Stack, is that general-purpose pretraining lets you try one on a new classification task without first training a model of your own. You supply context in natural language, ask a question about it, and get a numeric score your application can use to choose a branch.
In the models Chambers describes, that score comes back in a single forward pass. There’s no token sequence to generate. That can make a decider attractive for a choice that sits on the critical path of every request. A model router, for example, can use a score to send routine prompts to a smaller model and reserve a more capable one for harder jobs. The potential savings come from both the routing decision itself and the downstream work it saves.
When an agent can skip the memory search
Chambers tried the idea with the open-source Strands framework and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory. He put Strands Decider in front of the memory lookup to judge whether an incoming message called for fetching anything from past conversations. A greeting could go straight through. A request that depends on something the user said earlier could still trigger a search.
He also tried using a decider after retrieval. A memory service can return the top matches to a query, but some may have little bearing on the task at hand. A decider can score each result for relevance before the agent includes it in the context it sends to the model. One decision can save a service call. The other can give the model less extraneous material to sort through.
A predictable output still needs testing
A number in a predictable JSON field makes a decider easy to wire into an application. Whether that number is reliable enough to act on takes testing. “Will the number be correct? That’s for your testing to be able to go and figure out whether that’s the case or not,” Chambers said.
Chambers calls his memory experiment experimental. The interview also gets into what happens when the stakes rise. A missed preference might mean a mediocre coffee recommendation. An agent about to spend money is a different matter, and Chambers argues for checks outside the agent’s loop and human approval for decisions that are hard to reverse.
Watch the full interview on The New Stack’s YouTube channel for Chambers’ walkthrough of the memory experiment and a look at where developers are taking open-source deciders next, from documents to robotics.

articles.title: Hack2Skill, Yourstory launches voice AI hackathon with Rs 8 lakh prize pool in collaboration with Google Cloud India
articles.text:
YourStory launches voice AI hackathon with Rs 8 lakh prize pool in collaboration with Google Cloud India
Virtual hackathon invites working professionals to build voice AI prototypes using Gemini Enterprise and the Google Cloud AI stack - powered by Hack2Skill.
The evolution of Voice AI - from conversational tools to intelligent, action-oriented interfaces - has opened the gates for businesses to rethink customer engagement, streamline operations and unlock new opportunities for growth. From helping field teams access enterprise information hands-free to enabling transactions through spoken instructions, Voice AI helps businesses operate, interact with customers and deliver outcomes.
To encourage the development of practical solutions that leverage Voice AI, technology partner Google Cloud, YourStory, and Hack2skill have launched Build with Gemini – Shape What's Next, a fully virtual hackathon aimed at driving hands-on adoption of the Gemini stack among working professionals across India.
The hackathon invites developers, AI/ML engineers, data scientists, and technical founders to identify business challenges and develop functional voice AI prototypes using Gemini.
Participants can register individually or in teams of up to four members. Students and non-professionals are not eligible for this edition.
Registrations and idea submissions are open till December 3, 2026. Participants must submit an idea addressing one of four problem statements. Shortlisted teams will receive $100 in Google Cloud credits to develop their prototypes and submit a one-to-two-minute demo video.
Four problem statements
The hackathon focuses on building Voice AI solutions that go beyond answering questions to retrieving information, completing tasks, and taking action through connected systems.
Participants can choose from four problem statements.
1. Voice-powered enterprise knowledge and decision agent
Participants must build a real-time voice agent that helps employees retrieve information from multiple enterprise sources, including documents, support tickets, project wikis, and chats.
The agent should support regional languages and code-switched speech, retrieve information across languages and provide answers grounded in enterprise data. It should also carry out actions through connected systems, such as raising tickets, checking inventory, or updating records.
2. Voice-driven agentic workflow automation
This challenge focuses on using spoken instructions to complete business tasks without requiring users to navigate forms or websites.
Participants must build voice-first agentic workflows that convert multilingual spoken instructions into actions across APIs, ledgers, databases, or inventory systems.
The solution should coordinate multiple steps, handle exceptions, and involve a human when approval or judgment is required. Potential applications include logging field visits, recording deliveries, booking services, and filing claims.
3. Customer & frontline voice agents
Participants must develop a real-time voice agent that interacts directly with customers or assists frontline employees during live conversations.
The agent should understand intent, context, and sentiment; retrieve relevant information and complete tasks such as booking a slot, checking orders or raising support tickets.
It should work across languages and include a human hand-off mechanism for situations requiring judgment.
4. Open innovation: Real-world voice AI with Gemini
This category allows participants to identify an organizational challenge or opportunity in any industry and develop a voice AI solution.
The agent must use Gemini to understand and reason over spoken input, including Indic languages and code-switched speech, and connect that input to actions through APIs, ledgers, databases or inventory systems.
Across all four categories, participants are expected to demonstrate natural, low-latency voice interactions; regional-language capabilities; the ability to handle interruptions and background noise; and the execution of backend actions.
Prototypes should also demonstrate measurable value through factors such as time saved, tasks completed, improved accuracy, language reach or cost per interaction.
From idea submission to prototype
The hackathon follows a seven-step process, beginning with free registration and idea submission.
Shortlisted teams will receive Google Cloud credits and move into the development phase, where they will build prototypes using Gemini and submit a demo video.
Participants will have access to industry mentorship, office hours and guided sessions led by practitioners from Google Cloud and Hack2skill.
Submissions will be evaluated in two stages. The process includes AI-assisted and manual screening of ideas, technical pre-screening, rubric-based scoring and a final jury round involving Google Cloud subject matter experts.
The evaluation criteria include the use case and its business impact, effective use of Gemini Enterprise capabilities, product quality and execution, innovation, presentation and user-generated content.
Rs 8 lakh prize pool
The hackathon offers a total prize pool of Rs 8 lakh, with eight winning teams selected from a single national pool.
- Winner: Rs 3 lakh
- First runner-up: Rs 2 lakh
- Second runner-up: Rs 1.25 lakh
- Five consolation awards: Rs 35,000 each
All shortlisted teams will receive $100 in Google Cloud credits to support prototype development.
Every team that submits a valid prototype will receive an e-certificate. Selected participants may also have their work featured across YourStory, and Hack2skill channels.
Working professionals interested in building Voice AI solutions can register and submit their ideas until December 3, 2026.

articles.title: Une cyberattaque IA vient de frapper la Commission européenne : 10 jours de systèmes paralysés et des données volées
articles.text:
La Commission européenne a été victime d’une cyberattaque de grande ampleur. Le porte-parole Thomas Regnier indique que « des systèmes individuels ont été ciblés ». Conformément à ses habitudes, « la Commission européenne a pris les mesures nécessaires en réponse à une cyberattaque détectée ».
La cyberattaque a été détectée dès le 22 octobre. Pour endiguer l’attaque, la Commission a désactivé plusieurs applications internes, dont Sysper, la plateforme de ressources humaines. Celle-ci permet aux fonctionnaires de consulter leurs fiches de paie, de poser leurs congés et de déclarer leurs heures de travail. À la suite de l’offensive, la plateforme s’est retrouvée hors ligne pendant une dizaine de jours. Au moment de la rédaction de cet article, le système de remboursement des frais médicaux était encore et toujours hors ligne. L’attaque a donc considérablement affecté le fonctionnement de la Commission.
A lire aussi : « CRITIQUE » – après le chaos PHP2Shell, PHP alerte sur de nouvelles failles de sécurité
ARTEX, l’outil de piratage à l’origine de la cyberattaque
Selon le porte-parole, la cyberattaque s’est appuyée sur ARTEX, un outil d’IA accessible à tous les internautes sur Internet. Développé par un certain Autumn-27, l’outil est capable de mener des intrusions en toute autonomie, en fonctionnant en synergie avec des modèles d’IA. Ce dispositif, initialement conçu comme un outil dédié à la traque de failles, a suscité les inquiétudes des autorités cette semaine. Le CERT-EU, le service chargé de la cybersécurité des institutions européennes, a tiré la sonnette d’alarme il y a quelques semaines, soulignant qu’Artex est massivement utilisé par des hackers.
Dans le sillage du CERT-EU, le FBI a publié une alerte analogue. La police fédérale américaine explique qu’Artex a été « détourné par des acteurs malveillants pour automatiser plusieurs phases des cyberintrusions à la vitesse de la machine ». Il permet aussi à des pirates « ayant une expertise technique minimale » de mener des opérations complexes contre plusieurs cibles simultanément.
Des données personnelles compromises ?
Pour le moment, on ignore si des données personnelles ont été compromises durant l’attaque. Thomas Regnier précise que « l’enquête est toujours en cours », mais que la Commission n’a pas « détecté d’élément indiquant une violation de données touchant l’ensemble du personnel ». L’institution n’a reçu aucune demande de rançon et n’attribue pas l’attaque pour le moment. Les plateformes qui ont été piratées contiennent pourtant des informations sensibles sur les fonctionnaires, à savoir leurs noms, leurs grades, leurs adresses personnelles et leurs coordonnées complètes.
Ce n’est pas la première fois que la Commission se retrouve dans le viseur des cybercriminels. En mars dernier, la Commission a repéré une intrusion dans l’infrastructure cloud qui héberge Europa.eu, son portail web officiel. Plus de 90 Go de données ont été dérobées. Un mois plus tôt, une attaque a frappé l’infrastructure de gestion des smartphones et appareils mobiles, exposant des noms et des numéros de téléphone de membres du personnel. L’affaire s’inscrit surtout dans le cadre d’une explosion des cyberattaques menées grâce à l’IA. Ces dernières semaines, Google a d’ailleurs repéré des agents IA pirates lancés à l’assaut de plusieurs sites français.

articles.title: Mis 12 primeras horas jugando a 'GTA VI': Rockstar ha creado al fin el juego que llevaba años soñando
articles.text:
Acabo de terminar de jugar a 'GTA VI'. Mi pareja estaba al lado y le he preguntado.
- ¿Qué te parece?
- Está muy chulo.
La clave de esto es que a mi pareja no le gusta 'GTA'. No le gusta nada. Sin embargo, le flipó 'Red Dead Redemption 2'. Considero que esa es la idea más importante de estas primeras impresiones de 'GTA VI'.
He jugado unas siete horas y, realmente, no he hecho nada. Llevo esperando un nuevo juego de la saga desde que me terminé el anterior allá por octubre de 2013 y el Alex de hace 13 años se habría pasado ya la mitad de la historia y habría desbloqueado varios distritos.
El Alex de 2026 ha jugado el prólogo, ha hecho un par de misiones y se ha dedicado a dos cosas: dar vueltas por la primera zona y, sobre todo, pasar el tiempo en casa.
Pilla un café y acompáñame a lo largo de las siguientes líneas porque es verdad que no he avanzado mucho, pero sí hay mucho que contar.
El 'GTA' menos 'GTA'
Mi pareja no estaba prestando atención todo el rato a mi partida, pero entre los varios comentarios que ha soltado, creo que hay tres que resumen perfectamente cómo es este 'GTA VI'.
- "Es como el 'Red Dead', pero con coches".
Esa es la fácil, la más obvia, pero también la más entendible. A medida que se acercaba el lanzamiento, estaba entre los jugadores la duda de si sería más parecido a un 'GTA V' o al 'Red Dead Redemption 2'. Pensaba que sería lo primero porque 'GTA' es una saga superventas muy lejos del western de Rockstar y no pensaba que el estudio fuera a cambiar la fórmula.
Lo han hecho.
Todos los 'GTA' los empezamos a un ritmo frenético. Nada más empezar pillamos un coche, una bici o una moto. En el V empezamos en mitad de un atraco, pero no tardamos ni cinco segundos en liarnos a tiros y en coger un coche para huir de la pasma.
'GTA VI' empieza con una cinemática en la que muestran cómo se conocen Jason y Lucía, los dos protagonistas a los que vamos a controlar. Tras un picadito de imágenes de su relación y del mundo de Leonida (el estado ficticio que emula Florida), Rockstar nos pone al control de Lucía... en la cárcel.
No tardamos en saber cómo acabó ahí y, en estos primeros minutos, vemos otro cambio respecto a los 'GTA' anteriores. Los anteriores protagonistas eran pandilleros, ladrones profesionales, criminales del montón, un exsoldado en busca de venganza y un tremendo desquiciado. Jason y Lucía son dos pringaos.
La primera acaba presa y el segundo haciendo chanchullos mientras vive en una cabaña menos estable que mi salud mental. Está a medio hacer y, en cuanto me dieron el control libre para ir a misiones por el mapa, decidí hacer lo que hago cada finde: apañar la casa.
Nadie me lo ha dicho, no sé cuánto tiempo estaré en ese lugar o si la inversión de tiempo será en vano, pero me apetecía arreglar el techo, terminar una pared, pintarla, cambiar la escalera o rematar una barandilla.
A lo tonto, echas ahí unos minutos porque las acciones son lentas, como en 'Red Dead Redemption 2', y después me puse a hacer unas pesas con unas mecánicas perfectas, me hice un café, alimenté a Dolores, la serpiente, y me pegué una ducha.
Hecho todo esto, y transcurrido medio día, me fui a dar una vuelta con el coche. Tu coche es tu coche, y el juego te lo hace saber. Va un paso más allá del coche que tenías en el garaje en los anteriores: ahora es el caballo del 'RDR 2'. En él guardas armas y ropa, pero también puedes personalizar todos los aspectos del mismo y, en parado, activar las luces, poner las de emergencia, jugar con la música y las radios, aparcar y parar el motor manualmente para ver qué pasa.
O también puedes dar una vuelta y, en el caso de PS5, los gatillos adaptativos del DualSense te ayudan a, por fin, conducir a la velocidad permitida. Pulsando hasta la mitad tienes la velocidad de la vía para ir tranquilamente, pero si pulsas hasta el fondo, metes zapatilla.
Cada coche responde en función de su tracción (delantera, 4x4 o trasera) de una forma muy realista. En el caso del coche de Jason, tenía el depósito de gasolina casi lleno (sí, hay que repostar) y me fui a dar vueltas.
Conducir es un placer y es más fácil que nunca respetar tanto el tráfico como las señales. Las dimensiones del mundo son extremadamente realistas, o al menos así lo parece, por lo que es muy fácil jugar el rol de un buen ciudadano. Cuando me cansé, fui a una misión y la cosa no se descontroló demasiado, así que volví a casa, me eché y volví a salir a dar vueltas.
Hay mucho tráfico y bastante gente por las calles. Si te quedas parado, ves que la cosa se descontrola. Un atropello tontorrón por ahí, un par de tiros por allá... no tiene que ver conmigo, así que me acerco a la gente y hablo con ellos. Si les apuntas con el gatillo puedes ir de buenas o de malas. De nuevo: como en 'Red Dead Redemption 2'. Pensé que era lo menos 'GTA' del mundo y me estaba gustando pese a que esperaba algo más... 'GTA'.
Pero entonces, ocurrió.
Fui a hablar con un turista (literalmente) que estaba en un cruce cerca de mi casa... y la cosa se descontroló.
El 'GTA' más 'GTA' de todos
Me insultó y no me gustó. Y, como soy una persona que sabe que es un videojuego, pues saqué la pistola. No tenía intención de nada, sólo amedrentar un poquito porque soy un poco parguela y no saco la pipa para usarla, pero el fulano se me encaró y le pegué un tiro en la rodilla.
La retícula del arma se pintó de amarillo, lo que significa que no he disparado a un sitio letal, y ahí vi al turista arrastrándose mientras su pareja se iba corriendo, pillaba un coche, salía a toda prisa y atropellaba a otra persona que empezó a correr al escuchar el disparo.
Cartel de "un testigo ha reportado el delito", dos estrellas y tres iconos: un coche, indumentaria y un punto del mapa. Ahí está el 'GTA' que conocía y buscaba, pero mejorado. Conocía el nuevo sistema de búsqueda con estrellas de colores en función de si la poli está en busca activa o no, también el nuevo sistema de reconocimiento, pero no me acordaba y me fui a casa a ver si pasaba el temporal.
Error. Aviso de que no puedo entrar en mi piso franco (tiene sentido, para que la poli no sepa dónde vivo) y que tenía que buscarme la vida, en definitiva. Así que, entré en el menú de personaje, me quité la gorra y me puse unas gafas. Bien, icono de indumentaria borrado. También había cambiado de coche, así que la poli tampoco sabe qué vehículo llevo. Sólo quedaba salir del radio de búsqueda hasta que se calmara la cosa.
Cuando pasó, volví a mi casa, cogí el coche y me dirigí al mismo cruce con la intención de seguir mi camino, pero el coche de una señora se averió en ese mismo lugar y bajé a ayudar. No necesitaba mi ayuda, así que cogí mi coche, aceleré y pegué un frenazo porque me llevaba puesta una moto. Pero claro, el motorista me insultó y tuve que bajar del coche a ponerlo en su sitio.
Le pegué un par de puñetazos y seguía vivo, pero no podía permitir que quedara así la cosa y, para incorporarme a la autopista, digamos que... pasé con mi coche por encima de su pierna. Sin querer queriendo, ya sabes, y como nadie me vio, ni policía ni historias: me fui a dar una vuelta a la manzana.
- "Alex, me preocupas".
Yo me lo estaba pasando pipa porque eso es 'GTA'.
El tema es que la narrativa emergente es bestial y, al dar la vuelta, resulta que una patrulla de policía había parado a ver qué pasaba. Resulta que no debí aplastarle la pierna, sino el pecho, por lo que el motorista había fallecido y, a su alrededor, había un montón de gente mirando.
Es brutal cómo este juego hace que pienses que estás en un universo vivo. Y me encanta esa locura de la nada porque han mezclado a la perfección lo mejor de 'Red Dead Redemption 2', como es esa profundidad de los sistemas, con el caos de un 'GTA'.
Tenía mis dudas porque, encantándome el western de Rockstar, para 'GTA VI' quería algo con la misma profundidad en sus personajes, pero con un control algo más ágil para poder ponerme creativo en los tiroteos. No es igual de dinámico un juego que otro y está bien, pero la intro de este juego y el primer tiroteo que jugué me hicieron pensar que la cosa iría por otros derroteros y que ese desfase, quizá, no estaría.
Parece que me equivoqué y, aunque el control es lento, no me parece tosco. También hay mil acciones contextuales para un mismo botón y volverá a pasar que, como me tire una semana sin jugar, olvide lo que hacía cada uno. Pero, al final, tiene tanto de 'RDR 2' como de 'GTA', y viceversa. Y me encanta.
Y eso que, como decía, he jugado una ínfima parte y me queda mucho, muchísimo por descubrir. En los análisis se habla de sistemas casi de RPG y veo el porqué. Tengo muchas ganas de descubrir eso, pero también de ver si me acostumbro a sus gráficos.
El elefante en la habitación
- "Parece que vas por una carretera de verdad. La escala y el detalle es brutal".
Porque 'GTA VI' se ve bien, demasiado bien. Es algo que no voy a descubrir a estas alturas, pero sí tengo que decir que se ve tan, pero tan bien que, a veces, juega en su contra.
En el vídeo que puse al principio lo muestro. Quise ir a sigilo y me bajé a un enemigo con R2. No tenía un arma empuñada, así que R2 es el botón para noquear por la espalda. Cogí su fusil y fui agazapado a por otro protagonista de 'Cazadores del pantano' del Discovery Channel. Pulsé R2 intentando noquearlo, pero como tenía un arma empuñada, ahora el botón correcto era el cuadrado.
Total, que le pegué un tiro y empezaron a salir enemigos como si fueran los hijos del Cletus de 'Los Simpson'. Y... sufrí. No es que sea difícil, pero es que no conseguía ver a los enemigos.
En un videojuego, los enemigos tienen un contraste que hace que los diferencies claramente del entorno. No deja de ser un videojuego y hasta los más fotorrealistas hasta la fecha seguían esas reglas. Pero 'GTA VI' lleva ese realismo al absurdo y, de verdad, en ese escenario me resultaba complicado ver a los enemigos, que se mimetizaban a la perfección.
Y no es algo exclusivo del pantano. En una misión de las primeras, tenía que infiltrarme en un depósito de coches de la poli y había uno entre sol y sombra al que también me costó un montón distinguir. Y mi pareja me lo dijo, así que no es cosa mía ni me estoy quedando ciego.
Quiero acostumbrarme, ya te contaré en el análisis si lo consigo, pero tengo que decirte una cosa: si te resulta incómodo, puedes personalizar MUCHO la interfaz y añadir ese contraste a los enemigos.
En las opciones de accesibilidad e interfaz hay un montón de opciones para personalizar la pantalla y hay algo que me encanta: por primera vez, Rockstar nos permite usar subtítulos de diferente tamaño. Era una queja recurrente en juegos de una compañía en la que los personajes te dan la chapa cuando vas a caballo o en coche.
Los subtítulos de Rockstar eran siempre tan pequeños que parecían hechos a mala baba, pero ahora tenemos varios tamaños para escoger, amén de esas comentadas ayudas de visibilidad que se agradecen muchísimo.
Por lo demás, las imágenes hablan por sí solas y el juego es un absoluto prodigio. Ya entraré en profundidad en esto en otro texto porque hay muchísimo que contar, pero no me extraña que Digital Foundry haya comentado que son los gráficos más apabullantes que han visto nunca en tiempo real.
Mi queja es que, en una PS5 base, la tasa de frames rasca en ocasiones. Es el único juego que ha hecho que me arrepienta de no haber comprado la PS5 Pro o haber escogido una versión de Xbox Series X que parece algo más estable. Pero bueno, espero que algún día usen QSSR o lancen un parche para dejarlo como debe estar.
Y... hasta aquí estas primeras impresiones. Tengo muchas, muchísimas ganas de perderme en este universo y de seguir haciendo el payaso por Vice City y sus alrededores, pero estas primeras horas hacen que me explique dónde han invertido los 1.000 - 1.500 millones de dólares que, supuestamente, habría costado el juego.
No creo que sea el mejor juego de la historia y, ni mucho menos, el más influyente, pero sí considero que es el más monumental que se ha hecho en este joven medio. Ya veremos si, cuando lo termine, sigo opinando lo mismo.
Me piro a jugar. A ver si no se me atraganta el cruce que tengo junto a la casa. Otra vez, quiero decir.

articles.title: Black Friday : ENFIN une promo chez RED by SFR, le forfait 250 Go passe à 12,99€/mois

Alors que les prix des forfaits mobiles ne cessent de grimper depuis quelques mois, RED by SFR va à contre-courant pour le Black Friday. Son forfait 250 Go 5G Voyage, sans engagement, passe à 12,99 € par mois jusqu’au 30 novembre, contre 15,99 € dans notre guide des forfaits RED, mais il est réservé aux nouveaux clients.

articles.title: NAND flash prices fell 20% in the last two weeks, and are predicted to fall further in 2027
articles.text:
Forward-looking: NAND flash spot prices fell by around 20% over the past two weeks and could decline by a further 5% by Q2 2027 amid "a reversal in supply-demand dynamics." Contract prices were previously expected to decline in Q3 2027, but TrendForce, a market intelligence and research firm, now believes the decline could begin as early as Q2 2027. The revised outlook is driven by slowing enterprise demand in China and weakness in the global consumer electronics market.
While NAND flash prices have risen rapidly over the past year, 2027 could finally bring some relief to customers. According to TrendForce, the anticipated price correction could be attributed to two main factors: a large-scale reduction in enterprise SSD orders from Chinese cloud service providers and a marked downturn in the consumer electronics market.
The report notes that demand for enterprise SSDs from AI data centers and cloud service providers in North America will remain robust through 2027, despite the changing political landscape in the US. However, steady demand in North America will be offset by a pullback among Chinese technology companies due to GPU shortages, elevated inventories, and slower-than-expected AI monetization.
Adding to the slowdown in China, NAND flash manufacturers are also grappling with sluggish consumer demand worldwide, as steep prices have prompted many retail buyers to postpone their upgrade plans. Negative consumer sentiment and softening enterprise demand have created challenging market conditions for hardware manufacturers, resulting in oversupply and a likely price correction.
Curiously, most suppliers appear to be continuing their investments in new process nodes and increasing their use of QLC technology despite the gloomy market outlook. One of the few major exceptions is Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC), the world's third-largest NAND flash supplier by bit shipments, which has "slightly trimmed" its expansion plans in response to changing market conditions.
The predicted price correction also appears to have already begun, with NAND spot prices reportedly declining by an average of 20% in just two weeks amid weak consumer demand. According to a Bank of America study cited by Seoul Economic Daily, prices for 512Gb wafers fell by as much as 32% quarter over quarter (QoQ) to $14.30, while 1Tb products declined by 19% to $24.90.
TrendForce states that the extent and pace of the correction in NAND flash contract prices will depend on how quickly Chinese cloud service providers can reduce their inventories and how long OEMs continue producing laptops, smartphones, and other consumer electronics with downgraded hardware specifications.
The report also notes that the speed of approvals for new data centers in the US will influence the NAND flash market outlook. However, with bipartisan opposition to data center development growing across the country, it remains unclear whether all proposed projects will receive approval from local, state, and federal authorities.

articles.title: Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Use Kimi Code CLI with models on Amazon Bedrock
Kimi Code CLI is an open source coding agent from Moonshot AI, the creator of the Kimi series of open-weight foundation models. Previously, using Kimi Code with models on Amazon Bedrock meant configuring a generic connection “provider” with an Amazon Bedrock API key. For many AWS customers, this meant introducing an extra credential to obtain and protect.
With v2.7.0, Moonshot AI adds a native bedrock provider to the CLI. You can now configure the agent to use your standard AWS credential chain, including named profiles and single sign-on (SSO), instead of creating and managing a separate API key.
In this post, we show you how to connect Kimi Code CLI to models on Amazon Bedrock using your existing AWS credentials. We use Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed as an example, which supports streaming, configurable reasoning, image input, and client-side tool calling.
What’s new
Amazon Bedrock provides pay-per-token inference for a range of open and proprietary models from leading providers, available through standard APIs. Processing stays within the AWS data boundary, as detailed in the Data protection section of the User Guide. The model cards detail which APIs and features are supported for each model.
In older versions of the Kimi Code CLI, you could connect to Amazon Bedrock through a provider with type = "openai" or type = "openai_responses". These use the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions or Responses APIs, respectively. This approach required you to set the regional base_url and provide an Amazon Bedrock API key. The key could be short-term or long-term, but it was a separate credential for you to obtain and manage.
The native provider changes that setup:
- Use your existing AWS authentication workflow. The bedrock provider can resolve temporary credentials through the standard AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) credential chain. You can use the default chain or select a named profile, including a profile backed by SSO.
- Override the protocol for each model, if needed. The provider infers an API format and regional endpoint from the model ID, but you can change them as detailed in the “Override endpoint URL and protocol” section of this post.
AWS recommends short-term credentials over long-term credentials. This new path reduces reliance on manually managed API keys, but it doesn’t change your responsibility to protect AWS credentials and scope permissions appropriately.
How it works
The native provider handles authentication and request routing in four steps:
- Resolve AWS credentials. Unless you configure an Amazon Bedrock API key, the bedrock provider uses the standard AWS credential chain in your environment. You can set AWS_PROFILE to select a specific named profile.
- Generate a short-lived bearer token. The provider uses @aws/bedrock-token-generator to create a short-term Amazon Bedrock API key, and renews it when necessary. You don’t need to place any AWS access key or manually generated Amazon Bedrock key in the Kimi Code config.toml. However, an explicit key given through api_key or api_key_env takes precedence if you provide it.
- Build the regional endpoint. The provider resolves AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and constructs the appropriate bedrock-runtime endpoint for the model’s inferred API. For Kimi models, this resolves to the recommended OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions path.
- Call the selected inference profile. The model alias maps to an Amazon Bedrock model or inference profile ID. This example uses the global inference profile global.moonshotai.kimi-k3.1. The global. prefix selects the profile, while AWS_REGION determines the regional endpoint that receives your request.
The CLI then streams the model response and can use the model’s client-side tool-calling support during coding tasks. Authentication, authorization, model access, and network connectivity must all succeed for a request to complete. The ephemeral API keys generated by the provider are valid for up to 12 hours or your AWS session length, whichever is shorter.
Prerequisites
For this walkthrough, we use Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed as an example model, accessed through global cross-Region inference for broadest availability and lowest cost. Review the Amazon Bedrock pricing to understand expected costs before using the model.
To follow along, you need:
- An AWS account with access to the target model and inference profile in a supported source AWS Region. Check the Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed model card for current Region and inference-profile support.
- Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 or later. Follow the Kimi Code CLI installation guide and run kimi --version to check your installation.
- The AWS CLI, to follow the profile and identity-check commands in this post. The optional aws login workflow requires AWS CLI v2.32.0 or later.
- An AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) identity (user or assumed role) with permissions to invoke the target model and inference profile in your chosen AWS Region.
The following example IAM policy grants the permissions used by this walkthrough, for the Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed model and global inference profile only. Replace ${AWS_REGION} with your source Region (for example, us-west-2 for US West Oregon) and ${AWS_ACCOUNT_ID} with your 12-digit AWS account ID:
The foundation-model ARN without a Region or account ID is intentional and required for global cross-Region routing. The BedrockInvokeKimiK31DefaultProject statement is only required if using the openai_responses protocol, not with the default openai (Chat Completions).
Security of your AWS environment is a shared responsibility. Review and grant IAM permissions according to the principle of least privilege, particularly for production environments. Consider using a dedicated IAM role for Kimi Code CLI, separate from your regular AWS activities.
Get started with the bedrock provider
After your prerequisites are ready, follow these steps to configure AWS authentication, add the provider and model, and send a test request.
Step 1: Configure AWS credentials
There are different ways to authenticate with the AWS CLI, depending on your organization’s setup. With Named profiles, you can configure multiple AWS contexts and switch between them.
For example:
- If you use SSO through AWS IAM Identity Center, run aws configure sso --profile YOUR_PROFILE_NAME to set up a profile, then run aws sso login --profile YOUR_PROFILE_NAME to authenticate.
- To use AWS Management Console credentials with AWS CLI v2.32.0 or later, run aws login --profile YOUR_PROFILE_NAME. The console-credential login guide also describes a credential_process configuration for tools that don’t support the cached login session directly.
- Omit the --profile arguments to use your default AWS profile instead of a named one.
Whichever approach you choose, your session resolves to an IAM identity (user or role) that needs the Amazon Bedrock permissions from the prerequisites. A Region configured in an AWS CLI profile applies to AWS CLI commands, but you must still set the Region explicitly for Kimi Code in Step 2.
Verify that the AWS CLI resolves your intended identity. Omit --profile YOUR_PROFILE_NAME if you use the default profile:
Step 2: Add the provider and model
- Open or create ~/.kimi-code/config.toml in a text editor. If you set KIMI_CODE_HOME, use $KIMI_CODE_HOME/config.toml instead. If you have an existing file, back it up and merge these entries with your current settings rather than overwriting unrelated providers or models.
- Replace YOUR_SOURCE_REGION with your supported source Region (for example, us-west-2). To use a named profile, replace YOUR_PROFILE_NAME and uncomment the AWS_PROFILE line: The model alias bedrock-kimi-k3-1 is a local name used by Kimi Code CLI. The model value is the Amazon Bedrock global inference-profile ID. The example declares a 1-million-token context window and explicit reasoning, image-input, and tool-use capabilities. It omits api_key, api_key_env, and AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, so the provider uses ambient AWS credentials. A configured Amazon Bedrock key would take precedence.
- Save the file. The [providers.bedrock.env] table supplies configuration to the provider. It doesn’t export variables into your shell.
Step 3: Send a request and start a coding session
- Run a small non-interactive coding request:
- Confirm that the CLI streams a response without an authentication, authorization, Region, model-access, or network error. This request provides a more meaningful connectivity check than a provider status indicator.
- Start an interactive session in a project directory: 
         
         Because you set default_model, the session selects bedrock-kimi-k3-1 automatically. Ask the agent to explain the repository or propose a small change. Review its proposed file modifications and shell commands before approving them.
Configuration best practices
At the time of writing, the native bedrock provider has several configuration considerations. These practices help you avoid ambiguous status information and mismatched settings.
Use the configuration file to set up the provider
At the time of writing, Kimi Code’s desktop and web provider-creation interfaces don’t expose all the provider environment fields used by this credential-chain setup. Edit config.toml directly to set up the Amazon Bedrock provider. For further details, refer to Model providers in the Kimi Code documentation.
Declare model capabilities explicitly
Kimi Code doesn’t auto-detect the capabilities of most models on Amazon Bedrock, including Kimi models. Check the Amazon Bedrock model card for each target model and explicitly declare its capabilities to let Kimi Code make use of them.
For example, Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed supports always_thinking, thinking, image_in, and tool_use, but not audio_in or video_in, as reflected in the config.toml example shown earlier.
These declarations describe client behavior. You should only include capabilities that are supported for each target model and Amazon Bedrock API endpoint. Validate tool and image workflows for your application rather than relying on the capability labels alone.
Keep Region settings consistent and prefer cross-Region inference where possible
The bedrock provider requires an explicit AWS_REGION or AWS_DEFAULT_REGION in Kimi Code’s config.toml or the shell environment. It can’t infer a Region configured only in ~/.aws/config or through aws configure.
When you use cross-Region inference profiles (with prefixes such as global., us., or in.), the configured Kimi Code Region controls the source Region that receives your requests. For more information, refer to cross-Region inference in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
For workloads without data-residency requirements, start with the global inference profile. This model, like many others, is priced 10% lower for global inference than through geographic profiles. Review Amazon Bedrock pricing for current rates and geographic alternatives.
Override endpoint URL and protocol where needed
In some cases, the provider’s auto-detection might mistake the API protocol or target URL you want to use for a particular model. For example, you will need to set a different URL to use Amazon Bedrock through a VPC endpoint or the Mantle endpoints.
In the Kimi Code config.toml, you can:
- Set the protocol field to openai (Chat Completions), openai_responses, or anthropic (Messages) to configure a model to use a particular supported wire protocol. See the model cards for which models support which APIs.
- Set the base_url field to change the target URL, which must include any attached API path like /openai/v1 or /anthropic.
In the following example, we show a configuration to connect to the same model but using the OpenAI Responses API through an Amazon Bedrock VPC endpoint you’ve set up:
Treat connectivity status as a configuration indicator
In the Kimi Code desktop and web apps, the provider list can show connected for a bedrock provider. That status doesn’t validate the configured AWS credentials, IAM permissions, Region, model access, or network path. Don’t treat it as proof of a successful model request. Use the non-interactive prompt to test the complete path, and diagnose the actual response if it fails.
Cleanup
If you created a new AWS IAM identity or assigned new permissions to experiment with Kimi K3.1 Pro on Amazon Bedrock, remember to delete them when you’re finished testing.
You might also want to revert any local Kimi Code CLI provider configurations or AWS CLI profiles you set up. You can even uninstall the CLIs altogether if they’re no longer required. See the uninstall guides for Kimi Code and AWS CLI for details. Remember that deleting the local AWS configuration or CLI doesn’t by itself revoke IAM permissions or an active AWS session.
Amazon Bedrock inference for the models we showed is charged on a per-token basis, so there’s no persistent cloud infrastructure deployment to clean up.
Conclusion
We showed how Moonshot AI’s native bedrock provider in Kimi Code CLI v2.7.0 connects to Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed on Amazon Bedrock through the standard AWS credential chain. You no longer need a separately managed Amazon Bedrock API key.
Amazon Bedrock gives you access to open and proprietary AI models from leading providers, through standard APIs. Its governance controls and compliance validation programs can support even strictly regulated workloads.
If you’re already using Kimi Code CLI and want to run inference on AWS, upgrade today and give the new streamlined authentication a try.
For more information about Kimi K3.1 Pro on Amazon Bedrock, see our launch blog post and the Moonshot AI on AWS samples repository. To explore supported APIs and features by model, see the model cards in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. To discuss your use case with the Amazon Bedrock team, connect with us.

articles.title: JPMorgan Chase, Visa y Mastercard confirmaron un ciberataque a sus proveedores externos: el ataque expuso datos de sus clientes
articles.text:
JPMorgan Chase, Visa y Mastercard anunciaron que una vulneración en proveedores externos expuso datos de marketing y contacto de algunos clientes de sus clientes, aunque las tres compañías aseguraron que sus redes de pago y la información de las tarjetas no resultaron afectadas.
Por sus características, se cree que el ataque sería de la banda de ciberextorsión n0n. El grupo publicó el 16 de noviembre haber obtenido registros de interacción de titulares de tarjetas que incluían “cientos de miles de interacciones de campaña para decenas de miles de direcciones de correo electrónico de titulares de tarjetas distintas”.
La exposición de la información podría facilitar la identificación de los titulares de las cuentas y dejarlos más expuestos a intentos de fraude. La revista Newsweek advirtió que las direcciones de correo electrónico pueden utilizarse para rastrear otros datos personales, como domicilios y teléfonos, además de facilitar ataques de phishing.
JPMorgan contactará a los clientes que podrían haber sido afectados
JPMorgan Chase, el mayor banco de Estados Unidos, señaló en una publicación en la red social X que se comunicará directamente con las personas alcanzadas y que les ofrecerá asistencia, entre ella servicios de monitoreo de crédito. La entidad agregó que sus servicios operan con normalidad.
En los datos difundidos por n0n figuran más de 16.000 direcciones de correo electrónico de clientes, algunas acompañadas por números telefónicos y códigos postales, además de 124 direcciones corporativas que aparentemente pertenecerían a empleados del banco, según una revisión de Reuters.
Newsweek señaló que los datos parecerían corresponder al programa “Reserve” del banco, una tarjeta de crédito disponible únicamente por invitación y destinada, por lo general, a clientes con al menos USD 10 millones en activos bajo gestión.
La entidad aclaró que el ciberataque no está relacionado con los problemas que algunos clientes tuvieron esta semana al intentar procesar transacciones. Según Reuters, esas interrupciones se debieron a un error de software que también afectó a otros bancos.
We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack. Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. There is no disruption to our services. Where appropriate, we will contact affected customers directly and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. There is no connection to service disruption some customers experienced earlier this week.
— J.P. Morgan (@jpmorgan) November 19, 2026
Visa y Mastercard atribuyeron la exposición a prestadores de servicios
De acuerdo con The Washington Post y Reuters, Visa indicó que conoce los reclamos del grupo y los vinculó con un incidente en un proveedor externo de Asia-Pacífico. La firma sostuvo que sus sistemas no estuvieron involucrados ni sufrieron impacto y que no se expusieron datos de pago, como números de tarjeta.
Los archivos que n0n publicó bajo el nombre de Visa parecen concentrarse en mercados de la región, entre ellos Hong Kong, Taiwán, Corea del Sur, Japón, Filipinas, Singapur, Malasia, Australia y Macao. Contienen miles de supuestas direcciones de correo electrónico, teléfonos y datos de campañas de marketing.
Por su parte, Mastercard dijo que fue notificada recientemente de un incidente en un proveedor externo. Según la empresa, el hecho expuso una cantidad limitada de direcciones de correo electrónico y otros datos ajenos a pagos de un pequeño grupo de titulares inscritos en un programa específico de beneficios.
La compañía afirmó que la red de pagos de Mastercard no sufrió consecuencias y las tarjetas pueden seguir utilizándose. Los registros difundidos por n0n se refieren a campañas de marketing para clientes de América del Norte, Oriente Medio y África, y también incluyen una pequeña cantidad de correos electrónicos de empleados.
Una serie de fallas afectó servicios críticos e infraestructuras de Estados Unidos
El ataque se conoció en una semana marcada por otras fallas en servicios e infraestructuras de Estados Unidos.
Entre los episodios recientes, están la caída global del correo electrónico de Microsoft, la suspensión nacional de vuelos ordenada por la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA), las interrupciones en movimientos, envíos monetarios y operaciones con cheques en los principales bancos del país y la salida de servicio de una red interna que la Agencia de Seguridad Nacional (NSA) utiliza para comunicar información clasificada.
Tras la interrupción bancaria de esta semana, la Oficina del Contralor de la Moneda (OCC) consultó a los prestamistas para evaluar el alcance y la comunicación con sus clientes, indicaron fuentes del sector a Reuters.
El Departamento del Tesoro y el regulador también contactaron a los bancos poco después de conocerse el incidente para descartar que se tratara de un ataque informático y asegurar que estuviera bajo control.

articles.title: NAND Flash Prices Set to Decline in 2027 as Chinese CSP Order Cuts Outweigh North American Demand Growth
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
NAND Flash Prices Set to Decline in 2027 as Chinese CSP Order Cuts Outweigh North American Demand Growth
TrendForce's latest memory industry research indicates that the global NAND Flash market is expected to see a reversal in supply-demand dynamics in 2027. With supply set to grow rapidly, substantial cuts to enterprise SSD orders from Chinese CSPs—coupled with a potential further contraction in consumer electronics demand—are expected to exacerbate oversupply. 
TrendForce forecasts that the overall NAND Flash contract prices will begin declining in the first quarter of 2027, with quarterly price drops potentially widening as the year progresses. TrendForce estimates that global NAND Flash industry CapEx will increase 26.7% YoY to US$29.9 billion in 2027.Strong demand for high-performance storage in North America continues to drive manufacturers to expand capacity and upgrade process technology. Meanwhile, rising QLC penetration and the transition to higher-layer-count NAND technologies will further boost bit output. Although some suppliers may slightly slow their expansion plans in response to sluggish consumer demand, global NAND Flash bit supply is still projected to grow by somewhere between 25-30% YoY in 2027.
Enterprise SSDs remain the primary growth driver for the NAND Flash industry, but regional demand trends are increasingly diverging. In North America, U.S.-based CSPs have recently raised their 2027 demand forecasts again, supported by AI agent and general-purpose server projects already under construction. 
Chinese CSPs, however, are facing challenges including GPU shortages, elevated inventory levels, and intensifying competition over token pricing. As a result, they have reduced their total enterprise SSD orders for 2027 by an amount that exceeds the additional demand from U.S.-based CSPs.
In the consumer market, inventories of low-cost memory are expected to be depleted in 2027, putting upward pressure on finished-device prices and further weighing on shipments. Additionally, brands seeking to control bill-of-materials (BOM) costs will need to reduce storage capacity specifications, resulting in a significant decline in average capacity per device and further widening the demand shortfall.
NAND Flash prices forecast to fall 0-5% QoQ in 1Q27, with all product categories entering a downward cycle from 2Q27
TrendForce notes that continued downward revisions to global consumer electronics shipments, along with reduced enterprise SSD orders in China, have already begun to weigh on NAND Flash contract prices in the fourth quarter of 2026. 
In response, TrendForce has lowered its forecast for quarterly contract price increases to 8-13%. Weakening demand has also intensified inventory-clearing pressure in distribution channels, triggering a sharp correction of more than 20% in spot prices recently.
Looking ahead to 2027, cuts to enterprise SSD demand from Chinese CSPs are expected to offset order growth in North America, while supply growth will significantly outpace demand throughout the year. As oversupply intensifies, TrendForce forecasts that overall NAND Flash contract prices will decline by 0-5% QoQ in the first quarter, with all product categories entering a downward price cycle beginning in the second quarter.
TrendForce emphasizes that the market outlook will depend on the pace of inventory reduction among Chinese CSPs, changes to restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether consumer electronics manufacturers continue adopting lower memory specifications in 2028. 
Another key factor will be the direction of US policy following the mid-term election, particularly whether any changes affect major AI data center projects planned for 2028 that are still in the planning and permitting stages. The pace of project approvals and capital expenditure will directly influence advance inventory procurement in the second half of 2027.

articles.title: Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say
articles.text:
A Russian national has been indicted on suspicions he was a Russian spy who stalked and surveilled employees of a Silicon Valley company that was assisting Ukraine in its ongoing war with its eastern neighbor.
Igor D’iu, 25, allegedly photographed the employees and their computer screens as they worked at a coffee shop located near the company’s Palo Alto office, federal prosecutors said Wednesday. He also kept a list of home addresses of employees and a senior executive. At one point, prosecutors said, D’iu trailed an employee as she traveled home from Palo Alto to San Francisco. An affidavit filed in the case referred to the employee as FEMP1, short for female employee, and said the event left her “in a state of emotional distress.”
Evasive and irregular turns
“FEMP1 made evasive and irregular turns, took back roads, and turned into a grocery store parking lot where D’IU continued aggressively following her vehicle,” an FBI special agent wrote. “D’IU followed FEMP1 through U-turns, illegal left turns, and ran a red light to stay with FEMP1 for nearly thirty miles. FEMP1 called 911 while driving and was instructed to drive directly to San Francisco Police Department (“SFPD”) Mission Station. Near SFPD Mission Station, FEMP1 flagged an SFPD patrol vehicle and reported the incident. D’IU left once FEMP1 made contact with the patrol vehicle.”
When police later questioned D’iu about the incident, the defendant allegedly said he saw a woman get into a car and thought she was “beautiful.” He then told the investigators that he followed her because he “wanted to ask her out on a date.”
Prosecutors didn’t name the company, but both Reuters and Bloomberg, citing unnamed people with knowledge of the case, identified it as Palantir. Ars is unable to confirm that reporting. Palantir representatives didn’t respond to an email seeking confirmation.

Today's best office chair deal

articles.title: Black Friday: Warum die Deutschen den Rabatten so wenig trauen – und trotzdem kaufen
articles.text:
Black Friday: Warum die Deutschen den Rabatten so wenig trauen – und trotzdem kaufen
Rabatte, überall Rabatte: Es ist wieder so weit, der Black Friday steht vor der Tür. In diesem Jahr fällt er auf den 27. November. Das aus den USA stammende Verkaufsphänomen hat sich auch in Deutschland zunehmend etabliert. Vor allem im Internet, aber auch im stationären Handel werben Unternehmen kurz vor Beginn der Weihnachtszeit mit Rabatten. Wie wichtig sind die Aktionstage für Verbraucher und den Handel und worauf sollte man bei Sonderangeboten achten?
Wie stark ist das Verbraucherinteresse am Black Friday?
Knapp die Hälfte der Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher in Deutschland plant, am Black Friday etwas zu kaufen. Das ergab eine repräsentative Umfrage der Unternehmensberatung PwC. Im Schnitt wollen die Befragten fast 300 Euro ausgeben. Das sind 12 Prozent mehr als im Vorjahr. Besonders gefragt sind laut Umfrage Elektronik und Mode.
„Rabattaktionen wie der Black Friday bleiben gerade in wirtschaftlich angespannten Zeiten relevant. Händler müssen allerdings stärker als früher beweisen, dass sich Angebote tatsächlich lohnen“, sagt Marcus Kroth, Handelsexperte bei der Unternehmensberatung BCG. Laut einer BCG-Untersuchung sorgen sich 77 Prozent der Deutschen wegen der gestiegenen Preise für lebensnotwendige Güter wie Lebensmittel und Energie. Viele reagieren mit Sparmaßnahmen. Vor allem Haushalte mit mittleren und niedrigen Einkommen achten beim Einkauf verstärkt auf den Preis.
Das Interesse am Black Friday ist nicht in allen Bevölkerungsgruppen gleich groß. Ähnlich wie bei Halloween lasse sich auch in Bezug auf den Black Friday eine gewisse Spaltung in der deutschen Bevölkerung beobachten, sagt der Marketing- und Konsumforscher Andreas Baetzgen. Euphorie und Konsumbereitschaft seien in jüngeren und digitalaffineren Teilen der Gesellschaft deutlich stärker ausgeprägt. Zugleich gebe es viele Menschen, die den Black Friday „für einen Quatsch aus Amerika halten“.
Woher kommt die Skepsis gegenüber dem Black Friday?
Vor allem das Misstrauen gegenüber vermeintlichen Sonderangeboten ist in Deutschland groß. Die BCG-Studie zeigt: Nur 37 Prozent der deutschen Verbraucher vertrauen darauf, dass beworbene Black-Friday-Preise tatsächlich stark reduziert sind. Das seien 17 Prozentpunkte weniger als im weltweiten Durchschnitt und einer der niedrigsten Werte unter den untersuchten Ländern.
Eine mögliche Erklärung für die große Skepsis der Deutschen sei die hierzulande stark ausgeprägte Aufklärung durch Verbraucherportale, Verbrauchersendungen und kritische Berichterstattung, meint Konsumforscher Baetzgen. „Das weckt natürlich schon ein gewisses Misstrauen gegenüber solchen Extrempreisnachlässen.“
Black Friday 2026: 10 Tricks, mit denen du wirklich Geld sparst
Wie wichtig ist der Black Friday für den Handel?
Für Handelsunternehmen ist die Bedeutung des Black Friday inzwischen enorm. Der Handelsverband Deutschland (HDE) rechnet in diesem Jahr an den beiden Aktionstagen Black Friday und Cyber Monday mit einem Umsatz von 6,2 Milliarden Euro. Das wäre ein Anstieg von sechs Prozent im Vergleich zum Vorjahr und ein neuer Höchstwert.
„Man kann den Black Friday als Händler nicht mehr ignorieren. Das Mitmachen ist quasi schon Gruppenzwang“, sagt der Ökonom und Handelsexperte Gerrit Heinemann. Teilweise erwirtschafteten Unternehmen bis zu fünf Prozent ihres Jahresumsatzes allein am Black Friday.
Der Black Friday stelle Händler allerdings vor ein Dilemma: Er bringe nicht unbedingt zusätzliche Einnahmen, sondern ziehe vielmehr das Weihnachtsgeschäft vor, so Heinemann. Anschließend könne es zu sinkenden Umsätzen beim Geschenkeverkauf kommen.
Eine PwC-Untersuchung stützt diese Einschätzung: Drei von vier befragten Konsumenten kaufen demnach zumindest einen Teil ihrer Geschenke rund um den Black Friday. Im vergangenen Jahr entfielen bei mehr als der Hälfte der befragten Unternehmen über zehn Prozent des Weihnachtsgeschäfts auf die Aktionstage. Bei knapp einem Drittel der Firmen waren es sogar mehr als 20 Prozent. Auch Daten des Marktforschungsinstituts NIQ belegen, dass der Black Friday zwar Nachfrage aktiviere, sie aber selten neu erzeuge.
Worauf kommt es für Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher an?
Angesichts der Flut vermeintlicher Sonderangebote raten Verbraucherschützer zur Vorsicht. «Lassen Sie sich nicht von der unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung verwirren», warnt Andrea Steinbach von der Verbraucherzentrale. Ein gängiger Trick auf Händlerseite sei es, den Aktionspreis mit der unverbindlichen Preisempfehlung (UVP) zu vergleichen, statt mit dem tatsächlich üblichen Verkaufspreis. Da dieser meist deutlich unter der UVP liege, bedeute ein Rabatt von 50 Prozent auf die UVP oft nur eine geringe oder gar keine Ersparnis.
Steinbach empfiehlt, den Preisverlauf eines Produkts auf mindestens zwei Vergleichsportalen zu prüfen. Kaufinteressierte sollten dabei auf den niedrigsten Preis der vergangenen 30 Tage achten und ihn mit dem Angebotspreis vergleichen.
Welche Rolle spielt KI beim Black Friday?
Besondere Vorsicht ist bei unbekannten Onlinehändlern angebracht. Künstliche Intelligenz erleichtert es Betrügern, gefälschte Händlerseiten, sogenannte Fake-Shops, mit KI-generierten Bildern und Produktwerbung zu erstellen. KI kann Verbrauchern aber auch dabei helfen, vermeintliche Sonderangebote von echten Deals zu unterscheiden, denn die Anwendungen können aufwendige Suchprozesse deutlich beschleunigen. In einer Untersuchung der BCG geben 57 Prozent der Kaufinteressierten aus Deutschland an, KI bereits beim Einkaufen genutzt zu haben oder nutzen zu wollen.

articles.title: Intel 18A yields hit 70% as company signs Microsoft as EMIB customer — the first company to publicly commit to Intel's new packaging technology
articles.text:
Intel 18A yields hit 70% as company signs Microsoft as EMIB customer — the first company to publicly commit to Intel's new packaging technology
And inks long-term supply agreement with Microsoft.
Lip-Bu Tan, chief executive of Intel, said on Thursday that yields of chips made using the company's latest 18A (1.8nm-class) fabrication process have achieved 70%, which is more or less in line with what one would expect from an all-new manufacturing technology at this stage of its ramp. In addition, Intel and Microsoft have signed an agreement under which Microsoft will secure Intel Xeon supply capacity for years to come and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for in-house silicon.
"When I took over [as CEO in March, 2025], 18A yield was horrible; now we are at 70%," Lip-Bu Tan said at the TomorrowX conference (via @firesidealpha).
Lip-Bu Tan did not specify whether he meant functional yield, parametric yield, or percentage of sellable silicon. However, it is reasonable to expect a CEO of a semiconductor company to talk about functional die yield, the percentage of dies that pass basic electrical and functional testing.
Intel began volume production of compute tiles of its Core Ultra 300-series CPUs codenamed Panther Lake using 18A in the second half of 2025, so a 70% functional yield seems decent at this stage of the product ramp, though for Intel's economics a lot depends on parametric yield and how many advanced SKUs of Core Ultra 300-series 'Panther Lake' processors Intel can supply to customers at a premium. The same applies to Intel's Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest processors with up to 288 cores that are in high-volume production now and which use 18A-based compute chiplets along with Foveros Direct 3D stacking.
In addition to announcing an important 18A milestone, Intel also signed a long-term agreement with Microsoft, under which the latter will secure multi-year Intel Xeon supply capacity, including supply of next-generation Xeon processors codenamed Diamond Rapids, and will use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for multi-chiplet data center solutions developed in-house.
The EMIB agreement is arguably the biggest news. Microsoft is the first company to publicly commit to Intel's advanced packaging technology for its own silicon (i.e., it does not mean that Microsoft is the first third party to use EMIB; it is the first party to confirm usage of EMIB), which represents a significant commercial development for Intel Foundry in terms of publicity. However, the announcement does not identify the processors involved, their manufacturing process, production volumes, or deployment schedule. Microsoft was the first company to commit to use Intel's 18A for its data center silicon in 2024, though it is unclear whether the newly announced EMIB packaging agreement relates to the same solution or not. As the majority of high-end data center solutions tend to use multi-chiplet design, it is reasonable to expect Microsoft's future solutions for data centers to use EMIB for multi-die processors.
"Through use of our advanced packaging capabilities with EMIB to scale future generations of Azure infrastructure, Intel and Microsoft can combine the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale required for the AI era — giving customers new levels of performance and economics when interacting with Azure," said Naga Chandrasekaran, EVP, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The Xeon agreement provides Intel with greater visibility into future server CPU demand. Importantly, Microsoft has committed to using Intel's next-generation Xeon 'Diamond Rapids,' although the announcement does not disclose purchase volumes or financial terms.
The collaboration extends beyond processor procurement and EMIB. Specifically, Intel and Microsoft are jointly developing infrastructure capabilities that encompass processor architecture, heterogeneous integration, CXL memory expansion, QuickAssist Technology (QAT) acceleration, and Trust Domain Extensions (TDX) security.

articles.title: Geehy Launches G32R502 1kW Bidirectional Inverter Solution - EE Times
articles.text:
Driven by global carbon-reduction goals and the growing adoption of renewable energy, energy storage is expanding from large, centralized power stations to distributed applications such as residential, portable, and emergency backup power. According to Frost & Sullivan, the global residential energy storage system market grew at a compound annual growth rate of 58.3% from 2021 to 2025, increasing from RMB 10.8 billion to RMB 67.6 billion. The market is expected to reach RMB 290 billion by 2031.
The 1kW power segment bridges portable and light residential energy storage. It supports portability, parallel operation, and grid connection, making it a fast-growing market segment.
For outdoor energy storage, home backup, emergency power, and similar applications, Geehy has introduced the G32R502 1kW fully digital bidirectional energy storage inverter solution. Its fully digital control and two-stage totem-pole PFC + LLC architecture provide a cost-effective, reliable, and highly integrated reference design for low-power bidirectional energy storage inverters.
Applications of the G32R502 1kW Energy Storage Inverter Solution
Introduction to the G32R502 1kW Energy Storage Inverter Solution
The solution uses a two-stage totem-pole PFC + LLC power architecture:
The front-end totem-pole PFC stage supports both rectification and off-grid inverter operation. The G32R502’s built-in high-speed comparator enables cycle-by-cycle (CBC) inductor current control, allowing the system to handle output short circuits and sudden capacitive load connection.
The back-end isolated DC/DC stage uses a resonant LLC half-bridge converter controlled independently by a second G32R502. A hardware resonant channel enables soft switching across the full operating range, while a fixed-resonant-frequency no-load control strategy maintains high LLC efficiency under all operating conditions.
G32R502 1kW Energy Storage Inverter Solution Block Diagram
Solution Specifications
It supports 220V AC input and output, with the output frequency automatically following the AC charging input frequency. Its DC bus can be adjusted from 320V to 450V, while the 22V–28.8V battery input range supports 25.6V eight-cell LiFePO4 battery packs. The solution delivers 1000W rated output power, AC output voltage THD below 1%, and AC charging power of up to 1000W.
Core Advantages of the Solution
Fully digital bidirectional control: Combines inverter and charging functions in one solution. The output frequency automatically follows the 50Hz or 60Hz AC charging input frequency.
Independent dual-MCU control: Two G32R502 MCUs independently control the PFC and LLC stages. Analog signals can be sampled without isolation devices, simplifying peripheral sampling circuits and reducing BOM cost.
Efficient power topology: The totem-pole PFC + half-bridge LLC topology supports fixed-frequency LLC operation and soft switching across the full operating range.
High conversion efficiency: Peak discharge efficiency reaches 94.930%, with 94.02% efficiency at rated full load. Peak charging efficiency reaches 94.51%, with 93.90% efficiency under rated charging conditions.
High efficiency and low distortion: Power factor is ≥0.98, total harmonic distortion is ≤3%, and rated conversion efficiency is ≥90%. The pure sine wave output supports the safe and stable operation of sensitive equipment.
UPS functionality: The system automatically switches to inverter mode within 20ms of a mains outage, providing a smooth transition and uninterrupted power for critical loads.
G32R502 1kW Energy Storage Inverter Solution Demo Board
Test Data and Operating Waveforms
Discharge efficiency curve: Peak discharge efficiency reaches 94.930%, with 94.02% efficiency at full load. Output voltage harmonics remain < 1% under resistive-load conditions.
Voltage harmonic curve: Peak charging efficiency reaches 94.567%, with 93.936% efficiency at rated full load and a charging power factor >0.99.
Inverter output waveform at a 1000W AC load
AC charging waveform at 1000W constant power
Overall UPS switching waveform
The Geehy G32R502 energy storage inverter solution includes a flexible, user-friendly PC tool. It supports real-time operating status monitoring, online parameter configuration, program variable reading, variable recording, and waveform plotting.
Features of the G32R502 Real-Time Control MCU
1. High-performance computing: The MCU integrates the Helium™ vector extension and Geehy’s proprietary Zidian mathematical instruction extension unit. The Cortex-M52 core’s ACI capability allows custom instructions to run directly within the core, accelerating power-control algorithms such as filters, compensators, and phase-locked loops.
2. Precise real-time control: Fourteen built-in high-resolution PWM channels with 150ps resolution enable precise control of duty cycle, switching frequency, phase shift, and dead time.
3. Responsive signal sensing: Four comparator groups, each with two built-in 12-bit DACs, support blanking and filtering for peak current control, zero-crossing detection, and trip protection. Two 12-bit ADCs with a sampling rate of 3.73 MSPS support synchronized, low-latency signal acquisition.
Conclusion
Supported by the G32R5 series of real-time control MCUs/DSPs, comprehensive software and hardware tools, and an experienced solution design team, Geehy can meet the digital power requirements of industrial control, smart energy, and other applications.
Geehy works closely with multiple end-product manufacturers and will continue expanding its product portfolio while improving product features and performance. These efforts will help the digital power industry achieve higher efficiency, greater power density, and lower costs while supporting the energy sector’s transition toward a greener and more sustainable future.
To address a wider range of digital power applications, Geehy will continue to introduce G32R502-based reference designs, including a 2.2kW two-phase interleaved totem-pole PFC, a 10kW three-phase I-type three-level PFC, a 2kW PFC + phase-shifted full-bridge converter, a 48V/50A telecom power supply, and a 2.2kW full-bridge LLC converter. These designs will extend the G32R502’s use across a broader range of power levels and converter topologies, providing customers with more digital power design options.

articles.title: Google just gave Gemini the run of your Mac — three days after Apple tightened the rules
articles.text:
Google just gave Gemini the run of your Mac — three days after Apple tightened the rules
Google is adding computer use to its Gemini app for macOS. The assistant can now work across desktop applications and websites in a separate background window without taking over the user’s screen. Gemini handles tasks in the background while users continue working.
The feature includes a live preview in the chat so users can monitor the agent’s activity, pause execution, and approve actions when necessary.
The company’s announcement Thursday comes just three days after Apple introduced tighter permission controls for macOS automation.
The company’s announcement Thursday comes just three days after Apple introduced tighter permission controls for macOS automation. Google hasn’t explained how Gemini will operate under the new restrictions.
Apple tightens agent permissions
The macOS 27.3 beta 2 changes split Device Control and Data Access permissions into two categories; System & App Protection Override and Accessibility.
Apps requesting broad system access will face more explicit permission prompts, and users can approve individual requests instead of granting ongoing access.
Developers building desktop agents will also need to account for least-privilege access, since users can restrict or revoke permissions while an agent is running.
Gemini’s new Mac powers
Google says Gemini can extract shipping details from local PDFs, gather dashboard metrics for presentations, edit batches of photos, and work with 3D design software.
The company hasn’t detailed how the background environment is isolated from macOS, how it maintains state across applications, or which actions require user approval.
Google’s existing computer-use API
Google introduced computer use with Gemini 2.5 in October 2025 and later integrated it directly into Gemini 3.5 Flash.
According to the developer documentation, the model works from screenshots and returns actions for client-side execution. Developers manage the execution environment, while the API provides configurable safety policies, and optional screenshot scanning for prompt injection.
The new Mac feature is part of the consumer Gemini app, not a separate developer API.
The new Mac feature is part of the consumer Gemini app, not a separate developer API. It’s unclear whether the app uses the same execution architecture or whether Google plans to open its background environment to third-party developers.
Where Google stays silent
The company has documented prompt-injection safeguards for its developer-facing computer-use tools but hasn’t said which protections are built into the Mac app. Agents with access to local files and privileged applications also risk untrusted input reaching the agent harness, and influencing the actions it executes.
Reliability questions remain unanswered since the company has not shared any performance figures for the Mac app or explained what happens when an action fails, or an application behaves unexpectedly.
Rollout, requirements and tiers
Gemini computer use is rolling out in English in the United States for personal Google accounts belonging to users 18 and older. The feature requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS Sequoia 15.0 or later and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription.
