articles.title: Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Enable AI agents to pay for AWS Marketplace x402 products with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments
When Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments became generally available in August 2026, agents could autonomously pay for paid APIs, MCP servers, and web content over open protocols like x402 and MPP with payment limits and full observability. Today we extend that autonomy to AWS Marketplace, so agents can discover and buy x402-enabled software, APIs, data, and content, and pay in USD on the agent developer’s AWS bill, removing the need for stablecoin wallets or API keys.
Developers can also configure and automate discovery through the AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway. Existing guardrails carry over, developers can set spending limits and approved sellers using AgentCore policy, and the payment session cap is enforced by AgentCore payments, so an agent is unable to overspend. Transactions are auditable in AWS CloudTrail and AWS Cost Explorer. Because agent purchases run through AWS accounts on both sides, agentic purchasing meets the security and auditability enterprises expect.
The x402 catalog on AWS Marketplace is expanding with a growing roster of trusted, verified sellers. Tavily, a live search provider for agentic commerce, is one of them:
        Agentic commerce isn’t just about giving agents the ability to pay. It’s about giving enterprises the confidence to let them.
That conviction is driving Tavily’s collaboration with the AWS team on the design of Agentic Commerce. By bringing secure, x402 powered transactions to AWS Marketplace and connecting agents with trusted, KYC verified providers, AWS is laying the foundation for autonomous commerce at production scale.
This is what enterprise ready agentic commerce looks like.
— Rotem Weiss, Founder & CEO, Tavily
What’s launching today
Today’s launch adds AWS Billing as a payment option in AgentCore payments. An agent can now pay x402-enabled AWS Marketplace sellers per request, in USD, settling on their AWS bill.
When an AWS Marketplace seller responds with 402 Payment Required, its response includes a signed quote for the purchase. With AWS Billing, the agent can forward the seller’s x402 response to AgentCore payments. AgentCore payments checks session budgets, then returns a payment token. The agent retries the request to the seller with the payment token included and receives a successful response. AWS bills the charge to the AWS account where Payment Manager is set up, and the charge appears on that account’s AWS bill.
To set up AWS Marketplace purchasing, the developer creates a Payment Manager with an AWS Billing connector. The connector only requires you to set up a service-linked role to access AWS Marketplace. Then, for each task, developers can create a payment session with a spending limit and give the agent the session ID.
An agent’s first purchase from a seller creates an agreement for the AWS account with that seller, and AWS Marketplace automatically tracks later purchases against it. Each product will then show up as an AWS Marketplace line item. If your organization uses Private Marketplace, agents can only buy the products it allows.
In addition, to discover new sellers, we are launching a new AWS Marketplace connector in AgentCore Gateway. This optional integration helps agents find products and their endpoints. At launch, AWS Billing supports the x402 exact scheme, where the seller quotes a fixed price for each request.
In this post, we walk through a research agent that discovers a tool, pays for a single request through AWS Billing, and answers with sources, with nothing set up in advance. We also provide an accompanying GitHub sample that you can use to evaluate the setup in your own AWS account.
Sample walkthrough
Suppose a financial analyst asks the agent what was announced about agentic payments this week. The model wasn’t trained on this week’s news, so the agent looks for a search tool. Through AgentCore Gateway, it searches AWS Marketplace, reads the listing from Tavily, an AWS Marketplace seller, and requests the listing’s x402 endpoints.
The agent calls the endpoint and receives an x402 payload with price details. The agent then forwards the x402 payload to AgentCore payments. AgentCore payments checks it against the remaining session budget and returns a payment token. Once these checks are passed, the agent sends the request again with the token attached, and gets the search results. Its answer includes sources and states what it bought and what it cost.
In this workflow, agents can apply their reasoning to decide which AWS Marketplace tool to use.
How it works
1. Discover. The agent calls three read-only gateway tools in order: search listings, get a listing, and list its fulfillment options. Search listings tool only returns endpoints that accept x402. The last call returns the seller’s endpoint URL and the payment protocols it accepts.
2. Get a quote. The agent calls the endpoint with no payment attached. The seller answers with HTTP 402 and puts a signed quote in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header. AWS Marketplace checks the signature against the seller’s registered key, which means a quote with an altered price gets rejected.
3. Pay. The agent passes the quote to the ProcessPayment API with the payment type AWS_BILLING_X402. If budget remains in the session, AgentCore payments issues a payment token. If not, the call fails and the developer is not charged.
4. Redeem. The agent sends the request again, this time with the token in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header, and the seller returns the content. Payment tokens are valid for about five minutes, so the agent completes steps 2 through 4 in a single pass.
5. Settle. On the developer’s first purchase from a seller, AWS Marketplace creates the agreement with that seller. After that it meters each charge to their AWS bill. Settlement runs asynchronously and shows up in their AWS bill monthly.
Prerequisites
To create an AWS Billing connector, developers’ AWS accounts must have the AWS Marketplace service-linked role AWSServiceRoleForMarketplaceAgenticCommerce. AWS Marketplace uses this role to bill AWS Marketplace purchases that their agents make to their AWS account. Refer to the documentation for more details.
Hands-on
The open-source GitHub sample in the agentcore-samples repository runs through a demo of the new functionality. It can help you configure AgentCore payments for AWS Marketplace, connect Tavily, run the agent, and inspect the transaction. You can refer to the documentation for more details.
Step 1: Configure AgentCore payments
setup_aws_billing.py creates a payment manager with an AWS Billing connector, plus the AWS Marketplace service-linked role and three separate AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles. The session role can set budgets but can’t pay. Meanwhile the agent role can pay but can’t create sessions, so the agent has no way to raise its own budget.
Step 2: Connect Tavily
setup_gateway.py creates an AgentCore Gateway with the AWS Marketplace connector and gives the agent role the appropriate permissions to use it. The gateway’s role is limited to three read-only AWS Marketplace actions. If you choose to skip this step, you can instead set SELLER_URL in the environment variables to the seller’s endpoint, and the agent will pay that URL only rather than using AgentCore Gateway discovery.
Step 3: Run the agent
The script creates a payment session as the session role and then runs the agent as the agent role. By default the session budget is $0.05 and the per-request cap is $0.02.
The agent searches, looks at listings, gets an endpoint, and pays once. In this test run against a $0.01 seller, it compared two listings before buying:
Step 4: Inspect the transaction
When the run finishes, the sample will print the payment with its amount, AWS Marketplace product ID, and processPaymentId. The AWS Marketplace meters charges asynchronously, so the Tavily line item takes a moment to appear on your bill. Agent purchases will also show up in AWS CloudTrail and AWS Cost Explorer.
Step 5: Clean up
Run cleanup.py to delete resources. Make sure to validate deletion to avoid incurring additional resource charges.
Conclusion
AgentCore payments and AWS Marketplace provide the infrastructure for agents that can transact. The research agent in this post goes from “I need live web search” to sourcing an answer on its own, discovering premium paid content through tools, and paying for requests that settle on the developer’s AWS bill.
With AgentCore payments, developers can build with open protocols like x402, which opens them to a growing catalog of trusted, verified AWS Marketplace sellers. This gives agents more autonomy and developers more control. Governance is built in, with per-session spending caps and an approved seller list using AgentCore policy, and IAM identities that make it auditable in AWS CloudTrail and AWS Cost Explorer. The agent chooses the right tool for the task, and developers can keep the same billing, budgets, and controls they already trust.

articles.title: Lenovo Delivers Record Q2 Performance, Confident in Long-term Hybrid AI Opportunities
articles.text:
Thursday, November 19th 2026
Lenovo Delivers Record Q2 Performance, Confident in Long-term Hybrid AI Opportunities
Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) (ADR: LNVGY), together with its subsidiaries ('the Group'), today reported second quarter results for fiscal year 2026/27, demonstrating strong growth, a leap forward in profitability, and structural enhancements to the Group's business fundamentals.
Overall Group revenue for the second quarter reached an all-time high of US$30.2 billion, up 48% year-on-year. All business groups delivered record second-fiscal-quarter revenue while demonstrating strong profitability, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) becoming an engine of hyper-growth with operating profit surpassing US$1 billion for the first time. Adjusted net income was up 166% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion, with adjusted net margin improvements of two percentage points year-on-year. AI-related revenue grew 79% year-on-year, surpassing the US$10 billion mark for the first time and accounting for 36% of total Group revenue in Q2.Performance was underpinned by broad-based momentum across the Group's diversified portfolio and balanced growth across all sales geographies. Business fundamentals continued to strengthen as faster growth in higher-value segments reshaped the Group's profit mix. This diversification helps mitigate industry-wide cost pressures and exposure to device-demand cycles, supporting a more resilient and sustainable profitability profile.
The Group continues to maintain disciplined cash and capital management, balancing strong revenue growth and industry-wide higher component costs with controlled capital expenditure and credit risk controls for large AI infrastructure projects. In this quarter, it generated US$1.6 billion in operating cash flow and US$1.2 billion in free cash flow.
Market Outlook
Lenovo remains highly confident in the long-term growth opportunities across both infrastructure and devices. As AI shifts from training to inferencing, rapidly expanding real-world use cases are driving sustained compute demand across cloud, edge, and enterprise environments. Cloud Service Provider revenue for the Group grew nearly 170% year-on-year, and Enterprise & SMB infrastructure revenue was up 200% year-on-year. At the same time, AI democratization is creating new demand for intelligent, agent-enabled devices as well as new form factors, as more AI data and workloads are generated at the edge. With a full-stack Hybrid AI portfolio spanning devices, edge, infrastructure, solutions and services, Lenovo is uniquely positioned as a full-stack player to capture opportunities and value across the market, as well as extend its leadership.
Lenovo's Board of Directors declared an interim dividend of 9.0 HK cents per share.
Yuanqing Yang, Chairman and CEO"Lenovo delivered another exceptional quarter, where we have sustained strong growth, made a leap forward in profitability, and structurally enhanced our business fundamentals, together demonstrating the success of our transformation from a PC leader into a global full-stack compute leader. Now, the real-world AI adoption is booming, which will not only drive sustained growth in infrastructure demand but also unlock tremendous growth potential in the device market. With our Hybrid AI strategy, full-stack portfolio across Client-Edge-Cloud, as well as strong financial discipline and operational resilience, we are confident in sustaining this strong momentum and reaching US$100 billion in annual revenue as early as this fiscal year."
Winston Cheng, CFO"Our results this quarter demonstrate the strength of Lenovo's geographically diverse business and balanced customer mix, while marking further progress toward our long-term net-margin ambitions of more than 5%. This, combined with disciplined working-capital management and controlled capital expenditure, gives us the flexibility to invest in organic growth while maintaining strong liquidity, a resilient balance sheet and our investment-grade credit profile. Together, our operational excellence and financial discipline position Lenovo to capture long-term demand for AI compute and deliver sustainable, profitable growth."
Financial Highlights: Q2 results:
Intelligent Devices Group (IDG):
- Revenue for IDG increased 15% year-on-year to record second fiscal quarter revenue of US$17.4 billion, with double-digit year-on-year revenue growth from PCs and smart devices.
- IDG's industry-leading operating margin was well maintained at 7.1%, despite a challenging market environment, reflecting the Group's operational excellence, supply chain resilience, and continued innovation.
- Global PC market share leadership was further strengthened, reaching 23.8% and extending Lenovo's lead over the #2 player to an all-time high of more than seven percentage points.
- The smartphone business delivered record second-quarter revenue, with double-digit year-on-year growth.
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG):
- ISG delivered the strongest quarter in its history in terms of both revenue and profit, with revenue reaching US$11.3 billion, up 178% year-on-year, and operating profit exceeding US$1 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded to a record 9.6%.
- ISG strengthened its global market leadership in traditional server, ranking number one in global x86 server shipments for the first time with 16%[3]market share, up six percentage points year-on-year.
- Enterprise & SMB revenue grew 200% year-on-year. GPU server revenue grew more than 300% year-on-year, supported by a pipeline that grew 48% quarter-on-quarter to US$80 billion.
- In the first full quarter as part of the Lenovo Group, Infinidat delivered its best quarter ever - with the high-end storage portfolio expanding ISG's enterprise storage capabilities.
Solutions and Services Group (SSG):
- SSG delivered record quarterly revenue of US$3.1 billion, up 20% year-on-year, and surpassing US$3 billion for the first time. Operating margin expanded 3.7 percentage points to a record 26%.
- SSG is growing nearly 2x faster than the broader services market, an outperformance increasingly being driven by higher-value segments as enterprise AI-led offerings accelerate. Managed Services, Projects & Solutions reached a record 63% of SSG revenue, demonstrating the strength of SSG's tech-led, labor-light model.
- AI Services continued to deliver triple-digit year-on-year revenue growth, as SSG scaled repeatable AI-powered solutions and Lenovo IP across industries, with momentum in areas including retail, manufacturing and sports.
- AI Library is also scaling proven, validated use cases across industries and functions, helping customers move from AI experimentation to measurable business outcomes up to 24 times faster.
Corporate highlights
Achievements, announcements, and notable commitments over the past quarter include:
- Lenovo climbed 43 places to #153 on Fortune's annual Global 500 List, making it the highest ranking in the company's history and one of the most significant advances in recent years. The recognition underscores Lenovo's position as one of the world's 500 largest companies by revenue.
- Lenovo received the highest possible rating by Hang Seng Indexes company advancing from its AA+ rating of last year to AAA this year, as well as the highest Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) scores for any company within the technology industry.
- The Group was named to TIME's World's Best Companies 2026 list for the first time, ranking no. 51 globally among leading companies worldwide. The ranking, developed by TIME in partnership with Statista, recognizes top-performing companies around the world based on three primary dimensions: employee satisfaction, revenue growth, and sustainability transparency. Lenovo achieved an overall score of 87.51, with its growth performance categorized as "Very High."
- For the third year in a row, Fast Company recognized Lenovo among its annual Best Workplaces for Innovators list. The Group was named as a finalist in both the Best Workplaces for Innovators: AI, Automation and Machine Learning Excellence and Best Workplaces for Innovators: North America categories.
- Lenovo has been recognized as a World's Top Disability Inclusive business through the Disability Index, the world's leading benchmarking tool for measuring and advancing disability inclusion in business.
- Tech World, Lenovo's annual global innovation event, will return to CES 2027 in Las Vegas. Hosted at Sphere and part of the CES Keynote lineup, Tech World will bring together a visionary lineup of speakers and breakthrough innovations with a first-of-its-kind immersive technology and music experience.

articles.title: Pakistan undersea cable fault causes internet failure near Strait of Hormuz — fault detected offshore weeks after Iran threatened infrastructure in the region
articles.text:
Pakistan undersea cable failure causes internet outage near Strait of Hormuz — fault detected offshore weeks after Iran threatened infrastructure in the region
Pakistan's telecommunications authority says that Transworld Associates is looking into what caused the issue and when it expects it to be fixed, but traffic has been rerouted for now.
Pakistan's telecommunications authority, the PTA, has confirmed that internet connectivity issues affecting the country's residents are related to the failure of an international submarine cable. SEA-ME-WE 5 is located almost seven miles off the coast of Pakistan, near the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz, and connects the region with European networks via the Middle East. The TWA says that the outage may have caused intermittent connectivity issues and a decline in service quality, with Transworld Associates (TWA) working to identify the cause of the issue. No timeframe has been provided for when a fix will be available yet, but for now, internet traffic has been rerouted to minimize the impact of the outage.
The outage comes weeks after the Islamic Republic of Iran described several undersea fiber cables that run through the Strait of Hormuz as "legitimate new targets" in the ongoing tensions in the area. February's start of military action by the United States, Israel, and others has made the Strait of Hormuz a household name in recent months. General Hossein Mohebbi, a spokesman for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, pointed out that as many as seven "large cables pass beneath the Strait of Hormuz, and all internet and commercial data pass through them," going on to say they are "legitimate" targets for the group.
Notably, the SEA-ME-WE 5 cable does run through the Strait of Hormuz, although it should be stressed that there is currently no indication that this outage was caused by any act of sabotage. However, that is no doubt something that the TWA investigation will seek to confirm before it can apply whatever fix is necessary to fully restore services for those in the region.
Undersea cables are vital for maintaining connectivity between nations and continents, and Iran isn't the only one to have taken note. A Russian ship was chased from British waters by a Royal Navy attack helicopter earlier this year after it was found less than a mile from five undersea cables. The ship was in the area for 14 hours, and the cables it was near happened to connect the UK with Spain, Portugal, Canada, and the United States.

articles.title: Karnataka aims to raise its share in aerospace, defence sector to 75 per cent: Minister
articles.text:
Karnataka aims to raise its share in aerospace, defence sector to 75%: Minister
Industries Minister M B Patil said that the government is ready to support the creation of all necessary infrastructure and facilities, including Common Facility Centres, to facilitate investments in the aerospace sector.
Karnataka aims to increase its share of the country's aerospace and defence sector from 65% to 75% by attracting investment and strengthening infrastructure, Industries Minister MB Patil said on Thursday.
Addressing AeroConnect 2026, organised by the Aerospace India Association, he said the state government was inviting investors to explore opportunities in the sector and would extend all necessary support for infrastructure development, including establishing Common Facility Centres (CFCs).
"The government is ready to support the creation of all necessary infrastructure and facilities, including Common Facility Centres, to facilitate investments in the aerospace sector," Patil said in a release.
He added that Chief Minister DK Shivakumar was also keen on promoting investments in the sector.
Highlighting Karnataka's infrastructure and connectivity, Patil said the state has international airports in Bengaluru and Mangaluru, as well as airports in Shivamogga, Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi and Mysuru.
The airport at Vijayapura was ready for inauguration, while airport development projects in Hassan, Raichur and other places were progressing, he said.
Describing Karnataka as a major destination for aerospace and defence industries, the minister said the government had introduced a new Aerospace and Defence Policy for the next five years, with an investment target of Rs 60,000 crore.
"Karnataka currently accounts for 65 per cent of the country's aerospace and defence sector, and our aim is to increase this share to 75 per cent," he said.
The state offered a conducive business environment for aerospace and defence industries and had constituted a dedicated Vision Group to promote the sector, Patil added.

articles.title: iPhone Air 2 : Apple pourrait faire l'impasse sur une amélioration pourtant attendue
articles.text:
Sorti en septembre 2025, l’iPhone Air n’a pas vraiment rencontré le succès escompté, notamment en raison d’un prix assez élevé (1 229 €) et de performances photo peu convaincantes. Quoi qu’il en soit, Apple prépare son successeur et espère bien que le succès soit cette fois-ci pleinement au rendez-vous. Des rumeurs font notamment état d’un changement de design, avec un appareil encore plus fin et, enfin, un second capteur photo.
En théorie, cette nouvelle génération devrait aussi gagner en puissance. Des améliorations qui, si elles sont confirmées, sont plutôt enthousiasmantes. Mais une nouvelle information rapportée par le média ETNews pourrait venir quelque peu refroidir cet enthousiasme. Pour cause, l’iPhone Air 2 conserverait les mêmes caractéristiques d’écran que son prédécesseur.
L’iPhone Air 2 pourrait ne pas bénéficier d’améliorations au niveau de son écran
La raison ? L’entreprise à la pomme pourrait ainsi utiliser ses stocks de dalles OLED existants. Nous le savons, Apple recycle certaines de ses puces, et il semble que cela soit aussi le cas pour certains de ses écrans.
Samsung Display, le fournisseur exclusif de dalles OLED pour l’iPhone Air 2, aurait ainsi reçu peu de commandes de la part d’Apple, qui se sert en premier lieu dans ses stocks. Notons également que Samsung devrait commencer la production de ces dalles OLED en janvier, afin de permettre à Apple de lancer l’iPhone Air 2 au printemps 2027.
Apple aurait mobilisé la chaîne de production de l’iPhone Air pour fabriquer l’iPhone des 20 ans
Selon les informations du leaker Fixed Focus Digital, Apple aurait mobilisé une partie de la chaîne de production de l’iPhone Air pour lancer la production du téléphone célébrant les 20 ans de l’iPhone. L’entreprise à la pomme aurait ainsi réutilisé et adapté certains équipements initialement développés pour la fabrication de l’iPhone Air afin de produire les composants en verre de son futur iPhone d’anniversaire. Pour rappel, l’iPhone des 20 ans devrait être « principalement en verre, incurvé et sans aucune découpe dans l’écran », selon Mark Gurman, journaliste de Bloomberg.

articles.title: La agencia migratoria ICE paga a AT&T por acceder a registros de llamadas sin aprobación de un juez
articles.text:
El Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas de Estados Unidos (ICE) paga a la operadora AT&T para que sus analistas revisen datos telefónicos en bruto en una amplia variedad de investigaciones. Lo reveló 404 Media a partir de un documento interno de ICE. Especialistas en privacidad lo describen como un programa de vigilancia masiva.
El documento, obtenido mediante un pedido de acceso a información pública, dice que el contrato da a ICE “acceso a los datos en bruto de AT&T y a analistas con experiencia”. Los analistas convierten esos datos a un formato utilizable para las investigaciones de Seguridad Nacional (HSI, por su sigla en inglés), la rama de ICE que investiga delitos.
Los registros públicos de contratación indican que ICE pagó a AT&T más de USD 2,1 millones en 2025 y más de USD 2,2 millones en agosto de este año. El contrato puede superar los USD 10 millones en los próximos años, según 404 Media.
El texto sostiene que en el año fiscal 2025 aumentó la demanda de estos datos y que se prevé “un nuevo aumento significativo”. También afirma que AT&T es el único proveedor con acceso a sus propios datos: si la empresa no hace el análisis, “la capacidad se perderá”.
Un servicio heredero del programa Hemisphere
El servicio se llama Data Analytical Services. Según un documento que obtuvo la oficina del senador Ron Wyden, antes se llamaba Hemisphere, un programa que The New York Times reveló en 2013. En él, empleados de AT&T trabajaban junto a agentes antidrogas y les daban datos telefónicos que se remontaban a 1987.
Las autoridades dijeron que dejaron de financiar Hemisphere en septiembre de 2024 y que lo cerraron. Para Christopher Soghoian, experto en vigilancia que trabajó una década con Wyden, el nuevo contrato demuestra que la Casa Blanca de Joe Biden engañó al Congreso cuando aseguró que el programa había terminado.
Según documentos obtenidos antes por las organizaciones EFF y EPIC, el programa contiene más de un billón de registros telefónicos. Entre sus funciones figuran vincular varios aparatos o números a un mismo objetivo, detectar cambios de tarjeta SIM y saber si teléfonos de un objetivo internacional entraron en Estados Unidos.
Una citación que no pasa por un juez
AT&T dijo a 404 Media que entrega la información cuando recibe una orden legal válida. Los expertos señalan que basta una citación administrativa, que las propias agencias emiten sin autorización de un juez. Para Jeramie Scott, abogado de la organización EPIC, es un servicio de vigilancia que probablemente evita la supervisión judicial.
Scott añadió que, según su análisis, ICE no habría hecho una evaluación previa del impacto sobre la privacidad. También recordó que la Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos exigió una orden judicial para obtener datos de ubicación de teléfonos en el caso Carpenter, y planteó si el programa cumple esa jurisprudencia.
Wyden afirmó que el gobierno de Donald Trump creó “una versión zombi” de Hemisphere y se la entregó a ICE. Según el senador, los estadounidenses se indignarán al saber que AT&T permite buscar en los registros de sus clientes sin orden judicial ni supervisión.
El alcance puede ir más allá de los clientes de AT&T. Soghoian explicó que la compañía presta servicio mayorista a otras operadoras para completar llamadas, por lo que puede guardar y analizar registros de usuarios de otras empresas, incluso de conversaciones entre dos personas que no son clientes suyas. Por eso, dijo, los usuarios no pueden protegerse cambiando de operadora.
Un portavoz de AT&T respondió que la empresa debe entregar información a las fuerzas de seguridad cuando una orden legal lo exige y que verifica que cada pedido sea válido. ICE no contestó a las consultas de 404 Media, pero había dicho antes al Financial Times: “Nada nuevo aquí”.
El registro del contrato en el portal federal USAspending indica que corre hasta el 31 de agosto de 2027 y que puede extenderse hasta el 31 de agosto de 2030.

articles.title: The Game Awards 2026: No PlayStation title nominated for Game of the Year for the first time since 2014
articles.text:
Facepalm: Six nominees for Game of the Year 2026 were announced this week, and for the first time since 2014, Sony Interactive Entertainment does not have a single title on the list. The snub ends the company's 11-year nomination streak that began in 2015 with the critically acclaimed RPG Bloodborne.
The six nominees shortlisted for 2026's Game of the Year are 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto VI, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem, and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Voting is currently open on the official Game Awards website, with the ceremony scheduled to be held on December 10.
The Game Awards will be handed out in 24 categories, including several popular genres, such as Action, Action-Adventure, RPG, Fighting, SIM/Strategy, Sports/Racing, and Family, among others. Other major categories include Best Performance, Best Independent Game, Best Adaptation, Innovation in Accessibility, and Most Anticipated Game. You can check out the complete list of nominees here.
The lack of an in-house PlayStation title in the GOTY shortlist is a bit of a surprise, given that Sony had at least one nominee every year since 2015, winning with God of War in 2018, The Last of Us: Part 2 in 2020, and Astro Bot in 2024. The company also had two GOTY nominees in 2022 - God of War Ragnarok and Horizon Forbidden West - but neither won.
Several other Sony titles have also been nominated for GOTY over the past 11 years, including Uncharted 4: A Thief's End in 2016, Horizon Zero Dawn in 2017, Death Stranding in 2019, Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart in 2021, Marvel's Spider-Man 2 in 2023, and Death Stranding 2: On the Beach in 2025.
Since the nominees were announced, some gamers have expressed surprise that no Sony title made the GOTY shortlist despite several new launches, including God of War: Sons of Sparta, Marathon, MLB The Show 26, Saros, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, and Marvel's Wolverine.
Several of these games, such as Wolverine, received mixed reviews, but some gamers still hoped that either Saros or Marvel Tokon would make the cut, considering both received positive responses from players and reviewers alike. That said, a nomination for either was always unlikely, given how stacked this year's field was.
The Game Awards 2026 will be held on December 10 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. It will be livestreamed on Disney+ from 7:30 pm ET. Disney also revealed that it is creating new animated content leveraging popular game IPs, including a new original series called Death Stranding Isolations based on the popular action-adventure title. It will air on Hulu in the US and on Disney+ globally.

articles.title: An engineer didn't message his AI for 22 of 44 days. It built an Android app anyway.
articles.text:
An engineer didn’t message his AI for 22 of 44 days. It built an Android app anyway.
Cognition has spent nearly three years developing Devin as an autonomous engineer that takes a ticket and ships a pull request.
With Tuesday’s launch of Devin Bots, the company is moving into management, introducing persistent agents that oversee multiple Devin coding sessions, and take responsibility for engineering outcomes over days or weeks.
Coordination becomes the product
CEO Scott Wu argues that eliminating even a small amount of remaining human work could produce outsized productivity gains. In a post on X, he asks how much more developers could accomplish if coding agents went from handling 98% of their work to 99%, and says Cognition had seen enormous differences among beta testers and internal teams.
The percentages are hypothetical, but Wu is making the case that coordination, not just coding, is the next opportunity for automation.
From tickets to targets
Cognition founding team member Silas Alberti described the change in a post on X as a move toward assigning agents ongoing goals instead of individual tasks. He says the team has already used Devin Bots to compress weeks of research into days.
The company shares the example of keeping an Android app in sync with its iOS version. As new features are added to iOS, a Devin Bot can assign the corresponding Android work without an engineer having to create a ticket for every update.
The idea builds on a trend toward coding agents that function as team members. Devin Bots takes that a step further by putting an agent in charge of coordinating the work.
An Android app, barely supervised
When the company set out to build an Android version of Devin, it had no dedicated Android engineers. Instead, the company assigned the project to a Devin Bot on September 28 and let it coordinate the coding work.
Over the next 44 days, Cognition says the Bot merged 1,134 pull requests, wrote 344,651 lines of Kotlin and closed 1,217 tickets. It also ran 2,841 screenshot tests. The engineer overseeing the project sent 183 messages during that period, including none on 22 of those days.
In its write-up, Cognition explains that the Bot opened tickets and assigned them to individual Devin sessions, then merged changes once they passed continuous integration and Devin Review. The team could follow along through daily Slack updates that included screen recordings. The Android app is now in open testing on Google Play, though it still needs work before it matches the iOS version.
Cognition’s Layout Bot checks the company’s web app for visual bugs every three hours, rebuilds the latest production code, and tests the interface under different loading conditions. Engineers merged 159 of its fixes over three weeks, reducing layout lag by 70%, according to Cognition.
Cognition says the studio went from producing around 50 pull requests a week to 1,900.
A mobile game studio also has roughly 20 bots reporting to another agent named Super Jenny. Four times a day, Super Jenny brings decisions to a human operator. Cognition says the studio went from producing around 50 pull requests a week to 1,900.
Where oversight runs thin
Multiple coding agents working on the same project can introduce conflicting dependencies or bugs that affect other agents’ work. Cognition hasn’t explained how Devin Bots handle those conflicts.
Tasks requiring approval go to a “Needs You” inbox for an engineer to review.
Developers can protect specific CI checks and set compute spending limits before assigning a project to a Bot. Tasks requiring approval go to a “Needs You” inbox for an engineer to review. The company hasn’t disclosed how the supervising Bot decides when code is ready to merge or when repeated failures warrant human intervention.
Code verification remains another concern when agents write tests for their own implementations. Agent-generated pull requests are already putting pressure on conventional code review pipelines, and some teams are developing independent verification loops to catch errors that the original coding agent might miss.
The New Stack has asked Cognition for more information about how Devin Bots coordinate parallel agents, evaluate completed work and determine when human intervention is necessary.
Cognition hasn’t disclosed how much engineering time was spent reviewing the Bots’ pull requests or fixing failed implementations.

articles.title: Global cloud availability sets neocloud platforms apart - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Agentic AI pushes the neocloud race beyond GPU counts toward global platforms
The neocloud boom is entering a sorting phase, and global cloud availability is emerging as the line between providers built for enterprise AI and those built to rent out racks of graphics processing units.
With agentic AI moving from pilots into production, buyers are looking past raw GPU counts toward integrated platforms they can build on. That shift is redrawing the competitive map for cloud AI infrastructure. Enterprise practitioners are now starting ambitious agentic AI agendas, and they need the full stack of services behind AI-native applications rather than standalone clusters, according to Kevin Cochrane (pictured, right), chief marketing officer of Vultr.
“There are those providers that are trusted platforms, that are global cloud platforms that have the totality of services that are required for real agentic AI deployments,” Cochrane said. “We’ll continue to see a separation of the pack and there’ll be those that are trusted platforms that enterprises can rely on and there’ll be those that aren’t.”
Cochrane and Duncan Ng (left), vice president of solutions engineering at Vultr, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed why agentic AI is reviving demand for central processing units, how Vultr builds data centers as integrated systems and which neocloud providers are likely to survive consolidation. (* Disclosure below.)
Global cloud availability separates platforms from GPU islands
Calling a service an enterprise cloud takes more than racking accelerators. Vultr organizes its footprint into data center regions, each of which can control multiple facilities on one network. Developers get one application programming interface they can hook into a Terraform template, Cochrane explained. Many rivals, by contrast, stood up individual sites quickly to serve bespoke customer contracts.
“In traditional neoclouds, the data centers are actually islands. They’re not connected. It’s not one unified global network. It’s not one unified global platform,” Cochrane said. “These are like individual data centers stood up very quickly for bespoke customer contract. That is not a platform.”
Agentic AI is also reshaping the hardware mix inside those regions. Reasoning models now let agents chain dozens of steps, call tools and validate results in flight — work that leans heavily on CPUs, according to Ng. Vultr ran a cloud for more than a decade before the GPU rush and has used processors from Advanced Micro Devices Inc. as the backbone of its CPU fleet for several years, he added. The company has since extended that partnership to accelerators with a $1.2 billion order for AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems.
“This increased density, this increased usage — these are just new hosting companies,” Ng said. “This is just a new application that is 10 times more compute dense than the last that we’re trying to sell to.”
Enterprises are finally moving those workloads out of pilot and into production, Ng noted. One Big Four global systems integrator uses Vultr as the substrate for a risk management service. Vultr has been rolling out platform upgrades aimed at enterprise agentic AI to support that kind of deployment.
“What they’re doing is something that used to take consulting hours, people poring through spreadsheets and poring through invoices, poring through declarations,” he said. “They now are able to automate significant portions of this to serve a larger number of their customers and do a deeper dive into their risk supply chains.”

articles.title: Meta's new Muse Charm device may cost $300 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta plans to charge $300 for Muse Charm, its upcoming Tamagotchi-like AI device that was teased at the company’s Connect event earlier this year, The Information has reported.
When reached for comment by TechCrunch, a Meta spokesperson didn’t deny the claims, merely providing the following statement: “We’re charmed by the interest in our AI devices, and we’ll have more to share soon.”
So far, Meta has made a relatively successful push into consumer AI, launching Muse — its agentic helper — along with a variety of cute avatars that users can use to give the system more of a personality.
Muse Charm, the company’s push into AI hardware, will allow users to carry a physical personification of its software around in their pocket (or potentially wear it around their neck), talking to it, asking it questions, and giving it commands.
It remains to be seen whether customers will bite or not. AI wearables have had a rough go of it so far (here’s looking at you, Humane Ai pin), but companies continue to iterate on the concept in an attempt to break through to a broader audience.
Indeed, $300 is arguably a pretty steep price for a product the size of a keychain, although it’s also a price point that’s in line with what other companies have been charging. The wearable launched by Friend — the AI startup whose device lets you text and talk to an AI persona — is currently retailing for $250. On the other hand, Amazon’s all-new Bee Frontier wearable AI device — which transcribes conversations and tracks tasks — lists for $75 and is currently on a Black Friday, 30% off sale of $52.49. Even with its $99/year subscription to let it tie into a user’s apps (photos, emails, etc.), it’s still far less expensive than Muse Charm.

articles.title: Google turns to Blue Origin for a rocket, but its long-term problem remains
articles.text:
Blue Origin announced Thursday that its New Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company’s Project Suncatcher program.
Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research “moonshots.” The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy.
“Project Suncatcher is a long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit,” said Travis Beals, senior director of Project Suncatcher at Google, in the news release. “This dedicated launch with Blue Origin represents a crucial milestone on our roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what’s possible for the future of compute.”
Catching a ride while they still can
The announcement comes as US commercial heavy lift rockets, including New Glenn, are filling up their capacity through the year 2030. The Google mission will fly on the 7×2 variant of the New Glenn rocket, the smaller version of the vehicle that has launched three times to date.
The purpose of the 2029 launch will likely be to test the ability to network solar-powered satellites equipped with AI chips and demonstrate machine-learning compute in space. In that sense, it will be a technology demonstration. Google did not say who it was contracting with to build the satellites, which may weigh something on the order of several tons.
Perhaps the bigger question for Google is not whether it can make this technology work—but whether it is tenable for a company to have ambitions for a large constellation of orbital data centers in the 2030s without its own launch vehicle.
Need for super cheap launch
There remain a lot of questions about the economic viability of orbital data centers, but almost everyone agrees on one universal truth: Without ultra low-cost, heavy lift capability, there is no way that data centers in space can be economically competitive with terrestrial data centers.

articles.title: Ubisoft unveils new GenAI subsidiary after laying off nearly 200 Canadians
articles.text:
Ubisoft has founded a generative AI (GenAI) subsidiary called MotherBrain.
The company confirmed the new division alongside its latest earnings release. In the report, the French gaming giant notes that MotherBrain will serve as a “dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation, supporting all game creators in developing groundbreaking experiences.” Game File first reported on the existence of MotherBrain in September.
The timing of this reveal, however, is particularly questionable, given that Ubisoft just laid off 166 employees in Quebec. That comes amid a major restructuring that has seen multiple studios close, including Ubisoft Halifax and Winnipeg, and other layoffs as part of wider cost-cutting measures. Overall, the company’s headcount dropped by about 1,100 people between April and September alone.
Meanwhile, Ubisoft has shown no signs of slowing down with GenAI. Over the past few years, the company has touted all of the ways it’s been experimenting with the technology, from background dialogue writing to an experience called Teammates that focuses on deeper interactions with NPCs.
Naturally, though, Ubisoft pushing for GenAI while axing many of its staff certainly isn’t a great look. While the company has said all of these AI endeavours are meant to support developers, not replace them, that’s always going to be a legitimate concern, especially for a company that’s looking to cut significant costs.

articles.title: Silicon Motion demos SM8466 PCIe 6.0 SSD controller, expected to ship by 2028 — controller boasts improved quality of service, samples imminent
articles.text:
Silicon Motion demos SM8466 PCIe 6.0 SSD controller, expected to ship by 2028 — controller boasts improved quality of service, samples imminent
SM8466 taped out, sampling imminent.
Silicon Motion is showing off its PCIe 6.0 SSD controller for data center applications for the first time at the SC26 conference in Chicago. The final iteration of Silicon Motion's SM8466 controller was taped out recently, and drives based on the chip are due in late 2027 or early 2028. However, the new controller also has a secret weapon designed to ensure consistent performance of SSDs under concurrent workloads that may set it apart from competitors.
The new controller
Silicon Motion introduced its high-end MonTitan SM8466 enterprise SSD controller designed for next-generation data center and hyperscale storage applications at FMS 2025. The controller features a PCIe 6.x x4 host interface and 16 NAND channels to enable sequential transfer speeds of up to 28 GB/s, random performance of up to 7 million 4K IOPS, and capacities of up to 512 TB and beyond as newer 3D NAND devices emerge. Just like other high-end data center-grade SSD controllers released in recent years, the SM8466 complies with NVMe 2.0 and OCP NVMe 2.5 SSD specifications.
To improve performance and reduce latency, Silicon Motion has developed its Separate Command Architecture (SCA), which separates command and address transmission paths within the NAND interface to improve parallelism and increase effective throughput. Additionally, the controller supports Silicon Motion's 2nd Generation PerformaShape technology, which enables programmable performance limits and predictable quality of service (QoS) across concurrent workloads, which is arguably its most important differentiator against rivals who rely on different methods of guaranteeing performance.
In addition to its performance chops, the MonTitan SM8466 incorporates advanced error correction, virtualization, data protection, and security features. The controller's error correction engine supports low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with 4KiB codewords and Silicon Motion's 16KiB Collaborative Codeword (CoCo) technology to improve data integrity and reliability with advanced NAND flash memory. The controller also supports Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV), MPF virtualization, SMART diagnostics, and comprehensive data protection mechanisms. Security capabilities include Secure Boot, AES-256 encryption, TCG Opal compatibility, and firmware attestation. Together, these features make the SM8466 suitable for high-capacity data center drives that are expected to deliver high performance, predictable latency, and reliable operation under demanding data center workloads.
The tactical advantage
Silicon Motion's 2nd Generation PerformaShape technology builds upon the original PerformaShape architecture introduced with the company's PCIe 5.0-based MonTitan SM8366 enterprise SSD controller several years ago. The 1st Generation implementation uses dedicated hardware accelerators and two-stage leaky-bucket regulators to control read and write performance in terms of IOPS and throughput, both for individual workloads and for the SSD as a whole. This approach enables data center operators to prevent one workload from monopolizing SSD resources at the expense of others.
PerformaShape 2 retains these capabilities but doubles the number of supported quality-of-service (QoS) sets from 256 to 512 and introduces more sophisticated performance controls to accommodate a larger number of concurrent workloads with different requirements. One of the key additions to PerformaShape 2 is Multi-Dimensional Shaping, which enables the controller to coordinate performance limits across multiple I/O characteristics rather than enforce each limit independently. This gives data center operators greater flexibility when allocating SSD resources among applications with different performance requirements.
Another important enhancement of PerformaShape 2 is support for NVMe TP4176, a proposed extension to the NVMe specification that aims to standardize performance management and QoS controls. Whereas the original PerformaShape relies on Silicon Motion's vendor-specific NVMe commands and a dedicated host driver, TP4176 could eventually enable compatible host software to configure performance policies through a standardized mechanism. The technology is particularly relevant for cloud environments where SSDs serve numerous virtual machines, containers, and applications whose storage requirements can change considerably over time, according to the company.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Wird GTA 6 das Gaming verändern? Wahrscheinlich kaum - aber andere Branchen dafür schon
articles.text:
Wird GTA 6 das Gaming verändern? Wahrscheinlich kaum – aber andere Branchen dafür schon
Bei diesem Hype, diesen Wertungen und dieser Rezeption sollte man meinen, dass Gaming nach Grand Theft Auto 6 ein komplett anderes sein wird, als vorher. Und tatsächlich: GTA 6 ist natürlich ein sehr gutes Spiel. Es ist in vielen Aspekten sogar ein beeindruckendes Spiel. Aber wird es das Gaming verändern? Werden Videospiele zukünftig mehr wie GTA 6 sein? Daran kann man begründete Zweifel haben. Doch andere Branchen werden sich das Spiel wahrscheinlich genau ansehen.
Rockstars Open-World-Formel
Es gibt sie, diese Spiele, die eine Art Zäsur sind. Demon’s Souls, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Minecraft, um nur einige zu nennen. Spiele, die Entwickler:innen und Studios beeinflusst haben. Die etwa neue Spielmechaniken einführten, Gameplay-Möglichkeiten neu ausloteten oder Genres neu definierten. Es sind Veröffentlichungen, bei denen man in der Rückschau, einige Jahre später, sehen kann: Da hat ein Wandel eingesetzt.
Grand Theft Auto war auch so ein Spiel – mit dem dritten Teil, der 2001 erschien. Dieses Spiel hat neu definiert, wie eine Open World funktioniert, und viele andere Games danach haben – mal mehr, mal weniger erfolgreich – versucht, sich dieses Muster zu eigen zu machen. Seitdem sind die Teile der GTA-Reihe aber iterativ. Sie bauen auf dem auf, was die Vorgänger schon geschaffen haben.
Rockstar hat eine Open-World-Formel, die freilich sehr gut ist und hervorragend funktioniert, die das Studio aber eben schon vor vielen Jahren geschaffen hat. GTA 6 ist die Kulmination dieser vielen Jahre. Es baut deutlich auf dem 2013 erschienenen GTA 5 ebenso wie auf Red Dead Redemption 2 von 2018 auf und macht alles noch größer, immersiver und detaillierter. Freilich nimmt das Spiel auch einige neue Spielmechaniken hinzu, wie etwa die Möglichkeit, Beziehungen zwischen Charakteren zu pflegen (oder zu versauen). Aber das mag neu für GTA 6 sein – neu fürs Gaming ist es nicht.
GTA 6 dürfte also schon deshalb das Gaming als solches nicht stark verändern, weil das schon die Vorgänger gemacht haben. Und der aktuelle Teil gameplaytechnisch nichts radikal neu oder anders macht, sondern auf dem aufbaut, was schon da war.
GTA 6 muss man sich leisten können
Spätestens mit Grand Theft Auto 5 hat die GTA-Reihe einen Umfang und wird mit einem Aufwand entwickelt, mit dem sich kaum ein Studio messen kann. Mit GTA 6 hat Rockstar Games das nochmal bei weitem überboten. Kein Videospiel hatte bisher ein so großes Budget – über eine Milliarde US-Dollar sollen es gewesen sein. Die Entwicklung hat, inklusive der Vorproduktion, die kurz nach der Veröffentlichung von GTA 5 begonnen haben dürfte, über zehn Jahre gedauert. Und zu Spitzenzeiten sollen 4.711 Menschen an diesem Spiel gearbeitet haben – einige davon anscheinend unter schlechten Bedingungen.
Möglich gemacht hat das zu einem großen Teil, neben den reinen Verkaufserlösen von GTA 5 und Red Dead Redemption 2, auch GTA Online. Der Live-Service von Rockstar Games, der im Oktober 2013 startete und bis heute jedes Jahr Umsatz in dreistelliger Millionenhöhe macht. Ohne ein so erfolgreiches GTA Online hätte Rockstar wohl kaum so viel Zeit und Geld investieren können, um GTA 6 zu entwickeln. Es ist auch davon auszugehen, dass ein Online-Modus für GTA 6 nicht sehr lange auf sich warten lassen wird – allein schon, um die Investoren nicht zu beunruhigen.
Rockstar ist in der Gaming-Branche also die absolute Ausnahme. Es kann zu großen Teilen einfach nicht nachgeahmt werden. Vielmehr kann der Gaming-Markt überhaupt nur wenige Spiele in dem Ausmaß von GTA 6 tragen. Denn die Zeit (und auch das Geld) von Gamern ist begrenzt und ein dermaßen gigantisches Spiel wie GTA 6 braucht enorme Verkäufe, um lukrativ zu sein. Das funktioniert jetzt auch, weil Gamer eben 13 Jahre auf einen Nachfolger warten mussten, nicht 13 Monate.
Bezüglich des Gameplays und auch des schieren Ausmaßes der Produktion dürfte GTA 6 das Gaming als solches also deutlich weniger beeinflussen, als es aktuell dank des gigantischen Hypes den Eindruck macht. Interessant dürfte hingegen zu beobachten sein, ob Rockstar mit Grand Theft Auto 6 die Branche in Bezug auf künstliche Intelligenz beeinflussen wird.
Weniger in Bezug auf die Ingame-KI, also die künstliche Intelligenz im Spiel, die etwa die NPCs (nicht spielbare Charaktere), den Verkehr oder auch Veränderungen innerhalb der Spielwelt steuert. Auch hier hat Rockstar mit seiner hauseigenen Spiel-Engine RAGE (Rockstar Advanced Game Engine) ein Alleinstellungsmerkmal, das nicht einfach so kopiert werden kann.
Der Wert des Handgemachten
Vielmehr geht es um den Einsatz von KI in der Spieleproduktion. Rockstar Games und die Muttergesellschaft Take-Two Interactive haben mehrfach beteuert, für die Produktion von GTA 6 gänzlich darauf verzichtet zu haben. Wie weit dieser Verzicht genau geht, ist zwar kaum nachzuvollziehen, denn inzwischen hat so ziemlich jedes Programm zur Entwicklung von Videospielen integrierte KI-Tools. Doch zumindest soll keine generative KI zum Einsatz gekommen sein, so sagt es Strauss Zelnick, CEO von Take-Two Interactive:
“Was im Speziellen GTA 6 betrifft, so spielt generative KI bei der Entwicklung durch Rockstar Games absolut keine Rolle. Ihre Spielwelten sind von Hand gestaltet – genau das zeichnet sie aus. Sie entstehen von Grund auf: Gebäude für Gebäude, Straße für Straße, Viertel für Viertel. Sie sind nicht prozedural generiert – und das sollen sie auch gar nicht sein. Genau das macht großartige Unterhaltung aus.”
Das ist natürlich ein Statement. In einer Zeit, in der immer mehr Spielestudios verlauten lassen, wie hilfreich KI für sie ist – und tausende Entwickler und Entwicklerinnen deswegen bereits ihren Job verloren haben. Gleichzeitig macht ein (zumindest lauter und sichtbarer) Teil der Gaming-Community noch immer sehr deutlich, dass sie generative KI in der Games-Entwicklung ablehnen. Es kommt regelmäßig zu Boykottaufrufen, wenn herauskommt, dass etwa Artwork oder Voice Acting von KI übernommen wurde.
Wenn Publisher und Studio betonen, dass die Welt von GTA 6 ganz von Hand erstellt wurde und dieser Umstand in der Öffentlichkeit sehr wohlwollend aufgenommen wurde, kann das durchaus Einfluss haben. Womöglich ist GTA 6 dennoch das letzte große Videospiel, das ohne generative KI erstellt wurde. Womöglich hat diese Veröffentlichung aber auch gezeigt, dass das Künstlerische und Originäre in Videospielen noch immer einen Wert hat.
Von Marketing, Filmbranche – und Stadtplanung
In Zeiten, in denen Filmen vorgeworfen wird, dass das generische Skript von einer KI geschrieben wurde, und Unternehmen wie auch Influencer kritisiert werden, wenn sie Bilder und Videos mit KI erstellen, dürfte Rockstars KI-Verzicht in anderen Branchen durchaus für Aufsehen gesorgt haben. GTA 6 fühlt sich auch deshalb so lebendig an und wird so gut besprochen, weil sehr deutlich wird, wie viel Arbeit dahintersteckt – und wie wenig hier von der KI-Stange kommt.
Zudem zeigt das Spiel, wie man erfolgreich einen Hype erzeugt. Freilich hat auch hier die lange Zeit ihren Anteil: Fans warten seit 13 Jahren auf dieses Spiel, das kann man als Unternehmen nicht eben so duplizieren. Doch ist es bemerkenswert, dass Rockstar und Take-Two Interactive das Interesse trotz diverser Verschiebungen immer weiter steigern konnten – und zwar durch eine sehr reduzierte Kommunikation.
Statt großer Versprechungen und wöchentlich neuer Trailer gab es in den Monaten vor dem Release nur wenige ausgesuchte Werbemaßnahmen, wie etwa die Kooperation mit Netflix. Die wurden dafür aber direkt zu Events, bei denen viele Millionen Menschen zugeschaut haben. Das große Hypen wurde also in weiten Teilen der Öffentlichkeit überlassen – und die hat es in Form von Medien und Social Media gerne übernommen. Auch das muss man sich freilich leisten können.
Doch auch außerhalb vom Spektakel, von Marketing, Verkaufsrekorden und zuhauf genommenen Urlaubstagen könnte GTA 6 andere Branchen interessieren. Es sind die inneren Werte, die vielen komplexen, auch KI-getriebenen Systeme, die unterhalb der Oberfläche ineinander übergreifen. GTA 6 ist auch eine gigantische Simulation. Eine Welt, in der sich Menschenmassen bewegen, Verkehrsströme fließen und das Wetter sich ständig verändert.
Vielleicht wird GTA 6 so auch etwas dazu beitragen, dass sich unsere reale Welt, unsere Infrastruktur, unsere Städte und Verkehrsnetze verändern. Denn Technologien aus der Gaming-Industrie werden schon seit einiger Zeit auch in Branchen wie der Architektur oder der Stadtplanung eingesetzt, um etwa Staus oder Windzüge zu simulieren. Vielleicht blicken wir also in einigen Jahren zurück und sehen, dass GTA 6 zwar nicht das Gaming selbst radikal verändert hat – aber die Technologie dahinter jetzt für flüssigeren Verkehr sorgt.

articles.title: Amazon Prime India head Abhinav Agarwal steps down after 16 years
articles.text:
Amazon Prime India head Abhinav Agarwal steps down after 16 years
Abhinav Agarwal has been director of product and engineering at Amazon Prime in Bengaluru since October 2021, leading the product, marketing and engineering teams responsible for growing Amazon's Prime programme in India.
Abhinav Agarwal, Director and Head of Amazon Prime India, has left the company after 16 years, saying in a LinkedIn post that his next role will be at the intersection of commerce, logistics and product, with more details to come soon.
"After 16 incredible years, today is my last day at Amazon," Agarwal said in the post on Thursday.
According to his LinkedIn profile, Agarwal has been director of product and engineering at Amazon Prime in Bengaluru since October 2021, leading the product, marketing and engineering teams responsible for growing Amazon's Prime programme in India.
He moved from supply chain to advertising to running Prime during his time at the company. "Not many places let you reinvent yourself that many times without leaving," he said.
Before the Prime role, Agarwal was director of product tech and performance ads in Seattle from April to September 2021, according to his profile. He joined Amazon in September 2010 as a network planning manager.
"At Amazon, you rarely find yourself the smartest person in the room, and that held true for 16 years. To my teams across supply chain, advertising and Prime: thank you for raising the bar every day.
"Like every good book, this one must come to an end. I'm grateful for every chapter. As for what's next, it will be at the intersection of commerce, logistics and product. More on that soon," he wrote.

articles.title: « CRITIQUE » : après le chaos PHP2Shell, PHP alerte sur de nouvelles failles de sécurité
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 18 novembre, l’équipe de sécurité de PHP a de nouveau tiré la sonnette d’alarme. Dans un avis publié sur le site officiel, l’équipe annonce des mises à jour de sécurité pour toutes les versions de PHP toujours prises en charge, à savoir 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 et 8.5. L’avis indique que « la gravité la plus élevée est CRITIQUE ». Des correctifs seront publiés dans l’après-midi du jeudi 19 novembre.
« Les utilisateurs sont vivement encouragés à se préparer à mettre à jour rapidement dès que les versions seront disponibles », insiste l’équipe de PHP, ajoutant que « les détails techniques et les numéros des versions corrigées seront publiés en même temps que les mises à jour ».
À lire aussi : « Improbable et grave » – l’IA a découvert une faille planétaire dans un langage informatique « dont nous dépendons tous »
Une faille moins préoccupante que PHP2Shell
Cette annonce réveille évidemment de mauvais souvenirs. En octobre, deux failles critiques dans PHP, baptisées PHP2Shell, ont en effet semé la panique sur Internet. Découvertes avec l’aide de l’IA, elles permettaient de prendre le contrôle d’un serveur à distance, sans le moindre identifiant. Toutes les équipes de sécurité s’étaient ruées sur les correctifs pour éviter une vague de cyberattaques. De nombreux sites avaient même été coupés par précaution dans le monde entier, plongeant une partie d’Internet dans le noir. Cette fois, PHP se veut un peu plus rassurant, en dépit de la mention « CRITIQUE » dans sa communication.
« Les problèmes classés critiques nécessitent soit une configuration différente de celle par défaut, soit une installation peu courante », précise l’équipe, soucieuse de ne pas semer la panique.
En clair, la grande majorité des sites n’est pas censée être exposée à la faille la plus grave. Contrairement au mois dernier, les développeurs ne doivent pas agir dans l’urgence. Il s’agit en effet d’une mise à jour prévue de longue date, qui fait partie du « cycle régulier de quatre semaines » du projet.
« Une combinaison inhabituelle »
Par ailleurs, l’une des failles corrigées est déjà connue. Révélée dès le 23 octobre, deux jours après PHP2Shell, elle peut permettre à un pirate d’exécuter son propre code sur un serveur, mais seulement dans des conditions très particulières. PHP évoque « une combinaison inhabituelle de configuration et de code applicatif », ce qui laisse penser que la vulnérabilité n’est pas du tout courante. Elizabeth Barron, directrice de la PHP Foundation, juge même l’exploitation de la faille improbable « dans un usage pratique de PHP », rapporte The Register.
Néanmoins, les experts ne prennent pas l’alerte émise par la PHP Foundation à la légère. En effet, l’installation des correctifs dans le code de PHP peut parfois mal tourner. Selon CBS News, les correctifs d’urgence liés à PHP2Shel ont fait planter le réseau interne de la NSA, l’agence américaine de renseignement, le 17 novembre. Jay Clayton, le directeur du renseignement national américain, révèle que « certains systèmes n’ont pas redémarré comme prévu » après la mise à jour de PHP.
Si vous avez un site hébergé chez un prestataire grand public, comme OVHcloud, o2switch ou Hostinger, l’hébergeur installe normalement lui-même les mises à jour de PHP. Par prudence, vérifiez quand même que votre site tourne sur une version récente de PHP(8.2 ou plus), car les versions plus anciennes ne reçoivent plus de correctifs. Les entreprises et les administrateurs qui gèrent leurs propres serveurs doivent installer les nouvelles versions dès leur sortie, puis redémarrer PHP.
