articles.title: Qui est Won-Joon Choi, l’homme du Galaxy S26 et du Z Fold8 qui prend la tête de l’activité smartphone de Samsung ? — Frandroid
articles.text:
Samsung vient d’officialiser ce qu’il démentait encore il y a un an et demi. « TM Roh n’est pas remplacé par Choi Won-joon », assurait l’entreprise au printemps 2025, quand des rumeurs annonçaient un changement de patron pour sa branche mobile. C’est pourtant bien Won-Joon Choi qui prend désormais la tête de Mobile eXperience (MX), la division qui conçoit les smartphones, tablettes et montres Galaxy. Le démenti de l’époque n’était pas un mensonge pour autant, puisque TM Roh ne quitte pas l’entreprise. Il garde simplement une casquette au lieu de deux.
TM Roh (de son nom coréen Roh Tae-moon) dirigeait MX depuis début 2020. Après le décès brutal du co-PDG Han Jong-hee en 2025, il a hérité en plus de la division Device eXperience (DX), qui chapeaute smartphones, TV et électroménager, avant d’être nommé co-PDG fin 2025.
Selon l’annonce officielle de Samsung, il conserve ces deux fonctions, aux côtés de Young Hyun Jun, qui pilote les semi-conducteurs. Won-Joon Choi était depuis le printemps 2025 COO de MX, c’est-à-dire directeur des opérations : en pratique, il gérait déjà le quotidien et a mené les lancements des Galaxy S26 et Z Fold8. Le même remaniement place Sang Joon Hwang, qui dirigeait le développement des DRAM (la mémoire vive des ordinateurs et téléphones) et des HBM (des mémoires empilées indispensables aux puces d’IA), à la tête de toute la branche mémoire, celle qui porte aujourd’hui les bénéfices records du groupe.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
    Pour aller plus loin
Quel smartphone Samsung Galaxy choisir en 2026 ? Nos recommandations par budget
            
Un ingénieur des puces aux commandes des Galaxy
Won-Joon Choi n’a rien d’un homme de marketing. Formé à l’université nationale de Séoul puis à Stanford, il a conçu des puces chez Atheros, spécialiste du Wi-Fi racheté par Qualcomm, avant de rejoindre Samsung en 2016. Il y a dirigé le développement des pliables, puis celui de toute la gamme smartphone, un poste par lequel TM Roh était lui-même passé avant de prendre MX.
Ce parcours tombe bien : selon la presse coréenne, Samsung a rattaché début 2026 son équipe d’architecture SoC à la division mobile. Le SoC, c’est la puce qui réunit processeur, partie graphique et modem, et ceux qui dessinent les futurs Exynos travaillent désormais au plus près de ceux qui conçoivent les Galaxy. De quoi espérer des puces maison mieux taillées pour les smartphones, à la manière d’Apple, même si rien n’est annoncé en ce sens.
Un héritage entre IA, pliables et polémiques
Le bilan que récupère Won-Joon Choi est flatteur sur le papier. Sous TM Roh, Samsung a présenté le Galaxy S24 comme le premier « smartphone IA », et les pliables sont devenus une gamme à part entière, avec plus d’un million de précommandes en Corée pour la série Z7. Le passif existe aussi. En 2022, l’affaire GOS, un service qui bridait les performances des Galaxy S22 dans de nombreuses applications, avait valu à TM Roh une fronde d’actionnaires en assemblée générale. Les Galaxy S successifs sont régulièrement critiqués pour leurs évolutions timides, et le déploiement de One UI 7 a pris des mois de retard.
Pour les propriétaires de Galaxy, rien ne bouge à court terme : TM Roh reste le supérieur direct de son successeur, et le prochain Galaxy S est sans doute déjà largement figé. Ceux qui boudent les versions Exynos ont en revanche une raison de suivre le dossier de près.
Samsung doit annoncer dans les prochains jours les nominations sous le rang de président, dont le nom du nouveau COO de MX. Le prochain Galaxy S, qui devrait arriver début 2027, servira de première vitrine au nouveau patron.
TM Roh devrait de son côté consacrer davantage de temps à la robotique, à la tête d’une nouvelle structure dédiée, selon le Seoul Economic Daily.

articles.text:
Meet the 8 women powering India’s deeptech future; Anthropic raises a record $81.3B in IPO
On Women’s Entrepreneurship Day, we look at women founders pushing the boundaries of Indian deeptech, building frontier technologies, and opening new possibilities for innovation and entrepreneurship.
Dear Reader,
Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion in its IPO, surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion offering and valuing the Claude maker at an estimated $1.5 trillion. The Nasdaq debut comes as rapid revenue growth is accompanied by widening losses, testing how much public-market investors are willing to bet on AI.
The shift is also reshaping the workplace. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has explained the company’s decision to offer buyouts to 60,000 employees, saying it is part of a broader transition to an AI-first organisation—not simply a plan to replace people with technology. He expects employees to direct and manage AI agents, changing how work gets done and teams are structured.
The rapid expansion of AI is also raising concerns about its environmental footprint. According to a new International Energy Agency (IEA) report, carbon emissions from data centres are projected to rise 70% by 2030 as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI ambitions. Data centres are expected to consume twice as much electricity by the end of the decade, with AI accounting for three-quarters of the additional demand.
Meanwhile, six Indian startups have secured places in Hub71’s Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi, having been selected from 10 finalists in the UAE-India Start-Up Series 2.0, which attracted more than 11,000 applications. Working across AI, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and digital finance, the startups will gain access to mentorship, investors and potential partners as they explore the UAE market.

Women founders are building solutions to complex engineering challenges in India. Their ventures are addressing critical gaps across sectors such as energy, healthcare, space and manufacturing. On Women’s Entrepreneurship Day, HerStory spoke to eight founders across seven companies, along with investors, about the opportunities, funding hurdles, and gender-based assumptions shaping women's journeys in deeptech.

articles.title: iPhone 20 Pro : à peine passé à l’aluminium, Apple voudrait déjà revenir au titane
articles.text:
Chez Apple, l’amour d’un matériau dure parfois le temps d’un cycle produit. Après avoir vanté les mérites du titane sur les iPhone 15 Pro et 16 Pro, la firme de Cupertino avait surpris son monde en 2025 en revenant à une coque unibody en aluminium sur l’iPhone 17 Pro et confirmé sur le 18 Pro.
Un choix dicté par la physique : couplé à une nouvelle chambre à vapeur, l’aluminium offrait une bien meilleure conductivité thermique pour maintenir les performances dans la durée. Mais ce pragmatisme a laissé un goût d’inachevé chez certains utilisateurs, nostalgiques du toucher plus noble et de la résistance accrue du titane. Qu’ils se rassurent : à en croire les dernières indiscrétions relayées par MacRumors, la parenthèse aluminium pourrait déjà toucher à sa fin.
Un châssis en titane et des courbes inspirées de l’iPhone Air
L’information émane de Fixed Focus Digital, un leaker actif sur le réseau social chinois Weibo. Selon lui, Apple testerait actuellement des prototypes d’« iPhone 20 Pro » dotés d’un cadre en titane et d’une silhouette nettement plus arrondie. L’informateur compare cette esthétique à celle de l’iPhone Air, mais avec des courbes beaucoup plus prononcées.
Plus tôt dans la semaine, cette même source affirmait déjà que les modèles du 20e anniversaire reprendraient le verre de l’iPhone Air, retravaillé pour s’incurver sur les quatre côtés autour d’une fine bordure métallique polie. Dès le mois d’août, Fixed Focus Digital soutenait d’ailleurs qu’Apple avait adapté les lignes de production de l’iPhone Air pour façonner ces nouvelles pièces en verre.
Ce scénario rejoint très directement les révélations de Mark Gurman. Le journaliste de Bloomberg, lui aussi très bien informé lorsqu’on parle de la firme à la pomme, indiquait récemment que Cupertino préparait des façades avant et arrière en verre s’incurvant sur les tranches autour d’une mince bande métallique. Un compromis retenu après l’abandon en cours de route d’un prototype encore plus radical où le verre remplaçait davantage de métal, avance-t-il.
La plus grosse refonte depuis l’iPhone X, mais deux designs en balance
Aux yeux de Mark Gurman, ce chantier représente tout simplement la plus vaste refonte de la gamme Pro depuis l’iPhone X. Toutefois, l’ampleur exacte de ces nouvelles courbes ferait encore l’objet d’arbitrages en interne.
Le leaker Ice Universe a aussi ajouté son grain de sel. Il assure ainsi qu’Apple planche sur quatre modèles répartis selon deux philosophies : deux appareils équipés d’un verre plat, et deux autres dotés d’un verre incurvé sur les quatre bords.
La firme explorerait cette piste depuis déjà trois ans. Sur les déclinaisons incurvées, les bordures mesureraient environ 1 mm et deviendraient quasi imperceptibles de face grâce à l’effet optique du verre.
Reste à savoir ce qui survivra réellement aux phases de validation industrielle. Les rumeurs portent sur du matériel encore au stade de l’ingénierie préliminaire, laissant la porte ouverte à des ajustements d’ici la commercialisation attendue à l’automne 2027. D’ici là, Apple aura encore tout le temps de trancher sur le matériau final.

articles.title: Waymo ha retirado sus robotaxis de todas las autopistas de Estados Unidos tras el veto de sus vehículos en California
articles.text:
Waymo ha retirado sus taxis sin conductor de las autopistas de todo Estados Unidos, un día después de que el DMV de California (su Departamento de Vehículos Motorizados) prohibiera a la empresa circular por las autovías del estado. De momento, los viajes por las calles de la ciudad continúan con normalidad.
Pausa indefinida. Estados Unidos es el mercado más grande de Waymo actualmente, y se suponía que las autopistas iban a ser el siguiente paso en la expansión de la firma. La empresa puso en marcha los viajes por autopista en el Área de la Bahía de San Francisco hace casi un año, según señala The New York Times. Ahora ese servicio está congelado en todos los lugares donde existía, y Waymo no ha dicho cuándo volverá.
Qué ha pasado. El DMV de California emitió la orden el pasado 11 de noviembre, prohibiendo a Waymo tanto operar como probar vehículos sin conductor en las autopistas estatales. La agencia calificó las operaciones de la empresa como un “peligro inminente para la seguridad pública”, según el portavoz del DMV, Jonathan Groveman, quien se comunicó con el medio The Guardian. Señaló dos incidentes recientes.
Las causas de esto fueron principalmente dos sucesos. El primero el 5 de noviembre, en el que tres vehículos Waymo sin conductor entraron en una zona de obras activa en la ruta 101. En el otro caso, un Waymo intentó rodear vehículos de la Patrulla de Carreteras de California (CHP), los cuales estaban ralentizando deliberadamente el tráfico en la interestatal 280, San Francisco. El suceso se puede ver en un vídeo, habiéndose viralizado en redes.
Lo de Waymo no es nuevo. Groveman describe “incursiones recurrentes” en zonas de obras donde hay trabajadores y maquinaria, y dijo que ya habían ocurrido incidentes similares el 18 de mayo. Y Waymo tiene un buen puñado de antecedentes en este aspecto. En junio, llamó a revisión alrededor de 4.000 robotaxis para realizar actualizaciones de software después de que los coches entraran en zonas de obras en Phoenix y San Francisco, según el NYT. Otra llamada a revisión independiente, en mayo, abarcaba vehículos que podían adentrarse en carreteras inundadas.
La respuesta de Waymo. La empresa dice que el episodio de la ruta 101 no implicó heridos ni colisiones. También decidió ampliar la pausa a nivel nacional. En un comunicado recogido por Ars Technica, dijo que había “restringido temporalmente las operaciones en autopista en nuestros otros mercados operativos para evaluar nuestro rendimiento”. También dijo a The Guardian que las pruebas en autopista continúan con especialistas formados al volante.
Los lugares afectados incluyen el Área de la Bahía, Los Ángeles, Phoenix, Miami y Austin. Waymo afirma que su servicio en calles urbanas no se ve afectado, completando más de medio millón de viajes a la semana.
Velocidad. Las autopistas parecen el entorno más sencillo, ya que no hay peatones, ciclistas ni tráfico transversal, pero la velocidad cambia la ecuación. “Es muy difícil matar a alguien a 25 millas por hora [unos 40 km/h]. Es muy fácil matar a alguien a 65 millas por hora [unos 105 km/h]”, contaba al NYT Matthew Wansley, profesor en la Facultad de Derecho Cardozo de la Universidad Yeshiva.
Y ahora qué. California dice que la prohibición se mantiene hasta que Waymo “demuestre al departamento que ha tomado medidas correctivas eficaces”. No hay un plazo fijado. Waymo dice que está trabajando con autoridades de California y de otros estados para reanudar el servicio en autopista. Sus datos de seguridad, que según afirma muestran un 95 % menos de siniestros con lesiones graves que los conductores humanos, pueden contar poco aquí.

articles.title: Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Amazon SageMaker AI now detects latency drift, idle GPUs, and missed optimizations on your inference endpoints
Every inference endpoint is well tuned the day it goes into production. Teams choose an instance type, serving configuration, and scaling settings that suit the model and its traffic at launch. With the endpoint serving smoothly, they understandably move on to the next priority. The workload, however, rarely stays still. Traffic patterns evolve, prompts grow longer, serving engines such as vLLM ship new releases, SageMaker inference develops new optimization techniques, and new fine-tuned checkpoints change the resources your model needs. Over time, a well-tuned endpoint quietly drifts. Latency and time to first token edge upward. A configuration that was never quite ideal keeps missing available performance gains. A GPU provisioned for demand that never materialized sits idle week after week. Because nothing has failed, no alarm sounds, and the drift goes unnoticed until users feel it or the bill reflects it.
Amazon SageMaker AI now monitors your generative AI inference endpoints and tells you when a change could improve performance or lower cost by using Generative AI optimized inference recommendations feature with Agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker Studio. Monitoring is on by default for SageMaker AI inference endpoints using vLLM serving containers and GPU instances, with no setup required, and you can opt out of endpoints. SageMaker AI looks only at operational signals: latency, GPU utilization, and the endpoint’s serving configuration. It does not read your requests or responses. From those signals, it surfaces three kinds of findings:
- Latency drift: A week-over-week rise in median (p50) end-to-end latency or time to first token.
- Unused capacity: GPUs you pay for that sit mostly idle.
- Configuration gaps: A serving container that’s missing newer performance improvements or security patches, or an optimization such as speculative decoding or GPU kernel tuning that your model supports but the endpoint doesn’t use.
SageMaker AI sends a finding through AWS Health, with one notification per endpoint that covers that endpoint’s findings. When a notification arrives, you can act on it in one place. It opens the SageMaker AI agentic experience in Amazon SageMaker Studio with the endpoint, and its recent traffic already filled in. From there, you run inference recommendations to benchmark your current configuration against alternatives and compare them side by side on response time, throughput, and cost per million tokens. That turns a judgment call into a decision backed by data. Benchmarks run on separate compute, and nothing changes on your endpoint until you choose to apply a result.
In this post, we show how SageMaker AI monitors your endpoints and how to read the notifications it sends through AWS Health. We then show how to go from a notification to a benchmarked decision in SageMaker Studio. We walk through three example scenarios, show how to apply or dismiss a recommendation safely, and explain how to opt an endpoint out of monitoring.
Solution overview
SageMaker AI inference recommendations follow a four-step loop: observe, notify, recommend, and decide. Each step is designed so that you stay in control, and your production endpoint isn’t changed without your explicit action.
- Observe – Monitoring of latency and capacity usage is on by default for eligible endpoints. It doesn’t read your requests or responses, and it carries no additional GPU cost.
- Notify – When there is something worth acting on, you receive a plain language notification in AWS Health, plus email, explaining what was observed, why it matters, and a recommended next step.
- Recommend (opt in) – One selection opens the SageMaker AI agentic experience in SageMaker Studio, prefilled with the endpoint and its observed traffic, so you can benchmark alternatives on separate compute.
- Decide – Compare response time, throughput, and cost side by side. Production is not changed until you apply a result.
The feature produces a few types of findings. The following table summarizes what triggers each one and what gets tested when you choose to benchmark.
| Finding | What triggers it | What a benchmark tests | 
| Latency drift | Response time moves relative to the endpoint’s week-over-week trends | Tensor parallelism settings and alternate instance types or sizes | 
| Underutilized GPUs | GPU utilization stays well below capacity over the window | Cheaper instance types and smaller sizes at observed peak traffic | 
| Speculative decoding not enabled | Model and container support it, but it is off (configuration based) | Current configuration compared to speculative decoding enabled | 
| Serving container | The endpoint’s serving container has a newer version with a performance improvement and security patches for critical and high finding Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). | Current compared to updated container | 
| Untuned GPU kernels | Kernel configuration is not tuned for the model and hardware | Default compared to tuned kernels | 
Prerequisites
Monitoring itself needs no setup, it is on by default. The following prerequisites apply when you choose to act on a finding by running a benchmark and, optionally, applying a change:
- Access to AWS Health and the AWS User Notifications console.
- A SageMaker Studio domain and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to run inference recommendation jobs and update endpoints.
- Sufficient service quota for the benchmark instances you want to test.
Cost note: Monitoring has no GPU cost. Benchmarks use standard SageMaker AI charges, or your machine learning (ML) reservation if you have one.
Understand a finding notification
You receive notifications in AWS Health on the console and by email and each one follows the same structure, so it’s quick to scan:
- Endpoint: Which endpoint the finding applies to.
- What we noticed: The observation, stated plainly, with estimates clearly labeled as estimates.
- Why it matters: The impact on latency, capacity, or cost.
- Recommended action: A single selection into the agentic experience in SageMaker Studio to investigate.
Notifications report observations and label estimates. No benchmark has run at this point. A representative notification reads as follows:
| Subject: [Action may be required] SageMaker AI inference improvements for your endpoint SageMaker AI tracks the latency and capacity usage of your inference endpoints by default, and found improvements for one of them. It does not read your requests or responses. What we noticed: Over the past week, time to first token on this endpoint increased compared with the week before. Recommended action: Open SageMaker Studio to benchmark alternatives on separate compute. Your production endpoint is not changed. | 
Cadence: Each endpoint gets one notification that covers the applicable findings. You get at most one notification per endpoint at a time, covering all its findings, and SageMaker AI limits how many an account receives at once. Notifications are AWS Region specific, so you see an endpoint’s findings when you’re signed in to that endpoint’s Region.
Walkthrough: From notification to decision
In this section, we review a few scenarios of endpoint optimizations that will trigger findings to be reported.
Scenario 1: Catch week-over-week latency regression
A team runs a chat assistant on a single SageMaker AI endpoint. They add retrieval to improve answer quality, so every request now carries pages of retrieved context and prompts get much longer. Nothing breaks, and no alarm they set trips, but responses start more slowly.
SageMaker AI compares the endpoint’s median (p50) time to first token and median end-to-end latency with the previous week. When either one rises enough over the week, it flags the change. Because the comparison is against the endpoint’s own history, the team doesn’t need to set a threshold in advance.
- Notification: AWS Health reports that time to first token increased relative to the prior week.
- Studio session: One selection opens the agentic experience, prefilled with the endpoint and its observed traffic.
- Benchmark: The session tests tensor parallelism settings and other instance types or sizes on separate compute.
- Decision: The team compares latency, throughput, and cost, then applies the winning configuration to one variant.
The following screenshot shows an AWS Health event for a latency drift finding. The message reports that median time to first token rose about 200 ms week over week, and the Recommended actions pane links to SageMaker AI to run inference recommendations.
Scenario 2: Turn on an optimization your traffic can benefit from
A platform team hosts an internal code-completion model on a SageMaker AI endpoint. They deployed it with default serving settings and never revisited them. The model and serving container support speculative decoding, a technique for faster responses, but it isn’t enabled. SageMaker AI flags this as an opportunity. Whether it helps depends on the endpoint’s traffic, such as how many requests run concurrently and how long prompts and responses are. The notification recommends running inference recommendations, which benchmarks speculative decoding against the endpoint’s recent traffic and shows whether it’s worth turning on.
- Notification: AWS Health reports that a technique designed to make responses faster is supported but not enabled.
- Studio session: The agentic experience opens with the endpoint configuration loaded.
- Benchmark: The session compares the current configuration with speculative decoding enabled. Results may differ at peak compared to off-peak traffic.
- Decision: If the gain holds at the traffic that matters, the team applies it. Otherwise, they keep the current configuration.
The following screenshot shows an AWS Health event for a speculative decoding finding. The message reports that the model and serving container support speculative decoding, but the endpoint doesn’t use it. The Recommended actions pane links to SageMaker AI to run inference recommendations.
The notification explains that speculative decoding can make responses faster, and that the benchmark compares response time with and without it on the endpoint’s recent traffic.
Scenario 3: Right-size underutilized GPUs
A summarization endpoint was sized for a launch that drew a fraction of the planned audience, so its GPUs sit mostly idle for a week. This scenario also shows a case where the right decision may be to make no change at all.
- Notification: AWS Health reports that the endpoint paid for GPU capacity that largely went unused.
- Studio session: The agentic experience opens with the endpoint and its observed peak traffic.
- Benchmark: The session tests cheaper instance types and smaller sizes at observed peak traffic.
- Decision: The team weighs the monthly savings against the headroom they want for planned growth and may decide to keep the current size.
The following screenshot shows an AWS Health event for an unused capacity finding. The message reports that for most of the week, even the endpoint’s busiest GPU used 12 percent or less of its capacity. The Recommended actions pane links to SageMaker AI to run inference recommendations.
You can choose Open in SageMaker AI from the recommended actions as shown in the screenshot above to apply or dismiss a recommendation. Lets walk through this in next section.
Apply or dismiss a recommendation
You stay in control throughout, and nothing deploys automatically. When you choose Open in SageMaker AI from a notification’s recommended actions, Amazon SageMaker Studio opens a JupyterLab space and shows the prompt that will run in the agentic chat. The following screenshot shows the prompt for a latency drift finding on an endpoint that also runs an older vLLM serving container:
When you choose Run, the agentic experience opens in a chat panel in JupyterLab space in SageMaker Studio. It summarizes the finding in plain language, restates what you asked it to do, and checks with you before it takes any action. The following screenshot shows the agent summarizing the findings and asking to continue:
After you confirm, the agent generates a notebook that creates an inference recommendation job for the endpoint. The notebook uses the SageMaker Python SDK, takes the model from the endpoint and the traffic profile from its metrics, and tags the job with the AWS Health event so you can trace the results back to the finding. Each step is a separate notebook cell, so you can review or edit it before you run it.
The following screenshot shows the notebook cells that record the job details and start a recommendation job across three candidate instance types.
When the job completes, you can compare your current configuration with the alternatives on response time, throughput, and cost. When you are ready to act on a benchmarked result, we recommend a safe rollout pattern:
- Review the proposed change before applying it, including the configuration difference and the benchmarked latency, throughput, and cost.
- Apply to one production variant first and keep the current configuration available for rollback.
- Holding or dismissing a finding is a normal outcome. The notification stays in your AWS Health event history.
Manage monitoring and notifications
You can manage monitoring and how you are notified:
- Manage how you receive notifications in the AWS User Notifications console.
- Optionally, schedule recurring recommendations, for example monthly.
What is and is not collected: Monitoring reads aggregated latency and capacity telemetry at the endpoint level. It doesn’t read your request or response content, and it carries no GPU cost.
Opting out of monitoring: If you don’t want SageMaker AI to monitor an endpoint, set the OPT_OUT_TRACKING environment variable, with a value of your choice, on the model’s container. You set it in the Environment map when you call CreateModel, either on PrimaryContainer or on another container in the model.
If a container on the endpoint carries this variable, SageMaker AI collects no monitoring telemetry for that endpoint, including engine metrics, GPU metrics, and startup configuration details. As a result, it sends no notifications for that endpoint.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, clean up the resources you created while following this post:
- Delete any test endpoints or resources you created for the walkthrough.
- Remove benchmark artifacts in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), if applicable.
- Revert any test configuration changes you applied.
Conclusion
With SageMaker AI inference recommendations now monitoring your endpoints automatically, optimization moves from a point-in-time snapshot to an ongoing signal.
Your endpoints keep telling you when they have drifted, when they are missing an improvement, or when they are paying for idle capacity. A single selection takes you to a benchmarked, side-by-side decision that you control.
For more information on how to get started, visit Amazon SageMaker AI and see the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation.

articles.title: IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
articles.text:
IDrive wants to back up your coding agents, too
Coding agents need backups, too, or at least that’s what IDrive is arguing.
Backup and storage service IDrive on Thursday announced AI Agents Backup, a feature in its desktop app that finds the data these agents store locally for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Cline and copies it to the user’s IDrive account.
By default, agents tend to keep a lot of their state on a developer’s machine, including session transcripts, instruction files, and MCP server configurations. The problem is that most of this sits in hidden folders that developers rarely look at.
Thing is, some of this data is actually valuable. A session transcript, after all, is a record of how a developer and an agent got to a fix, and this local data also helps agents like Claude Code and Codex pick up from old sessions to continue a task days later. Then, there are the AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files and things like MCP configurations that involve some setup work that few developers will want to have to redo when something goes awry.
As IDrive CEO Raghu Kulkarni notes in the announcement, “Most of that data lives only on the local machine and has been left out of backup plans.” The history and configuration these agents build up, he says, is “a real work product.”
Session history is easily lost
Some of this data is also easy to lose. By default, Claude Code deletes session transcripts older than 30 days. Users have actually filed a long list of GitHub issues about history that disappeared without warning and Cursor’s forum has plenty of threads from users whose chat history disappeared after an update.
What IDrive backs up
For Claude, the new backup feature covers Claude Code history from both the terminal and the desktop app, plus settings, instruction files, and local MCP server configurations. It also picks up Cowork scheduled tasks that Team and Enterprise users chose to keep on their own machine.
The Cursor backup includes chat history, workspace data, keybindings, extensions, and the Cursor Agent CLI’s sessions. Codex and Cline get similar treatment.
It’s worth noting that IDrive skips caches and temporary files. It also doesn’t back up source code and repositories, because the company expects users to protect them with its regular file backup. Any chats that live on a provider’s servers are also out of bounds.
When a user wants to restore these files, IDrive puts them back into their original location. One thing to note is that, for Claude, IDrive’s documentation says it replaces whatever is there. Restoring also only works between machines that run the same operating system, which means a Windows setup can’t be restored to a Mac, for example.
Open source backup alternatives
This idea, of course, isn’t entirely new. Developers can already use a plethora of open source tools to sync and back up their agent’s state.
There are tools like bak, which syncs agent configurations, and commercial services like Agent Bak. Agent-archive, meanwhile, ships session transcripts to an S3 or R2 bucket and backup specialist Backblaze’s labs team has published an open source engine for backing up agent state to its B2 storage service.
IDrive’s version is built into a consumer backup app and can automatically detect the four agents on its own. It also comes with a restore flow that is meant for moving to a new computer.
AI Agents Backup is available now in the IDrive desktop app for all users, the company says. Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf aren’t on the supported list.

articles.title: DDR6 memory modules could be 44% shorter than DDR5 while delivering over 50% more bandwidth
articles.text:
Forward-looking: JEDEC is looking forward to a point when buying DRAM doesn't require selling a kidney and DDR6 is available. In an early preview of the next-gen memory standard, the organization noted that not only would it bring several upgrades, but the proposed modules would also be around 44% shorter than DDR5 versions.
As VideoCardz notes, a full-size DDR5 stick measures just over 133 mm from end to end. The design JEDEC has in mind for DDR6 measures 74 mm, putting it within a few millimeters of those little SO-DIMMs found in laptops. Unfortunately, you can probably guess who stands to benefit most from being able to squeeze more memory into the same amount of motherboard space.
Sure enough, JEDEC singles out AI inference and agentic AI as two workloads that could use more memory close to the CPU. The speed figures it gives are for registered DIMMs, the kind typically found in servers. DDR6 RDIMMs are expected to start at 12,800 MT/s, up from the 9,200 MT/s ceiling for DDR5 RDIMMs, with 14,400 MT/s and higher speeds to follow.
That works out to a roughly 39% increase in the transfer rate right from the start. There's also the data bus, which goes from 64 bits wide to 96 bits, allowing the module to move more data with each transfer. JEDEC expects those two changes to deliver more than 50% additional bandwidth at launch. It's also developing low-power modes specifically for use in data centers.
As for how much memory you could get on one of those shorter sticks, DDR6 is expected to support 128-gigabit dies. That's 16GB on a single die, and manufacturers will be able to stack several of them in the same package. Micron offered some idea of where that could lead last month when it outlined plans for a 1TB server module.
The big question now is when DDR6 might make its way into your next build. Don't expect it anytime soon. JEDEC lists the unbuffered DIMMs used in desktop PCs and the low-profile CAMM design among the formats under consideration, though it hasn't put a date on any of them.
Back in May, we heard that Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron were already working with substrate suppliers on DDR6, with the first commercial modules expected in 2028 or 2029. Whether those first modules will include a reasonably priced kit for a gaming PC is another matter, but here's hoping.

articles.title: Todos los trucos de GTA 6: códigos para conseguir dinero, armas, vehículos y munición infinita
articles.text:
GTA 6 recupera los trucos clásicos de la franquicia con hasta 61 códigos para obtener dinero, armas, vehículos, munición infinita, cambios de clima y efectos visuales, aunque no estarán disponibles desde el inicio. Los jugadores deberán completar la historia y superar desafíos específicos antes de activar estas ventajas en Leonida.
La novedad cambia el papel de los códigos en Grand Theft Auto VI. En entregas anteriores, bastaba con introducir una combinación para modificar la partida. En esta ocasión, Rockstar vincula cada truco a un objetivo previo, desde ganar carreras o completar saltos hasta conseguir medallas en galerías de tiro.
Los trucos se desbloquean después de terminar la historia
Los códigos no funcionarán durante la primera partida. Tras completar la campaña, el menú de Progreso mostrará una nueva sección llamada “Trucos”, donde aparecerán las opciones disponibles y sus requisitos.
Cada ventaja exige un desafío concreto. Para obtener granadas, por ejemplo, será necesario realizar un número determinado de lanzamientos. El acceso a vehículos, armas o filtros visuales también dependerá de retos de exploración, combate, conducción, actividades en pareja y coleccionables.
Para activar un código, hay que abrir el móvil con la cruceta hacia arriba. Después, se deben mantener pulsados L1 y R1 en PlayStation, o LB y RB en Xbox, e introducir la combinación correspondiente. Si el proceso funciona, la pantalla mostrará los trucos activados.
Los trucos desactivan trofeos, logros y autoguardado. Si el personaje muere después de usarlos, el progreso posterior a la última partida guardada puede perderse. Por esa razón, conviene crear una partida manual antes de probarlos.
Dinero, blindaje y vehículos reparados entre los trucos de personaje
Entre los códigos de personaje destaca el que entrega 250.000 dólares de forma inmediata. Para usarlo, será necesario completar la historia y pulsar:
Arriba, derecha, abajo, izquierda, arriba, izquierda, abajo, derecha.
También estarán disponibles opciones para emborrachar a los protagonistas, aumentar o reducir el nivel de búsqueda, activar concentración ilimitada, evitar daño por caídas, conseguir un paracaídas y añadir blindaje corporal.
El truco de reparación permitirá recuperar por completo el vehículo actual. Se desbloqueará al ganar 10 carreras en circuitos como Gellhorn, Mud Club, Thrillbilly y Boone. Habrá además nitro y combustible ilimitados tras completar 50 saltos acrobáticos.
Estos códigos se conectan con el mundo abierto de Leonida, donde la conducción será una parte central de los desplazamientos entre Vice City, los Leonida Keys, pantanos, rutas industriales y parques naturales.
Las galerías de tiro desbloquean munición infinita
El apartado de combate incluirá tres niveles para gestionar munición. El primero llena las reservas al máximo; el segundo activa munición infinita; el tercero elimina también la necesidad de recargar.
Para conseguir munición infinita, el jugador deberá obtener 25 medallas de plata o superiores en las galerías de tiro. La combinación es:
Abajo, arriba, derecha, abajo, izquierda, izquierda, arriba, abajo, abajo, abajo.
El juego también incluirá armas explosivas, munición incendiaria, cócteles que explotan al recibir daño, escopetas de proyectiles explosivos y un lanzador Hauners H-AT.
Otros trucos modificarán el comportamiento de los impactos. Fuerza de ataque hará que balas y golpes cuerpo a cuerpo lancen a los objetivos por los aires. Las pelotas explosivas transformarán los balones deportivos en proyectiles, mientras que Potencia del vehículo aumentará el efecto de las colisiones.
GTA 6 permitirá generar coches, motos, barcos y un tanque
La lista de vehículos incluye una ambulancia Interstate, Airboat 09, Bravado Banshee, BMX Tuff, Maibatsu Boomazoom, Nagasaki Carbon RS, Vapid Dominator de 1965, Progen Emerus, taxi Vapid Stanier G2, camión de bomberos MTL y bulldozer HVY.
También se podrán generar un Lapwing Mallard, un carrito de golf Brimstone, una Maibatsu Sanchez, una Nagasaki Sear Sparrow, una Speeder 700 GT, una Truffade Thrax y una Western Zombie Bubber.
Los códigos más exigentes permitirán obtener un Hauners P-996 Lazer y el tanque Hauners Rhino, asociado a la superación de todos los desafíos de supervivencia. El juego incluirá incluso un flotador de flamenco, que se desbloqueará después de destruir 50 flamencos con munición.
El clima y los filtros alterarán el aspecto de Leonida
Los trucos de entorno permitirán avanzar o detener el tiempo y cambiar la climatología tras revelar todo el mapa. El código para ajustar el clima será:
Abajo, derecha, arriba, abajo, derecha, arriba, derecha.
Habrá filtros como Jungla de neón, Cataclismo, Cinta de vídeo, Espejo oscuro, Migraña, Casa de muñecas, Pixel Art e Infernal. Algunos alterarán los colores; otros añadirán niebla, efecto de televisor antiguo, distorsión, cámara de vídeo u ojo de pez.
GTA 6 llegará a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S con un sistema de trucos condicionado por el progreso. Antes de activar dinero, armas o vehículos, será necesario terminar la historia de Jason y Lucía y cumplir los retos que desbloquean cada código.

articles.title: Uber tests rides for kids as young as 10, with extra pay for drivers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Uber has opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities as the company tests whether there’s a market for shuttling tweens without an adult by their side. The program, called Uber Kids, launched quietly over the past few weeks in Austin, Texas, Nashville, Tennessee, and Madison, Wisconsin.
The program, which builds on Uber’s existing teen ride-hailing service for passengers ages 13 to 17, is the latest bid by Uber to expand its customer base. Uber is describing this as a limited pilot program, which means it may never expand beyond these cities or even exist by next year. But if successful, it could open up a potentially lucrative market for Uber: busy families with active kids.
The Uber Kids program is stacked with mandatory requirements for parents and drivers. Parents or guardians are the only ones who can order a ride for their child, which they can do by adding the child to their family profile and completing a mandatory onboarding that explains the built-in safety features. A parent or guardian must be present at the pickup locations for the trip to begin and also have to include a note to the driver that explains the drop off.
Meanwhile, only highly rated drivers who have been invited are allowed to participate. Those drivers are required to complete an education module that includes step-by-step instructions and must be opted into live video streaming so parents can watch the trip in real time, according to Uber.
Uber said it also requires PIN verification for every Uber Kids trip, and says all recordings will be encrypted and not available to the driver, and will use sensors and GPS data to detect if the ride goes off course, stops unexpectedly, or ends early.
Drivers who are willing to adhere to those rules to shuttle kids will get a pay bump for the effort, according to Uber. Eligible drivers will earn $7 more on every Uber Kids trip compared to a standard one, the company says on the dedicated Uber Kids web page. Drivers will receive an extra $20 for the first Uber Kids ride they complete.
The extra compensation underscores a key challenge Uber faces as it expands into this younger age group — how to convince drivers to take on that added responsibility. If the program does expand it could eventually compete with existing transportation services such as HopSkipDrive and Zum.
Uber opened its ride-hailing service to minors in 2023 when it launched Uber for Teens, although the company had conducted early pilots several years prior. As the program expanded nationwide, Uber introduced a live video streaming feature.

articles.title: Deployment services drive Supermicro's race to time to online - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Today’s data centers weren’t built for AI racks, so liquid-cooling sidecars get bolted on
Deployment services are becoming the real battleground in AI infrastructure as buyers discover that shipping hardware is only half the job. With GPU supply tight and refresh cycles accelerating, neoclouds and enterprises are judging suppliers on how quickly an AI factory actually goes live.
Server makers that once competed on time to market are now measured on time to production. Super Micro Computer Inc., which reported a $60 billion order backlog in July, has stretched its server building-block model to cover entire data centers and is putting speed ahead of GPU count. Neoclouds want factories running fast, while enterprises now see inference and agentic AI as here to stay, according to Matthew Thauberger (pictured), chief revenue officer of Supermicro.
“It’s not just enough to deliver to the customers. They want it online as quickly as possible. Time is money,” Thauberger said.
Thauberger spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how deployment services are driving the race to time to online and how liquid cooling retrofits help older facilities take on modern AI racks. (* Disclosure below.)
Deployment services and the race to time to online
Customers are leaning on suppliers for far more than boxes. Allocation and deployment services are the two biggest requests Supermicro hears, and its service teams bring systems up, run customer workloads and hand off only once everything is running, Thauberger explained.
“We know that we’re in a constrained environment. There’s no secret on that. So customers are basically asking Supermicro how quickly you can get allocation, how quickly you can bring it online, and how quickly you can have people out on site to deploy those,” Thauberger said.
Older facilities pose another hurdle. Many weren’t designed for the liquid cooling and power density of modern AI racks, so Supermicro offers retrofit options such as sidecars and in-row coolant distribution units, according to Thauberger. The company has also added pre-assembled AI racks to its building-block lineup to shorten installs.
“We have the largest liquid cooling capacity based in California. We’re a U.S.-headquartered company, and the ability for us to have as much liquid cooling capacity as we have inside the U.S. allows us to deploy to these AI factories quick inside the United States,” Thauberger said.

articles.title: Google will launch Android app verification requirement globally in January 2027
articles.text:
Google announced Android developer verification last year, and despite numerous objections from developers and users, the company is forging ahead. It began blocking the installation of unregistered apps in some countries this fall, and the system is expanding globally soon. Google says it will start rolling out the requirement in all regions in January 2027, and it urges devs who still haven’t registered their apps to do so soon.
The apps you download from the Play Store all come from verified developers, and Google’s new requirement expands that requirement to apps from third-party sources. Once developer verification is live in your region, you won’t be able to sideload apps unless the developer has registered with Google, which is framed as a security measure. Verification requires providing government identification and paying a $25 fee, which will allegedly make it harder for nefarious actors to distribute malware and scammy apps.
In September, Google launched verification in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apparently, nothing exploded, so the company is now ready to expand. It previously said verification would go global in 2027, and it’s not wasting any time with the January start. It says that verification will reach all devices within “several months.”
So far, Google is getting what it wanted from this initiative, with “millions” of non-Play apps already registered. The company says this accounts for more than 99 percent of global Android app installs.
The verifier system service has already been rolled out to Google-certified devices running Android 8 Oreo or higher, which accounts for just about every Android device in the world outside of China and Russia. Google has also partnered with the biggest third-party app stores to enforce verification: Galaxy Store, Honor, Oppo, Xiaomi, Transsion, and Vivo. The system-level verifier is responsible for blocking installs, but these stores will only list verified apps once Google flips the switch.

articles.title: ANPD nega recurso do Discord e mantém lives suspensas no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ANPD nega recurso do Discord e mantém lives suspensas no Brasil
Conselho rejeitou por unanimidade o recurso da plataforma. Discord terá de comprovar mecanismos de proteção a crianças para retomar transmissões ao vivo.
O Conselho Diretor da Autoridade Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) rejeitou, por unanimidade, o pedido do Discord para voltar com as transmissões ao vivo no Brasil. A decisão foi tomada nessa quarta-feira (18/11) e mantém a medida preventiva adotada contra a plataforma em agosto.
A restrição vale para a função Go Live e outros recursos equivalentes de transmissão e compartilhamento de vídeos ao vivo com vários usuários. O Discord, no entanto, não foi bloqueado no país: mensagens de texto, conversas por voz e chamadas individuais continuam disponíveis.
Segundo a ANPD, a suspensão busca reduzir riscos de exposição de crianças e adolescentes a situações de violência, coerção, automutilação e incentivo ao suicídio. A agência avalia que o Discord ainda não demonstrou a adoção de salvaguardas suficientes para prevenir e responder a esses casos.
A medida tem caráter preventivo, provisório e reversível, e não representa uma penalidade à empresa. Para solicitar a retomada das lives, o Discord deverá comprovar a eficácia de mecanismos de proteção, incluindo verificação de idade, controles preventivos e capacidade de identificar e responder a situações de risco. A reativação depende de autorização prévia e expressa da ANPD.
A ANPD determinou a suspensão das transmissões ao vivo em 12 de agosto, após abrir um processo de fiscalização para apurar possíveis falhas na proteção de crianças e adolescentes. Na ocasião, a agência afirmou ter identificado problemas em medidas estruturais e procedimentos usados para prevenir violações graves de direitos de menores.
A fiscalização também considera a arquitetura técnica do Discord. Segundo a agência, a plataforma não tem acesso ao conteúdo das transmissões de vídeo enquanto elas acontecem, o que dificulta a análise audiovisual e a identificação de violações em tempo real.
Criado em 2015, o Discord é uma plataforma de comunicação que reúne mensagens de texto, chamadas de voz e vídeo em servidores organizados por canais. Popular entre gamers, o serviço também oferece recursos de áudio de baixa latência.

articles.title: Scammers have met their match — this bizarre AI retirement home lets you unleash a whole neighborhood of grannies on unwanted callers
articles.text:
Scammers have met their match — this bizarre AI retirement home lets you unleash a whole neighborhood of grannies on unwanted callers
How to get your own back on scammers
- A new free service offers AI grannies ready to handle your scam callers
- Forward calls to the AI granny number, or merge calls and listen in
- There are four different AI grannies available to take calls
Earlier this year I wrote about Daisy the AI granny, who was designed to ensnare phone scammers in an endless loop of meandering conversations, and generally waste their time. It was one of the most original and downright funny uses of AI I’ve seen so far.
Thanks to how far AI voice models have progressed, it was virtually impossible to tell that Daisy wasn’t a real person. ‘She’ sounded exactly like a forgetful old lady, and ‘she’ could happily waste scammers time for hours.
And now Daisy has a bunch of friends: a whole retirement home full of AI grannies, who are available for you to send pesky scam callers to, has just come online. SPRVILLAS is a satirical retirement community whose AI residents are ready and waiting to entertain scam callers for as long as their patience holds out.
“Each character is part of a larger fictional world built around a simple idea: if scammers want to waste people’s time, why not return the favor?”, explains SPRVILLAS' creator, Jesse Wroblewski. The best thing is that you can take advantage of these old ladies’ services for free, and send your own unknown callers straight to them — and they’re online 24/7.
How to use the AI grannies
“You can either use the granny number (888) 892 – 9375 when filling out information online instead of your own number,” explains Wroblewski, “or you can wait for a call to come in and simply merge the call with a granny and listen in”. Instructions on adding a handy quick call icon to your smartphone Home Screen are included on the site.
Each resident has their own unique AI personality to keep the scammer engaged. We have Delores, who is a conspiracy-minded and suspiciously wealthy. Next is Francis, a sweet storyteller who will keep asking innocent questions and at some point tell you about the time Nixon visited her church. Betsy is a MAGA-obsessed granny who insists on asking everyone where they are “really from”. Finally, MiMi who speaks entirely in meme culture, using phrases like “no cap” and “rizz”.
I asked Wroblewski if he had a favorite resident of the retirement home: “Right now it is Delores”, he says. “She’s the kind of no-nonsense, question everything/do your own research type of gal that really lets scammers have it. MiMi is great, but her conversations make me cringe — which is the intended effect I guess.”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I hate the scam calls I receive, and while call screening on my iPhone helps to minimize the problem, I really like the idea of a virtual retirement home full of AI models designed to waste scammers time and energy. For once, it feels like you’re actually doing something to fight back.

articles.title: Standard, Paperwhite oder Colorsoft? So findest du den passenden E-Reader von Kindle zu Weihnachten
articles.text:
Kindle zu Weihnachten verschenken: Das sind die neuen E-Reader von Amazon
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Ein E-Reader ist das perfekte Weihnachtsgeschenk für alle, die gerne lesen, aber keine schweren Bücher mehr mit sich herumtragen möchten – egal, ob im Urlaub oder zu Hause. Amazon hat im Oktober seine neue Kindle-Generation vorgestellt, die es seit Kurzem auch in Deutschland gibt. Die Geräte sind in mehreren Größen und Farben erhältlich. Wir erklären dir, wie sich die Modelle unterscheiden und wo du aktuell sparen kannst.
Kindle E-Reader: Das musst du vorab wissen
Ein E-Reader ist ein tragbares, elektronisches Gerät für digitale Bücher und Zeitschriften. Das zentrale Element ist die sogenannte E-Ink-Technologie. Sie sorgt dafür, dass das Display gedrucktem Papier ähnelt und die Sonne beim Lesen nicht spiegelt. In der Regel haben die Modelle keine Hintergrundbeleuchtung und stellen Inhalte in Graustufen dar. Das schont einerseits die Augen und sorgt andererseits dafür, dass der Akku deutlich länger hält als zum Beispiel bei Tablets.
Unter den Pioneers Picks stellen wir dir regelmäßig weitere praktische Tools und Gadgets vor.
Kindle zählt in Deutschland zu den beliebtesten Anbietern von E-Readern. Nutzer:innen kaufen ihre E-Books direkt bei Amazon und verwalten sie in ihrem Konto. Mit Kindle Unlimited können sie sich außerdem für ein Abonnement entscheiden, das ihnen Zugriff auf Millionen Titel gewährt. Das geschlossene System hat aber auch Nachteile. Gekaufte E-Books sind durch einen Kopierschutz ausschließlich auf Kindle-Geräten lesbar. Wer später das Gerät eines anderen Herstellers nutzen möchte, kann seine Amazon-Bibliothek also nicht übertragen.
Günstiges Einstiegsmodell: Der Standard-Kindle
Laut Amazon wurde die neue Kindle-Generation so gestaltet, dass sie noch besser in der Hand liegt. Das Standard-Modell ist dünner und leichter als sein Vorgänger und Bücher sollen sich 30 Prozent schneller öffnen. Das 6-Zoll-Display zeigt Texte kontrastreich und blendfrei an, die Helligkeit lässt sich flexibel einstellen. Mit 16 Gigabyte internem Speicher bietet das Gerät Platz für Tausende Bücher. Eine einzige Aufladung hält bis zu sechs Wochen.
Insgesamt stehen beim Standard-Kindle vier Farben zur Auswahl. Neu ist, dass die Vorderseite jetzt in der gleichen Farbe gestaltet ist wie die Rückseite. Wahlweise ist das Modell auch mit einem Aluminiumgehäuse erhältlich. Das günstige Einstiegsmodell kostet regulär 174,99 Euro. Im Rahmen der Black-Friday-Aktion senkt Amazon den Preis der Variante ohne Werbung aktuell um 20 Prozent auf 139,99 Euro. Die Variante mit Werbung ist noch etwas günstiger.
Größeres Display und wasserfest: Der Kindle Paperwhite
Auch der neue Kindle Paperwhite ist dünner und schneller als sein Vorgänger. Sein 7 Zoll großes Display stellt Texte ebenfalls kontrastreich und blendfrei dar. Zusätzlich bietet das Modell einen Dunkelmodus und die Möglichkeit, die Farbtemperatur anzupassen. Mit nur einer Akkuladung soll das Gerät laut Amazon bis zu zwölf Wochen durchhalten.
Da der Kindle Paperwhite wasserdicht ist, können Nutzer:innen auch bedenkenlos in der Badewanne oder am Pool lesen. Die reguläre Variante ist in der Farbe Graphit mit 16 Gigabyte Speicher erhältlich. Ohne Werbung kostet sie 209 Euro. Die Signature Edition hat 32 Gigabyte internen Speicher, ein Aluminiumgehäuse und ist zusätzlich in Grün erhältlich. Sie kostet 259,99 Euro.
Für Fans von Graphic Novels: Der Kindle Colorsoft
Der neue Kindle Colorsoft hat wie der Paperwhite ein 7-Zoll-Display, 16 Gigabyte internen Speicher und ist ebenfalls wasserdicht. Anstelle eines Schwarz-Weiß-Displays stellt er Farben wie auf Papier dar – ideal für Comics und Graphic Novels. Spiegeleffekte gibt es aber auch hier nicht. Zusätzlich können Leser:innen ihre Lieblingsstellen in den Farben Gelb, Orange, Blau, Pink und Grün markieren.
Auch hier gibt es die Möglichkeit, die Farbtemperatur zu verstellen oder den Dunkelmodus zu nutzen. Eine einzige Aufladung hält laut Hersteller bis zu acht Wochen. Der reguläre Kindle Colorsoft ist in der Farbe Graphit erhältlich und kostet ohne Werbung 299,99 Euro. Die Signature Edition bietet 32 Gigabyte Speicher, ein Aluminiumgehäuse und ist zusätzlich in Grün erhältlich. Sie kostet 329,99 Euro.

articles.title: GTA 6 : les meilleurs réglages TV et HDR sur PS5 et Xbox Series
articles.text:
Enfin ! GTA VI est maintenant disponible en France et nul doute que de nombreux joueurs n’ont pas tardé à lancer le jeu, mais l’ont-ils fait dans les meilleures conditions ? Avant d’explorer Leonida de fond en comble, quelques minutes dans les menus du téléviseur, de la console et du jeu lui-même peuvent aider à faire une vraie différence à l’écran. Du mode jeu au flou cinétique en passant par le HDR et le VRR, on a fait le tri dans les conseils et les options à appliquer.
Premier point à garder en tête, GTA 6 tourne à 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles, PS5 Pro comprise. Selon Digital Foundry, le jeu s’appuie sur une résolution de base de 1440p sur PS5 comme sur PS5 Pro, reconstruite ensuite pour l’affichage en 4K. Le jeu ne propose aucun mode graphique et si vous disposez d’une PS5 Pro, l’upscaling PSSR et les ombres en ray tracing s’appliquent automatiquement. Pour le dernier jeu du studio Rockstar, inutile donc de courir après le 120 Hz ou un TV dernier cri pour en profiter. Les réglages intéressants ici sont ceux qui touchent à la latence, au rendu du HDR et à la sensation de fluidité.
Sur le téléviseur : priorité au mode jeu et HGIG
Le premier réflexe est de vérifier que le mode Jeu s’enclenche bien sur votre téléviseur. La PS5 et les Xbox Series basculent normalement toutes seules grâce à l’ALLM, mais certains écrans capricieux demandent un coup de pouce manuel. L’activation de ce mode est indispensable pour couper les traitements d’image gourmands en latence. Dans la même logique, résistez à la tentation d’activer le lissage de mouvement (TruMotion chez LG, Motionflow chez Sony, Auto Motion Plus chez Samsung ou MEMC ailleurs) pour compenser les 30 images par seconde : vous y gagnerez surtout un retard à l’affichage pénible et des artefacts autour des personnages. Le Game Motion Plus de Samsung, pensé pour le jeu, limiterait un peu la casse, mais la réactivité en prend tout de même un coup.
Si votre téléviseur propose l’option HGIG (parfois cachée dans les réglages de mappage tonal chez Sony), activez-la et coupez le mappage tonal dynamique : cela évite que l’écran ne bidouille la luminosité par-dessus les réglages de la console. On vous conseille également de désactiver le mode éco qui bride la dalle, tout comme le contraste dynamique. En ce qui concerne les câbles, une simple prise HDMI 2.0 suffit pour la 4K à 60 Hz, mais pourquoi se priver si votre téléviseur dispose de prises HDMI 2.1 ? Vous pouvez y brancher la console pour vos autres jeux, en gardant à l’esprit que la prise eARC est souvent réservée à la barre de son. Le HDMI 2.1 peut d’ailleurs apporter un léger plus sur Xbox, comme nous le verrons plus bas.
Reste le VRR (fréquence de rafraîchissement variable), sur lequel PS5 et Xbox ne sont pas logées à la même enseigne. Sur PS5, Digital Foundry rappelle que le VRR du système ne fonctionne qu’au-dessus de 48 images par seconde et ne gère pas la compensation des basses fréquences (LFC) : le forcer ne change donc rien dans un jeu à 30 images par seconde. Sur Xbox, la console peut en revanche afficher le jeu dans un signal à 120 Hz avec VRR, une fonction gérée par le système qui permet, selon nos confrères, « une expérience légèrement plus fluide ». La latence, elle, ne bouge pas vraiment selon Digital Foundry qui a mesuré environ 180 millisecondes entre la manette et l’écran sur Xbox Series X, manette sans fil et téléviseur compris, que la console sorte en 60 Hz, en 120 Hz ou en 120 Hz avec VRR.
Sur la console : vérifier la sortie vidéo et le HDR
Sur PS5, direction Paramètres > Écran et vidéo > Sortie vidéo. Laissez tout en automatique, passez le HDR sur « Activé lorsque pris en charge », puis lancez l’outil « Ajuster le HDR ». Ne bâclez pas ces trois écrans de réglage, car ce sont eux qui indiquent à la console le pic lumineux réel de votre TV.
Sur Xbox Series X et S (Paramètres > Général > Options TV et Affichage), sélectionnez la 4K UHD. Si vous êtes branché en HDMI 2.1, cochez le 120 Hz pour débloquer le VRR, mais restez en 60 Hz avec du HDMI 2.0 pour ne pas sacrifier la définition. Cochez ensuite HDR10, VRR et ALLM dans les modes vidéo, laissez l’espace colorimétrique sur « Standard » (le mode RVB PC n’a d’intérêt que sur moniteur) et passez par l’application de calibrage HDR. Le Dolby Vision est aussi de la partie sur Xbox, mais face à un HDR10 bien calibré avec l’HGIG, l’écart ne saute pas forcément aux yeux.
Pour le son, une barre de son ou un ampli branché en eARC devra recevoir le flux sans conversion, en réglant la sortie audio du téléviseur sur « Passthrough » ou « Bitstream ». Sur Xbox, le jeu propose le Dolby Atmos, y compris au casque via l’application Dolby Access. Sur PS5, c’est l’audio 3D Tempest qu’il faut activer pour un casque, dans Paramètres puis Son.
Dans le jeu : le calibrage HDR à ne pas bâcler
Une fois dans les menus du jeu (Paramètres > Affichage > Calibrage HDR), vous tomberez sur trois curseurs : luminosité maximale, niveaux de noir et blanc papier. Ils sont précédés d’un interrupteur HDR sur PS5, absent sur Xbox. Par défaut, la luminosité maximale est réglée à 600 et cela demeure trop timide pour beaucoup d’écrans récents, surtout quand on sait que Digital Foundry a mesuré des pics au-delà de 1 500 nits dans le jeu. Vous pouvez pousser le curseur jusqu’au maximum réel de votre dalle pour profiter pleinement du rendu HDR. Pour les niveaux de noir, suivez la consigne affichée et ajustez jusqu’à ce que le logo soit à peine visible. Quant au blanc papier, il gère la luminosité globale et celle de l’interface : calmez-le si vous jouez dans le noir complet. Inutile de copier les réglages trouvés sur internet, chaque dalle réagit différemment et il vaut mieux prendre deux minutes pour trouver le réglage idéal, propre à votre TV.
Toujours dans l’onglet Affichage, le réglage « Intensité du flou cinétique » va de 0 à 10 et se trouve sur 3 par défaut, et on serait tenté de dire qu’il n’y a pas de bonne ou de mauvaise situation. À 30 images par seconde, ce flou masque en partie la saccade entre deux images : sans lui, l’image paraît plus hachée lors des mouvements de caméra, un effet encore plus visible sur un téléviseur OLED, dont la dalle très réactive accentue la sensation. Si ce flou vous gêne, notamment lors des poursuites en voiture, vous pouvez le baisser, voire le couper, en acceptant une image plus saccadée. Cette valeur par défaut s’apparente à un compromis raisonnable, qu’il reste possible d’ajuster selon votre sensibilité.
Enfin, les joueurs sujets au mal des transports ne trouveront pas de réglage du champ de vision. L’onglet Caméra propose en revanche une rubrique Confort où il est possible de désactiver les secousses de la caméra, de réduire les mouvements de caméra et le balancement de l’arme. Dans la rubrique Cinéma du même onglet, baisser le réglage des accidents cinématographiques évite aussi que la caméra ne vous retire la vue lors d’une collision en pleine poursuite. De quoi rendre les longues virées en voiture et les fusillades plus supportables.

articles.title: Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Inside Amazon Connect Talent: The science of structured AI interviews
For organizations hiring hundreds or thousands of people, every interview presents the same challenge: How do you give candidates a consistent opportunity to demonstrate their skills while gathering the evidence needed to make informed hiring decisions?
Structured behavioral interviews offer a research-backed approach to this challenge. They use consistent, job-related questions and clear scoring criteria to give candidates an opportunity to demonstrate their skills. Decades of research in industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology have shown that structured interviews help organizations evaluate candidates and predict job performance (Schmidt & Hunter, 1998; Sackett et al., 2022). Yet delivering structured interviews at scale requires significant time and expertise to develop competencies, create questions, train interviewers, and evaluate responses consistently.
Amazon Connect Talent brings established hiring science to AI-led interviews at scale. Connect Talent uses structured questions, adaptive follow-ups, and evidence-based scoring to help organizations gather consistent, job-related information while giving more candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their strengths.
We built Connect Talent around three core design principles and evaluated how well the service applies them through a combination of internal research and independent expert review. The findings offer a closer look at the science behind Connect Talent’s AI-led, structured interviewing.
Three core design principles
1. Build interviews around job-related evidence
Connect Talent builds each interview around the competencies required for the role. The service uses job requirements and established occupational frameworks to create behaviorally anchored scorecards. Each scorecard defines specific strength and concern signals, and every interview question targets the behaviors it aims to uncover.
The AI interviewer also adapts to each response. After every answer, it checks whether the candidate has provided enough evidence for the competency being assessed. When details are missing, it asks targeted follow-up questions. This approach preserves the structure of the interview while giving candidates more opportunities to explain their experience.
2. Separate interviewing from scoring
Connect Talent separates the interview conversation from the evaluation. The AI interviewer gathers evidence but does not assign scores. Afterward, a separate evaluation process identifies which behaviors the candidate demonstrated and cites the supporting transcript passages.
The service calculates each competency score from 1 to 5 using a fixed formula. When the transcript lacks sufficient evidence, Connect Talent flags the competency instead of producing a score. Hiring teams can review the evidence behind each rating, and missing evidence does not automatically count against the candidate.
3. Build fairness protections into the design
Connect Talent evaluates transcribed candidate responses without using video, voice tone, or physical appearance to calculate competency scores. The service also excludes candidate identity information from scoring and evaluates each competency separately. These safeguards help focus assessments on job-related behaviors and limit the influence of unrelated information.
What the research shows
To understand how well these design principles work in practice, we combined independent I-O psychology evaluations with internal research. We examined whether the service generates job-relevant interview content, identifies behavioral evidence in line with expert assessments, gathers more complete responses through follow-up questions, and distinguishes between levels of demonstrated competency.
Connect Talent keeps interview questions focused on job-relevant skills
The quality of a structured interview starts with the skills it measures. Candidates need questions that reflect the requirements of the role, and hiring teams need confidence that the interview assesses those skills.
Amazon engaged an independent I-O psychology firm to evaluate Connect Talent’s AI-generated interview content. The firm reviewed the service’s baseline output before human editing and examined how well its competencies, questions, and rubrics aligned with job requirements. The evaluation found that Connect Talent retained critical job information in 100% of the job descriptions reviewed. Of the competencies generated, 91% were clearly traceable to the job description. The firm’s psychologists also found that 98% of interview questions targeted the intended competencies, and 94% of rubric signals clearly measured the intended competency.
These findings show that Connect Talent generated job-relevant interview content that met independent expert criteria in a vast majority of cases. Hiring teams can then review, select, and edit the competencies, scorecards, and questions before using them. This human oversight gives organizations control over the interview process while helping them apply structured hiring practices at scale.
Connect Talent’s candidate scoring matched independent expert decisions more than 89% of the time
Relevant questions provide the foundation for a structured interview. The next challenge is evaluating the evidence candidates provide with consistency.
To examine this, an independent I-O psychology firm reviewed 36 interviews assessing whether candidates demonstrated specific strengths and concerns, creating 252 rubric signals.
Connect Talent evaluated the same transcripts, reviewed hundreds of rubric signals, and aligned with expert scoring decisions in 89.3% of cases. Scoring alignment reached 97.6% when candidates provided clear evidence and 92.9% when only considering candidate concern signals, which identify behaviors that may indicate a poor fit for the intended role.
The evaluation also produced a Cohen’s kappa of 0.79, a statistical measure that eliminates random chance coincidence. A Cohen’s kappa of 0.79 is just under the standard of 0.81 for almost perfect agreement. This outcome indicates substantial agreement between Connect Talent and the independent expert candidate scoring.
Follow-up questions give candidates more opportunities to demonstrate their strengths
Candidates may have relevant experience but leave important details out of their first response. In a traditional one-way video interview, a candidate may receive a fixed question and have only one opportunity to answer it. Hiring teams must then evaluate the information available, even when the response leaves many important questions unanswered.
Connect Talent uses adaptive follow-ups to gather more complete evidence. For example, a candidate might describe improving a slow system. The AI interviewer can ask what changed, which actions the candidate took, and how they measured the improvement. These questions help candidates explain their contributions and results in greater detail.
We studied the impact of follow-up questions by comparing assessments based on a candidate’s first response with assessments based on the full interview conversation. In a preliminary evaluation, scores based only on the first response were up to 1.14 points lower on a five-point scale than scores based on the full conversation. Assessments using the full conversation also came closer to expert evaluations.
Without follow-up questions, the scoring process identified fewer strength signals and more concern signals. In some cases, the candidate’s initial response simply lacked the information needed to demonstrate a relevant behavior. The full conversation captured more of what candidates demonstrated and gave hiring teams a more complete record of their experience.
Structured scoring helps hiring teams recognize meaningful differences
Hiring teams need scores that reflect meaningful differences in demonstrated skills. Yet research has found that some AI scoring approaches concentrate ratings within a narrow range, making those differences harder to recognize (Zhu et al., 2026).
Connect Talent uses behaviorally anchored scorecards to evaluate specific strength and concern signals. Rather than asking an AI model to assign an overall rating, the service identifies evidence for each behavior and calculates the competency score using a predefined formula.
Consider the competency “collaboration”. A general AI scoring approach might evaluate a candidate’s overall collaboration skills based on the interview transcript. Connect Talent examines specific behaviors, such as whether the candidate sought input from colleagues before making a decision. Each finding contributes to the final score.
We evaluated this approach across hundreds of expert-rated interview assessments. Connect Talent’s structured scoring used all five points of the rating scale, while holistic LLM-as-judge scoring concentrated its ratings within the middle three points.
This wider distribution allows the scoring system to represent more levels of demonstrated competency. The behaviorally anchored scorecards also help hiring teams understand the evidence behind each rating.
Bringing hiring science to AI-led interviews
Connect Talent brings the rigor of structured interviewing to more people while giving each candidate a meaningful chance to demonstrate their skills. The result is a new opportunity for organizations hiring at scale: more candidates can show what they can do, and more hiring teams can make decisions grounded in the evidence that matters.
Learn More at AWS re:Invent 2026
Join us at AWS re:Invent 2026 for BIZ332: Every Candidate, Every Time: AI-Led Structured Interviews with Amazon Connect Talent, an interactive Chalk Talk led by Sunitha Srivatsa and Gerald Friedland.
The session will explore the science behind Connect Talent, including structured interviewing, adaptive follow-up questions, and evidence-based scoring.
Session 1: Monday, November 30, 2026, 10:00–11:00 AM, Caesars Forum – Level 1, Academy 409.
Repeat session: Thursday, December 3, 2026, 3:00–4:00 PM, MGM Grand, Premier 309.

Booth, B. M., Hickman, L., Subburaj, S. K., Tay, L., Woo, S. E., & D’Mello, S. K. (2021). Bias and Fairness in Multimodal Machine Learning: A Case Study of Automated Video Interviews. Proceedings of the 2021 International Conference on Multimodal Interaction, 268–277. https://doi.org/10.1145/3462244.3479897
