articles.title: A “headless Slack”: Vercel’s new message board lets Claude Code and Codex agents work together
articles.text:
A “headless Slack”: Vercel’s new message board lets Claude Code and Codex agents work together
For AI agents to work together effectively, they need a way to communicate and divvy up tasks — much as humans already do through a swath of digital collaboration tools.
Vercel is tackling this with Board, an experimental shared message board through which agents can claim tasks, exchange findings and track progress across different tools and environments, while allowing developers to follow and intervene in the work.
In a blog post published on Wednesday, Vercel says it developed Board for its own engineering operations, first using it to coordinate security agents investigating vulnerabilities and submitting fixes. It then rebuilt v0’s software factory around Board, which Vercel says now “merges over 50% of PRs.”
“It packages what we’ve learned about coordinating work across agent fleets.”
“It packages what we’ve learned about coordinating work across agent fleets and builds towards a future where multiple teams of humans and agents orchestrate swarms, software factories, and other agentic workflows,” the company writes.
The coordination conundrum
OpenAI demonstrated the importance of multi-agent communication in September when it announced that its agents had solved the Navier–Stokes problem, a longstanding mathematical challenge concerning the behavior of fluids.
The company said some 10,000 agents operated concurrently in the group that produced the result, exchanging information as they worked.
“In the process of resolving the Navier–Stokes problem, the agents sent 2.7 million messages and used approximately 130 billion output tokens,” the company wrote.
The need to manage multiple agents in parallel is becoming increasingly apparent in software development. Just last week, Google and Cursor introduced competing approaches to coordinating coding agents, with Google focusing on agents working on behalf of a single developer and Cursor enabling agents belonging to different teammates to communicate.
Then on Tuesday, Replit introduced Missions, bringing multiple agents together to tackle larger development projects.
Elsewhere, companies are also turning to existing collaboration platforms to bring humans and AI agents together. Devin Bots, which Cognition launched on Tuesday, uses Slack to connect agents with their human teammates.
In an X post published on Thursday, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says more than 226,000 custom agents have been deployed to Slack from across the major agent-building platforms. Notably, he says that he hadn’t anticipated this use of Slack when Salesforce acquired it back in 2021, acknowledging that companies are now using the platform as “trusted agent infrastructure.”
Vercel itself added its Agent to Slack code channels in August, allowing teammates to follow its work, give instructions and review proposed changes.
With Board, Vercel provides channels and threaded discussions where agents can pick up assignments, exchange findings, monitor dependencies and record completed work. It also maintains a history of activity, allowing developers to follow what their agents have been doing.
Crucially, Board is designed to accommodate agents built on different technologies. Vercel explicitly lists Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, eve, fx, Mastra and LangChain, as tools that can work together through Board.
“This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research.”
In an X post published on Wednesday, Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch described the technology as a “message board infrastructure primitive.” Or, a “headless Slack” for agents.
“This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research, where the human prompting is just the seed of the system, and millions of agents can operate in a decentralized fashion,” Rauch writes, adding that Board is designed to work independently of any particular model, agent harness or hosting provider.
“Just bring your agents, give them our CLI, and watch magic happen,” he adds.
Keeping humans in the loop
Board also connects agents to the tools developers already use, including Slack, GitHub and Linear. For example, a developer can submit a request through Slack, which an agent can then pick up and break into smaller assignments for other agents to complete.
The ensuing discussion, task ownership and progress updates are maintained in Board.
As work progresses, Board can synchronize information with GitHub, allowing agents and developers to follow changes to pull requests and review feedback, without having to manually relay information between systems. It also supports event-driven triggers, so agents can resume work when new messages arrive or task statuses change.
It’s worth noting that human oversight remains a crucial part of the process. Agents can report findings and wait for developers to approve changes before proceeding, while Board also provides channel-level permissions that determine which people and agents can access information or perform particular actions.
The security question
The ability of agents to communicate independently raises key questions about who controls those conversations and what information they can exchange.
Indeed, Rauch points to the OpenAI/Hugging Face cybersecurity incident from July as another high-profile example of message boards facilitating agent coordination. During the breach, agents repurposed an internal software repository to exchange findings and coordinate their activities.
“A core part of why we built Vercel Board was to fulfill our own needs for security and auditability.”
Thus, security and oversight are key considerations for systems such as Board. Vercel says it built access controls and activity logs into the service, allowing teams to restrict which agents can interact with particular channels and track their actions.
“A core part of why we built Vercel Board was to fulfill our own needs for security and auditability,” the company writes.
The accompanying documentation also warns that agents may “read messages as instructions,” making it important to control who can post in channels where agents receive tasks. By default, channels are accessible to team members, project deployments and installed apps unless administrators restrict access. Vercel recommends creating private channels or restricting permissions where necessary, and keeping sensitive information such as API keys and tokens off Board entirely.
Vercel Board is available now as an experimental feature on all Vercel plans, accessible through the Vercel CLI or JavaScript SDK. It’s free during the experimental period, though Vercel says it may introduce charges later.

articles.title: Dans GTA 6, tout est permis… sauf tromper Lucia et Jason, et ça fait jaser
articles.text:
Dans GTA 6, disponible depuis le 19 novembre 2026, on incarne deux personnages à la personnalité bien trempée. Jason et Lucia forment un couple uni dans une vie de criminels essayant de joindre les deux bouts. Cette dynamique nourrit la narration de GTA 6, qui intègre des éléments de romance, mais aussi le gameplay, puisque nos actions et nos choix dictent directement les liens sentimentaux entre Jason et Lucia.
D’aucuns se demandent alors s’il est possible de tromper Jason ou Lucia pendant nos balades dans les environnements de GTA 6. Les deux héros se font d’ailleurs régulièrement draguer. Sauf qu’il est impossible de passer à l’acte, comme le confirme le guide officiel conçu par IGN en partenariat avec Rockstar Games. Un choix qui divise déjà, non sans raison.
Jason et Lucia sont fidèles l’un à l’autre dans GTA 6
Dans la partie consacrée au sexe et à l’amour, le guide indique : « Contrairement à la plupart des autres jeux GTA, il n’y a aucun autre personnage avec lequel le joueur peut entamer une relation ou avoir des rapports sexuels. Ce niveau d’intimité est réservé à la dynamique entre Jason et Lucia, et à la façon dont vous choisissez de les faire interagir l’un avec l’autre. »
En d’autres termes, il n’y a pas de place pour l’adultère dans GTA 6. Cela peut sembler étrange, alors même que l’on peut choisir de ne pas entretenir du tout la relation entre Jason et Lucia (en retapant sa maison, par exemple), ce qui a des répercussions sur l’intrigue et la proximité du duo. En choisissant cette voie, certains auraient sans doute voulu se tourner vers un autre partenaire, comme on peut le faire dans des dizaines et des dizaines de jeux.
Le jeu interdit même la rupture. La relation entre Jason et Lucia se mesure sur quatre niveaux, et négliger son ou sa partenaire fait chuter la jauge, mais il est impossible de rompre pour de bon. En délaissant le couple, on obtient au mieux deux associés en affaires, jamais deux célibataires.
« Apparemment, on ne peut pas tromper ou rompre avec Lucia pour aller voir ailleurs. Je pense que c’est nul », estime cet internaute, qui ajoute : « Ce devrait au moins être une option dans l’histoire. Aucun couple n’est incassable. Il devrait y avoir une fin où ils cessent de s’aimer et s’éloignent au point de commencer à chercher d’autres personnes pour obtenir ce qu’ils pensent qu’il leur manque. Ce serait très amusant. » De son côté, le créateur de contenu Jasontheween ne comprend pas pourquoi Rockstar Games ne le laisse pas tromper Lucia, comme le montre ce clip. « Honnêtement, une relation heureuse et saine dans le milieu du crime est probablement l’élément le plus fantaisiste de GTA 6 », ironise un autre joueur.
Rockstar Games assume ce choix. Interrogé par Game8, le studio explique que GTA 6 raconte avant tout l’histoire d’un « couple dans le pétrin, d’amants en cavale », et que le gameplay suit cette ligne en n’offrant aucun autre partenaire.
Bien évidemment, l’idée n’est pas d’encourager absolument l’adultère. C’est simplement une question de logique de design. GTA 6 a des promesses de liberté et de réalisme assez poussées. Elles se heurtent ici aux choix de scénario, qui brisent l’immersion et limitent les actions possibles. Rockstar Games mise tout sur son duo, au point de limiter ce que les joueuses et les joueurs peuvent réellement faire dans le jeu. GTA 6 supprime aussi les prostituées, présentes dans la série depuis GTA 3 en 2001. Les clubs de strip-tease et leurs danses privées restent en revanche accessibles, à Jason comme à Lucia.

articles.title: Annoncée début octobre, l’Alexa Tablet 8 d’Amazon est déjà à moitié prix pour le Black Friday : 114,99€
articles.text:
Annoncée début octobre à partir de 230 €, la gamme Alexa Tablet d’Amazon voit déjà son plus petit modèle perdre la moitié de son prix pour le Black Friday. Amazon affiche l’Alexa Tablet 8 à 114,99 € au lieu de 229,99 € : une tablette Android avec Google Play, que nous n’avons pas encore testée, mais dont notre prise en main souligne les airs d’iPad mini.
L’Alexa Tablet 8 est le plus compact des trois formats de la gamme d’Amazon, qui compte aussi des modèles de 11 et 12 pouces. Elle tourne sous Android et donne accès à Google Play, contrairement aux anciennes tablettes de la marque, sous Fire OS.
Amazon la propose en version Graphite, avec 4 Go de RAM et 64 Go de stockage : l’Alexa Tablet 8 est affichée à 114,99 € au lieu de 229,99 €, sous la mention « Top Offre Black Friday ». Cette remise s’adresse d’abord à ceux qui cherchent une petite tablette pour des usages simples.
L’Alexa Tablet 8 (Graphite, 4 Go de RAM, 64 Go) est à 114,99 € au lieu de 229,99 € chez Amazon, soit 115 € d’économie sur le prix conseillé.
Pourquoi choisir l’Alexa Tablet 8 ?
- Un prix divisé par deux : Les 115 € d’économie sur le prix conseillé de 229,99 € ramènent la tablette à 114,99 €. Pour une première tablette ou un achat secondaire, la dépense reste mesurée.
- Android et Google Play : Amazon quitte Fire OS sur cette gamme et ouvre l’accès au Google Play Store. Vous retrouvez l’écosystème d’applications d’Android, ce qui n’était pas possible sur les anciennes tablettes de la marque.
- Un format compact façon iPad mini : Avec son écran de 8,7 pouces, elle se prête à la lecture dans le canapé ou dans les transports. Notre prise en main de la gamme relève que le format 8 pouces rappelle l’iPad mini d’Apple.
Une petite tablette pour les usages de tous les jours
Avec 4 Go de RAM et 64 Go de stockage, la fiche technique place l’Alexa Tablet 8 du côté des usages simples. Google Play donne accès aux applications Android habituelles, et Alexa+ s’intègre à l’interface. Dans notre prise en main de la gamme Alexa Tablet, nous avons relevé un chatbot accessible en bas à droite de l’écran, une page « Pour vous » et une Dynamic Tab en haut à gauche. L’application Kindle propose en outre un mode liseuse (noir et blanc, notifications coupées), sans que nous sachions s’il équipe ce modèle.
L’Alexa Tablet 8 conviendra à une tablette de salon, de cuisine ou de voyage : lire, regarder une vidéo, dialoguer avec l’assistant. Elle est moins adaptée à qui veut jouer, retoucher des photos ou travailler sur plusieurs applications à la fois. Les modèles de 11 et 12 pouces de la gamme embarquent 8 Go de RAM, le double de ce modèle, et Amazon n’a pas précisé le nom de la puce lors de notre prise en main.
Face à l’iPad mini et aux tablettes plus chères
À 114,99 €, l’Alexa Tablet 8 joue dans une autre catégorie de prix que l’iPad mini qu’elle évoque. Dans notre comparatif des meilleures tablettes, la Xiaomi Pad 8 est annoncée à partir de 365 euros, soit plus de trois fois son prix, et l’iPad mini 7 y figure aussi. Cet écart de prix a une contrepartie : moins de mémoire et une puce dont le nom n’est pas communiqué. Un point reste à vérifier avant d’acheter : nous n’avons pas pu confirmer l’étendue des fonctions d’Alexa+ disponibles en France.
✅ Les points forts
- Un prix de 114,99 € au lieu de 229,99 €, soit -50 % sur le prix conseillé
- Android avec accès à Google Play
- Alexa+ intégré à l’interface, avec un chatbot
- Un format compact de 8,7 pouces
- Une batterie annoncée par Amazon pour tenir toute la journée
❌ Les limites
- 4 Go de RAM, soit moitié moins que les modèles de 11 et 12 pouces
- Un nom de puce non communiqué par Amazon
- Pas encore testée par Clubic
- Fonctions d’Alexa+ à vérifier en France
Si cette tablette compacte correspond à votre usage, la remise de 115 € sur le prix conseillé s’applique à la version Graphite, à 114,99 € sur Amazon.
À 114,99 €, l’Alexa Tablet 8 est une bonne affaire pour qui veut une petite tablette simple : lecture, vidéo, applications Android et assistant Alexa+. La remise de 50 % se calcule sur le prix conseillé de 229,99 €, au niveau du prix de lancement de 230 € annoncé début octobre. La tablette a été annoncée il y a six semaines à peine : le prix conseillé est donc encore celui du lancement.
Elle n’a pas vocation à remplacer une tablette plus musclée : avec 4 Go de RAM et une puce dont Amazon n’a pas donné le nom, mieux vaut la réserver aux usages légers. Nous n’avons pas encore pu la tester : l’écran, l’autonomie annoncée à la journée par Amazon et la fluidité restent à valider. Elle reste un achat raisonnable si le budget compte, à condition de vérifier ce qu’Alexa+ propose en France.

articles.title: „Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“: Was der Job als Fluglotse für Lieferdrohnen mit sich bringt
articles.text:
Bevor die Eistorte auf den Bürgersteig stürzt: Wie Fluglotsen Lieferdrohnen koordinieren
Als Trevor Wischnewsky hörte, dass in seiner Nachbarschaft in Texas Pizza und Sushi per Drohne ausgeliefert sollten, stand sein Entschluss fest. „Das war unglaublich faszinierend“, sagt er. „Ich wollte einfach sofort ein Teil davon sein.“ Und es klappte: Mittlerweile trägt Wischnewsky den Titel RPIC, also „Remote Pilot in Command“ und ist bei der Firma FlyTrex tätig.
Was der Job als Fluglotse für Drohnen mit sich bringt
Ein RPIC ist so etwas wie ein Fluglotse. Doch statt Flugzeuge sind diese Art von Piloten für Flotten von Hexakopter-Drohnen zuständig. Die Drohnen liefern Fracht zu Haushalten und Unternehmen in einem Umkreis von knapp fünf Kilometern. Wischnewsky sorgt nicht nur für den sicheren Transport der FlyTrex-Pakete, sondern stimmt sich auch mit den anderen Anbietern wie Zipline, Amazon und Alphabets Wing ab. Sie alle bevölkern mit wachsenden Schwärmen von Lieferdrohnen den Himmel über Dallas.
Ein kleiner Rückblick auf Wischnewskys Einstieg: Als er sich bei FlyTrex bewarb, absolvierte er gerade eine Ausbildung zum Berufspiloten und Fluglehrer. Er war bereits von der Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) als Drohnenpilot zertifiziert. Das Unternehmen verlangt diese Qualifikation. Außerdem ist ein mehrwöchiger, von der FAA anerkannter Schulungskurs erforderlich. Damit soll sichergestellt werden, dass eine Pilotin oder ein Pilot auch darauf vorbereitet ist, bei Bedarf selbst die Drohne zu steuern. Ansonsten überwacht Wischnewsky aber den Lieferprozess vom FlyTrex-Einsatzzentrum aus mithilfe von Daten aus GPS, Lasern und einer Reihe von Sensoren.
Für Drohnenpiloten gilt es, der Automatisierung zu vertrauen
Angesichts seiner Ausbildung als Berufspilot war es für Wischnewsky anfangs die größte Herausforderung, der Technologie zu vertrauen. „Im Bereich der bemannten Flugzeuge sagt man dir: ‚Vertraue der Automatisierung nicht‘“, sagt er. Der Großraum Dallas-Fort Worth ist jedoch ein Testgelände für das Verkehrsmanagement unbemannter Flugsysteme (UTM) – ein Netzwerk, das es autonomen Drohnen von FlyTrex und seinen Mitbewerbern ermöglicht, ihre Koordinaten in Echtzeit auszutauschen. So sollen Kollisionen auch außerhalb der Sichtweite des Piloten vermieden werden. Sobald Wischnewsky sich vergewissert hat, dass eine Drohne flugbereit ist, ihr Flugweg frei ist und die Wetterbedingungen gut sind, übernimmt UTM den Rest.
Digitalförster
Manager für Weltraumschrott
Hitzemanager
Wettermacher
CO₂-Buchhalter
Spezialist für Klimagerechtigkeit
Job an der weltgrößten Kamera
Wildtier-Ersthelfer
Psilocybin-Pilzzüchter
Fachpersonal für Weltraumerlebnisse
Biorisikoberater
Die Fähigkeit, unter Druck ruhig zu bleiben
Wenn viel Betrieb ist, hat Wischnewsky bis zu zehn Drohnen gleichzeitig im Blick. „Man ist als Sicherheitsnetz da“, sagt er. Aber auch die beste Automatisierung ändert nichts daran, dass bei den Verantwortlichen ein ausgeprägtes Situationsbewusstsein vorhanden sein muss.
Vor allem das Wetter ist eine Gefahr. Wischnewsky erinnert sich an einen besonders stressigen Tag: Eine Drohne war erst seit wenigen Sekunden in der Luft, als der Wind so plötzlich auffrischte, dass er eingreifen musste. Er brachte sie sicher zurück und verhinderte so, dass die beförderte Eistorte auf den Bürgersteig prallte.

articles.title: ‘My dream is to make WeWork India the default choice for workspaces’
articles.text:
‘My dream is to make WeWork India the default choice for workspaces’
CEO and Managing Director Karan Virwani speaks to YourStory about WeWork India's first year as a public company, its expanding product portfolio, the impact of AI, market opportunities, and his ambitions for the business.
A year after WeWork India announced its IPO in October 2025, CEO and Managing Director Karan Virwani is satisfied with the company’s performance despite a subdued market.
“I think from an investor standpoint and a shareholder standpoint, we've done good. And if you compare it to the relative market, I think we've done really well,” he tells YourStory.
Virwani says founders spend much of their time raising funds and ensuring they have enough liquidity to sustain their businesses. Going public, he believes, removes some of that pressure, allowing them to focus on execution and growth.
“WeWork India has grown by 30%, both from a revenue perspective and an EBITDA perspective. Our digital products also crossed an annualised revenue run rate of Rs 100 crore. So we are doing pretty well,” he says.
Launching Rivet and expanding the product portfolio
Virwani says WeWork India’s digitally enabled products, including Virtual Office and Workplace, have performed well. The company earns more than Rs 100 crore in subscription revenue, with the business growing 30% year on year.
“We have been noticing this post COVID. People have been using our spaces on-demand, sort of like how one uses Uber. We own the plug-and-play co-working space sector completely. There’s no major competitor really,” he says.
The company’s managed offices business, which was a new vertical a few years ago, has also expanded.
“It’s grown to become 25% of our business. We did some really large deals this year with big players like T-Mobile, JPMorgan and Amazon.”
WeWork India recently launched Rivet, its design-and-build vertical, to serve existing customers who started with smaller workspaces but now require larger offices.
“Rivet was a way for us to take what they love about WeWork and design-build it for them specifically, based on their requirements and branding,” Virwani says.
He believes Rivet differs from other design-and-build companies because WeWork India also operates physical workspaces, rather than focusing solely on designing and handing over offices.
Working with GCCs and adopting AI
In its early years, particularly 2017 and 2018, WeWork India primarily catered to startups and freelancers. Today, about 40.8% of its business comes from global capability centres (GCCs), including large, mid-sized and smaller operations.
“A lot of these GCCs are in an exploratory phase when they enter a country like India. They’re starting or they’re testing if they can hire. They’re really seeing if this offshoring model works for them,” Virwani says.
He cites the example of Moss Adams, which has since merged with Baker Tilly under the latter’s name.
“They started with us with like 25 seats and now we've done a 600-person managed office for them. All in a span of roughly two years.”
Virwani is also optimistic about the opportunities created by AI. He says WeWork India has seen an acceleration in demand from a new group of AI-focused companies that have become its customers.
He believes AI is increasing the need for collaboration and, in turn, collaborative workspaces. He also expects entrepreneurship to grow faster over the next three years than it has in the previous three, as technology makes it easier for more people to start businesses.
“Those entrepreneurs will either join mid-sized businesses, smaller businesses, or they'll start their own businesses. And that will definitely benefit us because that's the type of audience that we're aimed at,” he says.
WeWork India has also introduced AI into its own operations, from routine tasks to more advanced applications. These include spatial analytics using CCTV footage to understand how people use its offices and improve workspace design.
“Contrary to popular belief, AI is not actually reducing our employee headcount. It's not like I can let go of a few hundred people. In fact, it's making everyone much more proactive. The quality of output has definitely increased,” he says.
Expansion plans and bigger ambitions
WeWork India currently operates across eight metropolitan markets: Bengaluru, Mumbai, Gurugram, New Delhi, Noida, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Pune.
Virwani says the company will consider expanding into other cities and towns when there is sufficient demand.
“I don't view it as Tier II or Tier III. Tomorrow, if any city starts to show a type of demand, which is a combination of enterprise and startups, and there is good supply coming in, we would 100% look at it as a serious growth city,” he explains.
For now, however, he would prefer to expand into areas on the outskirts of Bengaluru rather than enter an entirely new city. The priority is to operate where demand and supply are concentrated.
According to Cushman & Wakefield’s Global Trends in Flexible Office 2026 report, India ranks as the world’s most mature flexible office market.
Virwani expects the Indian market to double over the next five years.
“I really see the overall industry doubling in the next five years, which will mean that it’s roughly growing at about 20-odd per cent year on year. I see us trying to beat that growth, and so the business itself will more than double in that time period.”
He says WeWork India is evolving from a coworking space provider into an end-to-end real estate services platform.
While the flexible workspace sector has relatively low entry barriers, Virwani believes scaling a business remains difficult. He also sees enough room in the market for WeWork India and its major competitors to grow.
His mid-term ambition is to increase WeWork India’s market capitalisation from around Rs 10,000 crore to closer to Rs 50,000 crore.
“My aim or my dream would be that WeWork India becomes just the default. When you think of a workspace, you think of us,” Virmani says.
Edited by Teja Lele

articles.title: Google enviará al espacio satélites con sus chips de IA a bordo de un cohete de Blue Origin en 2029
articles.text:
Google eligió el cohete New Glenn, de la empresa espacial Blue Origin de Jeff Bezos, para lanzar los satélites de su proyecto Suncatcher, un experimento para ejecutar sistemas de inteligencia artificial en el espacio. Las compañías informaron el acuerdo este jueves y fijaron el lanzamiento para el primer trimestre de 2029.
Será el primer vuelo de carga pesada que Google dedica a Suncatcher. Los satélites llevarán los procesadores que Google diseñó para correr programas de IA, conocidos como TPU, según el comunicado de Blue Origin. Cada uno tendrá una capacidad de cómputo comparable a la de un estante de servidores de un centro de datos tradicional.
Los aparatos entrarán en una órbita sincrónica con el Sol, que les da luz casi continua. Esa luz es el motivo del proyecto: Google sostiene que su plan consiste en aprovechar la energía solar abundante en órbita para ampliar la infraestructura de IA.
Un prototipo ya está en órbita
Suncatcher no parte de cero. Google y la empresa de imágenes satelitales Planet Labs lanzaron en octubre un primer prototipo a bordo de un cohete de SpaceX, y ambas dijeron que el satélite funcionaba como se esperaba tras establecer contacto con la Tierra, según Reuters.
Ese aparato prueba si los chips resisten las fuerzas del despegue, la radiación y las temperaturas extremas. También permite estudiar cómo enfriarlos, ya que en el vacío no hay aire que circule: el calor debe liberarse mediante tubos y paneles.
The Verge informó que, en esa prueba, el satélite encendió sus procesadores y usó el modelo Gemma 4, de Google, para enviar a la Tierra un haiku generado por IA.
El vuelo de 2029 usará un cohete distinto. Travis Beals, director sénior de Suncatcher en Google, lo calificó como un hito de la hoja de ruta del proyecto, que describió como una apuesta de largo plazo.
Un negocio importante para Blue Origin
El acuerdo también importa para Blue Origin. Reuters señaló que la empresa le da un encargo de peso a New Glenn en un momento en que busca ampliar su negocio de lanzamientos tras varios retrasos y una explosión en su plataforma de lanzamiento en mayo.
Jordan Charles, vicepresidente sénior de New Glenn en Blue Origin, afirmó que el proyecto representa las misiones ambiciosas para las que se diseñó el cohete. Su gran capacidad de carga y el volumen de su compartimento permiten, dijo, llevar nuevas capacidades a órbita.
Google no es la única que mira al espacio. Según Reuters, SpaceX, de Elon Musk, y la startup Starcloud también exploran centros de datos en órbita, a medida que el uso de IA aumenta la demanda de cómputo y presiona la infraestructura en tierra.
Reuters recogió además que los especialistas advierten que los altos costos de lanzamiento, las dificultades de ingeniería y la limitada producción de satélites pueden dejar estos centros de datos a años de un uso comercial.
Por ahora, el único hito con fecha es el lanzamiento de Blue Origin, previsto para el primer trimestre de 2029.

articles.title: En 1917, Dinamarca vendió unas islas a EEUU por 25 millones de dólares. Sin esclavos para recoger azúcar no eran rentables
articles.text:
Los vínculos entre Estados Unidos y Dinamarca también han pasado por el Caribe. Hay unas islas que estuvieron relacionadas con el negocio del azúcar que Copenhague vendió a Washington. Fue en 1917, en plena Primera Guerra Mundial. El precio fue de 25 millones de dólares en oro. Desde entonces pasaron a llamarse las Islas Vírgenes de Estados Unidos.
El traspaso también afectaba a Santo Tomás, San Juan y Santa Cruz, más los islotes cercanos. Hasta ese momento eran conocidas como las Indias Occidentales Danesas.
Es importante conocer que el sistema económico de estas islas estaba basado en las plantaciones y la compraventa de esclavos. Aunque la esclavitud había sido abolida en 1848, el negocio del azúcar empezó a perder interés.
Según el Museo Nacional de Dinamarca, los barcos daneses llevaron a unas 120.000 personas esclavizadas de África al Caribe. En las islas se basaba el sistema de producción azucarera en mano de obra forzada.
En la historia del archipiélago también hay episodios de resistencia de la población esclavizada. En 1733 hubo una rebelión en San Juan. Se alzaron contra el dominio danés. En el reglamento del gobernador Philip Gardelin se detallan algunos de los castigos extremos que se practicaron.
La libertad llegó antes que la venta
En 1847 se había previsto un proceso de emancipación paulatina de 12 años. Para los esclavos era inaceptable y por eso en julio de 1848 hubo otra revuelta en Santa Cruz. Los rebeldes amenazaban con quemar Frederiksted, haciendo que el gobernador Peter von Scholten tuviera que declarar la libertad.
Con la abolición, los plantadores tenían que pagar por el trabajo que antes imponían. Además, los rendimientos comenzaron a bajar. Por dos razones: el agotamiento de los suelos y la competencia del azúcar de remolacha. En un informe diplomático de 1911 se explican las dificultades.
Aunque se había dado la libertad legalmente, las autoridades establecieron un duro sistema de regulación laboral. Así se buscaba garantizar mano de obra para las plantaciones.
Por todo esto, apareció el interés de liberarse de la colonia. Hubo varios intentos de venta. En 1902 se llegó a negociar una venta por cinco millones de dólares, la cual recibió el apoyo del Folketing (Cámara baja) de Dinamarca, pero falló en el Landsting (Cámara alta).
Volvió a ponerse en marcha en plena Primera Guerra Mundial. Se unió el temor de Estados Unidos de que Alemania pudiera conseguir una base en el Caribe con los problemas laborales en las islas por el alza de precios de los alimentos.
Las negociaciones se mantuvieron en secreto entre las autoridades danesas y el entonces presidente de Estados Unidos, Woodrow Wilson. Finalmente, hubo un referéndum en diciembre de 1916 en Dinamarca donde ganó la opción de la venta. El 31 de marzo de 1917 se hizo efectivo.
En la negociación también entró en juego Groenlandia. En la declaración del acuerdo se decía que Estados Unidos “no estará en contra de que Dinamarca extienda sus intereses políticos y económicos a toda Groenlandia”. Fue el secretario de Estado Lansing quien lo manifestaba.

articles.title: Disney's new Star Wars robots use AI to react to guests in real time
articles.text:
First look: Walt Disney Imagineering R&D has built three small Star Wars robots that watch and listen to visitors and choose their own responses without a hidden puppeteer. The Audio-Animatronics prototypes are modeled on the Anzellan aliens from this year's film The Mandalorian and Grogu, and they send camera and microphone data to several AI models running on Amazon Web Services. Those models decide in the moment what each character says and how it moves, but every line and gesture they can pick from was written ahead of time by Disney's Imagineers.
The characters are named Vilo Vele, Kado Bre'a and Jibu Bre'a. Their first public appearance will be at AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas later this month, where conference attendees can interact with them. Disney has not committed to a park debut. However, the characters and the technology behind them could eventually show up in Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge and other attractions.
The project changes how Disney's animatronics have worked for decades. Since the first Audio-Animatronics figures sang in Disneyland's Enchanted Tiki Room, the company's figures have mostly performed choreographed shows that run the same sequence every time. Even the most lifelike recent figures either follow predefined routines or rely on an operator out of view. The Olaf robot Disney introduced recently is an example of the second approach, since a handler drives it with a Steam Deck.
The Anzellans have no handler. Each figure carries hidden cameras and microphones that capture what guests do and say. That input goes to AWS cloud servers, where the processing is divided between models of different sizes.
A fast-decision model handles split-second reactions, such as making a character lock eyes with a guest who has just walked up, so the figure appears to be paying attention. Larger models work more slowly and plan longer exchanges by weighing the wider context of the interaction.
That split addresses the hardest problem for any interactive character: timing. If a guest waves and the robot reacts a second late, the illusion falls apart. Disney says each part of the system has been tuned for latency so the characters respond fast enough to feel natural.
Running the heavier reasoning in the cloud while a lightweight model covers immediate reactions lets the figures seem responsive while still drawing on more compute for decisions that can wait.
The characters also respond to each other, not just to guests. In one scenario Disney describes, a visitor approaches and all three figures turn at once. One speaks in a mix of English and the Anzellan language, another blinks and tilts its head, and the third studies the guest before saying, "we have something special for you."
What the system does not do is just as important as what it does. The AI never generates new speech or motion. Instead, it selects from prerecorded audio clips, which are played back alongside dynamic animations. Imagineers wrote every line of dialogue and designed every movement, including personality quirks that make each Anzellan distinct. The models decide which piece of material to use and when, but they cannot step outside the script.
That design keeps the characters on-brand and predictable for the people who built them, which matters for a company protective of its intellectual property. Disney summed up the goal this way: "The result is a set of characters that surprise the guest, without surprising its creators or artists." The approach also avoids the risks of open-ended generative AI in a family theme park, where an unscripted line from a Star Wars character could become a public relations problem.
The prototypes build on an existing business relationship. AWS already serves as a public cloud infrastructure provider for Disney+, and the Anzellan project takes that partnership from streaming into physical, guest-facing entertainment. AWS supplies the cloud and AI capabilities that handle each character's sensing and decision-making, while Disney controls the creative content the system draws on.
The re:Invent demonstration will be the first chance to see how well the system performs with real crowds. A conference floor is noisy and unpredictable, and it will test whether the fast-decision layer can keep reactions feeling immediate when many people are competing for the characters' attention. If it works, Disney will have a template for park characters that behave differently with each visitor while performing only material its artists have approved.

articles.title: Mouse fight club might explain why we like to watch violent things
articles.text:
There’s something about watching violent events that broadly appeals to us, whether it’s the latest John Wick movie, a video game, or a live UFC bout. Scientists have debated whether watching violent things could make us more aggressive, but it could also be an adaptive survival strategy. Male mice, for instance, who watched other mice fighting learned enough about how to fight to better protect themselves (compared to mice who didn’t watch fights) when pitted against stronger, more aggressive opponents, according to a paper published in the journal Nature.
The team randomly assigned male mice to three groups—fighters, spectators, or novices—and then subjected each group to eight days of training with three 10-minute sessions per day. The novices played with stuffed mice in isolation, while the spectators watched various pairs of fighter mice battle from a raised platform behind a transparent barrier—a set-up chosen to let them smell and listen to the fights as well as observe them.
The ninth day was “fight night,” when all the mice had to face a daunting opponent in three 4-minute rounds. Each fight was filmed from above so that the mouse behavior could be analyzed. To monitor corresponding changes in brain activity, the team engineered the rodents’ excitatory brain cells to glow green whenever they were activated, while inhibitory brain cells glowed red. They also implanted tiny optical fibers into 12 interconnected brain regions so they could track changing activity in every brain region simultaneously.
How did they get the mice to fight? “Mice are naturally territorial,” co-author Jorge Iravedra-Garcia of Princeton University told Ars. “A traditional behavioral assay that experimenters use is called resident intruder. You just drop mice that are bred to be slightly weaker, and a little bit more docile, into the home cage of strains we know are more on the aggressive side. Those strains are typically very good at just naturally evoking that behavior.”

articles.title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.
U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.
The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.
By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 17, 2026: Nvidia posts strong quarterly earnings, says it does not plan to reinstate Huang
Nvidia reported its quarterly earnings on Tuesday, which beat Wall Street expectations with $115.8 billion in revenue, up 103% year-over-year. Despite the unknowns the company faces without Huang involved, interim CEO Colette Kress said that full-year revenue is also on track to exceed expectations. The company also plans to raise its outlook for the 2028 fiscal year, indicating confidence that this unexpected leadership change won’t get in the way of its trajectory.
“We have the best technologists on the planet with a world-class multi-year roadmap,” Kress said. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual. We’ve engaged with our customers, we’ve engaged with our suppliers, our partners. They’re all 100% behind us.”
Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones affirmed that the company is not considering reinstating Huang. Kress also said that Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.
November 17, 2026: Huang says he sees ‘outpouring’ of calls for him to return, says he ‘would be honored’ to return as CEO
Jensen Huang posted his first public statement since he admitted to having an extramarital affair more than a week earlier.
“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.
Many of Huang’s colleagues in the tech industry, including Elon Musk, Anduril founder Palmer Luckey, and Y Combinator President and CEO Garry Tan, have called for his return.
November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang as ‘broken’
More reports continue to roll out that illustrate the shock and severity of Huang’s resignation from Nvidia.
Bloomberg reported that Huang looked “broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted” by the time he surrendered his role on Wednesday night, uttering phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”
Separately, The Wall Street Journal reported that Huang had been critical of his CFO and current interim CEO, Colette Kress. Huang is said to have described Kress as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation this summer, and he had described Kress as someone who could not help him steer strategy or decision-making.
November 12, 2026: Democrats launch investigation into Nvidia; Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick summoned to testify before Senate Banking Committee
In a scathing letter sent to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Representative Richard Neal (D-MA) and Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) said they will investigate how the Trump administration handled Nvidia’s chip sales to China, especially after Trump was briefed about Huang’s relationship with a purported Chinese spy.
“Although [Lutnick] and President Trump were reportedly briefed on this intelligence, the Administration did not appear to acknowledge this evident national security threat. On the contrary: despite reportedly learning of Mr. Huang’s compromising relationship last fall, President Trump granted Nvidia permission to sell its advanced H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a cut of the export sales,” the letter states.
That same evening, Senator Tim Scott (R-SC) requested that Huang and Lutnick both testify before the Senate Banking Committee.
“The American people deserve answers,” Scott wrote on X.
November 12, 2026: Huang was having a third affair with another Nvidia employee, according to Reuters
After Huang was already ousted from Nvidia, we continued to learn more incriminating claims about the former CEO. According to Reuters, Huang had a third affair with an additional, unnamed employee of Nvidia.
November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigns, CFO Colette Kress named as interim CEO; Huang agrees to testify before Congress
Nvidia said its board had accepted Huang’s resignation on Wednesday. The company’s current CFO, Colette Kress, will take over as interim CEO while still fulfilling her CFO duties. Nvidia is expected to conduct a larger search to determine a permanent successor to Huang.
Harvey C. Jones, a managing partner of Square Wave Ventures and former CEO of Synopsys, was appointed as the company’s first-ever chair of the board of directors. Jones has been on Nvidia’s board since 1993.
Later in the day, Huang confirmed that he would testify in Congress at some point before Thanksgiving, which falls on November 26.
“Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but Nvidia is a very important company to the United States of America,” House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said to reporters. “I don’t want to see anything hurt in Nvidia, but he has some very serious questions to answer.”
The testimony is expected to take place behind closed doors, but Mast believes the briefing will be recorded and transcribed.
November 11, 2026: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
After reports of a second extramarital affair, Nvidia’s board reportedly plans to meet to discuss Huang’s future at the company, per The Wall Street Journal. Stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and is down 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said. The company has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
November 11, 2026: Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, NYT says
The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also had an affair with Nvidia vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to the CEO.
According to the report, Huang and Powell were captured on film “being affectionate” at a hotel during a conference earlier this year.
November 11, 2026: Congress plans to subpoena Huang to answer questions about affair
Huang has not responded to a request from three Republican congressmen to appear for a closed-door briefing for questioning about his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. House China Committee Chairman John Moolenaar said Wednesday on Fox Business that if Huang doesn’t agree to the briefing, he’ll likely be subpoenaed.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: Anthropic: dona do Claude estreia na bolsa valendo US$ 1,5 trilhão • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Anthropic: dona do Claude estreia na bolsa valendo US$ 1,5 trilhão
Famosa pelo Claude, empresa de inteligência artificial chega à bolsa dos EUA com ações cotadas a US$ 83, um valor notável.
Esta quinta-feira (19/11) registra um momento histórico para a Anthropic: a empresa especializada em inteligência artificial realiza, hoje, a sua oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês). A estreia na bolsa (Nasdaq) ocorre com a companhia tendo um valor de mercado estimado em US$ 1,5 trilhão (R$ 8,86 trilhões).
Um número tão grande é efeito, em parte, da valorização do preço por ação. Inicialmente, esperava-se que cada papel custasse algo entre US$ 70 e US$ 78, mas o preço individual ficou em US$ 83 na estreia. Tamanho ajuste na precificação inicial indica que há mais investidores interessados em comprar as ações da Anthropic do que o previsto.
980 milhões de ações foram oferecidas nesta IPO. Considerando o preço individual de US$ 83, isso representa um montante de US$ 81,3 bilhões em valor bruto. Desse total, cerca de US$ 80 bilhões irão para os cofres da Anthropic, enquanto o restante ficará com acionistas anteriores que aproveitaram a estreia para vender parte de suas ações.
Não termina aí. A Anthropic também está realizando uma operação fechada de venda de ações, esta direcionada a investidores institucionais e parceiros estratégicos, que incluem big techs como Google, Nvidia e Microsoft. A arrecadação desta operação é estimada em US$ 26 bilhões.
Se somarmos a IPO e a operação fechada, a arrecadação bruta com a venda de ações chega a notáveis US$ 107,3 bilhões.
É curioso pensarmos no valor de mercado de US$ 1,5 trilhão porque ele vem de uma empresa que tem custos operacionais elevados. E, pelo menos até o momento, a Anthropic não dá lucro. Para você ter ideia, a companhia encerrou o terceiro trimestre de 2026 com prejuízo operacional de US$ 567 milhões.
Por outro lado, a empresa registra receitas expressivas. Ainda considerando apenas o terceiro trimestre do ano, a receita da Anthropic ficou em quase US$ 17 bilhões. Isso se deve ao interesse cada vez maior de usuários individuais e organizações por soluções de IA da família Claude.
Em linhas gerais, os investidores veem potencial para que a Anthropic ganhe ainda mais destaque no mercado e, finalmente, se torne lucrativa.

articles.title: Ukraine deploys homemade 'flying modems' in daring drone attack to destroy Crimean Bridge, ditching Elon Musk's Starlink — airborne relay stations allow pilots to dodge Russian air defences to deliver 1,200kg payload
articles.text:
Ukraine deploys homemade 'flying modems' in daring drone attack to destroy Crimean Bridge, ditching Elon Musk's Starlink — airborne relay stations allow pilots to dodge Russian air defenses to deliver 1,200kg payload
Ukraine used a network of so-called "flying modems" to maintain a live video feed of the attack despite Russia's attempts to jam the signal.
Ukrainian forces ditched Elon Musk's Starlink wireless system and used their own relay network of "flying modems" to maintain a live feed of an attack on the Crimean Bridge, even amid Russian attempts to block the signal. The attack, which led to the partial collapse of the bridge, was significant for a number of reasons. The bridge is one of Russian President Vladimir Putin's most symbolic assets due to its linking of the occupied Crimean Peninsula and Russia. But perhaps more importantly, the attack's use of Ukrainian connectivity technology highlights the country's lessening of its reliance on Starlink. The modems were crucial to the success of the mission, with the FT reporting that they kept missiles connected to their pilots while they manoeuvred through Russia's air defenses.
Videos of the attack showed Flamingo missiles, carrying a 1,200kg warhead, being remotely piloted towards the bridge. Flamingo missiles are capable of traveling at around 590 miles per hour, requiring a stable and reliable video feed. It's reported that the Ukrainians deliberately chose not to use Starshield, the military version of Musk's Starlink, for the operation, with the company's satellite network having been restricted in recent weeks. That restricted service would have been insufficient for the Crimean Bridge attack, forcing Ukrainian forces to find another solution. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said this week that he has not been told why Starlink's connection has been throttled, with neither the White House nor the Pentagon being forthcoming. SpaceX, Starlink's parent company, has also so far not provided any explanation. However, relations between Zelenskyy and Musk appear to be strained, with the SpaceX CEO saying that Ukraine had "gone too far" by striking Russian data centers.
With Starlink, or Starshield, no longer fit for Ukraine's needs, it turned to the "flying drones" instead. The flying communications towers were used as a relay, boosting the signal sent from individual missiles so that it could more readily reach their pilots. This approach allowed the weapons to fly farther while still maintaining a reliable connection, allowing them to bypass Russian air defense systems and attempts to block their signals in the process. Without the relays, Ukrainian drone pilots have previously had to program missiles with coordinates and then rely on their autopilot system. They were inevitably shot down because they could not be steered away from Russian defenses.
Perhaps ironically, Ukraine isn't the first country to use flying communications towers. Russian forces were using similar technology as early as 2023, before the system began using a Chinese mesh networking system.

articles.title: Seagate’s shuckable 20TB desktop hard drive is down to $500
articles.text:
Seagate’s shuckable 20TB Expansion desktop hard drive drops to $500 ahead of Black Friday
An early Black Friday price cut on one of our favorite desktop hard drives for work and media backups
When it comes to desktop hard drives , Seagate remains one of our favorite picks - notably, the Expansion line, which comes in a range of capacities. But for serious storage, I recommend the 20TB version for archiving, business use, and media backups.
The cheapest I can find it is direct from Seagate, where the Expansion Desktop 20TB is down to $500 (was $630). That works out at around 2.75 cents per usable gigabyte once the drive is formatted. At Newegg, it's still selling for $700, while it's $730 at Amazon. So the manufacturer is offering the best deal ahead of Black Friday.
This hard drive unit gives you plenty of disk-based storage for backups, expanding a desktop's capacity, or consolidating large files. It’s also an ideal option if you need somewhere to archive years’ worth of photos or videos. It's also shuckable - which is great for NAS and home server builders looking to prise open the enclosure and slot their own SATA drive inside (warranty be damned!).
Today’s best Seagate Expansion 20TB hard drive deal
The 20TB model is cheaper from Seagate than anywhere else I've seen right now. Featuring fast USB 3.0 transfer speeds, it's compatible with Windows, macOS, and ChromeOS. The unit also comes with Seagate's Rescue Data Recovery Services software for additional backup protection.
Why we recommend the Seagate Expansion 20TB
Reliability and that huge storage capacity are the two main reasons why we recommend the Seagate Expansion Desktop Drive.
But what I especially like is the simple plug-and-play nature of the device. Connecting over USB, it's a case of connecting it to your Windows, Mac, or Chromebook and you're ready to start backing up.
It includes Seagate Rescue Data Recovery Services, alongside a two-year limited warranty. It's also worth noting that this isn't a portable drive. There's no BUS-power here, so it uses an external power adapter, which is included. For a home office setup, it's ideal.
Price context and historical value
At $499.99, the drive comes to about $27.47 per usable terabyte after formatting, which makes this a very tempting option for large-scale desktop storage, backup, and expansion.
As I've noted, this is the cheapest price I've found on the drive, which is being sold for over $200 more at Newegg and Amazon. And for comparison, Newegg has the 16TB model priced at $450. So, for the extra $50, you're gaining an additional 4TB storage.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Seagate Expansion if… you need a large and reliable desktop drive for backups, media, and long-term storage
❌ Skip the Seagate Expansion if… you need portable storage or fast SSD-level transfer speeds.

articles.title: 138 km/h sur une trottinette électrique : la police saisit deux bolides hors normes
articles.text:
Lors d’un contrôle de routine ciblant la circulation sur les pistes cyclables espagnoles, les forces de l’ordre de Valence sont tombées sur un véhicule « tuné » un peu spécial. Passées sur le dynamomètre de la police, deux trottinettes électriques ont affolé le compteur en grimpant jusqu’à 138 km/h, pulvérisant ainsi de plus de cinq fois la limite légale de 25 km/h.
Un débridage inquiétant des trottinettes
Après analyse, les forces de l’ordre ont constaté que le matériel d’origine de la trottinette avait été profondément modifié. Pour atteindre de telles pointes de vitesse, les propriétaires n’ont pas hésité à greffer sur leurs trottinettes électriques des composants directement issus du monde de la course automobile, totalement inadaptés à une utilisation sécurisée sur la voie publique. Plus inquiétant encore, ces modifications ne sont pas si complexes à effectuer. Certains revendeurs spécialisés commercialisent en effet ces modèles apparemment conformes, mais qui intègrent un système de restriction qu’il est possible de désactiver à distance en quelques secondes via une simple télécommande ou une application sur son smartphone.
 Voir cette publication sur Instagram
À une telle vitesse sur un châssis léger et dépourvu d’équipements de protection adéquats, le moindre obstacle ou écart de trajectoire peut avoir de graves conséquences. Les autorités rappellent ainsi qu’à 138 km/h, ces véhicules ne représentent pas seulement un danger pour leur conducteur, mais constituent également une menace directe pour les piétons, les cyclistes et les autres usagers de la route.
Des amendes salées pour les conducteurs
Les deux engins ont été confisqués et retirés de la circulation sur-le-champ, et leurs conducteurs devront régler des contraventions pouvant atteindre 500 euros chacun. À cette somme déjà conséquente viendront s’ajouter des sanctions financières complémentaires spécifiquement liées aux modifications apportées aux véhicules.
À lire : Test Xiaomi Electric Scooter 6 Ultra : la trottinette électrique ultime à moins de 800 euros ?
Mais les autorités ne s’arrêtent pas seulement aux utilisateurs croisés sur la route. Une enquête a en effet été ouverte contre les commerces et boutiques spécialisées qui vendent ces modèles modifiés et fournissent les outils de déverrouillage. Les forces de l’ordre suspectent ces établissements de violer la réglementation relative à la protection des consommateurs en distribuant du matériel dangereux pour leurs utilisateurs.

articles.title: TCL C1 : ce vidéoprojecteur Full HD compact, qui projette des images au plafond, ne dépasse pas les 200 € pendant le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Après avoir fait ses preuves sur le marché des téléviseurs, TCL entend également s’imposer sur celui des vidéoprojecteurs. À ce jour, la marque commercialise trois modèles en France : l’original PlayCube, l’honorable A1s et enfin le C1, le plus abordable des trois (299 euros au lancement en mai, contre 399 euros pour l’A1s et 799 euros pour le PlayCube). C’est justement ce dernier qui nous intéresse à l’approche du Black Friday. Ce modèle compact, facilement transportable et orientable est proposé à moins de 200 euros.
Les atouts du TCL C1
- Un modèle léger et orientable
- Des images Full HD jusqu’à 120 pouces
- Google TV
Auparavant proposé à 299,99 euros, le TCL C1 est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 199,99 euros sur Amazon.
Un vidéoprojecteur qui s’installe rapidement
Le TCL C1 est tout d’abord un modèle très compact (13,8 x 14,5 x 23,1 cm) qui affiche en prime un poids contenu de 1,77 kg. Ce vidéoprojecteur peut donc être déplacé d’une pièce à l’autre sans problème. Il est par ailleurs posé sur un support inclinable à 285°, qui lui permet notamment de projeter des images au plafond. Ce support, ramené vers le haut, peut également servir de poignée pour transporter l’appareil. Attention, ce modèle n’intègre pas de batterie. Il doit donc être branché sur une prise secteur pour fonctionner.
Côté connectique, le C1 embarque un port HDMI 2.1, pour brancher une console par exemple, un port USB-A et une prise jack 3,5 mm pour connecter un casque filaire ou une enceinte externe. Il prend aussi en charge le Wi-Fi 5 et le Bluetooth 5.1. Concernant l’installation du vidéoprojecteur, le C1 dispose de plusieurs fonctions automatiques d’ajustement de l’image. Il propose ainsi la mise au point, la détection des obstacles, la correction du trapèze ainsi que l’ajustement de l’image à l’écran. De quoi profiter, en théorie, d’images nettes et bien rectangulaires.
Image Full HD, son Dolby Audio et Google TV
Le TCL C1 s’appuie sur une source lumineuse LED, dont la durée de vie dépasse les 30 000 heures, selon la marque. Son moteur optique est par ailleurs entièrement fermé, ce qui limite l’infiltration de poussière et contribue à préserver ses performances dans le temps. Une fois allumé, ce modèle peut projeter des images jusqu’à 120 pouces et affiche une résolution native Full HD (1 920 x 1 080 pixels). Mais il peut aussi prendre en charge des contenus jusqu’en 4K, qu’il adapte à sa définition native.
Côté luminosité, le C1 offre seulement 230 lumens ISO. On vous conseille donc de regarder vos contenus dans une pièce plongée dans le noir. TCL a aussi intégré sa technologie TrueHue, qui, selon la marque, ajuste automatiquement la luminosité, le contraste et la couleur image par image. Côté audio, le C1 renferme un haut-parleur de 8 W avec la technologie Dolby Audio. Sachez d’ailleurs que le vidéoprojecteur peut également faire office d’enceinte Bluetooth. Enfin, le TCL C1 tourne sous Google TV et offre un accès direct aux applications de streaming, sans avoir besoin de clé ou de box TV.

articles.title: Panique chez Meta : l’agent IA Muse serait un véritable cauchemar pour la vie privée des utilisateurs
articles.text:
Un vent de panique circule dans les rangs de Meta. D’après des documents internes, son agent phare, Muse, fouille des messages privés et fait peser un doute sur la protection des données de ses utilisateurs. Voici tout ce que l’on sait.
Lancé en septembre, Muse a trouvé son public en un temps record avec une ascension fulgurante. Sa promesse : accomplir toute une ribambelle de tâches à la place de l’utilisateur, qu’il s’agisse de répondre aux e-mails, de réserver un restaurant ou de faire des achats en ligne. Il représente la réponse tant espérée par Mark Zuckerberg pour venir concurrencer les OpenAI, Anthropic et Google. Mais cette montée en puissance ne se fait visiblement pas sans écarts, révèle une enquête édifiante de Reuters.
Les alertes internes se multiplient
L’agence de presse a en effet pu consulter de nombreux messages internes échangés entre les employés du géant des réseaux sociaux, spécifiquement dans un groupe où ils signalent les problèmes à l’équipe qui développe l’agent. Le constat est glaçant : Ils y décrivent une intelligence artificielle qui prend la parole sans qu’on le lui demande, et dont certains messages ne semblent pas leur être adressés.
Par exemple, un employé qui discutait météo et marées avec Muse a reçu, sans rien demander, les soldes de deux comptes bancaires qui n’étaient pas les siens. Sa collègue a eu droit à un rappel pour répondre à un message de sa sœur sur Signal, messagerie chiffrée qu’elle n’avait jamais connectée à l’agent. « Cela ressemble à une atteinte extrême à la vie privée. Je ne lui ai certainement pas donné accès à d’autres applications », a-t-elle écrit.
Une troisième personne s’est vue proposer de contacter le vendeur d’une table basse qui n’était pas la sienne, suggérant une potentielle fuite de données entre comptes. Et ce n’est pas tout, car certains y auraient même laissé de l’argent. Un salarié a ainsi vu l’abonnement d’assurance de son chien grimper de 200 à 888 dollars par mois, tandis qu’un autre s’est retrouvé avec une réservation Airbnb non remboursable validée sans son accord.
Un problème qui dépasse Meta
Alors que ces incidents sont survenus dès septembre, et se sont poursuivis jusqu’à novembre, Daniel Roberts, porte-parole de Meta, évoque des « incidents isolés » résultant d’hallucinations, pas de fuites de données.
Mais pour en avoir le cœur net, Reuters a contacté Signal et l’AI Now Institute, un organisme qui étudie l’impact de l’IA sur la société. Et leurs tests ont démontré que l’agent peut effectivement lire des messages en contournant l’outil de connexion prévu par Meta. Sur Android, il passerait par l’accès aux notifications, une permission accordée dès l’installation et qui serait activée par défaut. Si les requêtes sont bloquées sur iPhone, l’IA détournerait les outils d’accessibilité conçus pour les personnes en situation de handicap sur Mac.
Dans ce contexte, Meredith Whittaker, présidente de Signal, accuse Meta d’avoir lancé Muse « sans montrer le moindre respect pour la vie privée ou la cybersécurité de base ». Elle exige que les applications puissent purement refuser les agents IA, et que les systèmes d’exploitation fassent respecter cette règle. Pour sa part, Apple a déployé une mise à jour de macOS qui limite l’usage de ces outils d’accessibilité et crée des permissions dédiées aux agents.
Mais dans ses conditions d’utilisation, Meta rend l’utilisateur responsable des actions de Muse. Ces nouvelles dérives risquent malgré tout d’entacher la réputation de l’entreprise, une habituée des scandales liés à la vie privée. Car de nombreux abus ont également été constatés avec l’utilisation de ses lunettes connectées.
- Tâches complètes de bout en bout
- Contrôles d’accès très détaillés
- Travail autonome en arrière-plan

articles.title: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September
articles.text:
Broadcom has released security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server, a management platform organizations use to manage VMware virtualized environments.
According Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a vulnerable vCenter Server to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.
Successful exploitation can allow attackers to obtain administrative access to vCenter, giving them control over the virtual machines managed by the server.
Broadcom patched the vulnerability on November 19 in VMSA-2026-0009, which also fixes four other vulnerabilities affecting VMware SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows.
"You are affected if you are running any version of VMware vCenter, SDDC Manager, or VMware Tools for Windows prior to the versions listed as "fixed" in the VMSA," Broadcom's security advisory reads.
"This includes vCenter and SDDC Manager deployed standalone and as part of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Telco Cloud Platform, and VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure, as well as VMware Tools installed in Windows virtual machines."
The company considers the vCenter vulnerability as an emergency update, urging organizations to install the patches as soon as possible.
Broadcom says there are no official workarounds for the vulnerabilities, although network restrictions and firewall controls can help reduce exposure.
Furthermore, the vulnerability affects vCenter regardless of whether Enhanced Linked Mode is enabled.
While Broadcom has not confirmed that the flaw was exploited, researchers at Google's Mandiant have documented attacks exploiting CVE-2026-123890.
Chinese hackers exploited VMware zero-day
In a report published today, Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) revealed that a suspected Chinese state-sponsored hacking group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-123890 in early September 2026.
"Successful exploitation results in a remote authentication bypass which creates an authenticated session established as administrator@vsphere.local," explains Mandiant.
"Using the authenticated administrator session, the attacker can execute arbitrary commands and acquire files, including the data.mdb database, by leveraging the vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC interface vmdirdbcp."
Armory Castle is a cyberespionage group known for exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in enterprise network appliances, including Citrix NetScaler and Ivanti Connect Secure devices, to breach corporate networks and deploy custom malware.
The group was also recently linked to attacks exploiting a BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-102764, which has been exploited since late August.
Mandiant says the VMware exploitation was part of the same intrusion campaign, with the attackers first compromising BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances before moving laterally into internal Linux systems and targeting VMware infrastructure.
After gaining access to an internal Linux appliance, the hackers deployed the "SLIMSAVAGE" web shells to maintain persistent access, escalated privileges to root, and scanned the internal network for VMware systems.
The attackers then used a custom Golang exploitation tool named BONESAW to exploit CVE-2026-123890 and compromise a VMware vCenter Server.
Mandiant observed the tool successfully creating a vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO) administrator account and stealing the server's directory database, which can be used to extract further credentials.
BONESAW can also extract SAML signing keys, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens and gain administrative access to VMware environments.
Following the exploitation, the hackers deployed another tool called SAWSNAKE, which enables so-called Golden SAML attacks to forge authentication tokens, bypass multifactor authentication, and impersonate legitimate users.
During the attack, the attackers also deployed additional web shells and backdoors, including CAGEMATCH, BEARBONES, and LAZYBONES, to execute commands, transfer files, steal credentials, and maintain access to compromised systems.
The attacks ultimately allowed Armory Castle to move deeper into the victims' virtualized environments, access ESXi hosts, and extract sensitive information from virtual machines, including Windows Active Directory database files.
Mandiant says the use of two zero-day vulnerabilities in the same campaign, along with multiple malware families tailored to the targeted platforms, demonstrates the threat actor's technical expertise.
The researchers urge admins to apply the VMware security updates as soon as possible and configure additional security controls to protect their virtualization infrastructure against future attacks.

articles.title: Con un tubo y botellas de plástico, un estudiante chino de 14 años crea la solución perfecta para “fabricar” agua en el desierto
articles.text:
En las zonas áridas de Mongolia Interior (norte de China) es complicado que puedan sobrevivir los nuevos árboles debido a la escasez de agua. A Jia Mingxuan no le era ajeno este problema. De ahí que quisiera desarrollar un dispositivo que ayudara a regar. Con él ha ganado una medalla de oro juvenil en la feria de inventos de Núremberg con solo 14 años.
Tiene su origen en un momento en el que su madre estaba cocinando. Vio cómo el vapor formaba gotas de agua en los azulejos. Recordó lo que había estudiado en física sobre condensación y decidió aplicarlo para extraer humedad del aire y llevarla a la raíz de los árboles. Empezó con unos tubos de acero (de una ferretería) y unas botellas de plástico (que tenía usadas).
El tubo necesitó algo más que aire
Por medio de una caperuza situada en la parte superior, se dirigía el aire al interior de un tubo enterrado. El objetivo era aprovechar la diferencia de temperatura entre la superficie y el subsuelo para que se produjera la condensación de vapor y así llegara agua a la tierra. No se necesitaba ningún tipo de entrada de agua externa.
Sin embargo, en los primeros test no funcionó como esperaba. Tras cuatro intentos fallidos, añadió un dispositivo de condensación (recargable) para ayudar a generar esa diferencia de temperatura. Jia contó que entonces consiguió que se acumulase agua en el fondo.
Jia era interno y tenía que ir a 30 kilómetros de distancia a su casa para probar los prototipos. En alguna ocasión se tuvo que levantar a las 4 de la mañana para comprobar su dispositivo antes de volver a clase.
El objetivo es ayudar en la lucha contra la desertificación (en su región es importante ayudar a que sobrevivan los nuevos árboles en el proceso de reforestación). Una vez que obtuvo el premio, comenzó a trabajar con un equipo de Shanghái para seguir mejorándolo y hacerlo útil en zonas áridas.
