articles.title: Windows 11 : Microsoft va tuer son application To Do
articles.text:
Microsoft To Do vit ses derniers mois. L’application de gestion de tâches de Microsoft baissera le rideau à compter du 30 juin 2027. Microsoft vient de l’annoncer officiellement sur une de ses pages de support repérée par Windows Lastest. Si la firme de Redmond suggère aux utilisateurs professionnels de migrer vers Planner (aucune migration automatique n’est prévue), elle n’offre aucune solution de secours aux utilisateurs grand public. Microsoft To Do ne sera pas remplacé.
Microsoft tue Wunderlist une deuxième fois
La fin annoncée de Microsoft To Do va laisser, encore une fois, un goût amer aux utilisateurs. Car l’application de gestion de tâche de Microsoft était la digne héritière de Wunderlist, une application que Microsoft avait rachetée courant 2015, avant de supprimer celle-ci au profit de sa remplaçante, Microsoft To Do, qui avait été développée par l’équipe de Wunderlist.
La mort annoncée de Microsoft To Do pose désormais un sérieux problème aux utilisateurs, qu’ils soient grand public ou professionnels. Microsoft n’a en effet prévu aucune solution de remplacement pour les premiers. Le grand public devra en effet impérativement se tourner vers une solution tierce, Microsoft n’ayant prévu aucun transfert vers Planner, même pour les abonnés payants à Microsoft 365 Personnel ou Famille.
Les utilisateurs professionnels quant à eux auront la possibilité de transférer leurs tâches dans Microsoft Planner, mais la migration vers cet outil ne se fera pas automatiquement. Microsoft, qui a néanmoins promis qu’elle fournirait un outil permettant d’exporter les données To Do avant le retrait des différentes applications, tout en assurant que cet export n’assurait pas la possibilité de réimporter les données dans Planner.
Une régression majeure pour les utilisateurs professionnels
Les professionnels qui devront faire la transition entre Microsoft To Do et Microsoft Planner risquent de l’avoir mauvaise. Car les différences fonctionnelles entre les deux applications sont a priori conséquentes.
À titre d’exemple, Planner ne dispose d’aucune application de bureau native. Pour l’utiliser, il faudra donc soit passer par le Web ou par Microsoft Teams. Aucun accès hors ligne, comme c’est le cas avec Microsoft To Do, n’est prévu.
Par ailleurs Planner ne permet pas de configurer des rappels individuels programmables comme To Do. L’outil n’utilise en effet que des notifications basées sur les dates d’échéance des tâches. À noter également que Planner ne prend pas en charge les pièces jointes sur les tâches des plans privés.
Les futurs naufragés de Microsoft To Do dont vous faites peut-être partie ont encore quelques mois devant eux pour trouver une solution de remplacement. Il en existe plusieurs équivalentes à Microsoft To Do, comme Google Tasks, Super Productivity ou encore Vikunja.

articles.title: Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Fig Security partners with Elastic to show how data changes affect detection coverage
Security operations startup Fig Security Inc. today announced an integration partnership with Elastic N.V. that it says gives security teams visibility into how data changes affect their detection coverage.
The partnership sees Fig’s capabilities for mapping detection dependencies now integrating with Elastic Security, the open security operations platform from Elastic. The platform offers prebuilt integrations and detection rules to establish coverage from day one, with Fig claimed to help security operations engineers safeguard that coverage as their environments evolve.
Detection rules are dependent on data arriving in the structure they expect, including the fields and values needed to identify suspicious activity. According to Fig, those dependencies can break when changes are made in tools that the security team does not own. The resulting problem, which Fig calls drift, leaves rules active while the data feeding them is missing the information needed to catch an attack.
Once connected through a read-only application programming interface key, Fig’s Security Data Lineage feature maps an Elastic environment’s sources through pipelines, mappings and fields to the detection rules that use them. Any change to a source, pipeline or mapping is said to have Fig identify the affected detections, along with a suggested repair.
“Elastic gives security teams control over their data, and Fig gives them control over the engineering around it,” said Gal Shafir, co-founder and chief executive of Fig, who previously led global security architecture for Google Cloud Security. Teams are able to test each change against their own environment, he said, before shipping it as code.
Environments “never stop changing,” according to Jamie Hynds, director of product at Elastic, who said Fig traces those changes to the detection rules that depend on them so that SecOps teams can maintain their coverage.
Fig also works alongside Elastic’s Automatic Import and AI Agent, two features designed to help teams build new integrations and custom rules as their requirements grow. Changes tested in Fig against the organization’s own data can then be shipped as code using continuous integration and continuous delivery, with version control and one-click rollback included.
The integration is also aimed at organizations moving to Elastic Security from another security information and event management platform. After Elastic’s Automatic Migration has translated their existing detection rules, Fig checks each translated rule against the data available in Elastic ahead of cutover. Rules that need rework are flagged, with a recommended fix for each.
Founded in 2025 by Shafir, Nir Loya Dahan and Roy Haimof, Fig launched in March with $38 million in seed and Series A funding from Team8 and Ten Eleven Ventures. The company added an AI agent and software-style deployment tools to its platform in July.
The Fig and Elastic integration is available now, with demonstrations offered through Fig’s website.

articles.title: Google affirme que Gemini consomme très peu d’eau, mais la réalité est plus complexe
articles.text:
Selon Google, une requête adressée à Gemini ne consommerait que 5 gouttes d’eau. Mais ce chiffre ne tient pas compte d’un élément important.
Google est aux petits soins pour Gemini. Ses équipes ont récemment intégré l’agent Spark dans l’application Android de l’IA. Elles ont également déployé un nouveau modèle, Gemini 4 Argon, pour damer le pion à OpenAI et Anthropic et amélioré ses fonctions de synthèse vocale avec Gemini 3.8. Mais toutes ces évolutions ont un coût environnemental qu’il ne faut pas négliger.
Gemini ne consommerait que 5 gouttes d’eau par requête
Nos confrères de TechRadar se sont récemment penchés sur la consommation d’eau de Gemini : une étude technique publiée en août 2025 par Google indique à ce sujet qu’une requête ne consommerait que 0,24 Wh d’énergie et rejetterait 0,03g d’équivalent CO2. « L'impact énergétique par commande équivaut à regarder la télévision pendant moins de neuf secondes », peut-on notamment lire. Quant à la consommation d’eau, elle équivaudrait à seulement 0,26 millilitres d'eau soit 5 petites gouttes d’eau.
Mieux encore, Google se targue d’avoir divisé l’empreinte énergétique d’une requête par 33 en un an et son empreinte carbone par 44 tout en augmentant l’efficacité de ses modèles. « Nous sommes convaincus qu’il s’agit de l’évaluation la plus complète de cet impact », précise également la firme. Tout irait donc pour le mieux dans le meilleur des mondes.
Google n’aurait dévoilé que la partie émergée de l’iceberg
Pour ses calculs, Google a pris en compte les puces dédiées à l’IA, mais aussi les processeurs et la mémoire des serveurs, les machines en veille et le refroidissement. Cela vous semble complet ? Détrompez-vous : une information cruciale manque à l'appel.
Shaolei Ren, chercheur à l'université de Californie, estimait en 2023 qu’une requête IA adressée à GPT-3 consommait 500 ml d'eau. Ce même chercheur a remarqué que, dans ses calculs, Google s’était concentré sur l’eau utilisée pour refroidir les centres de données mais avait omis celle utilisée pour refroidir les centrales électriques qui les alimentent.
Ce qu’il faut bien comprendre ici, c’est que la consommation d’eau des centres de données ne se limite pas seulement à leur refroidissement. Il faut prendre en compte l'eau utilisée de façon directe mais aussi indirecte. Or ce dernier usage pèse lourd dans la balance. En France, par exemple, l’ARCEP a montré que les data centers ont utilisé 0,6 million de m3 d'eau potable en 2023. La production de leur électricité a, quant à elle, demandé 5,2 millions de m3 supplémentaires, soit près de neuf fois plus.
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau
On le sait, les centres de données ont un impact désastreux sur notre planète et plusieurs études dressent un tableau peu rassurant. On sait, par exemple, que la consommation électrique de Google a bondi de 37 % en 2025. La consommation globale des centres de données pourrait, quant à elle, doubler d’ici 2030.
Pour faire face à cet épineux problème, des initiatives commencent heureusement à voir le jour. Chez nos voisins espagnols, par exemple, un projet de décret souhaite imposer aux data centers d’utiliser 80 % d’électricité renouvelable, heure par heure. La commission européenne aimerait, quant à elle, noter les centres de données selon leur consommation. En France, la loi DDADUE impose aux centres de valoriser leur chaleur perdue.
Reste à savoir si ces mesures parviendront à limiter les dégâts.

articles.title: L'enceinte Sonos Play notée 9/10, aussi à l'aise dans le salon que dans le jardin, perd 70 € pour le Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
La Sonos Play est une enceinte saluée pour la qualité du son qu’elle diffuse, mais aussi son côté portable. Elle a décroché 9/10 lors de son test, notamment parce qu’elle reprend la philosophie de la Move 2 dans un format nettement plus compact et facile à transporter. Bonne nouvelle, avec le Black Friday, elle perd 70 euros chez Amazon, de quoi se faire plaisir (ou offrir) à l’approche des fêtes.
Les points forts de la Sonos Play
- L’architecture acoustique avec un haut-parleur de grave et deux tweeters indépendants
- Une double connectivité WiFi et Bluetooth avec multiroom et calibration automatique Trueplay
- La résistance IP67 avec batterie remplaçable et socle de recharge sans fil inclus
La Sonos Play est un beau petit produit tech qui est sorti à 349 euros en mars 2026. Mais jusqu’au 30 novembre, vous pouvez l’avoir à 279 euros sur Amazon.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant la Sonos Play. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Une enceinte compacte avec une bonne restitution sonore
On l’a dit plus haut : la Sonos Play reprend les grandes lignes esthétiques de la Move 2 mais dans un format plus facile à transporter : elle mesure 19,2 x 11,3 x 7,7 cm pour 1,3 kilogramme. Sa petite sangle en silicone intégrée permet de la transporter à la main ou de l’accrocher facilement à un support. Sa base souple évite aussi qu’elle glisse ou qu’elle abîme le meuble sur lequel elle est posée. Côté finition, elle propose une grille en aluminium anodisé avec des matériaux qui inspirent confiance. Elle bénéficie en plus d’une certification IP67, donc elle résiste à la poussière et supporte une immersion temporaire dans l’eau.
Mais c’est sur la qualité audio que Sonos cherche à se démarquer. La Sonos Play embarque un haut-parleur dédié aux basses et aux médiums, avec deux tweeters orientés vers les côtés pour élargir la diffusion des aigus. La dynamique est bien maîtrisée, même quand le volume augmente. Il faut toutefois accepter une limite physique : cette enceinte ne descend pas très bas dans les fréquences et ne peut pas rivaliser avec l’ampleur des basses de la Move 2. Mais vous pouvez associer deux Sonos Play pour profiter d’une véritable séparation stéréo, à condition de les connecter en WiFi.
WiFi, Bluetooth, Trueplay et batterie remplaçable
La Sonos Play joue surtout la carte de la double connectivité. À la maison, le WiFi donne accès au multiroom. La calibration automatique Trueplay est un vrai avantage : avec ses micros et ses capteurs, l’enceinte adapte automatiquement sa restitution à l’environnement. Vous pouvez donc la déplacer de pièce en pièce comme vous voulez, elle se débrouille pour adapter son rendu. L’application Sonos reste agréable à utiliser. Elle propose une égalisation simple (un réglage pour les basses, un pour les aigus) et une fonction Loudness qui renforce les fréquences extrêmes à faible volume. Côté commande vocale, elle est compatible Alexa et intègre aussi Sonos Voice Control, l’assistant maison.
Vous la sortez dehors ? La Sonos Play bascule en Bluetooth et peut fonctionner sans réseau WiFi. Elle dispose d’un port USB-C pour la recharge directe, qui peut aussi accueillir une entrée audio analogique avec un adaptateur vendu séparément. Ce port sert aussi à recharger votre smartphone : l’enceinte fait office de batterie externe.
Un socle de recharge sans fil est fourni, mais pas l’adaptateur secteur. Il faudra donc utiliser votre propre chargeur USB-C, entre 18 et 45 W. Sonos annonce jusqu’à 24 heures d’autonomie. Bon, notre test a démontré qu’en usage réel, avec le Loudness activé, on s’approche plutôt des 14 heures d’écoute à volume modéré. La bonne nouvelle, c’est qu’on peut remplacer la batterie sans outil, un bon point pour la durée de vie. Hors WiFi, vous pouvez quand même regrouper jusqu’à quatre Sonos Play ou Move 2 en Bluetooth pour diffuser la même musique en même temps, mais sans séparation stéréo.

articles.title: Sans l'aide de Rockstar, des scientifiques ont réussi à noyer une ville de GTA
articles.text:
Les joueurs n’ont d’yeux que pour Leonida, l’État fictif de GTA 6. Les premiers tests sont unanimes et le jeu, officiellement disponible depuis le 19 novembre 2026, livre déjà ses premiers secrets. Deux géoscientifiques sont pourtant retournés à Los Santos, la ville de GTA 5 calquée sur Los Angeles, pour la noyer sous les projections du Giec, le groupe d’experts du climat de l’ONU.
Paul Nörenberg, de l’université de Potsdam, et Hugues Lantuit, de l’Institut Alfred-Wegener (AWI), ont publié leur étude ce 17 novembre dans la revue Geoscience Communication, en pleine semaine de lancement du nouveau jeu de la saga, comme l’a relevé ScienceAlert. Ils y montrent que les quartiers du cinquième opus sont inondés dans le même ordre que ceux du vrai Los Angeles.
L’idée est bien antérieure à l’agitation actuelle autour de GTA 6. L’étude reprend en effet le mémoire de master de Paul Nörenberg, soutenu en 2020, sur l’épisode de 2013 de la saga Grand Theft Auto, vendu à plus de 225 millions d’exemplaires. Et le sujet n’a rien d’incongru pour la revue, éditée par l’Union européenne des géosciences : elle a déjà publié des travaux sur le réalisme des paysages de Zelda : Breath of the Wild ou sur la géologie d’Hokkaido dans Pokémon Legends : Arceus.
Comment noyer une ville qui n’existe pas ?
Rockstar a refusé de fournir ses données de terrain, au nom de ses droits d’éditeur. Les chercheurs se sont donc servis d’une carte 3D du jeu publiée par un fan sur le site Sketchfab, puis l’ont transformée en carte des altitudes dans un logiciel de cartographie. Pour régler les hauteurs, ils ont pris comme repère le mont Chiliad, point culminant du jeu à 798 mètres. Ils ont ensuite mesuré six pistes, ponts et routes avec le GPS du jeu, toujours au volant de la même berline, puis fixé le niveau de la mer à partir de 31 plages vérifiées en hélicoptère, dans le jeu.
Sur ce relief, ils ont appliqué deux scénarios du Giec aux horizons 2100, 2300 et 2500 : dans l’un, les émissions baissent fortement (RCP 2.6), dans l’autre, elles restent très élevées (RCP 8.5). Pour simuler une tempête, ils y ont ajouté la plus haute marée jamais mesurée à Los Angeles, 1,59 mètre le 10 janvier 2005. Avec des émissions élevées, l’eau monte à 5,18 mètres en 2300 et couvre 5,1 % des terres. En 2500, elle atteint 8,22 mètres et 6,5 % des terres, et le port, la station d’épuration et l’usine à gaz ne fonctionnent plus. Avec de fortes baisses d’émissions, en revanche, l’inondation s’arrête à 2,2 % des terres en 2300, sans toucher de grande infrastructure.
Un modèle simple qui surestime l’inondation
Ces chiffres sont pourtant à prendre avec prudence, et les auteurs le disent eux-mêmes. Leur modèle « en baignoire » remplit le relief jusqu’à un niveau fixe, sans simuler les vagues, l’érosion ni l’affaissement du sol, ce qui tend à surestimer l’inondation. « Ces cartes montrent quelles zones se trouvent sous ce niveau d’eau, pas où l’eau irait réellement », prévient Hugues Lantuit dans le communiqué de l’AWI. Le relief du jeu, précis à environ 2 mètres, ne tient pas non plus compte des bâtiments qui freineraient l’eau. Enfin, pour 2300 et 2500, les chercheurs ont retenu la fourchette haute de projections que le Giec juge peu fiables.
Alors, à quoi servent ces cartes ? Elles ne prédisent pas l’avenir de Los Angeles, car le jeu « ne peut pas remplacer un modèle d’élévation scientifique », reconnaît Hugues Lantuit. Les auteurs écartent aussi l’école, puisque GTA 5 est interdit aux moins de 18 ans, et orientent les enseignants vers des supports sous licence libre basés sur Minecraft. Ils pensent plutôt aux musées, aux vidéastes qui jouent déjà avec GTA 5 et à l’apprentissage de la lecture des cartes d’inondation, souvent mal comprises.

articles.title: Kickstarter-Hit Flipper One: Was du mit diesem kleinen Linux-Computer machen kannst
articles.text:
Flipper One: Dieses Linux-Multitool wird gerade zum Kickstarter-Hit
Es gibt Kickstarter-Kampagnen bei denen sich schnell abzeichnet, dass sie im Sand verlaufen und das jeweilige Produkt niemals wirklich das Licht der Welt erblicken wird – und es gibt das Projekt Flipper One. Nur zwei Tage nach ihrem Startschuss am 17. November hat die Kampagne schon das 46-Fache (Stand 19. November, 18:30 Uhr) ihres Finanzierungsziels erreicht. Mit 27 verbleibenden Tagen wird dieser Wert wohl noch deutlich weiter steigen.
Flipper One ist auf der Crowdfunding-Plattform also ein voller Erfolg. Grund genug, sich das kleine Gadget, um das es geht, einmal genauer anzuschauen.
Flipper One ist kein Nachfolger des Flipper Zero
Flipper One ist ein handlicher Linux-Computer, der als Netzwerk-Multitool genutzt werden kann. Der Hersteller Flipper Devices bezeichnet es als ein offenes Linux-Multitool für High-Performance-Computing und IP-Networking.
Anders als der Name vermuten lässt, handelt es sich nicht um ein Nachfolgemodell des Flipper Zero des Herstellers, den wir euch 2023 als Hacking-Tool vorgestellt haben. Stattdessen ist Flipper One ein eigenständiges Produkt, das allerdings ebenso nicht als Spielzeug konzipiert ist und in einer Vielzahl an Szenarien Anwendung finden kann.
Als Beispiele nennt der Hersteller etwa Netzwerkdiagnose oder auch Mediaplayer. Dazu ist der Flipper One mit allerhand Specs ausgestattet.
Diese Hardware und Anschlüsse bietet das Linux-Multitool
Das handliche Gadget, das 15,5 x 6,7 x 4 Zentimeter misst, wird von einem 8-Kern-ARM-Prozessor (RK3576) mit dedizierter NPU und GPU angetrieben. Als Betriebssystem läuft Flipper OS, das auf Debian Linux basiert, also quelloffen arbeitet. Das bedeutet, dass Nutzer:innen nach Lust, Laune und eigenen Fähigkeiten Apps und Anwendungen für den Flipper One entwickeln können.
Besonders ist die große Bandbreite in Sachen Anschlüsse, die kaum Wünsche für verschiedenste Anwendungsfälle offenlässt: Neben USB-C und HDMI-Ports verfügt der Flipper One auch über Gigabit-Ethernet-, PCIe-, SATA- und USB-3.0-Schnittstellen. Das Tool unterstützt Wi-Fi 6E, außerdem lässt es sich dank M.2-Slot beispielsweise um ein 5G-Modem oder ein LoRa Mesh-Networking-Funkmodul erweitern. Auf der Kickstarter-Seite wird zudem ein SDR-Radio-Modul (Software Defined Radio) als Erweiterung angekündigt.
Wichtig zu beachten ist, dass der Flipper One im Gegensatz zum Zero nicht auf NFC, RFID, Infrarot und Sub-1GHz-Frequenzen setzt.
Wann der Flipper One ausgeliefert werden soll
Laut Hersteller sind etwa 90 Prozent der technischen Spezifikationen final, Änderungen sind aber weiterhin möglich. Eine Auflistung aller Tech Specs findet sich auf der Website des Herstellers.
Auch ein Blick auf die Kampagnen-Seite bei Kickstarter lohnt sich, da Flipper Devices hier Anwendungsszenarien vorschlägt und alle Knöpfe, Anschlüsse und Kontrollleuchten im Detail zeigt und erklärt. Und auch die stetig kletternde Unterstützungssumme im zweistelligen Millionenbereich ist durchaus spannend zu beobachten.
Flipper Devices gibt an, dass die Auslieferung des Flipper One an Unterstützer:innen im Juli 2027 erfolgen soll. Angesichts der längst zigfach übertroffenen Zielsumme stehen die Chancen wohl gut, dass es wirklich zu Produktion und Auslieferung kommen wird. Die Kolleg:innen von Heise erinnern jedoch daran, dass der Flipper Zero trotz ebenfalls sehr guter Finanzierungskampagne erst ein Jahr später als angekündigt ausgeliefert wurde.
Wer selbst noch mit einsteigen möchte, hat noch bis zum 17. Dezember Zeit und kann sich das Multitool für 399 US-Dollar sichern. Bundles mit Erweiterungsmodulen werden ebenfalls angeboten.
! Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs
articles.text:
The PHP dev team released security updates for 18 vulnerabilities, including critical flaws that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on vulnerable servers.
The updates were released Thursday, November 19, for all supported PHP branches, with PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available.
Security firm Aikido reports that the updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP's core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components.
One of the most serious flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2.
According to Aikido, the flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute PHP code remotely on vulnerable servers that reuse connections to PHP-FPM under certain conditions.
The vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM.
Standard nginx and Apache configurations that do not reuse backend connections are not affected by the attack.
Other important vulnerabilities fixed in the updates include:
- CVE-2026-129474: A use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-129496: A timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-126714: A vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-115560: A session serializer mismatch vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution.
- CVE-2026-129291: A PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability that could lead to local privilege escalation.
- CVE-2026-128090: A PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability involving an algorithm downgrade.
Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and potentially unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs.
The releases follow a warning issued Wednesday by the PHP security team that the upcoming updates would address vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions, with the highest severity rated critical.
"The issues rated CRITICAL require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups," the PHP security team warned.
One of the vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-115560, was already disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory and relates to how PHP handles session data under certain configurations, potentially leading to remote code execution.
As a temporary mitigation, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restarting PHP workers. This setting was also recommended to mitigate the recent PHP2Shell flaws.
For CVE-2026-129289, administrators who cannot immediately install the security updates can mitigate the vulnerability by disabling persistent backend connections between their web servers and PHP-FPM, ensuring connections are closed after each request.
Aikido warns that these mitigations do not address all vulnerabilities fixed in the November updates and recommends ensuring PHP-FPM and LSAPI listeners are not directly exposed to untrusted networks.
Although the official security updates are limited to supported PHP branches, third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has also released patched packages for unsupported PHP versions dating back to PHP 5.6.
Aikido has similarly released hardened PHP container images containing backported security fixes for unsupported versions, including PHP 5.6, 7.0, 7.1, 7.2, 7.4, and 8.1.
PHP administrators are urged to upgrade to PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, or 8.2.36, depending on their supported branch, to address the newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

articles.title: El negocio circular de Anthropic: Amazon y Google son accionistas, proveedores y canal de venta a la vez
articles.text:
Anthropic sale por fin a bolsa en el Nasdaq, y su folleto de salida a bolsa, el S-1, ha puesto cifras a una relación muy peculiar. Amazon y Google...
- Son sus accionistas.
- También le venden la computación.
- Y también gestionan la tienda por la que pasa casi la mitad de lo que factura.
- Y las dos venden modelos que compiten con el suyo.
El rastro del dinero. Amazon y Google invierten en Anthropic, y Anthropic se gasta ese dinero en sus centros de datos. Además, los clientes de esas dos nubes contratan Claude desde su cuenta de siempre. Ganan por tres vías:
- Computación. Anthropic se ha comprometido a gastar unos 900.000 millones de dólares en infraestructura. Al menos 121.300 millones irán a Google y al menos 110.000 a Amazon. En el tercer trimestre, la computación se ha llevado el 58% de sus ingresos.
- Comisiones. En 2023, solo el 11% de los ingresos llegaban a través de los marketplaces de Amazon, Google y Microsoft. En el primer semestre de 2026 ha sido el 48%.
- Plusvalías. Tras la salida a bolsa tendrán cerca del 15% y del 14% del capital. Amazon ya se ha anotado unos 62.800 millones en el primer semestre por la revalorización de su participación.
Entre líneas. Sus acciones son de clase N y no tienen voto. Así que se quedan con la parte económica, pero no con el control, y a los reguladores les cuesta más ver ahí una toma de control encubierta. El regulador, la FTC, lo ha estudiado. El Departamento de Justicia llegó a pedir que Google vendiera su parte, pero luego se echó atrás.
Junto a la salida a bolsa hay una colocación privada de 26.000 millones. Entre los compradores están Google, NVIDIA, Broadcom, Microsoft, AMD, Micron y TSMC, casi todos tienen en común que son proveedores de Anthropic.
La amenaza. En esas tiendas, Claude compite con Gemini y con los modelos de Amazon. El propio prospecto lo incluye entre sus riesgos.
Sí, pero. Todo esto está publicado, y las empresas compran casi todo su software a través de su nube. Ningún cliente supera el 10% de los ingresos, y vender en tres nubes evita depender de una sola. Una cosa por la otra.
Y ahora qué. El momento es algo delicado. El FMI calcula que la financiación circular en la IA ya supera el billón de dólares, y que dos tercios son deuda. NVIDIA, la empresa que más ha practicado este modelo, acaba de perder a su fundador como CEO.
Quien compre acciones de clase A entrará en una empresa cuyos dos mayores accionistas no votan, pero sí que cobran por casi todo lo demás.

articles.title: How Nigerian startup Pocketfood is taking the hassle out of workplace meals - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Pocketfood is helping businesses organise, pay for and deliver meals to their employees through its corporate food management platform.
In 2022, Omolara Olarerin was struggling to find affordable and reliable lunch options while working in an office. She soon realised her colleagues were facing the same challenge and decided to do something about it.
“I realised my colleagues had the same problem, so I tested the idea with a simple online form, a weekly menu and one chef. We got our first orders through word of mouth,” Olarerin told Disrupt Africa.
That experiment became Pocketfood, which she founded in August 2022. Initially focused on individual meal subscriptions, the startup shifted to serving businesses in 2025 after identifying a bigger opportunity in corporate food management.
“We initially served individual subscribers before pivoting to B2B in 2025, where we saw a bigger opportunity to help companies manage staff meals,” she said.
Today, Pocketfood helps companies organise workplace meals without having to coordinate multiple restaurants, chase payments, monitor orders manually or manage the entire process themselves.
The startup has served more than 60 businesses and generated over NGN405 million (US$300,000) in revenue to date.
One platform for workplace meals
Through Pocketfood, companies can create a centralised meal programme for their teams. They can set meal budgets and delivery schedules, choose menus from vetted food vendors and decide how meal costs are shared between the company and its employees.
Employees can browse available meals, select their preferences and track their orders, while administrators can monitor spending, order history and vendor performance from a single dashboard.
The platform also offers flexible payment options, including employer-funded meal allowances and shared payments.
“Beyond the technology, Pocketfood manages the operational side of the service. We work with vetted food vendors, coordinate orders and delivery partners, monitor service quality and provide support to our corporate clients. This means businesses do not have to build their own catering infrastructure or manage several food suppliers independently,” Olarerin said.
The startup also supports one-off catering for meetings, team lunches and corporate events.
“In a nutshell, we are building the infrastructure that enables businesses to manage workplace food as a structured employee benefit rather than a daily operational headache. Our long-term ambition is to make workplace food management more accessible, reliable and scalable for businesses across Africa,” she said.
Building a business around a growing need
For many companies, managing staff meals can be a time-consuming process involving multiple food vendors, manual coordination and separate invoices.
“Companies often manage staff meals through multiple vendors, manual coordination and separate invoices. This creates unnecessary work for HR and operations teams, makes spending difficult to track and leaves employees with inconsistent meal options,” Olarerin said.
Pocketfood brings meal ordering, vendor management, budgeting, delivery coordination and payments into one platform. It also offers meal financing to help businesses manage food benefits more flexibly.
The startup competes with traditional caterers and food delivery platforms such as Chowdeck and Glovo, but Olarerin said its focus on corporate food management sets it apart.
“Most focus on food preparation or delivery. Our differentiation is the combination of a corporate food management dashboard, a vetted vendor network and meal financing,” she said.
Funding and traction
Pocketfood has raised around US$120,000 in pre-seed funding from Baobab Network and angel investors. Other key milestones include the acquisition of Balance Bowl, the expansion of its corporate offering, and the development of a network of business clients and food vendors.
“Uptake has grown steadily since we launched in 2022, with a network of corporate clients and vetted food vendors. Today, we’ve served over 60 businesses, helping them manage workplace meals more efficiently while connecting food vendors to recurring corporate demand,” Olarerin said.
Pocketfood currently serves businesses in Lagos, Abuja and Ibadan. Its immediate focus is on growing its corporate customer base, particularly among larger organisations, and strengthening partnerships with payroll providers, fintech companies and food vendors.
The startup makes money primarily by taking a commission on meals ordered through its platform, and also generates revenue from meal financing.
Lessons from a pivot
The road has not been without challenges, with Pocketfood’s original consumer model proving difficult to sustain.
“We started by delivering meal subscriptions to individuals, but rising food prices, currency devaluation, and customers leaving the country made it difficult to sustain that model. We had to rethink the business and pivot to corporate food management,” Olarerin explained.
Operations have been another major challenge, with food costs, delivery costs, unreliable logistics and the coordination of multiple vendors all able to “make or break a food business”. The team also had to learn how to sell to companies, which have different needs and longer decision-making processes than individual customers.
“These experiences taught us that having a good idea is not enough. You have to be willing to adapt, understand your customers deeply and build a business model that works in the market you operate in,” she said.
Backing from Women in Tech
Pocketfood was a participant in the Standard Chartered Foundation’s Women in Tech Accelerator. Implemented locally by the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC) with support from Village Capital, the multi-region programme supports impact-creating, tech-enabled, women-led startups across Africa, the Middle East and Pakistan.
“The programme gave us access to amazing business training, mentorship and a network of people who understand what it takes to build and scale a business,” Olarerin reflected. “It also gave me the opportunity to meet and learn from brilliant women founders who remain supportive friends to this day.”
“Being selected as one of the top five ventures and receiving a US$10,000 grant was a huge win for Pocketfood. The funding gave us additional resources to invest in the business, while the programme itself provided valuable learning and access to people who helped us think through our growth challenges.”
She would recommend the programme to other women founders.
“Building a business can be isolating, and access to the right support, networks and funding can make a real difference. My advice is to go in ready to learn, challenge your assumptions, and apply what you learn to your business,” Olarerin said.

articles.title: Rockstar explica por qué GTA 6 tendrá misiones menos rígidas que las entregas anteriores
articles.text:
GTA 6 cambiará la forma de afrontar las misiones al dar más libertad para completar objetivos y reducir los avisos de “Misión Fallida” cuando el jugador pruebe estrategias distintas. Rockstar Games explica que esta decisión busca borrar la separación entre las actividades del mundo abierto y los encargos principales de Jason y Lucía.
El cambio importa porque las entregas anteriores de Grand Theft Auto solían exigir acciones precisas durante determinadas misiones. En GTA 6, Rockstar pretende que cada jugador pueda usar vehículos, armas, rutas y tácticas de acuerdo con su propio estilo, dentro de un mundo abierto que abarca todo el estado ficticio de Leonida.
Rockstar quiere eliminar las fronteras entre misión y mundo abierto
Stephen Donkin, vicepresidente de diseño de Rockstar, explicó a GamesRadar+ que el equipo trabajó para “difuminar las líneas” entre las situaciones que ocurren dentro de una misión y las que suceden fuera de ella.
La idea afecta a la estructura de Grand Theft Auto VI. El jugador no tendrá que interpretar cada objetivo como una secuencia aislada del resto del mapa, sino como parte de un entorno donde puede recurrir a herramientas y situaciones presentes en Leonida.
Las misiones serán menos rígidas y admitirán distintas formas de resolver un mismo objetivo. Esa flexibilidad puede incluir el uso de rutas alternativas, vehículos disponibles en el escenario o respuestas diferentes ante los personajes que aparecen durante la partida.
El enfoque también busca reducir una situación habitual en juegos de mundo abierto: el aviso de fracaso por apartarse de una ruta que el diseño había marcado como obligatoria. Rockstar quiere que experimentar tenga menos castigos dentro de la campaña.
El objetivo es reducir los mensajes de “Misión Fallida”
David Hynd, vicepresidente de tecnología de Rockstar, indicó que el estudio adoptó una filosofía de diseño más abierta para esta entrega. La intención fue disminuir de forma considerable el número de ocasiones en que el usuario recibe el mensaje de “Misión Fallida” por intentar una acción inesperada.
Según Hynd, el equipo quería animar a cada persona a actuar según su estilo. El sistema buscará aceptar más decisiones del jugador en lugar de obligarlo a repetir una secuencia por desviarse del plan inicial.
La modificación puede afectar a actividades como persecuciones, robos, enfrentamientos y desplazamientos por el mapa. En lugar de limitar las soluciones a una única ruta, el juego permitirá que los sistemas habituales de conducción, armas, inteligencia artificial y exploración se integren en los objetivos principales.
Rockstar no detalló todas las situaciones donde se aplicará esta flexibilidad. Sin embargo, las declaraciones sugieren que la compañía trabajó para evitar que la libertad del mundo abierto desaparezca cuando comienza una misión.
La inteligencia artificial será clave para ampliar las opciones
Aplicar este modelo en un videojuego de la escala de GTA 6 exigió adaptar tecnologías y sistemas que Rockstar ya utilizaba. Hynd reconoció que mantener las misiones abiertas resulta más difícil en un proyecto de esta dimensión.
El estudio tuvo que aprovechar más sus mecánicas, inteligencia artificial y sistemas de juego dentro de los encargos. Esa integración busca que los personajes no controlados, los vehículos y las acciones disponibles respondan de forma coherente aunque el jugador se aleje de una solución prevista.
La libertad y la flexibilidad justificaron el esfuerzo técnico, según Rockstar. El equipo consideró que permitir respuestas distintas en cada misión compensaba la complejidad adicional del desarrollo.
La decisión encaja con un mapa que no se limita a una ciudad. Leonida reúne Vice City, los Leonida Keys, pantanos, carreteras, zonas industriales, pueblos en decadencia y parques naturales. Cada área tendrá vehículos, condiciones meteorológicas y riesgos propios.
Jason y Lucía serán el centro de la historia
GTA 6 seguirá a Lucía y Jason, una pareja criminal que intenta cambiar su situación mientras atraviesa el lado más conflictivo de Leonida. Lucía comienza la historia vinculada a una prisión de Vice City, mientras Jason tiene conexiones con el contrabando y las zonas rurales del estado.
Rockstar presenta su relación como una dinámica inspirada en Bonnie y Clyde, con robos, fugas y decisiones compartidas. El sistema de cambio entre ambos permitirá alternar sus perspectivas, habilidades y posiciones durante determinados momentos de la partida.
La campaña principal contará con misiones de violencia, robos y desplazamientos por el mapa, junto con actividades secundarias. También habrá comercios, playas, mercadillos, zonas para bucear, vehículos terrestres, lanchas y otros medios de transporte.
El clima también influirá en los recorridos. Las tormentas tropicales, la niebla y el oleaje podrán reducir la visibilidad al conducir o dificultar la navegación en las zonas costeras.

articles.title: Lumepay's Huang uses stablecoins to simplify African cross-border payments
articles.text:
For Harry Huang, the problem with moving money across borders was not something he discovered in a boardroom or at a fintech conference. He had seen it much earlier, through his family’s import-export business.
His parents were building a business in South Africa, dealing with suppliers and customers beyond the country’s borders. But making international payments was not always as simple as instructing a bank to transfer money. Sometimes it required personal connections, patience and navigating exchange rates that did not match what businesses expected.
“Sometimes, you had to find someone who knew someone just to get a payment done,” Huang said in an interview with TechCabal on Monday. “It wasn’t as straightforward as going to a bank. The exchange rates were also different from what you would see on Google or other platforms.”
For businesses trying to trade across borders, these are more than administrative frustrations. Delayed payments, unpredictable foreign exchange costs and difficulty moving money can determine whether a company pursues an opportunity in another market or walks away from it.
Huang believes he can help address some of those problems. As co-founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of South African fintech Lumepay, he is building cross-border payment infrastructure that combines traditional banking systems with stablecoin technology to help businesses collect, convert and move money across African markets.
Born in South Africa and raised for about 14 years in China, Huang has spent much of his life navigating two countries and their different ways of doing business. His professional journey has taken him from accounting and banking audits to the cryptocurrency industry, where he became convinced that digital assets could serve a purpose beyond speculation.
Now, he wants to use that experience to make it easier for African businesses to trade with one another and the rest of the world. Lumepay has disclosed a $6 million pre-seed funding round, alongside $10 million in capital float to support liquidity for clients. Huang insists the bigger ambition is to build infrastructure that allows businesses to pursue opportunities without worrying about how they will get paid.
Between two worlds
“I was born in South Africa, but my parents were busy building their business and trying to establish themselves in Africa. They sent me to live with my grandmother in China, where I spent about 14 years,” he said.
He returned to South Africa in Grade 7, settling initially in Port Elizabeth city, now Gqeberha. The transition was not without difficulty. He had to adjust to a different education system and learn Afrikaans while still finding his feet in English.
“One of the challenges I faced was learning Afrikaans at that stage. It was quite difficult because I couldn’t even speak English properly at the time,” he says.
He eventually enrolled at the University of Cape Town (UCT), where he studied finance and accounting. He took to Cape Town and stayed in the city as his career developed.
After completing his degree, Huang undertook the postgraduate studies required to qualify as a chartered accountant. He then joined PwC, a multinational audit and consulting firm, in Cape Town, where he was among a small group of trainees who gained experience auditing banks.
According to Huang, the work exposed him to some of South Africa’s largest retail banks and a business bank focused on foreign exchange. It also gave him an understanding of the systems and controls behind financial institutions.
Accounting, however, was never an end in itself. Huang says he chose the discipline because he wanted to understand how businesses worked, rather than pursue a career as an auditor.
“I studied accounting not because I wanted to become an auditor, but because I wanted to understand how businesses work. I saw accounting as one of the best ways to gain that understanding,” said.
From scepticism to stablecoins
“At the time, I didn’t know much about crypto and was initially more skeptical about the value of the industry,” he stated.
That was four or five years ago. But after interviewing with the founder of a cryptocurrency exchange, he became interested in the industry and the changes it could bring to financial services.
He joined the company as finance manager when it had no established finance function, tasked with putting the processes and systems in place to support its growth.
Huang had to build the finance department and recruit a team. After a few months, he was promoted to chief financial officer (CFO).
The role gave him a front-row seat to the cryptocurrency boom, when investors were buying digital assets in anticipation of rising prices. He also witnessed the growth of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and decentralised finance (DeFi).
But as the market cooled, Huang and his colleagues began to recognise another use for the technology, particularly in Africa: payments.
“People were using exchanges not necessarily because they wanted to invest in cryptocurrencies and wait for their value to increase, but because they needed to make payments, particularly using stablecoins,” he said.
Stablecoins are digital assets designed to maintain a stable value, typically by being pegged to a currency such as the US dollar. Their potential use in payments caught Huang’s attention because they offered another way to move value across borders.
Huang and a group of colleagues began discussing whether they could build a business around the problem. They believed they had the knowledge and experience to make cross-border payments easier for African businesses.
“That was how Lumepay started about a year ago,” he said.
Building a bridge for African businesses
Lumepay is designed to bring together different parts of the payments process rather than focus on a single transaction service. Its proposition is to handle collections, foreign exchange conversion and disbursements, using traditional banking rails and stablecoins where appropriate.
The company has two brands. Lumetrade houses its digital asset and cryptocurrency activities, while Lumepay focuses on traditional remittances, payment service provider services, local collections and payouts.
“Whether we use stablecoins or traditional payment rails, the customer doesn’t necessarily need to know which technology is being used behind the scenes,” Huang explained. “The customer’s main concern is moving money.”
In some cases, customers may not even realise stablecoins are involved, he added. What matters is that Lumepay delivers on the promised transaction speed and price, executes the payment and ensures the supplier receives the funds.
This retains both ideas while avoiding back-to-back quotations and the repetition around what customers need to know.
“There is enormous potential for intra-African trade, but some of that potential isn’t being fully realised because of the difficulties involved in moving money,” Huang said.
The company says it has established a presence across several African markets, although its ability to provide particular payment services depends on the regulatory permissions and partnerships available in each jurisdiction.
It lists markets including Nigeria, Ghana, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, Kenya and the West and Central African CFA franc zones, while noting that further regulatory approvals are required to expand payment capabilities.
In October 2026, Lumepay said it had received regulatory clearance from the Central Bank of Kenya and launched its payments solution there. In South Africa, Lumepay (Pty) Ltd is registered as a Third-Party Payment Provider, while related digital asset business Lumetrade holds a Category I financial services provider licence covering intermediary services in crypto assets, derivatives and deposits.
No one-size-fits-all Africa
“It’s a completely different book. You cannot take one approach and apply it everywhere,” Huang stated.
Payment habits in Kenya or West Africa, for example, can differ considerably from those in South Africa. Some markets have well-developed digital payment ecosystems and technology integrations. Others still rely heavily on cash, and payments can take four or five days.
The regulatory environment is equally varied. A payment service provider licence in one country does not automatically give a company the same capabilities in another. Businesses may need different licences and local partners to offer the services they want.
Huang believes coordinating the company’s product roadmap with regulatory approvals is a central part of his role. Expanding without understanding local requirements can leave a business with infrastructure it cannot fully use.
“It’s not enough to advertise that you can provide a particular service,” he shared with TechCabal. “Once customers start using a platform, they need to know that it can actually deliver, handle their volumes and resolve their problems.”
The company is also capital-intensive. Beyond developing technology and securing regulatory approvals, it needs sufficient liquidity to facilitate payments, support transaction flows and secure competitive pricing. The $10 million capital float disclosed alongside its funding round is intended to anchor that liquidity, It is separate from the $6 million pre-seed equity funding.
“Managing someone else’s money can be more stressful than spending your own,” bemoaned Huang. “It keeps you awake at night.”
He said responsibility is summed up in a short sentence: “There are no excuses.”
The Africa he wants to help build
Huang’s ambition for Lumepay extends beyond becoming another payments provider. He wants it to become a familiar name among businesses that trade across the continent, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises that may not have the resources to navigate complicated international payment systems.
But Huang’s measure of success is not simply the number of countries Lumepay enters or the volume of transactions it processes.
“What would motivate me is being somewhere in Africa, sitting in a coffee shop and hearing people talk about how they use Lumepay,” he said.
He imagines hearing from a business owner whose money was once stuck somewhere, but who managed to resolve the problem and is now doing more business.
“If I could hear those kinds of stories, I would know we had made a difference.”
The technology may involve banking networks, foreign exchange systems and stablecoins. But the purpose, he insists, is simply to help businesses move money so they can get on with doing business.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer
articles.text:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Jordan Cutler, Senior Staff Engineer and Web Platform Tech Lead at Pinterest, presented how the role of a staff engineer changes when every engineer has access to the same AI tools. The session argued that most "AI for engineers" content focuses on individual productivity, while the real question for staff engineers is where their leverage comes from now. According to Cutler, AI did not change what a staff engineer is for, but it changed where the leverage is.
The talk opened with a reflection on Cutler's previous conference talk, where he showed how AI could turn a four-hour task into four minutes. At that point he was shipping roughly as much as his whole team, which he described as multiplying himself rather than his team. That framed the central question of the session: what does a 10x engineer look like when everyone has AI?
To illustrate why this matters, Cutler shared internal Pinterest data on merged pull requests per engineer per week between Q1 2025 and Q3 2026. The top 10% of engineers went from 6.7 to 11.3 merged PRs per week, a 68% increase, while the bottom half went from 1.0 to 1.15, an increase of 14%. Everyone has AI, but not everyone uses it the same way, and the gap keeps growing. The presentation organized the response to that gap into three moves: multiply yourself, multiply your team, and multiply the system.
The first move, multiply yourself, is about going first. Cutler explained that he tries new tools before his team does, and that part of that work is hitting dead ends so others don't have to. He mentioned examples such as an agent harness that could not be steered mid-task and a remote agent runner that required too many follow-ups. Sharing those findings early means the team does not lose a week on the same experiments. Running many agents also revealed a new problem: he kept giving the same corrections in every session, such as avoiding em-dashes, adding a diagram to the PR description, and keeping pull requests small.
The second move, multiply your team, started from a limitation: the folder made him faster, but only he had it. With new people joining the team and a new area to ramp up on, Cutler found himself repeating the same comments in code review, such as asking why a value is null instead of fixing the cause, testing like a user would, and keeping PRs small. The talk emphasized that the value of encoding that judgment grows with every teammate who adopts it, compared to the flat curve of a single engineer working alone.
The third move, multiply the system, is about moving up a level. Cutler used the history of container shipping as an analogy: ports got better at loading cargo by hand, but the standard box changed the economics entirely, from $5.86 a ton to 16 cents a ton. At Pinterest, migrations were the cargo, one kind of change spread across hundreds of files and dozens of teams. Instead of running each migration by hand, the team built a system where a staff engineer points to a plan and an example, an engineer puts it on a schedule, and an agent running in a sandbox splits the work into PRs team by team. A class component migration ran three to five times faster than by hand, in the background while teams worked on other things.
The talk also covered what went wrong. One scheduled job looped and opened 16 PRs in two minutes, increasing CI wait times from under 30 seconds to 14 minutes. The lesson was not to wait for the perfect guardrail, but to ship a small one. Cutler encouraged attendees to find their own "any" problem: a first responder for any incident, a draft fix for any bug ticket, or an agent that triages any flaky test. Today, 40 engineers have scheduler jobs of their own.
The results were significant. Using the same AI tools as other web teams, Cutler's team now ships about four times as much per engineer, without counting his own PRs.
The presentation concluded with practical steps: write down what you repeat, put it where people already work, and build for every case instead of one. Some parts of the job cannot be written down, like an honest conversation with a teammate who is struggling, and those remain the staff engineer's responsibility. As Cutler put it, a 10x engineer isn't ten times faster, they are the reason ten other people are. As AI agents become part of everyday development workflows, the role of senior engineers may increasingly shift from personal output toward encoding judgment into the tools, defaults, and systems that entire organizations use.

articles.title: Es un gesto casi absurdo, pero es una forma práctica de abrir y guardar los paquetes de espaguetis en la despensa
articles.text:
Los paquetes de espaguetis son largos, estrechos y poco cómodos de guardar cuando ya están abiertos. Sacar una ración por el extremo superior es sencillo, pero después hay que recoger el plástico que sobra y buscar la manera de sujetarlo antes de devolverlo a la despensa. La forma de abrir el envase puede facilitar ese segundo paso.
El truco consiste en cortar el paquete a lo largo, siguiendo la dirección de los espaguetis. Así puedes acceder a la pasta por un lateral y utilizar el propio envoltorio para recoger lo que quede después de cocinar. Basta con unas tijeras y una goma o un trozo de celo para el cierre.
Cómo hacer el corte y volver a cerrar el paquete
Primero, tumba el paquete sobre una superficie y haz un pequeño corte en una de las puntas del plástico. Desde ahí, continúa hasta el extremo contrario. La abertura debe recorrer la longitud del envase, de modo que puedas separar sus bordes y sacar los espaguetis con la mano.
Retira la cantidad que necesites y deja el resto sobre el envoltorio. El plástico abierto queda alrededor de la pasta, como un estuche desplegado. Para cerrarlo, vuelve a envolver los espaguetis que han sobrado y sujeta el paquete con una goma. Si prefieres usar celo, puedes fijar con él el borde del plástico.
Guardarlo bien también depende del lugar y del cierre
Para conservar la pasta seca, Barilla recomienda un lugar fresco y sin humedad, tanto si el envase está abierto como si sigue cerrado. La marca señala una despensa o un armario como sitios adecuados y aconseja consumir sus productos dentro de la fecha de consumo preferente indicada en el paquete.
Barilla también desaconseja guardar las cajas de sus productos de pasta seca en la nevera o en el congelador, porque la pasta puede absorber humedad. Esta indicación se refiere expresamente a la pasta envasada en cajas, estén abiertas o cerradas.
Si buscas un cierre hermético, la Asociación Nacional de la Pasta de Estados Unidos recomienda guardar la pasta seca en un recipiente o caja herméticos. Sujetar el envoltorio con una goma sirve para recogerlo, pero no permite dar por hecho que el envase haya quedado sellado herméticamente.
La misma asociación aconseja terminar primero los paquetes que llevan más tiempo guardados antes de abrir otros nuevos. Puedes aplicar esa pauta al organizar la despensa y reservar para el siguiente uso el paquete de espaguetis que ya tienes empezado.

articles.title: Microsoft thinks it can make agentic AI work for the whole company, not just you
articles.text:
While there's been a tremendous amount of excitement surrounding agentic AI over the last year or two, the vast majority of the attention has focused on individual use of these tools. Everywhere you look, it seems, you can find stories of people who have done amazing work on their own with agentic AI.
Scaling the technology to groups and large companies, on the other hand, hasn't always been as easy. In fact, a number of stories have circulated lately about companies that haven't seen the return they expected on their agentic AI investments.
At the same time, much of the popular press on agentic AI has focused on high-profile model providers such as OpenAI and Anthropic and the tools they make, as well as others like Perplexity, Muse, and OpenClaw that tend to be seen primarily as tools for individuals.
When it comes to the enterprise, however, there's little doubt that Microsoft is still king of the hill – a fact that was dramatically reinforced last week when Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft services broke down and essentially halted productivity for businesses of all sizes for about an entire day.
Perhaps appropriately, then, at this year's Microsoft Ignite event in San Francisco, the company intentionally brought the agentic AI story to the enterprise, with the specific goal of addressing the key issues that arise when you try to scale a personal productivity tool to a group-focused enterprise level.
Through a wide-ranging set of announcements, the company tackled group co-working, specialized tools for different departments, leveraging corporate data and context to improve the quality of AI output and, most importantly, cost.
At a core level, Microsoft has expanded Copilot with several new modes and broader capabilities for both individuals and groups. In fact, the company even went so far as to call Copilot the new operating system for work, which certainly raises some interesting questions for the future.
Copilot Workspaces, for example, lets individuals and groups create long-running agentic workflows that can be used and edited by multiple people. If a group within a department wants to work collectively on a project, they can integrate Office documents (which are now directly editable in Copilot), Teams threads and more into a dynamic project that agents can modify and update.
The new Today option in Copilot, which just entered private preview, brings a proactive agent to individuals, reminding them of tasks they need to complete, documents to edit, emails to send and more. Both of these modes also have new auto-routing tools that can automatically send different tasks to the most appropriate model. For frontier-level clients, a new Autopilot will take these kinds of proactive steps even further.
To deliver these capabilities, the company has built an increasingly sophisticated and complex set of software layers and interconnection tools that let organizations customize and optimize agentic tools for their specific needs.
The newly announced Microsoft IQ, for example, brings together Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ into a comprehensive contextual layer that off-the-shelf and custom-built agents can tap into to create new business workflows, enhance existing processes and more. Though it sounds similar, it does not replace the Microsoft Graph. Instead, it adds an abstraction layer above Graph that's specifically designed for interactions with agentic tools.
Another critical capability of Microsoft IQ is a set of more than 350 "plug-ins" that serve as connectors between a wide variety of applications and data types. These matter because they help ease the seemingly insurmountable challenge of cleaning and prepping data stores for use with AI tools.
Virtually every organization that has had success with agentic AI, as well as many creators of agentic AI tools, has talked about how critical clean, custom data is to getting the most value from these tools.
Doing that work, however, has often proven more challenging than many organizations expected. With well-constructed plug-ins, many of those challenges can be removed because the import process can automatically put data into the proper formats for ingestion. On top of these connection tools, Microsoft also announced a new partnership with Salesforce called Copilotforce, which can integrate data and skills into the Microsoft IQ environment via MCP connections to Salesforce. For many organizations, these types of connector plug-ins could be a significant game changer.
Equally important to Microsoft's enterprise-wide agentic story is an extended range of its own smaller, specialized models in the MAI (Microsoft AI) family. The new MAI-Code-2 model, now available through GitHub, is claimed to offer 90% of the coding capabilities of today's latest frontier models at a fraction of the size. This, in turn, means lower token costs and the potential to move more workloads on-prem.
Even more important was the launch of the new Microsoft-Decision-1.1 tool, an intelligent model router that takes requests from an agent, breaks them into smaller pieces and sends each piece to the most appropriate and cost-effective model. This capability is an absolutely essential element of a hybrid AI environment that can work across the cloud, on-prem data centers and edge/client devices. While multiple other companies are working on similar routing capabilities, and there's still more work to be done, Microsoft's massive presence in the enterprise is bound to make this a very important tool moving forward.
In addition to software, Microsoft made a few AI infrastructure announcements on the hardware side. Notably, the company debuted its new Arm-based Cobalt 200 CPUs, which power Cobalt 200 virtual machines that offer 50% better performance on agentic workloads than the first-generation chips.
Microsoft also made an array of important security announcements, including additions to its Perception security stack, an integrated Security Operations Center and a new AI transparency initiative designed to give organizations more insight into how AI tools function and are governed.
The key takeaway from it all is that Microsoft is starting to fully leverage its privileged position within businesses around the world to extend agentic AI from the individual to the organization. It's not a transition that's going to occur overnight, but it's clear that an increasingly wide range of the tools needed to scale these efforts are starting to come into place.
Bob O'Donnell is the founder and chief analyst of TECHnalysis Research, LLC a technology consulting firm that provides strategic consulting and market research services to the technology industry and professional financial community. You can follow him on Twitter @bobodtech

articles.title: Vercel brings on Toronto team behind AI developer platform Traces | BetaKit
articles.text:
The Toronto team behind Traces is joining Vercel less than a year after releasing its flagship product.
The news: Traces founder Tarun Sachdeva announced this week that his Toronto-based company, a collaborative platform for coding with AI agents, is being acquired by US cloud and web hosting platform Vercel. All four Traces team members started work at Vercel this week as part of the deal, Sachdeva told BetaKit. Financial details were not disclosed. Vercel did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Existing Traces users can continue using the app and will retain access to their data, Traces said in an email to users, but the creation of new communities, or “orgs,” is paused. The deal does not give Vercel access to users’ data, the company said.
From the source: Sachdeva explained in a video with The Other Stuff podcast that Traces grew out of a desire to learn from other developers about how they were coding with AI agents.
“I wanted to keep that data, because I felt like it was so useful to keep those decisions that we make when we’re building products,” Sachdeva said.
The context: Sachdeva told BetaKit in a direct message that he launched the Traces developer platform in February after founding the company a few years ago. It had raised an undisclosed amount of funding from Canadian VCs Golden Ventures and Northside Ventures, as well as US VC Signalfire and angel investors from Shopify and Wattpad. Sachdeva is a longtime Canadian tech operator who worked in senior product management roles at Research in Motion and Wattpad.
Valued at $9.3 billion USD ($13.3 billion CAD) as of its Series F round in September 2025, Vercel has connected to the Canadian tech scene in other ways, too; this summer, its COO Jeanne DeWitt Grosser joined Shopify’s board.
Final thought: This deal is another indication that Silicon Valley’s developer community is paying attention to Canadian talent. It’s the second time this month that a Canadian-founded AI-native platform has been acquired by a high-profile US tech company within a year of its product launch. AI travel agent startup Odessia, led by former Sonder co-founder Francis Davidson, joined OpenAI last week.

articles.title: Ojo con el autoguardado de 'GTA 6': no es tan frecuente como crees y puedes perder tu progreso
articles.text:
GTA 6 ya está definitivamente entre nosotros y tanto el público como la prensa especializada lo están amando. Lo nuevo de Rockstar Games ha logrado estar a la altura del hype, cosechando calificaciones inmejorables, pero hay un apartado que está dando algunos dolores de cabeza: el autoguardado.
La función de autoguardado de GTA 6 cumple la misma finalidad que en cualquier otro videojuego: salvar el avance que has logrado en una misión o campaña sin que tengas que hacerlo de forma manual. Sin embargo, su implementación en la más reciente entrega de la saga Grand Theft Auto tiene sus bemoles.
Se supone que GTA 6 guarda automáticamente el progreso cuando terminas una misión principal o ciertas tareas secundarias. Pero han aparecido reportes de jugadores aseverando que el sistema no se ha disparado de forma consistente siguiendo esos parámetros. ¿Esto qué significa? Que tal vez al finalizar una misión sí se ha guardado el avance de forma automática, pero que al culminar otras no ha sucedido lo msimo.
Esto conlleva un riesgo bastante evidente, pues si das por hecho que GTA 6 va a guardar tu progreso al completar cada misión principal que se te presente, es posible que te equivoques. Y si por algún motivo el uso del juego se interrumpe de forma repentina (si se va la luz, por ejemplo), tal vez te topes con que debes repetir algo que ya habías cumplido.
El autoguardado de GTA 6 presenta inconsistencias
Todavía no está claro si la inconsistencia del autoguardado de GTA 6 es un bug o una característica. Es un hecho que Rockstar Games tiene medidas bastante concretas sobre cuándo se puede o no guardar el progreso de una sesión. Si estás en una pelea o te persiguen pandilleros o la policía, no puedes guardar tu partida de ninguna manera, sea manual o automática. Asimismo, los desarrolladores no permiten salvar el avance mientras estás en medio de una misión con Jason y/o Lucía.
Dicho todo esto, lo más recomendable es no confiar a ciegas en el guardado automático de GTA 6. El juego es tan vasto y lleno de posibilidades que puedes pasar horas y horas recorriéndolo, independientemente de cuánto progreses en tu carrera criminal o en la relación entre los protagonistas. Así que no está bueno dedicarle tanto tiempo para luego perder lo poco o mucho que consigas por culpa de un imponderable.
Si quieres evitar sorpresas desagradables, lo más saludable es guardar tu progreso de GTA 6 de forma manual cada vez que te sea posible. Grand Theft Auto VI tiene 15 ranuras para almacenar el progreso de tus sesiones frente a la consola, de las cuales una está dedicada exclusivamente al autoguardado. Si optas por guardar tus avances de forma manual puedes hacerlo en Juego > Guardar juego, ingresando desde el menú de opciones.
GTA 6 es, sin dudas, de esas propuestas que se ven una sola vez en una generación. De acuerdo con el seguimiento que lleva Sensor Tower, lo nuevo de Rockstar ha vendido más de 19 millones de copias. Una cifra que se espera que siga en alza con el correr de los días.

articles.title: 'Where are the jobs?' Modi tells industry to respond to tax relief with hiring, salary hikes
articles.text:
'Where are the jobs?' Modi tells industry to respond to tax relief with hiring, salary hikes
Prime Minister Narendra Modi lamented that despite reforms in areas of corporate tax, income tax and GST, it has not resulted in job creation by the industry.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday questioned industry leaders over the lack of commensurate job creation and salary increases despite the government's tax concessions, challenging businesses to translate higher consumer purchasing power into greater employment and economic activity.
Addressing the FICCI annual general meeting here, Modi said the government had taken several steps to improve the business environment, including reducing the basic corporate tax rate from 30% in 2014 to 22%, simplifying tax return and refund processes and lowering GST rates on several products.
"I know you won't applaud. I know that very well, because your appetite is so enormous that no matter how much you are given, it is never enough," he told industry leaders. "I have given income tax relief up to Rs 12 lakh. But have you increased the salaries of your employees? Have you increased the number of employees? No! It is always: 'Modi ji, you do it; we will see what happens.' This is how things will continue."
He also cited the income-tax exemption for annual incomes of up to Rs 12 lakh, saying the relief had boosted people's purchasing power and should translate into greater demand and business expansion.
"How much ever you give, their appetite is never satisfied," Modi said in a pointed remark to industry leaders, adding that businesses needed to do more for their employees rather than expect the government to shoulder the responsibility for growth.
He said a country could progress only by respecting its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers, and not by criticising them.
"No country can progress unless it respects its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers. A country cannot move forward by abusing them morning and evening," he said.
Modi recalled a gathering of the income tax department in Gujarat way back in 2001-02. He had become Chief Minister of Gujarat then.
"I did not understand much at the time; I had little knowledge and no experience either. But I delivered a speech there. This must have been around 2001-02, perhaps 25 years ago. All the senior officials of the Income Tax Department were present. I asked them: 'When will you stop treating everyone as a thief? What kind of approach is this? You, too, work for the country. Are we the only ones who have taken it upon ourselves to serve the nation? You also do your bit, and every citizen does their bit. Everyone deserves respect.'"
The Prime Minister also cautioned businesses against treating India's large domestic market as an assured source of sales, saying companies must improve product quality and become globally competitive.
"Do not consider the 140 crore Indians an assured market," he said, urging industry to shed the mindset that whatever it produces will automatically find buyers in the domestic market.
He criticised the practice of marketing products as "export quality" to Indian consumers, asking whether people in the country did not deserve the same quality as overseas customers.
"My countrymen deserve quality," he said.
Modi urged Indian businesses to take advantage of the trade agreements signed by India with several countries, saying these had opened doors to major global markets.
He described the agreements as a historic opportunity for Indian industry and asked businesses whether they had prepared plans to tap the new markets.

articles.title: TikTok revela os assuntos que mais cresceram entre jovens em 2026
articles.text:
O interesse por atividades manuais, leitura, esportes e viagens cresceu entre os jovens brasileiros no TikTok ao longo de 2026. É o que mostra o relatório Discovery On TikTok, divulgado pela plataforma com exclusividade ao Olhar Digital, que analisou os assuntos explorados e compartilhados por usuários de 16 a 24 anos. No Brasil, as publicações sobre crochê aumentaram 78%, enquanto as relacionadas a livros avançaram 103%.
O levantamento também identificou crescimento nas publicações sobre corrida, anime e dicas de viagem. Os resultados indicam a variedade de interesses que movimentam as comunidades da plataforma, que também tem sido utilizada pelos jovens para descobrir atividades, aprender novas habilidades e encontrar pessoas com gostos semelhantes.
Jovens usam TikTok para descobrir novos interesses
De acordo com a pesquisa, 82% dos jovens entrevistados afirmam que o TikTok os ajuda a descobrir coisas novas. Além disso, 58% dizem que a plataforma está entre os primeiros lugares que procuram quando querem aprender alguma coisa.
O relatório reúne dados de pesquisas de mercado e análises internas do aplicativo. Entre os assuntos que ganharam espaço globalmente estão esportes, entretenimento e atividades criativas, com diferentes tendências em cada país analisado.
No segmento esportivo, as publicações com a hashtag #SportsOnTikTok cresceram 155% globalmente. O interesse não ficou restrito ao futebol: modalidades como patinação artística, escalada, capoeira e corrida também apareceram entre os destaques.
No Brasil, as publicações com a hashtag #Running, relacionada à corrida, aumentaram 64% na comparação anual. Já a capoeira registrou crescimento de 147%, segundo os dados apresentados no relatório.
Anime e entretenimento também atraem a geração Z
O entretenimento é outra área que movimenta as comunidades de jovens no TikTok. Globalmente, as publicações com a hashtag #FilmTok, dedicada a conteúdos sobre cinema, cresceram 42% entre usuários de 16 a 24 anos.
As comunidades de anime e mangá também apresentaram números expressivos. Juntas, as duas hashtags somaram quase 13,5 milhões de publicações no mundo durante o último ano, considerando os conteúdos produzidos pelo público jovem.
No Brasil, as publicações com #Anime avançaram 40% em relação ao ano anterior. O relatório também destaca a criadora brasileira Amanda Brandão (@amandabrandao), que produz conteúdos sobre notícias de entretenimento, entrevistas e cultura pop. O perfil tinha 187,4 mil seguidores no levantamento.
Crochê e outras atividades criativas ganham popularidade
As atividades manuais também aparecem entre os interesses em crescimento. Globalmente, as publicações com a hashtag #CraftTok, que reúne conteúdos sobre artesanato e trabalhos criativos, aumentaram 46% entre pessoas de 16 a 24 anos.
No Brasil, um dos destaques foi o crochê, com alta de 78% nas publicações. Na França, o mesmo assunto avançou 65%. O levantamento também identificou crescimento de 94% nas publicações brasileiras com a hashtag #Drawing, relacionada a desenhos, e de 49% em #SpeedPaint, que reúne vídeos de processos acelerados de pintura.
Entre os criadores apresentados está Fernanda, conhecida como @femingos. A brasileira é artista e trabalha com canto, escrita e desenho, produzindo conteúdos em diferentes formatos. O perfil contabilizava 1,7 milhão de seguidores na publicação do relatório.
Livros e viagens estão entre os interesses dos brasileiros
Além das tendências detalhadas no documento, o recorte brasileiro apresentado pelo TikTok destaca o crescimento de outros dois assuntos: leitura e viagens.
As publicações com a hashtag #BookTokBrasil aumentaram 103% entre os usuários brasileiros de 16 a 24 anos na comparação anual. A comunidade reúne conteúdos relacionados a livros e experiências de leitura.
Já a hashtag #DicasDeViagem registrou crescimento de 81% no mesmo período. O resultado aponta para o aumento do compartilhamento e da busca por recomendações relacionadas ao planejamento de viagens entre os jovens brasileiros.
Como o levantamento foi realizado
O relatório Discovery On TikTok combina pesquisa quantitativa conduzida pela Qualtrics e análises internas de atividades realizadas no aplicativo.
A análise de hashtags considera o crescimento anual das publicações entre julho de 2024 e julho de 2025, em comparação com o período de julho de 2025 a julho de 2026.
Já os dados de buscas comparam dois intervalos de seis meses: agosto de 2025 a janeiro de 2026 e fevereiro de 2026 a julho de 2026.
O documento também apresenta uma pesquisa com jovens de 16 a 24 anos e dados de engajamento em seis mercados: Brasil, Reino Unido, França, Alemanha, Indonésia e Emirados Árabes Unidos.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).
