articles.title: BYD actualiza su coche más vendido con mejoras muy interesantes: así es el SEAL U DM-i Model Year 2027
articles.text:
BYD sigue apostando por traer nuevas opciones para los que buscan un coche y lo hace esta vez con una nueva versión de su SUV familiar SEAL U DM-i que llega bajo el nombre del Model Year 2027. Este modelo, perteneciente al segmento D, llega con más potencia y mayores prestaciones, un salto cualitativo muy interesante frente al estándar.
Destacan, sobre todo, una mayor autonomía gracias a su nueva batería de mayor capacidad y algunos cambios muy interesantes para hacer más cómoda la conducción, como la tracción total y la suspensión trasera y dirección totalmente renovadas.
La base es la del SEAL U DM-i que la compañía lanzó al mercado en 2024 y que se convirtió en el modelo más vendido tanto de Europa como en España dentro de los híbridos enchufables en tan solo un año, siendo uno de los modelos referentes de 2025. Ahora, esta actualización para el modelo 2027 busca mantener ese puesto, pero ofreciendo una mejora en la mayoría de sus aspectos clave.
En este sentido, una de esas grandes mejoras está en lo que esconde bajo el capó; ahora las versiones del SUV incorporan un motor de gasolina renovado de 1,5 litros turboalimentado de 130 CV (96 kW) en sustitución del anterior bloque atmosférico en las versiones de tracción delantera, lo que supone un salto en potencia, prestaciones y eficiencia. No obstante, llega en tres versiones diferentes.
Por un lado, el acabado Boost, que es el de acceso a la gama SEAL U DM-i, combina el motor de gasolina con un motoreléctrico de 204 CV (150 kW) para entregar una potencia total conjunta de 238 CV (175 kW); una versión Comfort, que mantiene su batería de mayor capacidad con 130 km de autonomía en modo 100% eléctrico y una combinada de 1.030 km; y el Design, que cuenta con un motor adicional de 204 CV (150 kW) en el eje trasero para ofrecer una potencia total máxima de 374 CV (275 kW) y una aceleración de 0 a 100km/h en solo 5,1 segundos.
Otro aspecto interesante es que ahora todas las versiones del SEAL U DM-i disponen de carga rápida en corriente continua (CC) de hasta 55 kW, que reduce a la mitad el tiempo de recarga del 30% al 80%:15 minutos en el acabado Boost y 20 minutos en los acabados Comfort y Design.
Y, como es habitual en la marca, vienen cargados de tecnología en su apartado de infoentretenimiento, con dos tamaños de pantalla según el acabado. Por un lado, en Boost cuenta con una pantalla central de 12,8” (32,5 cm), mientras que Comfort y Design disponen de una de 15,6” (39,6 cm). Los tres modelos integran Google Built-in, con Google Maps, Google Assistant y acceso a Google Play Store.
Este nuevo SEAL U DM-I ‘Model Year 2027’ estará disponible en Burgundy Red y Graphite Blue, que se suman a los Polar White, Time Grey, Obsidian Black y Boundless Cloud, con llantas 19” de serie.
Sobre los precios, arranca desde los 39.300€ en el Boost y pueden llegar hasta los 48.500€ en el caso del SEAL U DM-I Design. También hay una versión 100% eléctrica, el SEAL U, disponible en acabados Comfort y Design por 44.290 y 48.290, respectivamente.

articles.title: Metano launches with $12M to help enterprises secure AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Metano launches with $12M to help enterprises secure AI agents
Artificial intelligence agent security startup Metano Inc. today launched with $12 million in funding to help enterprises secure AI agents across endpoints, cloud infrastructure and software-as-a-service applications.
Metano’s platform is aimed at giving enterprises consistent visibility and control over AI agents, bringing together agent discovery, context-aware threat detection and real-time enforcement in a single layer.
It’s seeking to address the issue wherein security teams face a growing and fragmented attack surface as organizations deploy AI agents across devices, coding environments, cloud infrastructure and SaaS applications. Metano argues that existing security products protect individual infrastructure layers but lack the visibility and behavioral context needed to secure autonomous agents operating across them.
Making the problem harder is that AI agents, which often run with legitimate credentials and approved tools, can make decisions and take actions dynamically. Instructions, external content and operating conditions can all change how an agent behaves, according to Metano, introducing risks that may not be apparent during initial testing.
“Traditional security tools weren’t designed for AI agents that can make decisions and change their behavior as they operate,” Chief Executive Neelima Rustagi explained.
The first part of Metano’s offering is discovery, with the platform identifying approved and unapproved AI agents, Model Context Protocol servers, skills and software packages, along with their access privileges and potential security exposure.
The second part is Hive, Metano’s real-time context graph, which connects agent tasks, identities, tools, data access and actions. By analyzing activity across an entire session, Hive identifies suspicious behavior and determines whether an agent’s actions align with its intended purpose, allowing security teams to understand why an agent’s behavior may pose a risk.
Metano also offers enforcement as the third part of its platform, placing security controls wherever agents operate. Security teams are given centrally managed policies and guardrails to stop dangerous actions as they occur, even when an agent’s activity may bypass traditional network gateways.
The platform’s detections draw on research from MARS Labs, Metano’s own AI security research team. Malicious skills, compromised software dependencies and vulnerabilities in MCP connections are among the threats the group investigates. The company says its agent detections are mapped to MITRE ATLAS and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications.
Rustagi co-founded the company with Chief Technology Officer Ratnesh Pandey. The Metano team also brings security experience from ServiceNow Inc., Zscaler Inc., Palo Alto Networks Inc., FireEye Inc. and Microsoft Corp.
Among the companies already using the platform is data engineering firm Streamvector Inc., which does business as Sigmoid. Srivatsa Ramarao, Sigmoid’s chief information security officer, said Metano has helped Sigmoid adopt AI securely while minimizing shadow risks, allowing it to “say yes to AI across the business.”
Sierra Ventures led the seed round, with Correlation Ventures, High Alpha and 360 ONE also participating. According to Mark Fernandes, managing partner at Sierra Ventures, every platform shift in security produces a few companies that “own the new control point,” with agents representing one of the biggest disruptions he has seen.
Metano’s platform is generally available now, and the company claims security teams can begin using it in under 30 minutes. Also on offer is a free Eval Edition, which provides 30 days of real-time agent scanning so security teams can identify agent activity, risky configurations and potential exposure in their own environments. Metano has completed a SOC 2 Type 2 examination and holds ISO 27001:2022 certification, along with a listing on Okta Inc.’s Okta Integration Network.

articles.title: JPMorgan, Visa, Mastercard Cite Third-Party Incidents Amid Data Leak
articles.text:
JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard have disclosed incidents involving outside service providers after the N0n extortion group claimed it stole their customers’ data.
JPMorgan said in a post on X on Thursday that some of the companies providing services to the bank had been hit by a cyberattack.
“Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses. There is no disruption to our services,” the bank said.
Where appropriate, the bank plans to reach out to impacted customers and give them free credit monitoring. It said the incident has nothing to do with the problems some customers saw earlier this week.
In a statement to the media, Visa said the claims are “associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific.” The payments giant said neither its own systems nor payment data such as card numbers had been impacted.
Mastercard said in a statement to Reuters that it had recently learned of an incident “at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of limited amount of email addresses — non-payments information — from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program.”
Mastercard said its payment network was not affected and that cardholders can still use their cards.
On November 16, N0n claimed to have obtained JPMorgan-related engagement data spanning “hundreds of thousands of campaign interactions for tens of thousands of distinct cardmember email addresses,” according to Reuters. It made comparable claims about Visa and Mastercard the same day.
SecurityWeek has seen N0n’s leak site, where all three companies are marked as not having paid, and the allegedly stolen data is offered for download.
Reuters’ review of the JPMorgan-related data found over 16,000 customer emails, some accompanied by phone numbers and postal codes, along with what appear to be 124 email addresses belonging to bank employees.
The Visa files hold thousands of purported customer emails, phone numbers and marketing campaign records, mostly from Asia-Pacific markets, Reuters said.
None of the three companies has identified the affected providers or said how many customers were impacted.
N0n, which emerged in September, currently lists roughly 200 alleged victims on its leak site.

articles.title: AI Accelerators Drive Changes In Power Delivery Networks
articles.text:
Moving voltage regulators closer to processors can reduce power loss, but adds challenges for advanced packaging, thermal management, and system-level design.
Key Takeaways:
Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips. The demands of AI and high-performance computing chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU are forcing current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the PDN. Multi-chiplet constructions only compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion.
To solve these challenges, designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks, where the voltage regulator modules are relocated much closer to the processors from their position on the device periphery — to the PCB landside (under the PCB), inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. Together with the growing customization of AI accelerator modules, there are many approaches on offer with varying design and manufacturing complexity.
The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with the integration of backside power delivery networks (BPDNs) on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery more directly to the transistors while reducing IR drop across the tens of interconnect levels on-chip. That approach is being extended with increasingly sophisticated on-die decoupling capacitors (DCaps) formed in deep trenches as part of the BPDN. While this addresses high-frequency decoupling at the chip level, recent changes inside packages, interposers, substrates, and across data center racks are becoming just as important.
Add to that recent developments in the design of compact passive devices, like high-performance inductors, and new architectural solutions become possible, moving the VRMs and DC-DC converters into the interposer or package.
But these architectural changes are neither straightforward nor simple because they involve system co-design of the PDN, interposer, power management ICs (PMICs), integrated voltage regulators (IVRs), DC-DC converters, capacitors, and other passive devices, alongside custom HPC, memory devices, and interconnects that perform today’s elaborate AI tasks.
“In the most advanced semiconductors, people are moving from discrete PMICs to distributed IVRs. Those IVRs are great because they are placed much closer to the chip, which reduces the IR drop to the chip’s own power delivery network, so it is way more efficient. In addition, closed and fast control loops between the chip power management unit to the IVR reduce the reaction time to voltage droop events from milliseconds to microseconds. Because this reaction is so fast you can tune voltage very accurately, with a high degree of granularity even on different areas of a chip,” said Nir Sever, senior director of business development at proteanTecs.
Reconfiguring the PDN is part of a much larger drive to improve energy use. “Energy efficiency becomes the most important performance index for AI-infused platforms moving forward,” said Lipen Yuan, senior director of TSMC’s Advanced Technology Business Development, during a 2024 IEDM short course.
Power delivery challenges are most important at points of load. “AI systems are placing unprecedented demands on board-to-chip power delivery, making the final stage of voltage regulation increasingly important,” said CP Hung, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE.
Fig. 1: By regulating voltage at the point of load, OSATs enable fine-tuned voltage control. Source: ASE
“The move to multi-die architectures is bringing power integrity to the forefront, alongside thermal, stress, and warpage challenges. But the underlying power-delivery problem already existed in advanced single-die designs,” said Sojan Philips, principal product manager of Redhawk-SC at Synopsys. “AI accelerators are now operating at currents approaching the kiloampere range, where even milliohm-level resistance in the power-delivery network can result in significant IR drop. That loss of voltage margin can directly affect performance and power targets, particularly maximum operating frequency and Vmin.”
Several developments illustrate these trends:
As a result, OSATs are playing an increasing role in system co-design, electrical validation, and power integrity (PI) simulation. “The OSAT sits where die, substrate or interposer, passives, and board meet, so we are brought in earlier to model the package-level PDN and co-simulate it with the customer’s die power data,” said Alex Kizeev, technical director of signal and power integrity at Amkor’s design optimization team.
Kizeev breaks down the supply chain and responsibilities among different companies. “The best results come from a PDN budget partitioned across the die, package, and board. The foundry and fabless teams own the on-die PDN, including the die power map and the bump-map allocation. The substrate supplier defines what stackup and via/plane technology is possible. The OSAT optimizes the package-level pieces, including stackup choice, via and ball assignment, DCap selection and placement, warpage and reliability, and validation.”
“Backside power delivery can significantly improve power delivery by reducing IR drop and freeing up frontside routing resources for signals, but it doesn’t eliminate power-integrity challenges,” said Philips. “It also changes the thermal landscape. As power delivery and other structures move to the backside, the paths available for heat removal become more complex. This makes co-optimization of power integrity and thermal management increasingly important.
The overall trend is moving toward closer integration in advanced packages and dies, including the integration of inductors, capacitors, and power-conversion components into substrates and interposers.
Why power losses scale with increasing power
A simple illustration shows how the power efficiency drops as the industry scales from a 1kW GPU to a 5kW GPU (see figure 2). While losses from the voltage regulator itself stay constant at around 13%, resistive losses jump from 8% to 31%, and voltage droop rises from 17% to 31%. As a result, increasing power levels must be supplied to meet all the chip-level needs.
Fig. 2: At higher power levels, the PDN efficiency using motherboard voltage regulators degrades significantly due to VR losses, resistive losses, and droop. Source: Intel Foundry
With this lateral power delivery approach, power integrity (PI) becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as compute loads rise. As AI accelerators integrate increasing levels of compute, HBM, and interconnects between devices, the low supply voltage (0.7-0.9V) of devices means multiple kiloamp levels of current are needed to meet the high-power needs of modern GPUs. As if managing kiloamp currents is not enough, fast workload transients tend to magnify voltage droop, so designers apply voltage guardbands that further increase power consumption and reduce system efficiency. [1]
Next-gen data centers pull in 800V
For next-generation data centers built to meet AI demands, 800V DC power delivery is starting to replace traditional AC power distribution. The 800V DC power distribution coexists with multiple distributed regulators located much closer to individual loads.
To lower transmission losses from the grid to the microprocessor, next-generation PDNs begin at 800V DC and are stepped down in stages using DC-to-DC converters to 48V, 12V, and then 0.7V, for instance. One of the most critical junctures occurs at the point of load, where integrated voltage regulators supply the AI multi-chiplet package. By limiting the number of power conversions, system-level efficiency can improve while reducing thermal cooling requirements.
The voltage regulator module can be positioned underneath the PCB, a logical first step that is commonly referred to as vertical power delivery. However, chipmakers are embracing recent developments that shrink the size of various voltage regulator components, especially capacitors and inductors, to move voltage regulation inside the main processor package and below the SoC, called integrated power delivery. Finally, integrating voltage regulator components into the interposer itself is called fully integrated power delivery.
One step at a time
The approach companies take to voltage regulation integration depends on the company’s expertise, its partners, and the complexity of the system involved.
For this reason, companies are introducing suites of solutions. For example, ASE is offering a range of power delivery capabilities to enable PCB backside integration, which considers the limited space inside computer trays. [2] The company’s PowerSiP options can include double-sided connected capacitors sandwiched between coreless substrates; substrateless designs, solder-free cap array modules with exposed terminals for embedded substrate or PCB solutions; high-aspect-ratio 4:1 copper pin integration for lower packaging impedance; and high-density active and passive component integration using single- or double-sided molding.
“Power efficiency is becoming a defining challenge for next-generation AI systems,” said Harrison Chang, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE. “By shortening the high-current transmission path, our solution can reduce parasitic routing losses by 50% or more, translating directly into meaningful power savings at the system level,” he said in the release.
In June 2025, Marvell introduced its Package Integrated Voltage Regulator (PIVR) technology for AI and HPC. The PIVR replaces the conventional arrangement of discrete voltage-regulator components, often several inches away on the PCB, with compact silicon power converters and passive components tightly coupled to the processor. It’s designed to reduce the amount of low-voltage, high-current routing between the regulator and the processor. The PIVR can sit on the underside of the processor package, shortening the path from voltage conversion to the processor’s power connections. It also can sit next to the processor’s package or inside the advanced package.
Marvell is partnering with multiple companies on integration, including Infineon, which makes power semiconductors and packaged devices; Ferric, which specializes in designing integrated voltage regulators using thin-film magnetic inductors; Monolithic Power Systems, a developer of high-current-density power modules; and Empower Semiconductor, a developer of compact integrated power converters.
In July of this year, Analog Devices completed the acquisition of Empower Semiconductor, expanding ADI’s AI compute power delivery capabilities with integrated voltage regulators and silicon capacitors. “By enabling power conversion closer to the processor, the combined solution shortens the power delivery path and improves efficiency to support higher-performance, higher-density systems. Building on its leadership in high-performance power management, ADI is investing in its system-level platform to deliver a step-change in performance, density, and efficiency from grid to core.” [3]
In addition, on Nov. 2, onsemi announced it will acquire the assets of Ferric, which develops integrated voltage regulators, for up to $775 million. [4]
To understand these important acquisitions, it helps to take a closer look at IVRs.
What is an IVR?
An integrated voltage regulator is typically a 3D stack arrangement that replaces off-chip voltage regulator modules and bulky capacitors and inductors on the PCB with integrated magnetics and passives mounted onto the silicon or package using thin-film technology.
“The IVR is implemented as a 3D stack, bringing together the deep-trench capacitor, PMIC, and inductor, and embedding them directly into the substrate or interposer,” said Veshal Sridhar, product engineering architect, 3D IC at Synopsys. “Companies are moving it closer to the SOC for obvious reasons such as reduced signal parasitics between IVR and SOC die, but that introduces new thermal effects and stress effects because you’re bringing another 3D stack in and embedding it inside an interposer. There’s also potential noise coupling into the other dies from the IVR, because even for a simple 3D stack you are going to have noise coupling.”
In what Intel Foundry refers to as a Super High Density MIM (metal-insulator-metal), capacitance density can be improved by 10× compared to conventional MIM capacitors. [5] This may offer response times on the order of nanoseconds. As part of Intel’s collaboration with UMC for 12nm finFETs, the capacitors feature three metal layers for routing in a scalable design. “This broad adaptability highlights the HDMIM as a universal, highly scalable passive component, capable of heterogeneous integration with logic and power chips manufactured across diverse process nodes from various foundries.” [5]
Inductors have traditionally been one of the greatest passive bottlenecks due to their large footprint, but by integrating them into the package using copper-plated through-hole technology and advanced magnetic materials (see Figure 3), Intel is touting a high resistance-to-capacitance ratio while minimizing stray magnetic fields that could adversely affect surrounding circuits. [5]
Fig. 3: This in-package inductor uses copper-plated through holes embedded with high-permeability magnetics to improve the resistance-to-capacitance ratio and limit magnetic parasitic effects. Source: Intel Foundry
Intel’s FIVR platform uses switched-capacitor voltage regulators and hybrid buck converters to accommodate nanosecond transient spikes by computing cores without exacerbating voltage droop. FIVRs that allow a continuous switching range are superior to fixed SCVRs when it comes to delivering low-voltage inputs (e.g., 1.8 to 3V).
Finally, Intel’s low-voltage GaN MOSHEMT-on-CMOS devices are designed for >12V applications, where high density and high efficiency are essential, while minimizing the overall number of power conversions. By integrating both low voltage and high voltage MIM capacitors with active devices, it minimizes PDN impedance from VR to load. By monolithically integrating the GaN power switches with GaN nMOS drivers, the company can achieve even faster response to transients along with aggressive power density.
“Integrated voltage regulators provide unprecedented speed and granularity in voltage control, but realizing their full power-saving potential requires equally precise visibility into the silicon itself,” said proteanTecs’ Sever. “Traditional power management methods leave significant timing margin untapped. By continuously measuring timing margins across the full chip, cycle by cycle, under actual operating conditions, our embedded monitoring technology identifies where performance is truly limited and where voltage can be safely reduced. Combined with the fine-grained control of IVRs, this enables more aggressive power optimization without compromising performance or reliability.”
Can the system handle the power?
Multiphysics simulation plays an important role in power delivery planning. “A designer may have a simple stack in mind, interposer, base die, top die, and substrate. And it starts with a prototype grid and listing the power required for each die,” explained Synopsys’ Sridhar. “So there is a power budget that comes from the devices, and number of C4 bumps, number of microbumps, TSVs, etc. You want to determine whether your power delivery system can deliver the power needed from the C4 bumps through the top of the stack. Starting with a simple static IR-drop analysis, we can then leverage 3DIC Compiler together with signoff solutions like RedHawk-SC to help bridge the gap between early bump planning and PSE (power sourcing equipment) planning.”
In cases where the PDN cannot handle the power required of the system, design changes such as increasing the interposer size may come into play.
Sridhar noted how one customer brought system-level PI (power integrity) analysis into the early architecture stage, closing the loop between implementation and system analysis using 3DICC plus RHSC, turning iterations that once took days into hours and giving designers more freedom to explore before the architecture is frozen.
At the same time, the package assembly design kits that OSATs compile are becoming more detailed. “Kits are moving beyond geometric design rules to include electrical models, material properties, and validated reference designs. Teams now must consider bump pitch against current density, metal layers against cost, and DCap placement against thermal path early in the design,” said Amkor’s Kizeev.
Conclusion 
Power integrity and power efficiency have already become key differentiators in advanced AI accelerator-based data center designs. Companies are racing to incorporate leading power delivery solutions, including integrated voltage regulators, in positions closer to the GPU or AI accelerator modules where they can be most effective. Advanced power delivery began with the integration of wafer backside PDNs, but package-level and interposer-level solutions are coming fast.
Coordination among major companies in the supply chain is critical during early-stage PDN design. “Some of these design houses are not building the entire system, for instance, like HBM, where even the base die and the stack may be coming in from other design houses,” noted Synopsys’ Phillips. They want to make sure that the grid they’re designing in-house works with the other models. So they want a model exchange between these two, which is performed as part of a feasibility analysis.”

Moving the power delivery network to the backside of a chip reduces congestion, but it introduces new challenges for fabs.
GaN Power Devices Go Vertical
Why new designs and process flows could help overcome manufacturing challenges.
New Approaches To Power Decoupling
Strategic placement of decoupling capacitors and regulators is critical to keeping power stable, but no one approach is sufficient.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 19, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 19, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, November 19, 2026.
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Meet the women breaking barriers in deeptech, building technologies for tomorrow
On Women’s Entrepreneurship Day, we look at women founders pushing the boundaries of Indian deeptech, building frontier technologies, and opening new possibilities for innovation and entrepreneurship.
Anthropic raises $81.3B in IPO, surpasses SpaceX's record offering
Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion through its initial public offering (IPO), making it the largest stock market offering on record and surpassing Elon Musk-led space company SpaceX's $75 billion IPO. Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, above the previously indicated range of $70-78 per share. The company is set to make its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, at a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.
Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi
Six Indian startups have been selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi, following the UAE-India Start-Up Series 2.0 finale in Bengaluru. Hub71, Abu Dhabi's global tech ecosystem, is the cross-border partner which will connect the startups with investors, corporate and government partners, regulators, and prospective customers.
Funding news
Style Union raises Rs 485 Cr to expand beyond southern India
Nexon Omniverse Limited, the parent company of value-fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore in a Series E round led by Venturi Partners, a consumer-focused investment firm, and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners, a growth-stage investor.
Quick service restaurant chain Boba Bhai raises $18M in Series B round
Boba Bhai, an Indian bubble tea and Korean street food brand, has raised $18 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, alongside existing investors including Titan Capital.
InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO
InPrime Finserv, a tech-led NBFC, has raised Rs 101 crore in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. This round also saw participation from existing investors Z47 and Pravega Ventures.
Disseqt AI raises $8M to build enterprise AI safeguards
Disseqt AI, a Dublin-headquartered AI assurance company with a significant presence in India, has raised $8 million in a round led by Gresham House Ventures, the growth equity arm of investment manager Gresham House.
VitusCare raises $3 million in Series B funding
VitusCare, a dialysis care provider, has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round led by Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, with participation from HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, and angel investors. The company said its revenue has nearly tripled since its previous funding round in late 2024. Its network has expanded from 22 to over 60 dialysis centres across nine states and more than 50 cities.
VitusCare has treated over 35,000 patients and delivered 8 lakh dialysis sessions. It reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26. It plans to expand to over 100 centres by FY27, besides investing in technology, AI-powered solutions and workforce training.
Other news
Intuit inaugurates new technology campus in Bengaluru
Global financial technology company Intuit has inaugurated its new Bengaluru office at Embassy Tech Village, strengthening its investment in India as a strategic hub for technology and AI innovation. The two-tower campus houses the company's second-largest engineering centre and nearly a quarter of its global technology talent is based in Bengaluru. Intuit has maintained a presence in the city since 2005. The new facility features collaborative workspaces, focus zones and locally inspired artwork and design.
The company said the campus would support the development of AI-powered products and financial technology solutions for customers worldwide. Alex Balazs, Chief Technology Officer, Intuit, said Bengaluru teams were central to building AI-driven experiences that help customers prosper.
CoinDCX-backed Digital Suraksha Network partners Karnataka government
Digital Suraksha Network (DSN), a non-profit platform focused on combating digital financial fraud, has signed an MoU with the Centre of Excellence for Cybersecurity (CySecK), an initiative of the Karnataka government. The partnership will strengthen cybersecurity awareness, skills development and industry collaboration across the state. The organisations plan to conduct Kannada-language cyber safety campaigns targeting one crore citizens by 2027. They will also provide training resources and mentorship to students, government officials and cybersecurity startups.
DSN was launched by CoinDCX's co-founders in March 2026. According to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, over 65.89 lakh financial fraud complaints were registered between 2021 and 2025, involving reported losses exceeding Rs 55,050 crore.
Zurich Insurance Group to expand Hyderabad GCC to 1,000 employees by 2028
Zurich Insurance Group plans to expand its India Capability Centre in Hyderabad to approximately 1,000 employees by mid-2028, strengthening its global technology, engineering, data and AI operations. The centre forms part of the insurer's global operating model, with teams in India working alongside colleagues across international markets.
Zurich plans to recruit specialists in cloud and platform engineering, data and AI, application development, cybersecurity and quality engineering. The company also intends to increase the centre's responsibility for end-to-end ownership of projects, from defining business requirements to developing and implementing solutions. Amit Kalra, Global Head of Zurich Capability Centres, will lead the development of additional leadership and decision-making capabilities in India.
Cognizant launches immersive learning centre in Chennai
Cognizant has unveiled the first phase of its Cognizant Immersive Learning Center at its Siruseri campus in Chennai, reinforcing its focus on developing technology and AI capabilities among employees. The facility is designed to provide associates with opportunities to explore emerging technologies, acquire new skills and prepare for changing business requirements.
The initiative forms part of the company's broader workforce transformation strategy as AI adoption reshapes technology services and enterprise operations. Rajesh Varrier, President – Global Operations and Chairman and Managing Director, Cognizant India, said the company's focus was on harnessing AI to transform businesses while developing the skills employees need to lead that transformation. The centre is expected to support continuous learning and innovation.
InMobi launches agentic AI advertising platform for businesses
InMobi has launched InMobi Accelerate, a self-service agentic AI advertising platform designed to plan, build, launch and measure campaigns across multiple advertising channels through a single dashboard.
Targeted at small and medium-sized businesses and advertising agencies, the platform uses seven specialised AI agents covering business analysis, audience strategy, media planning, copywriting, creative design, campaign launch and optimisation. It supports Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Advertising, TikTok Ads and ChatGPT Ads, among other platforms. Advertisers can approve campaign plans, budgets and creatives before launch and subsequently manage campaigns through plain-English instructions.
InMobi said the platform also provides a consolidated cross-channel view of advertising performance, helping businesses measure returns and optimise spending.
Pine Labs launches stablecoin-linked payment infrastructure platform
Pine Labs has launched Staq Web3 Orchestrator, a technology platform designed to connect stablecoin balances with conventional card payment infrastructure. The platform aims to simplify the development and operation of stablecoin-linked card programmes by bringing together regulated card issuance, payment processing and programme management. It is being deployed in a stablecoin-linked card programme, with Reap serving as the issuer and BIN sponsorship partner.
Pine Labs will manage the customer proposition, programme operations, technology stack and ecosystem integration, while Reap provides card-issuing infrastructure. The platform supports virtual and physical prepaid cards and online and offline payment experiences. The launch marks Pine Labs' expansion beyond traditional merchant payments into digital assets and mainstream payment infrastructure.
Cashify reports Rs 6.49 Cr net profit in FY26
Cashify has reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 6.49 crore for FY26, compared with a net loss of Rs 10.56 crore in the previous financial year. Revenue from operations increased 50% to Rs 1,641.19 crore, while consolidated EBITDA rose to Rs 22.7 crore from Rs 1.98 crore in FY25.
The recommerce platform attributed its performance to growth in smartphone buybacks, refurbishment and sales, alongside improved operating efficiencies. Employee costs declined to 9% of revenue from 10.5%, even as total expenses increased 45.7%. Cashify now plans to expand beyond smartphones into laptops, tablets, smartwatches, gaming consoles and audio devices, extending its buyback and refurbishment model across consumer electronics.
IBM partners Axis Max Life to strengthen database security
IBM has partnered with Axis Max Life Insurance to strengthen database security across the insurer's hybrid technology infrastructure. The collaboration aims to improve oversight of sensitive customer and financial information distributed across on-premises and cloud environments.
IBM Professional Services delivered the implementation, which is designed to enhance data protection and security controls while supporting the insurer's digital transformation initiatives. The project is expected to help Axis Max Life strengthen its ability to monitor and protect critical databases as it modernises its technology environment. Mukul Jain, Chief Technology Officer at Axis Max Life Insurance, said building a robust data security foundation was important as the company continued to strengthen its technology and digital capabilities.
Siemens launches AI engineering agent in India
Siemens has launched its Eigen Engineering Agent in India, an AI-powered solution designed to automate industrial engineering tasks. Unlike generic AI tools, the platform operates within engineering systems and understands project-specific context and constraints. It can support tasks such as programmable logic controller (PLC) coding, human-machine interface development and engineering documentation.
Siemens said the solution completes AI-powered workflows two to five times faster than manual alternatives, with up to 80% higher solution quality. Sixteen Indian customers are already using the platform, including Pelican Rotoflex and Z System Intelligent Controls. The technology was among more than 20 industrial AI innovations showcased at Siemens India's seventh Transform Innovation Day, attended by around 500 industry leaders.
BharatPe launches digital ledger to help merchants manage festive business
BharatPe has introduced Udhaar Khata, a digital ledger designed to help merchants manage customer credit, payment collections and bookkeeping during the festive business season. The platform digitises the traditional bahi-khata system, allowing businesses to record customer dues, set payment deadlines and track outstanding amounts through a dashboard. Merchants can also send payment reminders through WhatsApp and SMS, accompanied by UPI-enabled payment links.
The company said the solution aims to simplify bookkeeping and improve collections for small businesses handling higher transaction volumes during festive periods. Udhaar Khata is part of BharatPe's broader strategy to offer technology-led services beyond payment acceptance, including its recently introduced Agentic AI Suite.
Cloud.in joins OpenAI Partner Network as Select Partner
Cloud.in, the cloud, AI, quantum computing and cybersecurity business of Hostin Services, has been named an OpenAI Select Partner within the OpenAI Partner Network. The recognition will support its efforts to help enterprises develop, integrate and operationalise AI solutions.
The company plans to combine OpenAI capabilities with AWS Bedrock to offer model-agnostic enterprise AI services, focusing on security, governance, performance and cost considerations. Its areas of focus include enterprise AI transformation, intelligent automation and governed generative AI adoption. Cloud.in said it would pay particular attention to data governance, security and regulatory requirements for sectors such as BFSI and the public sector. The company has more than 27 years of experience in enterprise technology services.
Naxatra Labs appoints Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as CPO
Indian deep-tech company Naxatra Labs has appointed Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as its Chief Product Officer. He will lead the company's product development, engineering and manufacturing functions as it expands its electric motor and propulsion technology portfolio. Naveen brings experience in electric motor engineering and powertrain development, having spent nearly five years at Ather Energy, where he led motor engineering and subsequently the E-Powertrain team. At Naxatra Labs, he will focus on executing the product roadmap, strengthening design and development processes and improving integration between engineering and manufacturing.
Bank of India joins government's Bharatkosh non-tax receipt portal
Bank of India has announced its association with the Government of India's Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP), also known as Bharatkosh, as an acquiring bank and payment gateway provider. The association will facilitate the collection of non-tax revenues through the government's integrated online platform. The arrangement is aimed at supporting digital payment transactions and providing users with an additional banking channel for making payments through the portal.
Bharatkosh enables the collection of various government non-tax receipts through an online mechanism. Bank of India's participation expands its role in digital payment infrastructure for government services and supports the government's efforts to make revenue collection more accessible and efficient.
Nupur Recyclers reports record Q2 FY27 performance
Nupur Recyclers reported its strongest-ever quarterly performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue rising 124.86% year-on-year to Rs 116.21 crore. EBITDA increased 148.48% to Rs 15.73 crore, while profit after tax grew 103.06% to Rs 8.80 crore. For the first half of FY27, revenue increased 90.27% to Rs 199.24 crore, EBITDA rose 130.34% to Rs 28.59 crore and PAT grew 93.19% to Rs 16.18 crore.
The company attributed the performance to improved production and capacity utilisation across its manufacturing and processing operations. Nupur Recyclers, which operates in ferrous and non-ferrous metal scrap processing, plans to strengthen capacity, improve operational efficiency and diversify across the recycling value chain.
Visage Lines appoints Vinod Nambiar as senior operating partner
Visage Lines, the parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, Bombae, The Mom's Co, rE and 100 Days, has appointed Vinod Nambiar as senior operating partner. Nambiar brings over three decades of experience in consumer businesses, brand building, retail and business transformation, including leadership roles at Hindustan Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive. He will work with the leadership team on manufacturing, product development, design and engineering, besides supporting the company's next phase of growth.
Indeed integrates employer services across Glassdoor and Indeed
Indeed has begun rolling out a unified login for employers across its job platform and Glassdoor, aiming to simplify recruitment and employer branding. The integration will allow businesses to manage their employer presence through a single account, access job listings across both platforms and use Indeed Smart Sourcing to identify candidates.
The companies will continue operating their respective websites independently. Job seekers will also be able to move between the platforms using one login, with shared information helping personalise their experience. Glassdoor reviews and conversations posted anonymously will remain unlinked to users' profiles. The development follows Glassdoor becoming part of Indeed earlier this year, as the companies seek to combine workplace insights with recruitment capabilities.
Apex Opinion launches independent medical advisory platform in India
US-based health technology company Krivox has launched Apex Opinion, an independent medical advisory platform for patients and families in India seeking specialist second opinions. Founded by Dr Saurabh Sanon, the platform connects patients with US board-certified specialists across medical disciplines. Patients can securely submit medical records and diagnostic reports for review and receive written second opinions, video consultations or multidisciplinary assessments through specialised panels. These include Heart Teams and Solid Tumor Boards.
Each opinion is signed by the reviewing physician, with a target turnaround time of seven business days after receiving complete medical records. Apex Opinion is accessible through its website and mobile applications. The company also plans to establish partnerships with hospitals and clinics in India.
Straive expands Microsoft partnership with 700-plus AI accelerators
Straive is deepening its partnership with Microsoft to help enterprises accelerate AI adoption and deployment. The company showcased its capabilities at Microsoft Ignite 2026, highlighting a portfolio of more than 700 data, analytics and AI solution accelerators. Its agent library brings together reusable workflows, AI agents and specialised tools designed to help businesses move beyond experimentation towards enterprise-wide implementation. Straive said customer-specific proofs of concept could be developed using customer data within seven to 14 days. The company recently achieved Microsoft's AI Platform specialisation and works across its Data and AI, Digital and Application Innovation, and Azure Infrastructure portfolios.
Hexnode adds native IT asset management to UEM platform
Hexnode has introduced native IT Asset Management (ITAM) within its Unified Endpoint Management platform, expanding its capabilities beyond enrolled devices to cover the broader workplace equipment lifecycle. The new functionality allows organisations to track laptops, monitors, accessories, furniture and other assets, alongside their assignments, purchase details, warranties and depreciation. It also includes QR-based physical audits and checkout records to help businesses manage equipment allocation and recovery.
The company has additionally introduced dedicated shared-device policies for Android and remote BIOS management for supported Windows PCs. The IT asset management capability is available to customers on Hexnode UEM's Enterprise plan and above, helping IT teams consolidate asset tracking and endpoint management.
Truecaller partners Bolna to bring transparency to enterprise voice AI calls
Truecaller has partnered with Indian voice AI platform Bolna to bring greater transparency and trust to AI-powered enterprise calls. The integration will allow Bolna's enterprise customers to use Truecaller for Business features without changing how their AI agents are developed. Businesses can display their name and logo during calls, provide personalised information about the purpose of each call and identify calls as AI-assisted.
The partnership also introduces post-call features that allow recipients to schedule callbacks when calls are missed or unanswered. The companies said the integration would benefit enterprises using voice AI for collections, renewals, KYC follow-ups and customer service. Bolna will manage conversations, while Truecaller will provide identity and contextual information.
Aurionpro secures additional order worth nearly Rs 100 crore
Aurionpro Solutions has secured an additional order worth nearly Rs 100 crore from a global hyperscaler for data centre infrastructure solutions. With the latest order, the aggregate value of engagements with the customer has exceeded Rs 400 crore, reflecting the expanding relationship between the two companies. The project is expected to strengthen Aurionpro's position in the data centre infrastructure segment as demand for AI-ready computing facilities accelerates. The company provides enterprise technology and data centre solutions, with capabilities spanning infrastructure, engineering and digital transformation.
Bhaskar Bhattacharya, Executive Vice-President and Head of Enterprise Business at Aurionpro, said the company appreciated the customer's continued confidence as it expanded its presence in the growing data centre market.
Mitra FMCG, Tanvi Foods announce Rs 600-crore strategic integration
Mitra FMCG and BSE-listed Tanvi Foods (India) have announced a strategic integration valued at ₹600 crore, aimed at strengthening their food processing, sourcing, procurement and distribution capabilities. The integration, exclusively advised by Bestvantage Investments, is expected to support expansion across domestic and international markets. The partnership will help Mitra leverage Tanvi Foods' export presence to enter high-value markets, including the US, UK and UAE. Mitra's distribution network will support Tanvi Foods' expansion in Northern India, while Tanvi Foods will help Mitra strengthen its presence in Southern India, particularly in household essentials. The arrangement will also provide Tanvi Foods access to raw materials such as flour, maida and edible oils through Mitra's sourcing ecosystem, improving procurement efficiencies and supply-chain operations.
UpTik crosses Rs 100 crore in cumulative investments
UpTik, an invoice financing startup, has crossed Rs 100 crore in cumulative investments. The platform recorded approximately Rs 21 crore in investments during FY26, followed by Rs 79 crore between April and October 2026. Notably, October alone contributed Rs 21.38 crore in investments, exceeding the platform's entire investment volume for the previous financial year.
Alongside this growth, UpTik has maintained an investor retention rate of 80%+, indicating sustained participation and confidence among its investor base. Founded with the aim of connecting investors with businesses seeking working capital, UpTik operates in the invoice financing space, enabling investors to participate in financing business invoices while helping enterprises address cash flow requirements.
OVH Group unveils 55 new cloud and AI products
The OVH Group has unveiled 55 new products across cloud and artificial intelligence at its OVHcloud AI Summit, marking an acceleration of its AI strategy. The offerings span infrastructure, orchestration, inference and AI-augmented platform-as-a-service solutions. The company is expanding its cloud portfolio with NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro, Blackwell B300 and Rubin R200 GPUs, alongside new virtual private cloud networking services. Its AI portfolio includes AI Fabric, serverless computing, AI Endpoints and enterprise-focused AI Agents and AI Search services. Through a partnership with Gladia, OVHcloud is also extending speech transcription and voice generation capabilities across more than 100 languages. The services will be available across public cloud, private cloud and on-premises deployment models, supported by three dedicated AI research laboratories.
Taboola completes acquisition of digital advertising firm Dianomi
Global performance advertising company Taboola has completed its acquisition of Dianomi, a digital advertising services provider focused on premium business, finance and lifestyle publishers. The acquisition strengthens Taboola's ability to offer specialised financial advertising solutions through its Realize performance advertising platform, which uses proprietary publisher inventory, first-party data and artificial intelligence. Dianomi connects leading advertisers, including with audiences across premium publishers. With a network of more than 600 advertisers and publishers, the acquisition is expected to expand Taboola's reach among high-value business and finance audiences.
Scalefusion wins Platinum award at 2026 MarCom Awards
Unified endpoint management platform Scalefusion has won the Platinum Level distinction at the 2026 MarCom Awards for its brand film, “One Platform. One Agent. We are Scalefusion.” The award recognises the creative execution of the film and its presentation of the company's unified IT platform vision. The film showcases Scalefusion's core offerings, including Endpoint Management, OneIdP and Veltar, highlighting how device management, identity access and endpoint security work together within an integrated IT environment.
Bansi Astro crosses 15,000 users within two weeks of launch
Bansi Astro, an AI-powered astrology platform founded by Writesonic CEO Samanyou Garg, has crossed 15,000 users within two weeks of launching its Android application. The platform combines traditional Vedic astrology with artificial intelligence to offer personalised readings, Kundli analysis and voice-based consultations in English, Hindi and Hinglish. Its proprietary astrology engine uses classical systems, including Parashari and Krishnamurti Paddhati, to calculate planetary positions and generate interpretations.

articles.title: The bottleneck just moved: why African startups should care about MCP - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Earlier this year, our four-person studio cleared a 126-item product backlog in a single 48-hour stretch. A few weeks later, an AI edited a 268,000-word manuscript overnight — coordinating a dozen sub-agents while the author watched from a terminal, writes Barrett Nash, former-founder of Rwandan startup SafeMotos and now CEO of InfiniteUp.
Neither happened because AI suddenly got smarter. Both happened because of a quiet piece of plumbing called MCP, and it deserves more attention from African founders than it’s getting.
What MCP actually is, in plain language
MCP — the Model Context Protocol — is an open standard, introduced by Anthropic in late 2024 and since adopted across the industry, that lets AI assistants operate software rather than just talk about it.
Think of any piece of software as having a front desk: a published list of requests it will accept. MCP lets an AI walk up to those front desks itself. Before MCP, you described a problem and the AI described a solution — then you did the work. With MCP, it does the work. Type “make the button on the contact page green,” and in your website builder, the button turns green.
That’s the entire idea. Everything interesting is downstream of it.
Why this matters more in Africa than almost anywhere
African tech has a long habit of turning constraints into architecture. M-Pesa didn’t wait for branch banking; it leapfrogged it. The constraint MCP erases is headcount.
A four-person team that restructures its work around these tools can genuinely outproduce a much larger one that has bolted a chat window onto an unchanged process. We know because we are one: 40+ production apps, users in 117 countries, including DOER Business, a product we built specifically for African small businesses. Meanwhile, the cost side has collapsed — our own AI bills fell roughly 100× in three years. Intelligence stopped being a premium feature and became affordable infrastructure, priced for markets where every dollar of runway counts.
For startups that could never afford a twenty-person engineering floor, that combination — AI that does the work, at prices that keep falling — is not an efficiency gain. It’s a different game.
What it looks like in practice
Real examples from our own workshop this year:
- Operations that run themselves. Connect an AI to your inventory, your payment provider and WhatsApp, and “check stock, reorder, notify the customer” stops being someone’s job and becomes a sentence.
- Localisation as market-building. Asked to translate our site for Gulf markets, the AI didn’t translate it — it deployed sub-agents that rebuilt every page’s argument for a different audience. The same approach applies to Swahili, Amharic or Lingala: not your words in another language, but your business argued to a different room.
- Grounded strategy. We fed our raw search data straight into the model and let evidence, not opinion, set our content strategy. Organic traffic responded within weeks.
- Finishing what AI started. A wave of founders have “vibe-coded” apps to 80% in tools like Lovable and Bolt — then stalled at the last, hardest 20%. Rescuing those apps is now real engineering work, and the demand is continental.
The honest caution
MCP hands AI a pair of hands, not judgment. We once watched an agent of ours report five consecutive rounds of “improving results” while measuring nothing at all — the numbers were real, the link to reality had quietly broken. Our rule since: more AI throughput means more human verification, not less. The teams that win with this won’t be the ones that automate everything; they’ll be the ones that know exactly what to supervise.
Where to start
You don’t need a research budget. Pick one painful, well-documented workflow — documentation quality is the real fuel here — connect an AI to the systems it touches, and supervise the first runs closely. If you want a shortcut: we’re offering a free 30-minute MCP consultation to any company that wants a concrete map of what this could do for their business — no pitch, just the map. The tools are the easy part. The reorganization is the work, and it’s the most interesting work in software right now.

articles.title: Amflow releases UE Carbon smart e-bike series built for commuting and cruising - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Amflow has unveiled an impressive fusion of technology and mechanics with the launch of the Amflow UE Carbon series commuter e-bikes.
The innovation-driven bike brand has been working for years on its e-bike engineering and technology to finally bring its product to commuters.
The UE series has a sleek lightweight design and combines it with an advanced drivetrain system to deliver comfort and performance without compromise.
The UE series is built for commuting, running errands or enjoying a weekend ride.
The bike has an ultralight 2.35kg carbon fibre frame has a total bike weight of 20.9kg, which means it offers ideal handling for commuting and is easier to load onto trains and elevators.
It’s available in Luna White and has a clean sleek look.
There are two models: the Amflow UE Carbon Pro and the Amflow UE Carbon. The biggest difference between the two is the drivetrain options.
Each offers intelligent electronic shifting with automatic shifting and smooth shift for easier seamless gear changes on all kinds of road conditions.
Tech Guide has received the Amflow UE bike to review.
It arrived in a large box and we had to put a few things together and attach a few items to get it ready for the road.
We will share our review in the coming weeks.
Amflow UE’s standard size can fit riders from 155cm to 190cm and has interchangeable stems in two heights to easily adjust your riding position and make it possible to share with family members and friends.
Amflow is planning on releasing a smaller version of the bike for riders 140cm to 160cm in 2027.
The bike has been designed to offer a 90 per cent upright posture between the saddle and the handlebars to prevent shoulder and back pressures.
It has a low step-through frame, which also makes it easy to mount and dismount.
Amflow UE is designed for comfort and comes with a suspension system to help reduce fatigue and soften the bumps.
Front forks have 65mm of travel to soak up impact and reduce vibration coming through to the handlebar.
The saddle has been designed to fold to the rider’s body for extra comfort.
Bike also has front and rear Magura 180mm disc brakes with a three-finger lever designed for reliable stopping power.
Also on board are 2-inch wide Maxxis 26 inch tyres to handle all surfaces and terrain.
And the whole bike is powered by the Avinox M2 e-drive system, which offers 125Nm maximum torque and 1,100W peak power.
The battery is removable for easier charging.
It provides enough power to climb 30 degree grades, even with a heavy load.
It also has an intelligent traction control system, which can judge your pedalling intent and guide how quickly and smoothly power is delivered.
This is particularly useful when going through stop-and-go traffic, inclines, or light off-road climbing.
The Amflow UE can run for up to 132 km on a single charge. A 600Wh swappable battery is also available so users can extend their rides.
The battery can also charge quickly and go to 100 per cent in 2 hours and 23 minutes.
It also has a built-in charge limit to protect long-term battery health.
AMFLOW UE CARBON PRO
It features a customised three-speed electronic internally geared hub and Gates carbon belt for a low-maintenance silent ride.
It has excellent climbing, relaxed cruising, and high-speed riding, and fast accurate shifting even while stationary.
AMFLOW UE CARBON
Includes a 10-speed electronic rear derailleur for precise gear increments.
Models have a smart auto boost feature, which automatically kicks in when road conditions and motor output need adjustment.
Automatic boost also can help with demanding urban riding conditions and offer additional power without manual input.
For example it will kick in when attempting steep inclines or pulling away at traffic lights with a loaded bike.
The bikes include the Avinox DP200 handlebar display, which has a 1.4-inch touchscreen mounted on the handlebars.
Also includes a phone mount to keep riders powered and connected, with 15W wireless charging and 20W USB-C fast charging.
Avinox Ride app also for connectivity and other features, including ride record merging, pairing multiple bikes, Apple Watch connectivity to sync health stats, smart heart rate control and DJI Osmo camera connectivity.
The bike also has carrying capacity with front rack that can support a 20 kg load and a rear rack with a 27 kg payload capacity.
On the security side the bike does have a key that locks both the frame and the battery.
If the bike is lost or stolen, riders can enable Lost Mode within the Avinox Ride app and report the serial number.
They are even able to lock down key components.
The bike can also be located because it integrates with the Apple Find My ecosystem and tracked in real time.
PRICING
Amflow UE Carbon Pro – $5,599
Amflow UE Carbon – $4,999

articles.title: L'écran du nouveau MacBook Pro fait mal aux yeux de certains de ses utilisateurs
articles.text:
Avec ce MacBook Pro Oled tout juste sorti, Apple s’est essayé pour la première fois aux dalles Oled sur ses ordinateurs portables. Un écran magnifique, mais Apple semble n’avoir pas réussi un point : le taux de scintillement de la dalle. Tant et si bien que certains clients se plaignent de cet écran qui leur causerait des douleurs aux yeux.
Maux de tête, yeux qui brûlent…
Certains acheteurs du tout dernier MacBook se plaignent en ligne. Par exemple l’un d’eux nommé pelzo0711 s’est exprimé sur le forum de MacRumors : « je me demande ce qui arrive à mes yeux. Ils me brûlent constamment et sont fatigués. Parfois, ma vision se dégrade ou je ressens simplement une douleur derrière les globes oculaires ». Même ressenti pour un certain HD4kAI sur Reddit : il explique ressentir des vertiges et que « ça rend la lecture de texte presque nauséabonde. » Dans les réponses, un autre internaute l’assure : « J’ai dû retourner mon 16 aujourd’hui pour cette raison. Écran magnifique, mais fatigue oculaire et nausées après utilisation. »
En bref, les symptômes sont multiples, mais tous ces témoignages convergent sur un point : ces gênes ne sont pas immédiates pour tous, mais surviennent souvent après une utilisation prolongée. C’est particulièrement le cas lorsqu’on lit du texte ou qu’on travaille sur des fonds sombres. La plupart de ces témoignages parlent d’une sensation de brûlure oculaire, les yeux qui piquent, une vision qui fatigue. D’autres parlent de maux de tête, de vertiges ou encore de nausées.
Pourquoi cet écran Oled peut faire mal aux yeux
Le point commun est le PWM, pour Pulse Width Modulation, une technique qui règle la luminosité de l’écran de ce MacBook en allumant et en éteignant les pixels à très haute fréquence. Grâce à la persistance rétinienne, en général cela ne pose pas de problème aux yeux, puisque ces derniers perçoivent une luminosité moyenne. Sur son dernier ordinateur, Apple est obligé d’utiliser cette technique puisque sur un écran Oled, il n’y a pas de rétroéclairage : pour ajuster la luminosité, il faut allumer et éteindre chaque pixel à une fréquence suffisamment élevée.
Le problème sur ce MacBook Pro Proled XDR, c’est que selon les mesures de Notebookcheck, le scintillement est réglé à 240 Hz dès que la luminosité n’est pas au maximum. Un taux extrêmement faible par rapport à d’autres écrans de smartphones ou d’ordinateurs, y compris chez Apple. Il faudrait plutôt monter à 3 125 Hz, un taux au-delà duquel on considère qu’on ne peut pas voir le scintillement à l’œil nu.
Il n’y a pas grand-chose à faire pour régler ces désagréments, mais si vous pensez acheter cet ordinateur, nous vous conseillons de l’essayer en magasin avant de vous décider. Apple n’a pour le moment pas réagi publiquement à ces plaintes : aucun correctif logiciel n’a été annoncé. Pourtant, il est possible de corriger ce problème : Google l’avait fait sur ses Pixel 10 l’année dernière.

articles.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
articles.text:
Ask many IT teams how they would recognize ransomware, and the answer is still “when files start changing extensions.” By then, the intrusion may already include credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion, recovery sabotage, lateral movement and data exfiltration.
Encryption is often a late-stage action, not the beginning of the attack. In data-extortion attacks it never happens at all: the operators steal data and threaten to leak it without encrypting anything.
Recent attacks against on-premises SharePoint servers illustrate that sequence. After exploiting internet-facing systems, operators used stolen credentials and legitimate administration tools to move through victim environments before deploying ransomware.
The practical lesson is simple: defenders need to detect the behaviors that precede encryption, not only the encryptor itself.
Acronis Cyber Platform (formerly Acronis Cyber Protect Cloud) natively integrates cybersecurity, data protection and endpoint management through a single agent, console and policy framework.
When the relevant capabilities are licensed and enabled, Acronis Active Protection, EDR, MDR and XDR can help detect, contain and recover from ransomware-related activity before widespread encryption occurs.
Five high-value signals deserve immediate attention:
- Defense tampering: Attempts to stop security services, modify protection agents, load vulnerable drivers or clear event logs.
- Privilege escalation and lateral movement: Unexpected privileged accounts, remote-execution tools spreading across hosts or unusual server-to-server remote access.
- Data exfiltration: Unusual outbound transfers from systems that do not normally upload large volumes of data.
- Recovery sabotage: Deletion of shadow copies, backup catalogs or recovery options with tools such as vssadmin.exe, wbadmin.exe or bcdedit.exe.
- Pre-encryption file behavior: Rapid file enumeration, repeated read-write-rename activity and encryption-like changes across local or network locations.
How do ransomware gangs typically gain initial access to corporate networks?
Ransomware attacks rarely begin with the ransomware payload itself. Operators first need an initial foothold, and common entry paths include exploitation of vulnerable internet-facing systems, abuse of stolen credentials, and social engineering.
An unpatched externally accessible service can provide a route into the environment, while compromised credentials can allow an attacker to enter through legitimate remote-access or cloud services.
Social engineering adds another path by targeting users and the processes around identity and access.
Once attackers establish access, the initial compromise can become the starting point for credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion and lateral movement.
Organizations should reduce unnecessary internet exposure, prioritize patching of high-risk systems, strengthen identity and access controls, and protect email and collaboration channels.
Monitoring endpoints for suspicious post-compromise behavior provides another layer when preventive controls do not stop the initial intrusion.
The article already establishes these pre-encryption stages as important signals defenders should detect.
Acronis Cyber Platform supports this layered approach from one platform.
On the detection and response side, endpoint protection, built on Acronis Active Protection and EDR, identifies and contains malicious activity once an attacker gains a foothold, while email security and XDR extend that detection to the attack surface beyond the endpoint.
On the prevention side, vulnerability assessment and patch management reduce exploitable exposure, security posture management and security policy management close configuration gaps, and data loss prevention limits what an intruder can take.
Together these create a progression from reducing opportunities for initial compromise to detecting and responding to activity after one occurs.
What are the warning signs of ransomware before encryption or data theft?
Encryption happens late in a ransomware attack, and data-extortion attacks may skip it entirely. Earlier warning signs include defense tampering, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, recovery sabotage and pre-encryption file activity.
Learn how to detect each signal, respond quickly and recover.
Try for Free
How does ransomware protection prevent an attack instead of only detecting it?
Stopping ransomware is rarely about a single control. Organizations need to reduce the opportunities attackers have to get in, detect and contain malicious activity when they do, and have a reliable way to recover if systems or data are affected.
That makes prevention, detection and response, and recovery different parts of the same ransomware defense strategy.
Acronis brings those layers together in one platform.
On the prevention side, patch management reduces exploitable exposure, security posture management and unified endpoint and security policy management close configuration gaps before an attacker can use them, data loss prevention limits what can leave the environment, and data protection with immutable backups removes the leverage that recovery sabotage depends on.
On the detection and response side, Active Protection, EDR, XDR and email security identify and contain malicious activity across endpoints, email and the wider environment. Integrated backup and recovery then provide the path to restoring affected systems and data.
That last layer is critical for getting operations back online, but it does not undo data theft, an important distinction in double-extortion attacks.
How do detection tools stop ransomware before it encrypts files?
Ransomware rarely goes straight to encryption. Endpoint detection tools can spot the suspicious activity that comes first, from attempts to disable defenses to lateral movement and unusual file activity. The table below breaks down five signals worth watching, the controls that can address them and how Acronis supports each response.
| Signal | Recommended control | Acronis implementation | 
| Recovery sabotage | Alert on recovery-tool abuse; stop the malicious process; maintain off-host, immutable recovery points. | Active Protection blocks ransomware behavior and restores affected files. Self-protection helps defend Acronis components and backups. Immutable Acronis Cloud Storage protects eligible recovery points. | 
| Defense tampering | Use agent self-protection, exploit prevention, vulnerable-driver controls and off-host logging. | Self-protection helps prevent unauthorized changes to the Acronis agent. EDR/XDR and SIEM integrations add incident visibility, subject to configuration. | 
| Privilege and lateral movement | Monitor privileged-account changes and remote-execution activity; isolate affected endpoints. | EDR/XDR correlates activity across workloads, presents the attack chain and supports endpoint isolation and response actions. | 
| Data exfiltration | Monitor unusual data flows and apply controls appropriate to systems and users, based on least-privilege principle. | XDR correlates endpoint activity with supported telemetry sources. Acronis DLP controls sensitive-data transfers on supported endpoints. | 
| Pre-encryption file behavior | Use behavioral detection and automated rollback; protect local data, network folders and servers. | Active Protection uses behavioral and AI/ML-based detection to stop ransomware and restore affected files. Network folder and server-side protection extend coverage where supported. | 
What should an organization do immediately after detecting ransomware?
The first actions should limit spread, preserve evidence and create a safe path to recovery. Organizations should pre-authorize automated actions for clearly defined, high-severity conditions and test them before an incident.
- Isolate the affected workload while preserving the management channel needed for investigation.
- Stop malicious processes and quarantine confirmed malicious files.
- Protect evidence, including process trees, command lines, network connections and relevant logs.
- Identify and disable the compromised account, token or remote-access path.
- Patch the exploited vulnerability or close the exposed service after containment.
- Restore affected files or workloads from a known-good recovery point, then validate the recovered environment before reconnecting it.
- Escalate to incident-response, legal, privacy, insurance and communications stakeholders according to the organization’s response plan.
Acronis EDR and XDR support investigation, isolation and response actions from the incident view. Recovery actions depend on the applicable backup and recovery licenses, available recovery points and configuration.
Acronis MDR by Acronis TRU adds 24/7 expert monitoring, investigation and response; managed remediation and recovery are included in the Advanced service tier within the agreed scope and permissions.
Turn pre-encryption signals into tested controls
The value of an early ransomware warning depends on what happens next. The five signals above can give defenders an opportunity to contain an attack before encryption spreads, but only if the response is already defined and tested.
Whether it is an attempt to delete shadow copies, data exfiltration, unexpected remote execution or a sudden burst of encryption-like file activity, suspicious behavior should trigger a clear containment and recovery plan.
Acronis Cyber Platform can connect prevention, detection, response and recovery through one integrated platform. Capabilities vary by edition, deployment model, configuration and licensing.

Iliyan Gerov is a cybersecurity product marketing leader at Acronis, where he focuses on EDR, XDR, MDR, emerging AI-driven security technologies, email and collaboration app security, DLP, and security awareness. articles.title: Fontaneros expertos sobre la situación en España: "Antes cambiar la ducha salía por 800 euros, ahora pasa de 1.900"
articles.text:
Cambiar la bañera por un plato de ducha es la reforma más solicitada en los baños españoles, y su precio ha cambiado mucho en los últimos años. Según fontaneros expertos con más de 25 años de experiencia: “antes salía por unos 800 euros, ahora pasa de los 1.900 si se hace bien”. Pero esa comparación parece mezclar dos obras diferentes.
Dos presupuestos diferentes. Esos 1.900 euros coinciden con la guía de precios de reformas de baño de Habitissimo, según la cual cambiar la bañera por un plato de ducha y alicatar la zona de la ducha ronda esa cantidad, con el desescombro, el alicatado, el plato y la mampara incluidos. Eso sí, la misma plataforma mantiene en su guía sobre el cambio de bañera por ducha precios de entre 700 y 900 euros para la sustitución básica con mampara de cristal, y una horquilla general de 900 a 2.300 euros.
Vamos, que lo que acabes pagando entre 800 y 1.900 euros suele depender ya no solo de los materiales escogidos, sino en lo que incluya estos presupuestos.
Por qué ha subido. La subida se debe a los materiales, a los salarios y a una mayor exigencia en impermeabilización y seguridad. Hay datos que lo respaldan: la Asociación Nacional de Constructores Independientes (ANCI) señala que el índice de costes de la construcción del Ministerio de Transportes subió más en el bienio 2021-2022 que en los quince años anteriores, y que la mano de obra siguió la misma tendencia desde 2021.
Lo que se queda fuera. El precio de partida tampoco suele ser el que acabas pagando, porque los presupuestos iniciales dejan fuera a menudo imprevistos como nuevas tuberías o desagües o la retirada de escombros. Para una reforma integral, la guía de reformas de Habitissimo calcula unos 3.500 euros en un baño de unos 5,4 metros cuadrados.
Cómo contener la factura. Para reducir la factura, puedes recurrir a platos cerámicos en lugar de los de resina de gama alta, mamparas correderas estándar, conservar lo que esté en buen estado y limitar el alicatado a la zona de la ducha.
Las ayudas públicas también pueden rebajar el gasto cuando la obra mejora la accesibilidad. En Bilbao, el programa Helduak-Mayores Renove Vivienda de la sociedad municipal Surbisa cubre en su edición de 2026 hasta el 50% del presupuesto protegible, para mayores de 70 años y personas con movilidad reducida o discapacidad sensorial.
