articles.title: Meet the St. Michael’s Hospital doctors building an AI tool to save lives in their ICU | BetaKit
articles.text:
There’s a patient who’s stuck in Dr. Bijan Teja’s head. He calls him “Bob.”
Last year, Bob was sitting in his hospital bed talking with his family and joking with his nurse as he recovered from surgery. Sure, his heart rate rose, and his blood pressure fell a bit throughout the day, but nothing dramatic happened. Everything seemed to be going well. But by midnight, Bob was back on a breathing machine and rushed into surgery. By morning, he was dead.
“The worst feeling as an intensivist is when the alarms only ring when it’s too late and you lose a patient.”
Dr. Bijan Teja,
AI Compass
“The worst feeling as an intensivist is when the alarms only ring when it’s too late and you lose a patient,” Teja, an ICU doctor at St. Michael’s Hospital in Toronto, said.
Teja has been working with Dr. Michael Sklar, his best friend at the hospital, on a new tool that might have been able to save Bob’s life: AI Compass. It will be fed data on tens of thousands of ICU patients to identify imperceptible patterns that emerge in patients’ health before they take a turn for the worse, potentially giving doctors more time to save a life.
“Bijan and I, as ICU doctors, think we know the patterns that exist when someone may deteriorate, and alternatively, when someone may be improving,” Sklar said. “Is it possible that there are signs in the data that we’re collecting that we just don’t know yet … that could signify deterioration?”
AI Compass isn’t in any ICUs yet, and it may sound theoretical right now, but Teja and Sklar have a reason to believe it will work. St. Michael’s Hospital already uses a similar tool called ChartWatch, which monitors patients in wards and provides an early warning if they need to head to the ICU. A hospital study found the tool led to a 26-percent reduction in unanticipated deaths in the general medicine ward, where there is much less data to work with than in the ICU. While wards collect a set of vital signs every four hours, and maybe labs once a day, Teja explained that the ICU collects data every minute, giving AI Compass even more to find patterns in.
“The volume of data is enormous, and on many more things too, including ventilator settings and life support, … many more parameters, and it’s predicting something different,” Teja said. “ChartWatch predicts who needs to go to the ICU; AI Compass predicts who in the ICU is at risk for deterioration and death.”
RELATED: Getting old is hard. This age-tech housing aims to make it easier.
AI Compass has a multidisciplinary team within St. Michael’s of 30 people, including Dr. Amol Verma, who led ChartWatch’s development. Teja and Sklar, who say they bring complementary skill sets to the project, have been working on AI Compass since roughly 2024. However, they didn’t feel like they were actually “getting it off the ground” until earlier this year, Teja said, when they started preparing to pitch for the St. Michael’s Hospital Foundation’s Angel’s Den competition. Angel’s Den claims to be Canada’s biggest medical research competition; earlier this month, it had $700,000 up for grabs, of which AI Compass secured $200,000 under the Mitchell Award for Health System Innovation.
The award is just a start for AI Compass. It buys the team time to train its AI model and get it ready for testing, but Teja stressed he’s “fighting hard” to secure even more because he knows they’ll need it. His ultimate dream is that this St. Michael’s-led project ends up in hundreds of ICUs across Canada and beyond.
“We want to see, looking retrospectively at St. Mike’s patients, would [AI Compass] have caught those patients like Bob earlier and given us more time?” Teja said. “We’ll need more support, but to get it at least to that proof-of-concept stage, already this $200,000 starts to move us toward [it].”
Feature image courtesy St. Michael’s Hospital Foundation.

articles.title: Former Alibaba exec's Everful raises $48.5M to connect retailers with Chinese factories | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Everful, a San Francisco- and Singapore-based startup that connects smaller retailers and brands with Chinese factories and manages the process from order to delivery, has raised $48.5 million in Series A funding.
The round was led by Vertex Ventures Southeast Asia & India and January Capital, with participation from existing investors Square Peg and Lightspeed.
Everful is on track to reach $100 million in annualized revenue by the end of the year, about two and a half years after its launch, co-founder Sisi Song said. The company ships over 5 million items a month to customers in more than 60 countries and works with over 30,000 factory partners, she added. Its online wholesale catalog includes more than 20 million products.
Song, a former Alibaba executive, and serial entrepreneur Kevin Han, who sold a previous company to Amazon, co-founded Everful in 2024. The company began as a jewelry wholesale business before evolving into a multi-category, factory-direct sourcing platform.
Retailers and brands often rely on intermediaries, face high minimum order requirements, and experience long sourcing cycles, which tie up capital in inventory before sales trends are clear. Song noticed the growing gap between fast-changing consumer trends and traditional wholesale sourcing models while working as a venture investor at Bessemer Venture Partners, where she mostly focused on cross-border sourcing and meeting numerous startups in the sector. That same gap shaped Everful’s goal to simplify buying directly from factories through an AI-enabled platform.
The B2B sourcing industry is highly competitive. Big Tech giant Alibaba connects international buyers with manufacturers and suppliers, while Faire, a San Francisco-based wholesale tech platform, enables retailers to purchase wholesale inventory directly from brands. According to Everful’s co-founders, its key differentiator is responsibility for the sourcing process, rather than simply facilitating transactions.
“We take care of everything,” Han said. “We handle sourcing, order consolidation, quality control, and logistics. That’s something the marketplaces don’t offer.”
Everful is built for smaller retailers and brands without dedicated sourcing teams, Song said, and it also verifies the factories it works with. While peers also offer services such as quality inspection, logistics, and AI-powered sourcing, Everful aims to integrate these capabilities into a more streamlined purchasing experience, creating an end-to-end process that reduces the work retailers must handle themselves.
Han added that Everful uses AI agents to automate labor-intensive sourcing tasks, including tracking consumer trends, identifying suppliers, coordinating orders across factories, and managing logistics.
Because Everful sources from Chinese factories, ongoing U.S.-China trade tensions and tariffs bear directly on its business. Song said the co-founders have been thinking about geopolitical issues since day one of building the company, and that this has shaped Everful’s strategy from the outset, leveraging her experience at Alibaba and Bessemer Venture Partners.
She mentioned the Trump administration’s suspension of the de minimis exemption, which had allowed eligible shipments valued at $800 or less to enter the U.S. duty-free, as one example of a shift in trade policy.
Song explained such changes could favor a model that combines overseas sourcing with local retail sales. “We’re empowering local retailers and brands,” she said. “Long-term cross-border commerce will be cross-border B2B sourcing plus local selling.”
Everful plans to use the Series A round to expand its presence in the U.S. and Europe, particularly the U.K., France, and Italy, while investing in AI to automate product customization and other sourcing workflows. It also aims to deepen integrations with e-commerce platforms, building on its Shopify integration as it works toward becoming an end-to-end infrastructure platform for global sourcing.
The startup employs about 70 full-time staff globally, including 45 in research and development. It has also established an AI operations team to connect engineering and business functions.

articles.title: Bell considering its own Telus proposal, held preliminary talks
articles.text:
Bell Canada Enterprises (BCE) reportedly held preliminary talks with Telus and is assessing what a potential Telus transaction would include in the wake of Quebecor’s push to acquire the Vancouver-based national telecom.
Three sources spoke to the Globe and Mail about Bell’s reaction to the Quebecor bid, which included preliminary discussions, hiring financial and legal advisors, and more. Bell is now considering possible next steps, including possible remedies Ottawa might require should Bell move ahead with a formal proposal. However, the considerations are still in the early stages.
The news comes after Quebecor, which owns Freedom Mobile, Videotron, and Fizz, made a roughly $31 billion proposal to acquire all of Telus’ shares. Quebecor first proposed the idea to Telus in June, and then published a revised proposal on Nov. 9.
If a deal were to go through, it would see Canada drop from four major carriers to three. The proposal sparked concerns from critics and politicians over the impacts on competition and affordability. Quebecor CEO Pierre Karl Péladeau, however, said in a recent interview that combining Quebecor and Telus would enable the companies to better fend off foreign competition, such as from satellite provider Starlink.
Telus is currently reviewing Quebecor’s proposal and considering its options. Telus’ special committee director Lisa de Wilde told the Globe that “all options are on the table” when asked about deals from other telecoms.
Notably, this isn’t the first time Bell and Telus have considered combining. The two carriers looked into it in 2007 but didn’t move ahead. However, some in the industry consider the companies to be good potential partners, given that they already have a network sharing agreement. Some made a similar argument for Telus and Quebecor, noting that Telus has a stronger footprint in Western Canada where Quebecor is more limited.
Regardless of the possible synergies Telus has with other telecoms, any combination will inevitably be bad for Canadians. Just look at the Rogers-Shaw merger from a few years ago. Since the companies merged, we’ve seen higher internet and TV costs, worse service, increased customer complaints, and significant cuts to Canadian jobs.
Source: The Globe and Mail

This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive on life support outside the body for seven weeks, smashing the previous record of about two weeks.
They achieved the feat by connecting a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste.
The approach could open up new possibilities in biomedical engineering, from repairing damaged organs to growing new ones. Some researchers are even exploring artificial wombs.
Take a closer look at the technology keeping human organs alive.
—Antonio Regalado
What a billion-dollar deal says about the US battery market
After a tough few years littered with high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US: Sila has signed a deal with battery maker Panasonic Energy to supply silicon-carbon anode material that could be worth more than $1 billion.
The agreement will help Sila scale production, potentially bringing smaller, lighter batteries to market. But it also reveals how battery politics have shifted. The factory is backed by a $1.4 billion loan from the Trump administration’s Defense Department—and the industry is increasingly focused on geopolitics rather than the energy transition.

articles.title: Critical Java vulnerability puts millions of sites, services, and devices at risk of remote code execution — triggers with 64 As and an '=' sign, OpenJDK optimization bug lets an attacker trigger it just by inputting repeated text
articles.text:
Critical Java vulnerability puts millions of sites, services, and devices at risk of remote code execution — triggers with 64 As and an '=' sign, OpenJDK optimization bug lets an attacker trigger it just by inputting repeated text
The Winds of Winter have arrived — just not written by G.R.R. Martin.
We've just had a few high-stakes security vulnerabilities making systems administrators run around with their heads on fire, and the deluge doesn't look like it's stopping any time soon. Java, the programming language that Oracle has always claimed is on billions of devices, has a critical security vulnerability that allows for remote code execution (RCE), often without even needing to log in to the application. The consequence is that an attacker can gain access to the target system, read user and internal data, and have a launch point for further shenanigans, including database access and potential system takeover.
The flaw was dubbed Java4Shell by Calif Research, the lab that found the vulnerability. The researchers say it rates 9.2 on the newer CVSS 4.0 scale, though individual reports from companies like Oracle itself and Red Hat give it their own ratings, but they're all in the 8 to 9.8 range depending on the vendor. The root cause is a bug in OpenJDK, the library that nearly every distribution of Java, whether Oracle's or anyone else's, derives their implementations from.
You can see an exploit of the bug in action below across multiple software services.
The actual bug is a flaw in an optimization for Base64 decoding, functionality that's ubiquitous in any programming language. Base64 is a format to allow for easy transformation of binary data into plain text. In the modern day, it's used to embed files in the middle of text, like inserting image data in the middle of HTML or CSS, attaching files to emails (internally they're all text-based), or simply representing data as text for visual inspection, like file checksums or cryptographic key fingerprints.
Oracle has already fixed the bug and issued updated versions of its wares. However, much like digital certificates, operating systems and even individual programs include their own copy of a Java executable, meaning that the potential blast radius is far wider than you'd expect at first glance. Calif listed many such common applications: at the time of the post, Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and PingFederate all had full unauthenticated RCE, while Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker have RCEs after authentication.
Because Java is so darn widespread, most every company has to issue security advisories and updates for their wares, including IBM, Red Hat, Siemens, and Broadcom. Because so many containers also use Java-based applications in some form, those too are vulnerable, and the count of individual vulnerable container images across registries everywhere is likely a high figure. This is likely not a bug that will be easily eradicated.
There is a condition to trigger the exploit, but it's not too difficult to fulfill. The Java instance in question must be running on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 support and the VBMI extension. In practice, that means chips from the Intel Ice Lake and AMD Zen 4 families, from 2021 and 2022 respectively, for their server variants. Older CPUs are not affected, as the code optimization that contains the bug is specific to VBMI.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The specific bug is in a hand-written assembly optimization that fails a simple bounds check. If an attacker inputs 64 As and an "=" sign as padding, they can overwrite neighboring memory, and then weaponize that corruption, similar to how Heartbleed worked. As usual these days, Calif says that the vulnerability was found by an AI bot, with $200 worth of tokens. Though unlike many other examples, this one was actually fairly deep, and it wasn't low-hanging fruit that illustrated poor code or network security hygiene.

He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: The GTA 6 photo mode is so good players are saying Rockstar accidentally shipped the 'best camera app of the year'
articles.text:
GTA 6 players hail the game's photo mode as a 'cinematography simulator' — pro lighting tools help capture its 'graphically beautiful' world
Forget the missions, it's time to go snapping
- GTA 6 players have discovered the game's impressive 'Photo Studio'
- The in-game photography mode gives you dozens of editing options
- Some have lauded it as a "cinematography simulator"
Our GTA 6 review hails the game as "graphically beautiful and striking" — and some early players are so struck by its visuals they're spending more time in the game's photo mode than on the missions themselves.
The GTA 6 'Photo Studio' can be found by pausing the game and pressing the square button on the PS5 or the X button on Xbox. As a photographer, I'm staggered by the number of technical and editing options on offer — and I'm clearly not alone.
The filmmaker Patrick Tomasso, for example, has hailed GTA 6 as a "cinematography simulator", using the custom lighting and editing tools to create the moody, neo-noir shots below.
These kinds of shots are possible because the game's photo mode goes well beyond offering basics like aspect ratio, depth-of-field control, exposure adjustments, and grain.
The 'Lighting' section lets you add layers (or slots) for sculpting the light in your scene, moving the lights around and letting you adjust their size, intensity, and beam angles. It's a photographic world within a world, and I wouldn't be surprised to see a real-world Grand Theft Auto 6 exhibition touring the world in 2027.
"The best camera app of the year"
As some have noted on X, Rockstar may well have "accidentally shipped the best camera app of the year". But other players think there's still room for improvement in a later 'Photo Studio' update.
For example, as IGN has noted, it isn't yet possible to adjust the facial expressions of characters like Jason and Lucia, or change their poses. You could argue this makes the 'photo studio' more akin to a real photography experience where part of the thrill is capturing unrepeatable moments, but it could also be a nice addition — and perhaps not unlikely, considering you can already tweak a vehicle's headlights, turn signals and more in post-production.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Still, for now, the GTA 6 'Photo Studio' offers more than enough depth for virtual photographers, and could join the ranks of the best video game photo modes alongside the likes of Cyberpunk 2077 and Ghost of Tsushima.
The video above provides a good run-through of some of the options on offer, and there's also a selection of 17 different filters plus a vignette setting to subtly draw the viewer's eye to your subject. Because GTA 6 is indeed a simulation based on real-world physics, all of the traditional photography rules apply — so it's a good time to brush up on skills like great composition.

articles.title: How Virtual Twins And Machine Learning Optimize DRAM Yield
articles.text:
Model process variation, detect multiple failure modes, and evaluate solutions with less wafer experimentation.
As memory technologies continue to scale, manufacturing processes are becoming increasingly complex.
Additional process steps, tighter process windows, and new sources of variation are making it progressively more challenging to reach acceptable yield.
Systemic failures are emerging as a source of yield loss during yield ramp. Unlike random defects, these failures are often driven by complex interactions between multiple process modules.
Rapid root-cause identification of these systemic defects is critical to quickly improving yield and accelerating time-to-market.1 But conventional failure analysis relies heavily on wafer experimentation and statistical analysis, which can be slow and costly as manufacturing complexity increases.
That’s where calibrated virtual twins and machine-learning optimization can help.
Fig. 1: Systemic failures are a key bottleneck during yield ramp. Faster identification and reduction of these failures can accelerate the yield ramp and shorten the time required to reach a targeted manufacturing yield.
Process engineers use virtual manufacturing models (SEMulator3D) with machine learning (ML) optimization (Fabtex Yield Optimizer) to predict process failures.
Using this technique, engineers can evaluate potential yield improvements, all with limited need for wafer-based experimentation.
As an example of this technique, we built a SEMulator3D model (virtual twin) of a DRAM manufacturing process sequence. During this model-building, we established virtual metrology measurements throughout the process sequence (Figure 2).
Fig. 2: Building and calibrating a DRAM virtual twin using process integration, virtual metrology, and silicon data.
ML was then used to calibrate the model against silicon data, enabling the virtual environment to better reproduce observed manufacturing behavior and serve as the foundation for downstream failure analysis and optimization.
For our specific case study, we built a calibrated virtual twin for our DRAM memory device that contained eight known systemic failure mechanisms.
Figure 3 displays examples of these failure mechanisms, including shorts, opens, and overlap-related defects between critical DRAM structures.
Fig. 3: Reproducing systemic DRAM failure modes and detecting them using virtual metrology.
We also specified (in the virtual twin) the virtual metrology needed to detect these failures. By translating each failure into a measurable geometric condition and monitoring it through virtual metrology, we were able to automatically detect and simultaneously analyze multiple failure mechanisms within a single study.
Using the calibrated virtual twin, ML was then applied to help us understand the impact of process and structural variations on the eight predefined failure modes.
We then searched for an optimized manufacturing solution (specific process changes) that provided the lowest failure rate across our eight predefined failure modes. Instead of addressing each failure mode independently, the optimization routine evaluated the impact of multiple process changes simultaneously and searched for process targets that improved the overall pass ratio.
As shown in Figure 4, the optimized process settings significantly reduced all eight systemic failure modes.
Fig. 4: Simultaneous reduction of multiple systemic failures through ML-based optimization and retargeting analysis. A sample retargeting plot for SNLP (storage node landing pad) open/short failures is highlighted.
Under the nominal process conditions used in the study, the predicted total yield was 0.1%. Following optimization, the predicted yield increased to 78.5%, with lower failure rates across all eight failure mechanisms.
This analysis also translated the optimized solution into actionable inline fab targets that can be directly applied in the real process, helping engineers identify which process and structural parameters should be adjusted to further reduce systemic failures.
This work demonstrates how the combination of process models and ML can be used to accelerate yield improvement during DRAM device development. By reproducing process variability in a calibrated virtual environment, and performing simultaneous optimization and retargeting, engineers can detect multiple device failures and investigate a broad solution space without the time and cost of extensive silicon experimentation.
1 I. Tirkel, “Yield Learning Curve Models in Semiconductor Manufacturing,” IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing, vol. 26, no. 4, pp. 564-571, Nov. 2013.

articles.title: Why groundcover's CEO says agents are the power users of observability
articles.text:
Why groundcover’s CEO says agents are the power users of observability
An AI coding agent can write a patch in minutes. Ask it whether that patch slows down the API endpoint your customers hit most, and suddenly it needs something that lives outside the repository. It needs to see how the software runs.
That’s the premise behind groundcover, an observability platform that wants to put production telemetry in the hands of developers and their coding agents. Yes, you read that correctly.
In a conversation with The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City, groundcover CEO and co-founder Shahar Azulay explained why he thinks the same data engineers use to troubleshoot an incident can help an agent write and test a better change in the first place.
Your new observability user is an agent
“Now agents are the power users of observability,” Azulay told TNS.
Groundcover exposes telemetry through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), giving coding agents a way to query it while they work. An agent investigating a slow API, for example, could use traces to see which service accounts for most of the latency. A developer writing a test could use observed application behavior to pick a scenario customers actually encounter.
Groundcover uses that approach internally. Its coding agents pull context from the company’s own telemetry, and agents involved in code review can look at measurements from staging deployments. It’s a way to give a reviewer something concrete to check when a patch looks perfectly reasonable in a diff.
Agents also give engineers something new to monitor. Azulay contrasts a familiar application trace that follows a request across several microservices with an agent run that can span hours and thousands of tool calls. A trace that long can make a Kubernetes incident look like light reading.
Developers may need to inspect prompts and tool calls or use evaluations to judge whether a run behaved as intended. A completed run tells you the agent stopped. The trace can help you figure out what it did along the way.
Less instrumentation work, more room for detail
Groundcover uses an eBPF sensor to collect application and infrastructure telemetry without requiring developers to add an SDK to every service. It also supports OpenTelemetry, so teams can keep sending the signals they already collect and add custom instrumentation where they need more detail. That gives developers a baseline for a new service and a way to get more specific when a particular path or business operation warrants it.
Where the data runs is part of the pitch. Groundcover’s bring-your-own-cloud model keeps telemetry and groundcover’s agent operations in the customer’s cloud environment, Azulay said. Customers pay for the underlying infrastructure, and groundcover manages the deployment.
For teams weighing how much telemetry to retain, the model puts the infrastructure bill in their own account. It also matters when prompts or tool calls may contain sensitive customer data and teams want to keep that information under their control.
We also ask what happens when the platform starts acting on what it sees. Azulay points to groundcover’s move into Kubernetes optimization, where the immediate work centers on cost and resilience. He sees a path from there to agents that can help address an incident on both sides of the deployment, proposing a code change and adjusting infrastructure configuration. The conversation also gets into the practical work of switching observability platforms, including what happens to the dashboards and monitors engineers have spent years building.
Watch the full KubeCon interview on The New Stack’s YouTube channel to hear how groundcover uses its own telemetry in code reviews and why Azulay thinks the next generation of coding agents will be a regular part of the observability stack.

articles.title: Instagram vous laisse enfin éditer vos stories
articles.text:
Qui n’a jamais publié un peu trop rapidement une story sur Instagram avant de le regretter, quelques secondes plus tard, à cause d’un oubli ou d’une vilaine faute ? Jusqu’à présent, Instagram n’offrait aucune solution permettant de corriger ce que vous aviez publié en story, vous obligeant ainsi à supprimer votre publication pour la recommencer ensuite. Mais les choses sont sur le point de changer.
Un délai de 15 minutes pour éditer vos stories
La bonne nouvelle a été annoncée officiellement par Adam Mosseri, le patron d’Instagram en personne sur son compte.
 Voir cette publication sur Instagram
 « Si vous avez déjà remarqué une faute de frappe juste après avoir posté une story, celle-ci est pour vous. Vous pouvez maintenant éditer du texte, de la musique, des autocollants et des dessins pendant 15 minutes maximum après le partage, sans perdre vos vues, vos likes ou vos réponses. » a-t-il ainsi expliqué en commentaire de sa publication.
Cette option d’édition, attendue de longue date par les utilisateurs, est accessible en tapotant le bouton Plus affiché en bas de la story, puis en sélectionnant Éditer la story. Attention toutefois, la possibilité de modifier une story n’est possible que dans les 15 minutes après la publication de celle-ci. Passé ce délai, vous n’aurez donc pas d’autre choix que d’adopter l’ancienne méthode, c’est-à-dire supprimer votre publication pour en refaire une nouvelle.

articles.title: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers
articles.text:
Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the flaws can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access.
The two HTTP/2 vulnerabilities were discovered independently by researchers at Xint, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, and Rapid7, while Xint also discovered three additional NGINX RCE flaws.
Censys later reproduced the underlying memory corruption conditions in four of the five flaws through lab testing, but did not achieve remote code execution.
The first of the two "nginx2root" flaws is CVE-2026-123007, a flow-control bug that can corrupt memory in an NGINX worker. It impacts all versions from 1.31.8 down to 1.9.5, released in 2015.
Wiz demonstrated unauthenticated remote code execution on a server hosting ordinary static files over HTTP/2 with TLS, while Xint demoed root access by chaining it with a separate Linux kernel flaw.
Xint says the separate vulnerability affects the Linux kernel's SCTP subsystem and can be used to escape an NGINX Docker container and gain root privileges on the underlying host.
The second flaw is CVE-2026-123633, a use-after-free problem that affects NGINX when it accepts HTTP/2 connections and proxies requests to a backend. It impacts all versions from 1.19.7 through 1.31.8.
When the worker runs low on connection slots, it can close an active connection and free memory that a request still uses. Wiz also demonstrated remote code execution via CVE-2026-123633, but the firm is not publicly releasing its proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits at this time.
The other three flaws the researchers discovered and F5 fixed are CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634, and CVE-2026-113425, all use-after-free vulnerabilities affecting HTTP/3 reverse proxying, DNS resolution with subrequests, and mail proxy authentication, respectively.
The flaws were fixed in NGINX Open Source 1.30.7 stable and 1.31.9 mainline. NGINX Plus users should update to versions 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1.
F5’s latest security update also addresses five more vulnerabilities not highlighted in the Wiz or Xint reports.
The most notable is CVE-2026-118899, a high-severity issue that allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a worker to enter an infinite loop while reading a request body over TLS 1.3, resulting in denial of service.
For system administrators, it is recommended to upgrade immediately to the latest NGINX release, or temporarily disable HTTP/2 until an upgrade is possible. However, this mitigation only covers the two "nginx2root" flaws.
Evaluating the risk
Regarding the real exploitability risk of "nginx2root," security researcher Florian Roth says it's worse than Node2Shell and Java2Shell, but doesn’t appear to be an imminent threat for most NGINX deployments.
Commenting on X, Roth said the flaws are exploitable in non-default configurations, warning that claims of widespread exposure based solely on NGINX version numbers are misleading.
Xint previously reported that 98.9% of NGINX hosts disclosing recognizable versions were running software within the affected range, but this does not account for whether HTTP/2 is enabled or security fixes have been backported.
The two HTTP/2 flaws require an unpatched server with HTTP/2 enabled on a listener an attacker can reach, while CVE-2026-123633 also requires NGINX to proxy requests to a backend.
Roth scanned a sample of a few hundred NGINX HTTPS endpoints from Shodan and found that roughly 66% of them support HTTP/2, but confirming actual exposure requires checking the server’s configuration and whether a fix has been backported.
According to Censys' live exposure tracker, approximately 8.8 million NGINX services were potentially exposed to CVE-2026-123007 as of November 19, based on affected version numbers and HTTP/2 support.
The company reports that more than 511,000 previously exposed services have already been patched or mitigated, while another 104 million NGINX services do not disclose their versions, making it difficult to determine whether they are affected.

articles.title: Meet SE à 59 €, Tiny 3 Lite 4K à 159 € : OBSBOT baisse ses prix
articles.text:
Pour le Black Friday, OBSBOT met plusieurs de ses webcams en promotion. De la petite Meet SE à la Tiny 3 Lite avec suivi intelligent en 4K, voici cinq modèles à considérer, avec des réductions pouvant atteindre 40 %.
Bien que discrète, la webcam tient une place importante dans nos usages. Réunions en visioconférence, cours à distance, streaming, création de contenu… Elle accompagne aussi bien les journées de travail que les loisirs. Et si les modèles intégrés à nos laptops peuvent suffire, ils montrent parfois leurs limites dès que l’on recherche une image plus nette, un cadrage plus soigné ou un son de meilleure qualité.
C’est justement sur ce terrain que la marque OBSBOT entend se démarquer. La marque profite du Black Friday pour réduire le prix de plusieurs webcams de sa gamme, avec des offres annoncées du 19 au 30 novembre.
Quelle webcam choisir pour les visioconférences du quotidien ? La Meet SE tombe à 59 €
Pour s’équiper, sans faire exploser la facture, la OBSBOT Meet SE constitue une porte d’entrée très intéressante dans l’univers de la marque. Cette webcam Full HD s’adresse avant tout à celles et ceux qui multiplient les appels vidéo, suivent des cours à distance ou souhaitent améliorer leur image pendant leurs sessions de streaming occasionnelles.
Son capteur CMOS BSI de 1/2,8” mise notamment sur de bonnes performances en basse lumière, avec une technologie HDR pensée pour mieux gérer les scènes contrastées. La Meet SE peut filmer en 1080p jusqu’à 100 images par seconde, tandis que ses fonctions AI Auto Framing ajustent automatiquement le cadrage pour garder l’utilisateur au centre de l’image. Petit plus toujours pratique, le contrôle par gestes permet également de piloter certaines fonctions, sans jamais avoir à manipuler directement la caméra.
Compacte et légère (33,2 grammes), elle dispose aussi d’un cache de confidentialité magnétique et peut être orientée en mode portrait. En somme, une webcam à la fois simple à installer et à utiliser, qui viendra aisément couvrir l’essentiel pour les appels du quotidien.
Son autre argument pendant le Black Friday reste évidemment son prix, puisque la Meet SE passe de 99 à 59 euros, soit une réduction de plus de 40 %. Une remise particulièrement intéressante pour qui souhaite remplacer la webcam intégrée de son ordinateur, sans investir dans un modèle haut de gamme.
Webcam PTZ 4K : la Tiny 3 Lite profite de 30 % de réduction
Pour des besoins plus avancés, on monte en gamme avec le modèle OBSBOT Tiny 3 Lite. Cette webcam PTZ (pour Pan-Tilt-Zoom) 4K de dernière génération intègre une nacelle motorisée à deux axes, capable de suivre physiquement les mouvements de l’utilisateur. Un atout indéniable pour les présentations, les cours, les démonstrations et autres sessions de streaming, durant lesquelles on ne reste pas forcément assis devant son écran.
Son système AI Tracking 2.0 propose même plusieurs modes de suivi, pour cadrer une personne, un groupe ou encore une zone définie en amont. De son côté, l’Auto Zoom adapte le plan en fonction des déplacements, tandis que les commandes vocales et gestuelles facilitent le pilotage à distance. De quoi conserver un cadrage propre sans jamais avoir à réajuster la caméra à la main.
La Tiny 3 Lite ne mise pas uniquement sur son suivi intelligent. Son capteur CMOS Exmor RS de 1/2” et 48 mégapixels permet de filmer en 4K à 30 images par seconde, mais aussi en 1080p à 120 i/s. Son système audio spatial à trois microphones propose cinq modes, qui permettent d’adapter le rendu à différents contextes, de la mise en avant d’une voix individuelle à un son stéréo immersif. La Tiny 3 Lite intègre également les fonctions Voice Locator et Voice Tracking. Elle peut aussi se connecter directement au microphone sans fil OBSBOT Vox SE.
Dotée d’un boîtier en alliage d'aluminium de seulement 73 grammes, cette webcam combine suivi mécanique, vidéo 4K et fonctionnalités audio avancées dans un format compact. Et vous l’aurez compris, l’autre bonne nouvelle, c’est que pendant le Black Friday, son tarif passe de 229 à 159 euros, soit plus de 30 % de réduction.
Meet Flip : la webcam 4K pliable qui mise sur la mobilité (et la confidentialité)
Tout le monde n’a pas nécessairement besoin d’une nacelle motorisée ou d’un suivi physique. Pour les utilisateurs qui se déplacent régulièrement, travaillent dans différents endroits ou souhaitent simplement avoir l’esprit tranquille grâce à un cache-objectif physique lorsque la webcam n’est pas utilisée, la OBSBOT Meet Flip propose une approche bien différente. Sa conception pliable et son poids de seulement 37,7 grammes en font une webcam particulièrement facile à transporter.
Son support réglable permet de la fixer rapidement (et solidement) sur un ordinateur portable ou un moniteur. Côté confidentialité, une fois repliée, sa structure recouvre physiquement l’objectif et active le mode veille. Un détail appréciable lorsqu’on souhaite être certain que la caméra ne filme pas. Malgré son format compact, elle embarque un capteur Sony Exmor RS de 1/2” capable de filmer en 4K à 30 images par seconde, avec HDR et autofocus PDAF (pour Phase Detection AutoFocus).
La Meet Flip intègre également deux microphones, plusieurs modes audio et une réduction de bruit par IA. Côté vidéo, l’Auto Framing ajuste automatiquement le cadrage pour garder les participants dans le champ, tandis que la fonction Gesture Control permet de piloter certaines fonctions à distance. Elle se distingue aussi avec AI Magic Notes, un outil capable de transformer les échanges en transcriptions, résumés et listes d’actions.
Pendant cette période de promotion, son prix passe de 129 à 103 euros, soit une remise de 20 %. Un tarif très intéressant pour une webcam 4K qui mise autant sur la portabilité que sur les fonctionnalités dédiées aux réunions.
Pour le Black Friday, deux autres modèles sont également concernés par les promotions OBSBOT. La Tiny 2 Lite, alternative PTZ 4K plus abordable à la Tiny 3 Lite, passe de 199 à 144 euros (-27 %). Enfin, la nouvelle Meet SE 2, qui apporte une définition 2K (2K en 30fps et 1080p en 100fps) à la gamme accessible de la marque, est quant à elle proposée à 92 euros au lieu de 109 euros (-15 %).
Les différentes offres Black Friday OBSBOT sont annoncées du 19 au 30 novembre. De quoi trouver une webcam adaptée à ses usages, que l’on cherche simplement à améliorer ses appels vidéo ou à s’équiper d’un modèle plus ambitieux pour créer du contenu.

articles.title: GTA 6 : être un furry est strictement illégal à Leonida et les chasseurs tirent à vue
articles.text:
Rockstar Games a beau avoir assagi certains réflexes historiques de sa licence comme la présence de prostituées dans GTA 6 pour servir la crédibilité de Jason et Lucia, sa plume satirique n’a rien perdu de son mordant dès qu’il s’agit de caricaturer les paniques morales américaines.
Dans sa version parodique de la Floride, les autorités locales ont ainsi trouvé leur ennemi public numéro un : les furries, ces fans d’animaux anthropomorphes dont certains se déguisent en costume intégral.
Propagande télévisée, presse locale et société secrète dans GTA 6
Rockstar décline cette interdiction dans tous les médias du jeu, de la télévision à la presse locale. En allumant la télévision dans leur planque, les joueurs peuvent tomber sur un spot publicitaire financé par une mystérieuse Anti-Furry Association. Sur le ton d’une campagne de sécurité publique paranoïaque, la vidéo sur GTA 6 rappelle que toute « activité furry » est illégale à Leonida et avertit les touristes que « la saison de chasse est ouverte ». Elle demande aux habitants de signaler tout comportement suspect, comme un « animal » qui dirait « uwu », « rawr xD » ou « hewwo ». Le dernier carton autorise même les chasseurs munis d’un permis à abattre à vue tout furry.
Sur le téléphone des héros, un article du Vice City Horn, le quotidien local, titre sans détour : « Le gouverneur déclare Leonida furry-free ». Poussant le vice jusqu’au bout, les scénaristes ont même imaginé un groupe clandestin baptisé les Furverts (contraction de furry et perverts), contraint d’opérer dans l’ombre face à la répression. La même télévision qui diffuse les spots anti-furry programme d’ailleurs un dessin animé dont la vedette est un alligator anthropomorphe, Macca the Gator.
Une traque jusque dans les rencontres aléatoires
Fidèle à sa philosophie de monde ouvert réactif héritée de Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar a également traduit cette loi absurde en mécanique de gameplay. Au détour d’une rue, un événement dynamique permet aux joueurs de croiser un individu en fursuit, un costume intégral d’animal, poursuivi par les forces de l’ordre. Libre alors à Jason ou Lucia d’ignorer la scène ou d’intervenir pour aider le fugitif à semer la police.

articles.title: Scientific simulation meets AI sovereignty and the CLOUD Act - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Enterprises fear AI success more than failure, because success means lock-in they can’t escape
The supercomputing world built its reputation on scientific simulation, but the artificial intelligence infrastructure now filling the same data centers raises a harder question. When models turn data into revenue, control over that data and the intelligence it produces becomes a board-level concern few companies discuss publicly.
A new buyer’s guide sets out to measure that control provider by provider. Sovereignty is not a single checkbox but a stack of control layers that buyers have to examine one at a time, according to Amit Eyal Govrin (pictured), lead analyst for sovereign AI at theCUBE Research and chief executive officer of Agentcy Labs.
“When it comes to sovereignty, it’s all about control,” Govrin said. “And when we have to look at control, there’s a lot of layers to go into it. And the first one is, are you in fact comfortable … ceding that control to somebody else? Are you comfortable being in somebody else’s jurisdiction where they can potentially compel your data if ever required?”
Govrin spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how sovereignty pillars, the U.S. CLOUD Act and incoming European regulation are reshaping the way enterprises choose AI infrastructure. (* Disclosure below.)
Beyond scientific simulation: The five pillars of AI sovereignty
The guide rests on five pillars — territorial, operational, technological, legal and financial. Territory, meaning where data centers sit and where data is hosted, is the pillar most providers get right easily, Govrin explained. The operational layer is murkier, and he pointed to Amazon Web Services Inc. as one example while noting that AWS does run a sovereign region in Brandenburg, Germany, covered by EU citizens.
“You’re in the AWS Frankfurt region as a German customer. Perfectly fine. Are you sovereign because you’re in that region?” Govrin said. “If that region goes down, that PagerDuty may not necessarily go to somebody out of Germany. It may go somewhere else. It may go into Seattle or to Hyderabad for all you know.”
To build the guide, Govrin and his team graded seven hyperscalers across 40 offerings and handed out 117 grades in five regions. The scoring framework uses 17 yes-or-no tests, with legal assessed separately because local laws make it a poor fit for pass or fail, drawing on more than 300 sources and hundreds of buyer interviews. Google LLC’s air-gapped offerings scored relatively well, but the finding that surprised Govrin most applied to every provider.
“No hyperscaler across the board had an answer to the U.S. CLOUD Act,” Govrin said. “Now imagine you’re a European entity or anywhere else outside the world, and now there’s a production order from a U.S. court system that states that this hyperscaler needs to turn over your data. At that point, there is no contest. Your data becomes Uncle Sam’s data.”
Furrier compared the stakes with the General Data Protection Regulation, a privacy rule he viewed as less operationally relevant. Sovereignty is more consequential because AI models running where data sits produce intelligence that drives revenue, according to Furrier.
“When money’s on the table, you know what happens,” Furrier said. “Everyone fights for it or argues for it. So I think this is a tinderbox moment where one match could blow everything up.”

articles.title: Nasa-Teleskop beobachtet Sternenfusion nur 47 Tage nach der Eruption – ein Novum
articles.text:
James Webb: Nasa-Teleskop beobachtet Sternenfusion nur 47 Tage nach der Eruption – ein Novum
In Doppelsternsystemen, in denen die Wechselwirkungen zwischen den Himmelskörpern über reine Gravitationskräfte hinausgehen, kann es schon mal passieren. Der größere Partner verschluckt sozusagen seinen kleineren Begleiter.
Common Envelope: Kurze Phase bei Fusion zweier Sterne
Bei diesem Prozess kommt es zu einem Stadium, das als Common Envelope (CE) bekannt ist, auf Deutsch also so viel wie „Gemeinsame Hülle“. Dabei kreisen die Sterne in einer lose gebundenen gemeinsamen Hülle umeinander, eben der Common Envelope.
Durch den Reibungswiderstand verengt sich die Umlaufbahn des kleineren Sterns spiralförmig. Dann verleibt sich der große Partner den kleineren Partner ein.
Die CE-Phase dauert in der Regel nur kurz, ein paar Monate bis zu wenigen Jahren. In kosmischen Dimensionen also einen Wimpernschlag lang. Deswegen ist es noch nie gelungen, sie von Anfang bis Ende zu beobachten.
Forschende verfolgten erstmals vollständige CE
Dies haben Forschende nun geschafft. Sie verfolgten die vollständige CE-Phase der Fusion zweier Sterne in der Andromedagalaxie. Das Resultat ergab eine Rote Nova, die AT 2025abao getauft wurde. Ihr Spitzname lautet Bao.
Das Team um Viraj Karambelkar, Nasa Hubble Fellow an der Columbia University, hat seine Erkenntnisse in einer Studie dargestellt, die gerade in der Zeitschrift Nature erschienen ist. Die Forscher:innen griffen unter anderem auf Daten des Nasa-Weltraumteleskops James Webb zurück.
So stießen die Forschenden auf das Doppelsternsystem
„Sternverschmelzungen sind in Echtzeit sehr, sehr schwer zu beobachten, da sie kaum vorhersagbar sind“, sagte Viraj Karambelkar in einer Mitteilung der Nasa.
Im Jahr 2023 bemerkten Karambelkar und sein Team, dass am Rande der Andromedagalaxie etwas „Ungewöhnliches vor sich ging“. Das Objekt, das später Bao genannt wurde, wies untypische Merkmale für einen Roten Riesen auf. Die Forschenden bekamen den Verdacht, dass es sich um ein Doppelsystem handeln könnte.
Roter Riese und ein kleiner Begleiter
Die Auswertung der Daten von James Webb und anderen Teleskopen ergab, dass es sich bei dem größeren Stern des Systems um einen Roten Riesen handelt, der sieben Mal schwerer ist als unsere Sonne.
Das Licht des kleinen, mittlerweile verschwundenen Begleiters ging aufgrund der Strahlkraft seines größeren Partners unter. Nur durch Modellrechnungen kamen die Wissenschaftler:innen zu dem Schluss, dass seine Größe 0,7 Sonnenmassen betrug.
James Webb beobachtete Nova nur 47 Tage nach Eruption
2025 kam es dann zu einer Eruption. Innerhalb von 25 Tagen wurde AT 2025abao um ein Hundertfaches heller. Seine äußere Hülle dehnte sich mit einer Geschwindigkeit von 330 Kilometern in der Stunde aus. Laut den Forschenden resultierte dies daraus, dass der kleinere Begleiter mit dem Heliumkern des Roten Riesen kollidierte. Damit endete die Phase der Common Envelope.
James Webb durchleuchtete das Sternensystem 47 Tage danach. So früh wurde der Vorgang einer solchen Fusion noch nie beobachtet. „Die Daten des Teleskops halfen uns dabei, zu charakterisieren, wie das System vor, während und unmittelbar nach der Verschmelzung aussah, was absolut atemberaubend ist“, gab Karambelkar zu Protokoll.
!!!! Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Mauvaise nouvelle, les prix des Samsung Galaxy A devraient encore augmenter en 2027 — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les Galaxy A ont déjà bien soufferts cette année. Début octobre, Samsung a relevé presque tous ses Galaxy A de 10 à 70 euros sur sa boutique française où le Galaxy A17 5G était passé de 229 à 299 euros.
Le constructeur sud-coréen remettrait pourtant le couvert au 1er janvier 2027. D’après des sources industrielles citées par le quotidien économique Seoul Economic Daily, huit Galaxy A prendraient de 20 à 60 dollars (environ 18 à 55 euros HT). Sur des smartphones qu’on achète justement pour leur prix, la hausse atteindrait près de 19 %.
La liste détaille six des huit modèles. Les prix sont américains, donc hors taxes :
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
- Galaxy A07 5G : de 199 à 229 dollars (+15,1 %)
- Galaxy A18 LTE : de 259 à 299 dollars (+15,4 %)
- Galaxy A17 5G : de 269 à 319 dollars (+18,6 %), la plus forte hausse en pourcentage
- Galaxy A27 : de 359 à 399 dollars (+11,1 %), un modèle déjà plus cher que son prédécesseur à sa sortie
- Galaxy A37 : de 439 à 499 dollars (+13,7 %), la plus forte hausse en valeur
- Galaxy A57 : de 549 à 599 dollars (+9,1 %), soit environ 545 euros HT
Les versions mieux équipées en mémoire sont aussi touchées : le supplément pour 128 Go de stockage ou 4 Go de mémoire vive en plus passerait de 80 à 100 dollars, soit 25 % de plus.
Samsung avait déjà augmenté le Galaxy A57 en octobre. Il était déjà plus cher de 50 euros à sa sortie par rapport au Galaxy A56. Là, on dépasserait les 600 euros pour le modèle de base qui, rappelons-le, est un smartphone de milieu de gamme.
La mémoire pèse désormais plus de la moitié de la facture
Samsung paie encore la flambée de la mémoire. Les fabricants de puces produisent davantage de HBM et de DRAM haut de gamme pour l’IA. Il reste donc moins de mémoire standard pour les smartphones abordables. Dans son rapport du troisième trimestre, Samsung indique que le prix moyen de la mémoire mobile qu’il achète a bondi de 263 % par rapport à la moyenne de 2025, contre 8 % pour les processeurs. D’après le cabinet Counterpoint Research, cité par le quotidien, la mémoire vive et le stockage représentent désormais 54 % du coût des composants d’un smartphone d’entrée de gamme, contre 20 % un an plus tôt.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quels sont les meilleurs smartphones pas chers à moins de 300 € en 2026 ?
            
Counterpoint ne voit pas d’accalmie avant la mi-2027, avec des prix de la mémoire qui devraient encore monter jusqu’au premier trimestre. Les acheteurs freinent déjà puisque les livraisons mondiales de smartphones ont reculé de 19 % au troisième trimestre 2026 sur un an, alors que le prix moyen des smartphones a grimpé de 20 % depuis le début de l’année.
Samsung prévoit d’ailleurs de réduire d’environ 20 % la production de ses Galaxy A ce trimestre. Il garde quand même la première place mondiale, avec 22 % de parts de marché contre 21 % pour Apple.
Faut-il acheter un Galaxy A avant janvier ?
Samsung n’a rien confirmé. Selon le quotidien coréen, la date et le montant des hausses varieront d’un pays à l’autre. La France a déjà eu sa hausse début octobre, au même moment que les Galaxy S26, augmentés de 100 à 120 euros. Pour autant, rien ne dit que la boutique française échappera à une deuxième vague, dont les nouveaux prix s’appliqueraient au 1er janvier 2027. Si un Galaxy A vous tente, regardez donc les offres du Black Friday chez les revendeurs, et comparez-les au prix de lancement plutôt qu’au prix barré.
    Pour aller plus loin
Black Friday 2026 : les meilleures offres du jour en DIRECT chez la Fnac, Darty, Boulanger…

articles.title: Nigeria gives crypto firms November 30 tax deadline
articles.text:
Nigeria’s tax authority has given cryptocurrency exchanges and other virtual asset service providers until November 30, 2026, to register on a new portal, adding a compliance deadline to an industry facing tighter regulatory oversight.
In a public notice seen by TechCabal, the Nigerian Revenue Service (NRS) said providers operating in Nigeria serving Nigerian residents must submit registration forms through its newly deployed VASP Tax Portal by that date. They must then integrate their systems with the portal by December 31, 2026, to complete the process.
The move is the latest effort by Nigeria’s tax authority to bring the crypto industry further into the tax net, giving the sector a formal registration and reporting framework as the government tightens oversight of virtual asset transactions. New virtual asset tax guidelines released in August impose a 1.5% stamp duty on token-to-fiat and fiat-to-token transfers.
The new rules apply to Nigerian and foreign businesses providing virtual asset services in Nigeria or to people resident in the country, regardless of their physical presence in Nigeria. It covers crypto exchanges, peer-to-peer platforms, brokers, custodial wallet providers, payment and remittance companies, and businesses involved in the transfer, exchange or safekeeping of digital assets.
Missing either deadline could attract statutory penalties and other enforcement measures, the NRS said in response to questions from TechCabal.
The NRS said the requirement applies regardless of a provider’s business name or regulatory status. Individuals using virtual assets for personal purposes are excluded, as are businesses that simply accept cryptocurrency as payment for their own goods and services. Their existing tax obligations remain unchanged.
The registration requirement follows provisions in the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025, and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. The NRS said Section 79 of the administration law and its Fifth Schedule subject persons engaged in virtual asset activities to tax obligations covering registration, record-keeping, reporting, filing, and payment.
It said it deployed the portal under Section 71 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, which provides for the use of technology to automate tax administration. It will also facilitate registration for anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and counter-proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF), in line with the Financial Action Task Force’s Recommendation 15.
Two steps to registration
The NRS has split registration into two stages. First, crypto providers must submit their business details, Tax Identification Number, contact information, virtual asset activities, and relevant AML/CFT/CPF registration information by November 30.
The second stage requires providers to integrate their systems with the portal. The NRS said detailed reporting requirements and application programming interface (API) specifications would be provided during the technical integration process.
The integration is intended to support transaction reporting, tax assessment, and the remittance of taxes collected in tokens. The NRS said a provider would only be considered registered after completing both the registration form and the integration process.
“A VASP is deemed registered only after completing both steps,” the tax authority said.
The portal will also support the administration of existing tax obligations, including Value Added Tax (VAT), Stamp Duty and Withholding Tax (WHT) payable in tokens. These functions will be introduced in phases, while taxes payable in fiat currency will continue to be administered through the NRS’s existing Rev360 platform and other channels.
The NRS said the portal does not introduce new taxes or create additional tax obligations. Providers remain responsible for taxes on their own taxable activities and, where applicable, for collecting or withholding taxes on customer transactions.
“The VASP Tax Portal introduces no new taxes,” it said, adding that existing Nigerian tax laws would continue to apply.
Not a crypto operating licence
The NRS clarified that registration on its portal does not authorise a business to provide virtual asset services.
The process is separate from licencing and approval requirements administered by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and other relevant regulators. Providers may register with the NRS while awaiting regulatory approval, but must still obtain any licence required for their activities.
The service said the relevant authorities would continue to supervise and enforce AML/CFT/CPF obligations. It added that it could share information collected through the portal with regulators and law enforcement agencies when the law permits.
It added that information collected, processed, or stored through the platform would be subject to applicable data protection laws and the NRS Data Protection Policy, including confidentiality and information security controls.

articles.title: Scarlett Johansson, sobre su película con Robert Redford en 1998: “Antes de cada escena, él me contaba la historia para ayudarme a encontrar mi lugar en la película”
articles.text:
Scarlett Johansson pasó un largo proceso de audiciones para trabajar junto a Robert Redford en la película “El hombre que susurraba a los caballos”. Esta película (estrenada en 1998) es anterior incluso a que Scarlett haya trabajado con Sofia Coppola o haya encarnado al personaje de Viuda Negra.
Además de dirigir la película, Robert Redford también participó en ella como actor. Antes de rodar cada secuencia, le contaba a Scarlett cuál era la situación de su personaje en la historia. En palabras de la propia actriz: “Antes de cada escena, él me contaba la historia para ayudarme a encontrar mi lugar en la película”.
Su personaje se llamaba Grace Maclean y era una adolescente que pierde una pierna en un accidente de caballo. En este sentido, la actriz encontró un punto de partida en el hecho de que su personaje era una adolescente y siente que sus padres no le hacen caso. “Fue fácil para mí meterme en el papel. Lo que fue más difícil fue crearlo”.
Preparar la escena antes de actuar
La noticia le sorprendió y supuso un alivio tras todo el proceso de audiciones. “No podía creerlo. Estaba impactada”, recordaba en una entrevista. Además de contarle la historia antes de cada escena, Robert Redford le aconsejó a Scarlett “no actuar”. Es decir, que controlase su interpretación.
Cuando la película llegó a los cines, Scarlett Johansson tenía 13 años. En realidad, cuando rodaron la película (cuyo rodaje empezó en 1997), la actriz tenía 12 años.
En estas conversaciones con el director estaba también presente el hecho de que tenía que reflejar los efectos de este accidente y el alejamiento de su madre (Kristin Scott Thomas).
También influyó que apenas se conocían cuando empezaron a trabajar juntas. Se presentaron y en un par de horas ya estaban rodando una escena. Esto ayudó a transmitir el desapego y la incomodidad que hay entre Annie y Grace.
La actriz lo recordaba así: “Fue muy rápido y ayudó con ese desapego entre los personajes de Annie y Grace y esa especie de sensación de incomodidad”.

articles.title: Jensen Huang y su esposa trasladaron USD 10.500 millones en acciones de Nvidia a un fideicomiso antes de los casos de infidelidad
articles.text:
Jensen Huang y su esposa Lori trasladaron más de 10.500 millones de dólares en acciones de Nvidia a un fideicomiso familiar irrevocable en marzo de 2026, ocho meses antes de que una serie de presuntas infidelidades, incluida la de una posible espia china, terminara con la renuncia del empresario a la dirección de la compañía que él mismo cofundó.
La operación, revelada por registros ante la Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) y citada por el medio Barron’s, consistió en el traspaso de 59 millones de acciones al Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust. Asesores patrimoniales consultados por esa publicación la describieron como “una de las transferencias de riqueza más impactantes” que hayan observado.
Cómo se armó el fideicomiso familiar de Huang
El movimiento no fue una decisión espontánea sino el desenlace de una estrategia diseñada una década antes. El 18 de marzo de 2016, un mes después de una presentación de resultados en la que Jensen Huang había destacado el futuro de la inteligencia artificial para los chips de la compañía (entonces usados sobre todo en videojuegos), el matrimonio constituyó cuatro grantor retained annuity trusts (GRATs).
Dos de esos fideicomisos tenían una duración habitual de cuatro años. Los otros dos, en cambio, se extendieron por una década, un plazo que Barron’s calificó como “mucho menos popular” entre este tipo de instrumentos por el riesgo que implica proyectar su crecimiento a largo plazo.
Un GRAT es un fideicomiso que permite transferir activos a herederos con una carga impositiva reducida: el beneficiario conserva una anualidad durante un plazo fijo y, al vencer, el remanente pasa libre de impuesto federal a la sucesión, generalmente a los hijos. Esa es la figura que usaron los Huang en 2016.
Los dos GRATs a diez años se financiaron con 51 millones de dólares en acciones de Nvidia. El valor de esos títulos escaló un 22.161% en ese lapso, impulsado por el auge del mercado de la inteligencia artificial, hasta transformar aquellos 51 millones en los 10.500 millones que finalmente ingresaron al fideicomiso familiar en marzo pasado.
El abogado especializado en fideicomisos y sucesiones Joshua Caswell lo resumió a Barron’s: “Esto para mí es indicativo de alguien que tenía mucha fe en sí mismo y en la compañía, pero que no sabía cuándo ocurriría el evento de liquidez”.
Según el medio, no trascendió cuál de los dos hijos adultos del matrimonio, Madison y Spencer, ambos empleados de Nvidia, resulta beneficiario del fideicomiso.
El escándalo que llegó meses después
La transferencia quedó formalizada en marzo, mucho antes de que se conociera la crisis que terminaría por sacar a Huang de la conducción de Nvidia. En mayo, el secretario de Estado Marco Rubio advirtió al presidente Donald Trump que la relación sentimental de Huang con una empresaria china representaba un riesgo de contrainteligencia para Estados Unidos, según había informado inicialmente The New York Times.
Esa mujer fue identificada como Alice Huang (sin parentesco con el empresario), señalada como una presunta espía vinculada a China. El Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de ese país calificó las acusaciones de “especulación infundada y un intento de difamar y manchar a China”, de acuerdo con CNN.
A ese episodio se sumaron luego versiones sobre otros dos presuntos vínculos extramatrimoniales, en estos casos con subordinadas dentro de la propia Nvidia.
El cúmulo de denuncias derivó en la renuncia de Jensen Huang como presidente y director ejecutivo el jueves 12 de noviembre, cargo que ocupaba desde que cofundó la empresa en 1993 junto a Chris Malachowsky y Curtis Priem. El directorio designó a la directora financiera Colette Kress como CEO interina.
El impacto llegó también a la cotización bursátil: las acciones de Nvidia cayeron un 3% el lunes 16 de noviembre, lo que borró unos 100.000 millones de dólares de su capitalización de mercado, según The Guardian, y acumulaban una baja superior al 30% en el último mes. De acuerdo con Bloomberg, el valor de mercado de la compañía quedó por debajo de los 4 billones de dólares por primera vez desde julio de 2025.

articles.title: Producing Healthy Code with Artificial Intelligence Costs Fewer Tokens
articles.text:
Agentic AI can speed up velocity, but the gains vanish within months as code complexity grows. In his presentation on AI-friendly code at GOTO Copenhagen, Adam Tornhill showed that healthy code makes AI perform better and costs fewer tokens. Safeguarding means keeping code health high through agentic refactoring, with an MCP supplying code health data, so AI can maintain the code it generates.
Developing software with agents is significantly harder than writing code manually, Tornhill argued. But with agentic AI, they can complete tasks two to three times faster, he added. It also helps them unblock themselves and reduces coordination needs.
Tornhill mentioned a study done on 1000+ open-source projects which showed that with AI, velocity went up during the first few weeks, but after two months the velocity gains were fully canceled out due to a massive increase in code complexity:
AI operates in a self-harm mode, often writing code it cannot reliably maintain later.
Code health measures how easy code is to understand, change, and maintain. Research done on human coding (before AI) shows that if you have healthy code, you can be up to 10x faster than someone who works on similar problems in unhealthy code, Tornhill said. The defect risk is reduced 15 times, and code reviews go twice as quickly, he added.
Building a prototype was never the hard problem in software; 95% of the costs for any software project come after the first release. This is where code quality, maintainability, and architecture start to matter, Tornhill said.
Recent research shows that large language models perform consistently better in healthy code. AI won’t generate perfect code; if we want to survive in the Agentic age, we need to focus on safeguarding, Tornhill said.
The average codebase has a code health of 5.15, where AI-friendly code starts at 9.5. Technical depth is a bottleneck for enterprise adoption of agentic coding; what’s needed is an agentic refactoring, Tornhill argued. Claude can be used to fix code health issues, but only to a certain extent:
As a best-case scenario, an agent can fix roughly 50% of the code health issues for lower-health code. Once the code health improves, the AI performance drops sharply, and Claude can only correctly refactor 20% of the code. AI tends to become conservative, doing small changes that don’t really move the needle on code quality.
Adding an MCP with code health data can lead to a 90%-100% fix rate, Tornhill said. Agentic refactoring turned out to be a predictable and mechanical process at scale, where AI was capable of doing codebase-specific refactorings.
Healthy code is also financially viable code, with healthy code, you can do things with 40% to 45% fewer tokens, Tornhill said.
By refactoring code, modularizing it and making it healthy, we can also reduce organizational friction, Tornhill said. Code quality at the module level is a largely solved problem with the automation we now have. Scaling AI friendliness to the design and architectural level is the next big challenge, he concluded.
InfoQ interviewed Adam Tornhill after his talk.
InfoQ: How can we measure code health?
Adam Tornhill: Code Health is a multifacetted concept, so we need to combine multiple metrics. We’ve found that it works best when combining measures from three levels of software design:
- Module level design: e.g. are your modules cohesive and do one thing well? Or are there multiple, unrelated responsibilities?
- Function level design: e.g. how well-designed are the individual function blocks? How expressive are their APIs?
- Implementation level: where you want to avoid any accidental complexity in how the code is written such as deeply nested logic, excessive copy-paste, etc?
InfoQ: How do you safeguard AI-generated code?
Tornhill: Safeguarding needs to happen at multiple levels, and all safeguards need to be completely automated in an agentic context. Examples of concrete safeguards include linting, code coverage, mutation testing to ensure your tests actually test, and higher-level metrics like Code Health. In practice, these safeguards are exposed to agents as local MCP servers or command-line tools.
InfoQ: How can we do refactoring at scale with agents?
Tornhill: The main steps are to establish a baseline, build a safety-net for behavior, and provide a feedback loop to the agents refactoring the code. The whole process is highly iterative.
- The baselining step focuses on measuring code quality to identify what needs improving.
- The safety-net is a reliable test suite that helps preserve the existing behavior of the codebase.
- The agentic feedback loop builds on objective code health information and test outcomes so that the AI can determine whether a change moves the code quality closer to the goal.
- Finally, enable the agents to learn. In our study on Refactoring at Scale with Agents, we instructed agents to build an evolving playbook of successful codebase-specific refactoring patterns.

articles.title: Anthropic hits Nasdaq exchanges at $111, 33% above IPO price | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Shares of Anthropic are now trading on the Nasdaq exchange, as the company successfully executes its initial public offering. In the early minutes of availability, shares were trading at $111.50, a 33% premium over the $83 IPO price.
Set on Wednesday, the IPO price was already higher than the projected range set by the company, which anticipated a price between $70 and $78 per share. All told, the offering will raise over $81 billion, directed to a combination of employees and the company’s own coffers.
The IPO funding, together with existing fundraising and new private offerings timed to coincide with the company’s public market debut, will leave Anthropic with an expected $220 billion in cash reserves. As one analyst told TechCrunch, “Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had.”
The share price continues to fluctuate, but the opening price would put the company’s market cap over $2 trillion, making it more valuable than Meta, Tesla, or Walmart. Only five companies boast a higher valuation by market cap: Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Microsoft.
In a speech before the opening bell, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei emphasized the company’s commitment to safety. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top.”

articles.title: From Metrology To Autonomy: Scaling Yield, Quality, And Innovation
articles.text:
Operationalizing intelligence across the manufacturing stack begins with trusted data.
With the growth of increasingly complex devices, improving yield, quality, and manufacturing speed requires a new approach. Across 14 presentations and posters presented at SEMICON West 2026, Intel Foundry leaders and engineers shared research and emerging solutions for the AI-ready foundry of the future. By combining end-to-end metrology, intelligent analytics, and industry-wide standards, we can unlock scalable innovation for our customers.
Semiconductor manufacturing is shifting from isolated optimization to connected intelligence, according to Intel Foundry’s Lalitha Immaneni, vice president of semiconductor research and development, advanced packaging technology and manufacturing (APTM), in her keynote at the conference. Factory autonomy will not emerge from AI alone. It requires a system-first mindset based on a common foundation of trusted measurements, interoperable platforms, and advanced test infrastructure.¹
For decades, metrology has served as a critical manufacturing checkpoint. Today, it is evolving into a control layer for proactive yield management. Modern semiconductor manufacturing demands more advanced metrology and defect control to address rising contamination risks, process sensitivities, and defectivity challenges. Hidden interactions among materials, equipment, chemicals, packaging polymers, and fab environments can undermine yield and often go undetected until late-stage manufacturing, increasing costs and slowing production. Rather than reacting to failures after they occur, semiconductor manufacturers like Intel Foundry are using predictive process control supported by continuous measurement and monitoring.²
The requirement for end-to-end visibility does not stop at wafer fabrication. The industry’s transition toward heterogeneous integration has introduced increasingly complex architectures built on chiplets, hybrid bonding, high-bandwidth memory, and advanced 2.5D and 3D packaging technologies. These innovations are blurring the traditional boundaries between front-end manufacturing and back-end assembly. Today’s advanced packaging environments require the same level of process intelligence found in leading-edge wafer fabs, such as nanometer-scale precision, process control discipline, and quality assurance capabilities.³
Test operations increasingly represent the final extension of this measurement strategy. Intel Foundry’s Advanced Chiplet Test services provide wafer-to-system test coverage designed to identify issues early, enable known-good die selection, and optimize back-end yield before expensive assembly operations begin. Through predictive die classification, intelligent die pairing, integrated optical testing, and closed-loop yield analytics, test data becomes a critical input for manufacturing intelligence.
Our work on automatic defect classification (ADC) illustrates how AI can help accelerate yield learning and turn complexity into productivity. Managing thousands of classification recipes across multiple technology nodes and manufacturing sites is increasingly difficult, so engineers developed a human-in-the-loop agentic workflow to assist with log analysis, knowledge retrieval, root cause investigation, and recipe reviews. AI-generated recommendations, combined with human approval checkpoints, speed investigations while maintaining auditability and engineering oversight.⁴
We’re also exploring new approaches to thermal intelligence. Our research combines AI with heat-transfer physics to predict how heat moves through semiconductor devices more accurately and with less training data.⁵ This research complements Intel Foundry’s broader investments in advanced test and reliability methodologies, including system-level testing, burn-in, and precision thermal control for increasingly power-dense AI and heterogeneous computing devices. Together, these capabilities help engineers identify yield limiters earlier, reduce manufacturing variability, and make faster, more reliable decisions across the production flow.
Precision measurements and intelligent analytics are key components, but scaling in high volume manufacturing requires a modern digital infrastructure. Traditional vendor-locked automation systems often create data silos that limit operational visibility and slow decision-making. By adopting hardware-independent automation architectures, connected data systems, and AI-enabled edge computing, manufacturers can reduce engineering cycles, lower operating costs, and enable predictive maintenance and AI-driven quality inspection.⁶
Finally, autonomy cannot be achieved by technology innovation alone. Industry standards will play a pivotal role. The Semiconductor Assembly Test Automation and Standardization Research Association (SATAS) consortium brings together more than 40 organizations to develop open standards, interoperable architectures, and automation frameworks that can be adopted across the global semiconductor industry, helping to move semiconductor manufacturing from highly automated operations toward true factory autonomy.
SATAS is a multi-year industry initiative sponsored by Japan’s New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) and the Ministry of Economy, Trade, and Industry (METI). Intel Foundry is helping advance interoperable architectures, automation frameworks, material-handling standards, and collaborative pilot environments that can accelerate back-end manufacturing transformation. By enabling a more connected and interoperable semiconductor ecosystem, Intel Foundry is making it easier for customers and partners to integrate processes, automate workflows, and adopt next-generation manufacturing capabilities.⁷
Operationalizing intelligence across the manufacturing stack is getting closer to reality. It begins with end-to-end metrology and trusted data. It extends through explainable, physics-informed AI and advanced failure analysis methodologies. It relies on resilient automation, edge computing, and advanced packaging platforms. And it scales through ecosystem-wide standards and interoperability. Together, these capabilities help customers lead in the next era of manufacturing.
