articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.text:
Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
By treating qubits like individual molecules, scientists can now predict their behavior faster and more accurately
- Date:
- November 13, 2026
- Source:
- Princeton University
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.
- Share:
A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors. Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications. The findings were recently published in ACS Central Science and have attracted attention from other researchers in the field.
One of the biggest challenges in developing quantum technology is finding materials that can maintain delicate quantum states under practical conditions. Many candidates require extremely low temperatures to function reliably. Diamond materials stand out because certain quantum properties can remain useful even at room temperature.
This capability could help advance technologies that are important to national research priorities and the development of next-generation computing. Quantum sensors promise levels of sensitivity and precision beyond those of conventional instruments, while quantum computers could eventually solve certain extraordinarily complex problems much faster than today's most powerful supercomputers.
Why Imperfect Diamonds Could Be the Key to Quantum Computing
Although diamonds are made of carbon atoms, a flawless diamond crystal is not enough to create a useful quantum computing system. The key lies in tiny irregularities within the crystal structure.
These imperfections, known as defects, can occur when a carbon atom is absent from its normal position, when another element replaces a carbon atom, or when both changes occur together. The atoms surrounding these defects can form qubits, the basic units used to store and process quantum information in quantum computers and sensors.
Finding the most useful defects, however, has been difficult. Accurately modeling their quantum behavior traditionally requires enormous computational resources, making it challenging to evaluate large numbers of possible candidates.
A Simpler Way to Discover Better Diamond Qubits
Mark Martirez, a staff research scientist at PPPL, developed a way to dramatically reduce the complexity of these calculations. Instead of simulating a much larger diamond structure, he isolates a small region containing just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect.
By "carving out" this tiny atomic cluster and treating it like a separate molecule, Martirez can use powerful computational methods that chemists have spent decades refining. These established techniques make it possible to analyze the quantum properties of diamond defects much more efficiently without sacrificing the high level of accuracy needed for the calculations.
"Because we're treating the qubits as molecules, the cost of calculating these defects is equivalent to the cost of just modeling a simple molecule," Martirez said. "This method really opened the floodgates" in terms of how qubits can be assessed.
The new technique allows researchers to calculate how different qubits respond to laser light and microwave pulses far more quickly than before. Using this approach, the team identified promising defects involving boron and oxygen that could serve as new types of qubits.
New Diamond Defects Reveal a Spectrum of Quantum Colors
Light plays an important role in how scientists interact with diamond qubits. Researchers use lasers and microwave pulses to manipulate their quantum states and retrieve stored information.
Much of the previous work in this area has centered on a defect known as the nitrogen-vacancy center. This structure forms when a nitrogen atom takes the place of a carbon atom in a diamond crystal, while an adjacent position that would normally contain another carbon atom remains empty.
Under laser illumination, this type of defect can emit red light when it occupies a particular quantum state.
The newly investigated defects offer different optical properties. Oxygen defects can produce blue light, while those involving boron emit ultraviolet light.
These differences could make it possible to combine several types of qubits within a single quantum device. Because each type responds differently to light, researchers might be able to interact with one group of qubits without disturbing another.
"One could imagine, then, combining different qubits of different responses, so you can basically probe one qubit but not the other," Martirez said.
Beyond identifying new candidates, the findings suggest a broader change in how researchers approach quantum technology. Diamond qubits have traditionally been studied primarily through physics, but understanding their underlying chemistry could provide additional ways to design them.
Martirez believes that researchers could eventually engineer qubits for particular functions using principles similar to those applied when chemists create specialized molecules, including compounds designed for new medications.
How Quantum Chemistry Could Transform Future Research
The potential benefits extend well beyond the development of quantum computers themselves. Martirez sees an intriguing possibility in which advances made possible by quantum chemistry eventually lead to quantum technologies that help improve the field of chemistry.
In other words, quantum chemistry could develop the very tools needed to "enrich itself" in the coming decades.
A practical quantum system containing multiple qubits could make molecular calculations substantially more accurate. That would allow scientists to study increasingly complex chemical structures, including large biological molecules and proteins, with a level of detail that is difficult to achieve using conventional methods.
"We could describe larger molecules, biomolecules, proteins and everything like that in a more accurate way, and that could improve all the chemical-adjacent industries, such as pharmaceutical science and materials science. Even our fundamental understanding of molecular systems could be enriched."
Such improvements could have far-reaching implications for pharmaceutical development, materials research, and the fundamental study of how molecules behave.
Martirez also hopes the research will encourage more chemists to explore solid-state physics. Although building advanced quantum computers is often viewed as a challenge primarily for physicists, he argues that chemistry offers valuable expertise that could help accelerate progress.
"At this moment in time, there's a great emphasis on building the first state-of-the-art qubit computer," he said. "But it's not just physicists who should be participating in this research. Chemists have decades of developed intuition about chemical systems that could be easily translated into understanding defects in solids as well."
By bringing these disciplines together, scientists may be able to develop more effective ways to discover, understand, and eventually engineer the quantum materials needed for future technologies.
The research was funded through PPPL's Laboratory Directed Research and Development program under prime contract number DE-AC02-09CH11466, with additional support from the DOE Office of Science, Office of Fusion Energy Sciences.

articles.title: TikTok muscle son contrôle parental, mais les parents ne verront pas tout — Frandroid
articles.text:
Sur TikTok, le contrôle parental s’appelle Family Pairing. Lancé en 2020, cet outil permet à un parent de relier son propre compte à celui de son ado de 13 à 17 ans. Il peut ensuite régler à distance son temps d’écran, ses messages privés ou les contenus qu’il voit. La plateforme l’enrichit régulièrement et y avait déjà ajouté en mars 2025 le blocage de l’application sur des créneaux choisis par le parent. TikTok vient d’annoncer une refonte complète de ce tableau de bord : en plus des réglages, les parents y trouvent un résumé de ce que fait leur enfant sur l’application, mis à jour chaque jour et consultable aussi depuis un navigateur web.
Le nouveau Family Pairing compte quatre rubriques, qui correspondent selon TikTok à ce qui compte le plus pour les parents :
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
- Temps d’écran : la moyenne quotidienne, l’usage la nuit et les limites réglées. Ces informations existaient déjà, mais elles s’affichent maintenant en premier.
- Interactions : l’évolution du nombre d’abonnés et d’abonnements, les comptes avec lesquels l’ado est connecté et ceux qu’il a bloqués.
- Centres d’intérêt : un échantillon de vidéos des créateurs certifiés que l’ado suit, pour se faire une idée des communautés qui alimentent son fil.
- Publications : ce que l’ado a posté publiquement chaque semaine, avec le nombre de vues.
Pour justifier ces choix, TikTok cite un sondage commandé à Qualtrics, une société spécialisée dans les enquêtes en ligne. Il a été mené du 11 au 14 août auprès de 2 000 parents d’ados de 13 à 17 ans aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, en France et en Indonésie, soit 500 par pays. Plus de 80 % d’entre eux disent vouloir voir les contenus suivis par leur enfant. Plus de 70 % veulent aussi des outils qui les aident à lancer la discussion avec leur ado, au-delà du simple contrôle de son compte. L’étude est financée par TikTok lui-même, mais elle inclut au moins des parents français.
Bientôt les messages, et une alerte sur l’automutilation
Deux nouveautés arriveront plus tard. D’abord, d’ici quelques mois, les parents pourront voir avec qui leur ado échange en messages privés sur TikTok. L’annonce parle bien des contacts, et rien n’indique que les parents pourront lire les conversations. Ensuite, TikTok prépare une alerte envoyée au parent quand son enfant cherche plusieurs fois des termes connus pour être liés à l’automutilation. Elle sera accompagnée de conseils pour aborder le sujet avec lui.
Pour construire cette alerte, la plateforme dit travailler avec le Digital Wellness Lab de l’hôpital pour enfants de Boston, avec le docteur Dan Reidenberg, de l’association américaine Mental Health Coalition, et avec l’Association internationale pour la prévention du suicide (IASP). Wendy Orchard, CEO de l’IASP, rappelle dans le communiqué que sur ces sujets « chaque mot compte », pour l’ado comme pour le parent qui reçoit l’alerte. TikTok ne donne en revanche aucune date. Au passage, la plateforme lance aussi un guide pour les enseignants, l’Educator’s Guide, disponible dans son Centre de sécurité.
Plus de visibilité, mais un aperçu choisi par TikTok
Sur le fond, une partie de ces informations était déjà là : depuis mars 2025, Family Pairing montrait les abonnés, les abonnements et les comptes bloqués de l’ado. La nouveauté tient surtout à la présentation : un suivi dans le temps, actualisé chaque jour et accessible depuis un ordinateur pour les parents qui n’ont pas l’application. On note aussi deux limites dans le communiqué : l’échantillon de vidéos ne vient que des créateurs certifiés, et seules les publications publiques apparaissent. Le parent ne voit donc jamais le fil « Pour toi » de son enfant, seulement un aperçu sélectionné par TikTok.
TikTok ne fait aucun lien avec l’actualité, pourtant l’annonce tombe alors que la plateforme est sous pression en Europe. Le 24 juillet, la Commission européenne lui a adressé des conclusions préliminaires selon lesquelles les comptes de mineurs ne respecteraient pas les règles de sécurité du DSA, le règlement européen qui encadre les grandes plateformes. En France, le Parlement avait adopté le 21 juillet une loi interdisant les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans. Le Conseil constitutionnel l’a censurée le 14 août, et le texte réécrit devrait plutôt viser les fonctionnalités jugées toxiques selon l’âge. Face aux régulateurs, TikTok pourra donc mettre en avant un tableau de bord plus complet pour les parents.
    Pour aller plus loin
Interdiction des réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans : la France repart à l’attaque avec l’aide de l’Europe
            
Comment activer Family Pairing sur le compte de votre ado
Il faut d’abord que le parent ait son propre compte TikTok. Dans l’application, allez dans Profil, ouvrez le menu (les trois traits en haut à droite), puis Paramètres et confidentialité, et touchez Family Pairing avant de choisir « Parent ». Votre ado scanne ensuite le code QR affiché depuis son téléphone pour valider le jumelage. Même sans jumelage, les comptes des 13-17 ans ont par défaut une limite de 60 minutes par jour, au-delà de laquelle il faut saisir un code pour continuer.

articles.title: Nous ne pouvons plus dépendre de SpaceX : ce rachat doit donner vie à un géant spatial made in europe
articles.text:
Le fabricant de satellites finlandais ICEYE veut racheter Avio, qui construit la fusée européenne Vega C. Un mariage qui pourrait changer la donne pour le spatial européen.
L’industrie des satellites panique : la retraite programmée du Falcon 9 de SpaceX suggère une pénurie prochaine de fusées, alors que ses rivales américaines subissent anomalie sur anomalie. Dans ce contexte, ICEYE, fleuron finlandais qui a déjà mis 84 satellites en orbite, a décidé de prendre les choses en main.
Une constellation de satellites d'observation
Et si son nom vous dit quelque chose, ce n’est pas pour rien. Car la start-up développe des engins radar, capables d’observer la Terre de jour comme de nuit. Des images prisées, qui lui sont achetées par des entreprises, mais aussi par des États, dont l’Ukraine, qui les exploite pour suivre les mouvements des troupes russes.
Leur valeur stratégique est telle qu’en octobre, le satellite russe Kosmos 2612 s’est suspicieusement approché de l’appareil ICEYE-X36, suscitant de vives inquiétudes. Pas de quoi freiner la société. Ce mardi 17 novembre, elle a lancé une offre pour mettre la main sur la société italienne Avio, cotée à Milan.
Surtout, elle construit Vega-C, l’un des deux lanceurs européens aujourd’hui en service aux côtés d’une certaine Ariane 6. Cette petite fusée, dotée d’une capacité de charge utile entre 2,5 et 3,3 tonnes pour l’orbite basse, a réussi 7 de ses 8 vols depuis 2022. Vous l’aurez compris : elle vole peu, moins de trois fois par an, et dispose avant tout de clients institutionnels à l’image de l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA).
Accès garanti à l’orbite
Mais l’intérêt pour ICEYE est évident, alors que quasiment tous ses satellites ont été acheminés dans l’espace sur Falcon 9. Mettre la main sur Avio lui garantirait un accès à l’orbite, tandis que le groupe italien gagnerait un client fidèle et surtout, les moyens pour produire davantage et voler plus souvent. Car le mois dernier, la firme nordique a en plus signé un partenariat avec Nokia pour bâtir une constellation de connectivité pour l’Europe, incluant 50 satellites lancés chaque année dès 2028.
Cette annonce intervient alors qu’AST SpaceMobile, autre opérateur de satellites, a présenté son projet de fusée maison, baptisée Blacklift. Elle vise un lancement dès 2028, sans la moindre expérience dans les lanceurs. Un calendrier qui peut donc paraître extrêmement optimiste, d’autant plus lorsque l’on prend en compte les difficultés rencontrées par les acteurs déjà établis, à l’instar de Rocket Lab avec Neutron.
Dans cette optique, le pari d’ICEYE semble bien plus malin. Encore faut-il que l’opération aboutisse : les conseils d’administration d’Avio et de Leonardo, son premier actionnaire avec 18 % du capital, doivent encore examiner l’offre. L’accord des autorités italiennes sera également nécessaire, celles-ci pouvant bloquer le rachat d’entreprises jugées stratégiques. « Si j’étais Leonardo, j’y réfléchirais à deux fois avant de quitter Avio », a lancé Guido Crosetto, ministre italien de la Défense.
De son côté, ICEYE espère boucler l’acquisition en quelques mois.
Sources : Ars Technica, Reuters, The Wall Street Journal

articles.title: Frapper n'importe quelle cible depuis l'espace : l'Europe a désormais son projet d'arme orbitale avec MBDA et Atmos
articles.text:
Bombarder la Terre depuis l’espace. Voilà, en somme, ce qu’est le concept de frappe orbitale de précision en profondeur, ou PODS (Precision Orbital Deep Strike). Et c’est justement une capacité qui pourrait prochainement se développer en Europe, et plus particulièrement en Allemagne, dans le cadre d’un rapprochement entre deux sociétés.
Atmos Space Cargo a en effet annoncé ce mercredi 18 novembre, dans un communiqué commun, avoir signé avec MBDA Deutschland (la branche allemande du missilier MBDA, l’un des géants de la défense en Europe) un accord pour concevoir, développer et tester un projet de Precision Orbital Deep Strike.
Pour Atmos, c’est un développement notable de son activité : jusqu’ici, la startup faisait plutôt de la logistique spatiale. Fondée en 2021 à Lichtenau, en Allemagne, cette jeune entreprise développe Phoenix, une capsule équipée d’un bouclier thermique gonflable, qui doit ramener sur Terre des expériences menées en orbite.
De son côté, MBDA est un poids lourd, spécialisé dans la fabrication de missiles et de systèmes hybrides, comme ce drone-missile conçu pour saturer les défenses aériennes adverses – les fameuses munitions téléopérées, qui se développent tous azimuts. Le groupe compte plus de 21 000 salariés et appartient à Airbus, BAE Systems et Leonardo.
Pour l’Europe, la capacité de frappe de précision lancée depuis l’espace est relativement inédite. Jusqu’à présent, ce terrain a plutôt été exploré par l’URSS, puis par la Russie et la Chine. Les États-Unis aussi ont mené des recherches dans cette direction. Désormais, c’est donc au tour du Vieux Continent de s’y mettre.
Il s’agit, selon Thomas Gottschild, directeur général de MBDA Deutschland, d’offrir aux forces armées « une capacité européenne souveraine et hautement innovante ». Sebastian Klaus, patron d’Atmos, voit dans l’aller-retour vers l’orbite une nouvelle couche d’« infrastructure stratégique », capable selon lui de renforcer la « dissuasion conventionnelle » de l’Europe.
À quoi ressemblerait une frappe orbitale ?
Le communiqué évoque d’abord des études sur l’architecture du système, sa faisabilité technique et l’intégration de charges militaires, avec de possibles démonstrations technologiques. Selon Zone Militaire, Atmos tirerait de Phoenix un véhicule de transfert et de retour orbital, capable de rester des mois en orbite grâce à sa propre propulsion et à son alimentation électrique. MBDA se chargerait de l’explosif et du guidage.
On aurait donc un engin placé en orbite basse, à quelques centaines de kilomètres d’altitude, qui plongerait dans l’atmosphère sur ordre pour frapper une cible spécifique. Les deux partenaires précisent que PODS sera un système militaire séparé des capsules Phoenix civiles. À ce stade, l’accord porte sur des études de faisabilité, et rien ne garantit que la technique fonctionne.
L’arme devra en effet supporter un long séjour dans l’espace, puis la chaleur extrême de la rentrée dans l’atmosphère.
Or, à ce stade, Atmos n’a qu’un vol à son actif. En avril 2025, Phoenix 1 a décollé sur une fusée Falcon 9 de SpaceX et a bien déployé son bouclier gonflable. Mais sa trajectoire a dû être modifiée pour les besoins de la charge principale du lancement, et la capsule est tombée dans l’Atlantique Sud, à environ 2 000 kilomètres des côtes du Brésil, sans pouvoir être récupérée.
Depuis, l’entreprise a levé des fonds pour construire d’autres capsules Phoenix 2, qui auront leur propre moteur pour choisir où elles retombent.
Des armes légales sur le papier, mais vulnérables ?
Sur le plan juridique, le Traité de l’espace de 1967 interdit de placer des armes de destruction massive en orbite, mais il ne dit rien des armes conventionnelles. Le projet profite donc d’une « zone grise », comme le relève Zone Militaire. En revanche, le même traité et la Convention de 1972 sur la responsabilité internationale pour les dommages causés par des objets spatiaux rendent l’Allemagne responsable de ce que feraient Atmos et MBDA dans l’espace.
C’est sans doute pour cela que le communiqué insiste autant sur le respect du droit et des autorisations nécessaires.
Sur le plan militaire, un engin en orbite basse ne peut pas rester au-dessus d’une cible : il défile autour de la Terre selon une trajectoire prévisible, que l’adversaire peut suivre. Pour rester au-dessus d’un point fixe, il faudrait orbiter à la même vitesse que la rotation de la Terre, ce qui se fait sur une orbite géostationnaire, qui se trouve beaucoup plus loin, à près de 36 000 kilomètres d’altitude.
En orbite basse, l’engin resterait à la portée d’une arme antisatellite à ascension directe, c’est-à-dire un missile tiré depuis le sol pour aller détruire un objet en orbite – cela générerait assurément un nuage de débris, mais le pays menacé préférerait sans doute pulvériser le PODS, jugeant que c’est un moindre mal face à une frappe orbitale réussie.
Atmos et MBDA n’ont donné ni calendrier ni budget, et précisent que les développements concrets feront l’objet d’évaluations et d’accords séparés.

articles.title: Knast für KI-CEOs? Diese Strafen für agentische Hacks kann sich eine IT-Ethik-Expertin vorstellen
articles.text:
Schäden durch KI-Agenten: Ethik-Expertin schlägt Haftstrafen für CEOs vor
Im Rahmen eines Pressebriefings des Science Media Centers zum Thema selbstverbessernde KI am vergangenen Mittwoch schlug die IT-Ethik-Professorin Judith Simon vor, Geschäftsführer von KI-Unternehmen für durch ihre Systeme verursachte Schäden mit Haftstrafen zu belegen. „Das scheint mir der einzige Hebel zu sein, damit Leute über die Konsequenzen ihrer Technologien nachdenken“, erklärt Simon, die den Lehrstuhl für Ethik in der Informationstechnologie an der Uni Hamburg leitet.
Aufgrund der Rekordumsätze durch den KI-Boom und die daraus resultierenden Vermögenswerte von KI-Unternehmer:innen wie Mark Zuckerberg, Sam Altman oder Dario Amodei wären Geldstrafen keine adäquate Abschreckung. Dass die Betreiber überhaupt haftbar gemacht werden sollten, begründet Simon damit, dass die Modellbetreiber selbst die Voraussetzungen für die sogenannten Ausbrüche von KI-Systemen aus ihren Sandboxes geschaffen haben.
Die Diskussionen um die Entschleunigung bei der KI-Entwicklung, die zuletzt auch Anthropic-Chef Amodei forderte, scheinen Simon zufolge schon wieder vorbei zu sein. Das zeigt sich auch am Rekordbörsengang von Anthropic. Eine persönliche, körperliche Haftung könne eher dafür sorgen, dass „Sorgfalt in diese Systeme Einzug hält und diese Beschleunigung vielleicht gebremst wird“.
Schuld bei KI-Hacks durch OpenAI oder Anthropic: Warum der AI Act nicht immer greift
Derzeit sieht der AI Act der Europäischen Kommission nur eine Produkthaftung vor, die zwischen Anbieter und Betreiber des KI-Systems unterscheidet. Eine Haftung für Forschungsfälle wie den Hack von Huggingface durch KI-Agenten von OpenAI ist nicht vorgesehen. Damit der dazugehörige Artikel 60 aus dem AI Act greift, müssten die Firmen das dazugehörige Modell unter „Realbedingungen“ testen. Ob eine Sandbox, aus der KI-Agenten ausschwärmen und reale Systeme attackieren können, dazu zählt, ist fraglich.
Die Frage nach der Haftung von Schäden, die durch KI-Tools und -Agenten, entstehen, treibt derzeit auch US-Gerichte um. Im Oktober 2026 reichte eine Non-Profit-Organisation Klage gegen OpenAI ein. Die Firma solle die Entwicklung von KI-Agenten stoppen, die andere Firmen hacken können. Der kalifornische Generalstaatsanwalt Rob Bonta legte am vergangenen Montag mit einer weiteren Klage nach. Darin fordert Bonta unter anderem eine Zahlung von 2.500 US-Dollar an alle Kläger:innen.
Dass Klagen mit finanziellem Hintergrund gegen Tech-Unternehmen Erfolg haben können, zeigt die aktuelle Rechtsprechung gegen Meta. Erst im Oktober verurteilte ein Gericht in New Mexico den Konzern zu einer Geldstrafe von insgesamt 25 Milliarden Dollar. In Europa hatte Italien Meta erst kürzlich mit einer Strafzahlung von rund 800 Millionen Euro belegt.

articles.title: Oppo Reno 17: Price, release date and full specs
articles.text:
Table of contents
Oppo launched the Reno 17 in China on November 16, 2026, alongside the Reno 17 Pro. It packs an 8,000mAh battery, the biggest Oppo has ever put in a Reno phone, and four 50MP cameras. This time, the standard model is bigger, while the Pro is the compact one.
Prices start at CNY 3,599, which is about ₦728,330. Oppo has not said when the phone will come to Nigeria. This guide covers the release date, price, full specs, and how the phone compares with the Reno 16, so you know what to expect.
Oppo Reno 17 release date
Oppo announced the Reno 17 at a launch event in China on November 16, 2026. Oppo also launched the Watch 5 and Pad Air 6 at the same event. Pre-orders are now open in China, and sales start on November 20, 2026.
Oppo has not announced a launch outside China yet. Here is what we know so far:
- Global version: A global Reno 17 (model CPH2975) and a cheaper Reno 17 F (CPH3013) have appeared on certification databases in Thailand and India. This usually means a global launch is close.
- India: Tipsters expect the phone in India between December 2026 and early 2027. Oppo has not confirmed either date.
- Nigeria: Oppo Nigeria launched the Reno 15 and Reno 15 F on March 10, 2026, about 113 days after their China debut. If the Reno 17 follows that pattern, it could reach Nigeria around March 2027. Treat this as a guess based on past launches.
- The Reno 16 gap: We found no official Nigerian launch for the Reno 16, so the Reno 17 could skip Nigeria too.
Keep one more thing in mind. For the last two Reno series, Oppo sold different phones under the same name in China and in global markets. Leaks point to a global Reno 17 with a smaller 6.32-inch screen and a 7,000mAh battery. If that is true, the phone that reaches Nigeria may not match the China model in this guide.
Oppo Reno 17 price
The Reno 17 comes in four versions in China. Here is what each one costs:
| Version | China price | US dollars (approx.) | Naira (conversion) | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 8GB + 256GB | CNY3,599 | $533 | ₦728,330 | 
| 12GB + 256GB | CNY3,799 | $563 | ₦768,804 | 
| 12GB + 512GB | CNY3,999 | $592 | ₦809,278 | 
| 12GB + 1TB | CNY4,899 | $726 | ₦991,411 | 
The naira figures are straight conversions at ₦202.37 per yuan (XE, November 17, 2026). They are not Nigerian prices. They leave out shipping, import duty, VAT, and dealer margins, and the naira rate changes daily.
Buyers in China can also use the national subsidy program to get the base model for CNY3,099. That offer only works in China.
What could it cost in Nigeria? Slot sells the Reno 15 (12GB + 512GB) for ₦949,900. If Oppo Nigeria launches the Reno 17, we estimate the 12GB + 512GB model could land between ₦850,000 and ₦1,000,000. This is our estimate, not an official price.
For context, the global Reno 16 launched at €899 in Europe and Rs 61,999 in India. Expect the global Reno 17 to cost more than it does in China.
Detailed specs
1. Display
- 6.56-inch flat OLED screen with 2,624 x 1,208 resolution (1.5K) and 440ppi
- Up to 120Hz refresh rate and 240Hz touch sampling
- 10-bit color with full DCI-P3 coverage
- 800 nits in normal use and 1,800 nits in high-brightness mode
- Up to 6,000 nits at its local peak
- Oppo Crystal Shield glass on top
2. Processor and performance
- Qualcomm Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 (4nm, up to 2.8GHz) with an Adreno 722 GPU
- LPDDR5X RAM and UFS 3.1 storage
- A 5,000 sq mm vapor chamber to keep the phone cool
- Oppo’s own touch chip and network chip working alongside the Snapdragon
The Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 is the same chip inside the global Reno 16 and the Reno 15 sold in Nigeria. It is slower than the Dimensity 8550 Super in the China Reno 16. Early chip-level scores put it about 45% behind on AnTuTu. Reno 17 benchmark tests are still to come, so wait for reviews before you judge it.
3. Memory and storage
- 8GB RAM + 256GB storage
- 12GB RAM + 256GB storage
- 12GB RAM + 512GB storage
- 12GB RAM + 1TB storage
There is no microSD slot, so pick the storage you need on day one.
4. Cameras
All four cameras use 50MP sensors:
- Main: 50MP, f/1.8, with optical image stabilization (OIS). Notebookcheck reports it is a Sony LYT-600 sensor.
- Ultrawide: 50MP, f/2.0, with a 116-degree view
- Periscope telephoto: 50MP, f/2.8, with OIS, 3.5x optical zoom and up to 120x digital zoom
- Selfie: 50MP, f/2.0, with autofocus
You also get these camera extras:
- 4K video at 60fps on both the front and back cameras
- 4K Live Photos at every zoom level, with clips that now last six seconds instead of three
- Oppo’s Natural Tone 3.0 engine for better skin tones in portraits
- Support for the OPPO Bubble, a small magnetic screen that lets you frame selfies with the rear cameras. It costs CNY 399 in China.
5. Battery and charging
- 8,000mAh battery (7,765mAh rated), the largest ever in a Reno phone
- Silicon-carbon cell with 15% silicon, which packs more power into a slim body
- 80W SuperVOOC and 80W UFCS wired charging
- Works with other fast chargers too, including 55W PPS and 44W UFCS
Charging is wired only. Oppo does not list wireless or reverse charging, and it has not shared an official full-charge time.
6. Design and durability
- Size: 157.64 x 75.27 x 8.28mm
- Weight: 206g (the cat edition is 8.47mm thick and weighs 208g)
- Metal frame with a glass back
- IP66, IP68, IP69, and IP69K ratings for dust and water protection
The Reno 17 comes in Ice Moon White and Cocoa Brown. It also comes in a light blue special edition called Qiyu Miao (some outlets call it Encounter Cat), with a cat design that floats inside the glass back.
Other features include an under-display fingerprint sensor, face unlock, an IR blaster for controlling your TV or AC, NFC, and stereo speakers.
7. Connectivity
- 5G with dual nano-SIM support
- Wi-Fi 6
- Bluetooth 5.4
- USB-C 2.0
8. Software
The Reno 17 runs ColorOS 17 based on Android 17. You can read what Android 17 brings to your phone and check which phones are getting it.
Oppo has not shared an update promise for the China model. For comparison, the global Reno 16 gets five years of Android updates and six years of security patches.
Oppo Reno 17 vs Oppo Reno 16
Oppo launched the China Reno 16 on May 25, 2026. Here is how the two China models compare:
| Spec | Oppo Reno 17 (China) | Oppo Reno 16 (China) | 
|---|---|---|
| China launch | November 16, 2026 | May 25, 2026 | 
| Starting price | CNY3,599 (8GB + 256GB) | CNY3,499 (12GB + 256GB) | 
| Display | 6.56-inch OLED, 120Hz, 6,000 nits peak | 6.32-inch OLED, 120Hz, 3,600 nits peak | 
| Chipset | Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 | Dimensity 8550 Super | 
| RAM | 8GB or 12GB | 12GB or 16GB | 
| Main camera | 50MP with OIS | 200MP with OIS | 
| Telephoto | 50MP periscope, 3.5x | 50MP periscope, 3.5x | 
| Battery | 8,000mAh | 6,700mAh | 
| Charging | 80W wired | 80W wired | 
| Weight | 206g | 188g | 
| IP rating | IP66, IP68, IP69, IP69K | IP68, IP69K | 
| Software at launch | ColorOS 17, Android 17 | ColorOS 16, Android 16 | 
What you gain with the Reno 17:
- 1,300mAh more battery, about 19% more than the Reno 16
- A bigger screen with a much brighter peak
- More water and dust ratings
- Android 17 out of the box and 4K Live Photos at every zoom level
What you give up:
- The 200MP main camera
- The smaller, lighter body (the Reno 17 is 18g heavier)
- Speed, since the Dimensity 8550 Super scores much higher in chip tests
- Some RAM on the base model, which drops to 8GB while the price goes up by CNY100
For you in Nigeria, the more useful comparison is the global version of the Reno 16. It already uses the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 and a 50MP main camera. That makes the China Reno 17 a global Reno 16 with a bigger screen and battery.
Pick the Reno 17 if battery life and a big screen matter most. Pick the Reno 16 if you want a smaller phone with a sharper main camera and more speed. If you want a compact phone with a 200MP camera on the newer generation, look at the Reno 17 Pro.
Where you can buy the Oppo Reno 17
- China: Oppo Mall, JD.com, Tmall, and Oppo’s other authorized stores, from November 20, 2026
- Nigeria: Oppo has not started sales here. As of November 18, 2026, we found no Reno 17 listing on Oppo Nigeria, Jumia, Slot, Konga, or Jiji. Watch Oppo Nigeria’s official pages for launch news.
If a Reno 17 shows up in Nigeria before Oppo launches it here, it is a grey import of the China model. Check these before you pay:
- Network bands: The China model lacks 4G bands 7 and 20. Industry data shows MTN uses these bands for 4G in Nigeria, so you may get a weaker MTN signal. The phone does support band 3 and 5G on n78. Check with your network before you buy.
- Google apps: China models ship without Google apps. Users report that you can switch on Google services in settings, but features like Google Wallet may not work.
- Software: The China software comes with Chinese apps first, though you can set English as your language.
- Warranty: Expect no local warranty. Ask Oppo Nigeria before you buy.
If you can wait, your best move is to hold on for Oppo Nigeria’s official launch. You get a phone set up for Nigerian networks, with a local warranty.

articles.title: En 1974, Stephen King entró en la habitación 217 de un hotel vacío buscando una cama. La pesadilla que tuvo aquella noche dejó una leyenda para toda la vida
articles.text:
La noche del 28 de septiembre de 1974, un joven escritor y su esposa llegaron a un hotel de Colorado que estaba a punto de cerrar por el invierno. No había otros huéspedes y los pasillos parecían interminables. Lo que sucedió durante aquellas horas acabaría convirtiéndose en una de las historias más rentables de la literatura de terror, aunque nadie podía imaginar hasta dónde llegaría el negocio.
Una pesadilla de 1974 de 400 millones. El 15 de mayo de 2025, el histórico Stanley Hotel de Estes Park, Colorado, protagonizó una operación financiera de casi 400 millones de dólares para cambiar de manos y financiar una ambiciosa transformación. La propiedad, famosa por haber inspirado El resplandor de Stephen King, pasó a manos de una entidad vinculada a la autoridad de financiación cultural y educativa de Colorado.
El objetivo era ampliar sus instalaciones y convertirlo en un gran destino turístico y cultural dedicado, entre otras cosas, al cine de terror. La ironía es que buena parte de su fama nació de una sola noche que King pasó allí 51 años antes.
Un hotel de lujo que se quedó sin huéspedes. El Stanley Hotel había abierto sus puertas el 4 de julio de 1909, impulsado por F. O. Stanley, empresario relacionado con los automóviles de vapor Stanley Steamer. Situado junto a las Montañas Rocosas, ofrecía lujo, aislamiento y vistas espectaculares, pero en septiembre de 1974 estaba preparando su cierre invernal.
Stephen King, que acababa de publicar Carrie, llegó con su esposa Tabitha y descubrió que eran los únicos huéspedes. Se instalaron en la habitación 217 y el escritor comenzó a recorrer unos pasillos desiertos que parecían diseñados para una historia de fantasmas.
La noche en que una manguera creó un monstruo. Mientras dormía, King tuvo una pesadilla en la que su hijo de tres años corría aterrorizado por los pasillos del hotel, perseguido por una manguera contra incendios. Despertó sobresaltado, encendió un cigarrillo y se sentó a contemplar las montañas desde la ventana.
Según explicó posteriormente en su web oficial, antes de terminar aquel cigarrillo ya tenía prácticamente concebida la estructura de la novela. Tres años después, en enero de 1977, publicó El resplandor, la historia de Jack Torrance, un escritor que acepta cuidar durante el invierno un hotel aislado mientras una presencia siniestra comienza a apoderarse de su familia.
Kubrick convirtió el hotel en inmortal. En 1980, Stanley Kubrick llevó El resplandor al cine con Jack Nicholson y Shelley Duvall, creando algunas de las imágenes más reconocibles del terror cinematográfico. Sin embargo, el Stanley Hotel no fue el escenario principal del rodaje: el director utilizó otros establecimientos y decorados, y cambió la habitación 217 de la novela por la 237.
King criticó duramente la adaptación porque consideraba que había eliminado buena parte de la evolución psicológica de Jack Torrance. Paradójicamente, aquella película que disgustó al escritor ayudó a convertir el hotel que lo había inspirado en un lugar de peregrinación para los aficionados al género.
El hotel descubrió que los fantasmas eran un negocio estupendo. Con el paso de los años, el Stanley Hotel dejó de limitarse a ofrecer alojamiento y comenzó a explotar su conexión con El resplandor. Organizó recorridos paranormales, visitas a sus instalaciones y festivales de cine de terror, mientras los huéspedes podían ver la película de Kubrick en sus habitaciones.
Según contó CBS News en 2014, solo durante 2012 unas 81.000 personas participaron en las visitas guiadas del establecimiento. La habitación 217 se convirtió en uno de sus grandes reclamos, alimentada además por una leyenda anterior a King: una explosión de gas ocurrida en 1911 que había dejado herida a una empleada del hotel. La ficción y el pasado real del edificio terminaron mezclándose en una maquinaria turística extraordinariamente eficaz.
De habitación maldita a museo del terror de Hollywood. La operación de mayo de 2025 permitirá ampliar el complejo, que ocupa unas 41 acres de terreno, equivalentes a 16,6 hectáreas. Según el anuncio oficial, el proyecto contempla 65 nuevas habitaciones, un centro de eventos de unos 6.000 metros cuadrados, un auditorio para 864 personas y un museo de cine de terror diseñado con la colaboración de Blumhouse Productions, responsable de franquicias como Paranormal Activity e Insidious.
También se prevén exposiciones renovadas periódicamente y actividades culturales durante todo el año. La operación incluye financiación pública y privada, entre ella hasta 46 millones de dólares procedentes de un programa estatal de promoción turística. La idea es convertir un hotel famoso por una novela en un centro permanente de entretenimiento.
Los 400 millones tienen truco. Porque la cifra de aproximadamente 395 millones de dólares no representa los beneficios obtenidos gracias a El resplandor, ni tampoco el presupuesto exclusivo del museo. Se trata de una emisión de bonos destinada a financiar la adquisición del complejo, refinanciar obligaciones anteriores y acometer las nuevas instalaciones. Por supuesto, gracias a su reconocimiento mundial por aquella pesadilla del escritor.
La operación ilustra hasta qué punto la leyenda creada alrededor del Stanley ha terminado formando parte de su valor comercial. Stephen King pasó allí una sola noche en 1974 y salió con la semilla de una novela que cambiaría su carrera. 51 años después, el hotel consiguió financiación cercana a los 400 millones para reinventarse alrededor de una identidad que aquella pesadilla ayudó a construir. Probablemente, pocas noches de insomnio han resultado tan productivas.
Imagen | Wally Gobetz, Renoman58
En Xataka | Stephen King recomienda sin medias tintas el nuevo número 1 de Netflix: es "un placer absoluto"

articles.title: Tiene 31 años, dejó Buenos Aires y construyó una casa de 56 m² con barro y 5.000 botellas de vidrio junto a su pareja en las montañas de Córdoba, Argentina
articles.text:
Ailu tiene 31 años y hace unos años que dejó atrás Buenos Aires para irse a vivir con su pareja, Jerónimo, a las montañas de Córdoba, en Argentina. Allí ambos acabaron acabaron construyendo con sus propias manos una casa sostenible de 56 metros cuadrados hecha de barro y materiales reciclados, una historia que contaron en una entrevista para el canal de YouTube Historias de Valientes.
De un terreno a un hogar. Después de unos cuantos años de búsqueda y de viajes, la pareja acabó convirtiendo un terreno de Los Hornillos, en el valle de Traslasierra, en su casa. Allí han puesto en marcha un proyecto de permacultura que combina la bioconstrucción, la producción de alimentos y diferentes prácticas sostenibles con las que quieren reducir su impacto ambiental, según explican en la propia entrevista.
Eso sí, aunque en algunas fases de la obra recibieron ayuda de otras personas, la mayor parte del trabajo la hicieron ellos solos.
Quincha y botellas bajo el suelo. Para las paredes utilizaron la quincha, una técnica de construcción que combina madera y paja para conseguir que la estructura tenga un buen aislamiento térmico.
Pero uno de los detalles que más llaman la atención está debajo del suelo, donde hay más de 5.000 botellas de vidrio colocadas para crear una especie de cámara de aire. Vamos, que pisan sobre miles de botellas recicladas que hacen de colchón de aire. La vivienda también tiene un techo verde y un calentador solar con el que aprovechan la energía del sol para calentar el agua.
Muebles de barro y herencias familiares. Por dentro, la casa tiene muebles de obra hechos de barro y una cocina integrada. Además, hay diversos objetos que la pareja ha reutilizado y que le dan un toque propio a la decoración de cada estancia, y algunos de ellos tienen valor sentimental, como las mesitas de noche que pertenecían a la abuela de Ailu. Otras piezas y materiales les llegaron como regalo y acabaron teniendo una nueva función después de adaptarlos.
La vivienda cuenta también con una habitación extra que funciona a la vez como estudio, zona de descanso y sala de lectura. Y en la planta de arriba está el dormitorio, con un ventanal amplio que da a las montañas.
Frutales y zonas verdes. Fuera, en el terreno, cultivan diferentes árboles frutales, como manzanos, cerezos, mandarinos, melocotoneros y aguacates, y tienen varias zonas verdes que forman parte de su idea de vivir en armonía con el entorno.
Por qué dejaron la ciudad. Antes de instalarse en Córdoba, los dos pasaron por diferentes experiencias que les hicieron replantearse la vida urbana y buscar una forma más cercana y consciente de relacionarse con lo que les rodea. Jerónimo empezó a viajar con 19 años y pasó buena parte de los años siguientes llevando una vida nómada.
Ailu, por su parte, siempre ha tenido curiosidad por otras culturas y por conocer otras formas de vida. Con el tiempo, los dos se dieron cuenta de que compartían las ganas de vivir más en contacto con la naturaleza y de estrechar lazos con la comunidad.
Pero la casa es únicamente una parte de un proyecto más grande, el de crear un espacio de convivencia basado en la sostenibilidad y la vida en comunidad. Por ahora viven allí con sus dos gatos, aunque su intención es seguir levantando otras casas y compartir lo que han aprendido sobre bioconstrucción con quien quiera apostar por este estilo de vida.

articles.title: La vida salvaje de GTA 6 al descubierto: estos son los animales, aves y peces descubiertos hasta ahora
articles.text:
GTA 6 ya está disponible y recorrer su mundo también significa encontrarse con animales en distintos ambientes. En Leonida, el territorio ficticio donde transcurre la historia, hay especies terrestres, aves y criaturas marinas.
De acuerdo a diferentes publicaciones, se han encontrado más de 170 animales en las primeras horas del videojuego, aunque el catálogo completo todavía no se conoce. La fauna se distribuye por ciudades, zonas rurales, playas y humedales.
Entre los animales terrestres figuran caimanes, ciervos, perros, gatos, mapaches, nutrias, zorros, iguanas y serpientes. También se encuentran especies asociadas con Florida, como el manatí y la pantera de Florida. Los caimanes destacan por aparecer en lugares muy distintos, incluidos espacios urbanos y zonas cercanas a viviendas.
La diversidad de especies hace que los encuentros cambien según el lugar que se visite. En la ciudad pueden aparecer mascotas y animales callejeros; en los pantanos y el campo, la fauna silvestre ocupa un lugar más visible. Las zonas costeras y las aguas abiertas, por su parte, reúnen animales marinos.
Aves y animales marinos de Leonida
La lista recopilada incluye flamencos, pelícanos, garzas, gaviotas, patos, cormoranes, grullas y espátulas. Se calcula que habrá más de 60 tipos de aves en el juego. Estas especies forman parte de los distintos paisajes y ayudan a diferenciar, por ejemplo, las zonas húmedas de las playas y los espacios urbanos.
En el agua se pueden encontrar delfines, tiburones, ballenas, tortugas marinas, rayas y medusas. La recopilación también menciona anguilas y mantarrayas. Leonida permite explorar playas, ríos, pantanos y mar abierto, por lo que la fauna marina cambia de acuerdo con el entorno.
Los jugadores también pueden acercarse a los animales mediante actividades como la pesca, el buceo y los recorridos en kayak. La observación bajo el agua permite descubrir especies marinas durante la exploración. La pesca está presente, aunque todavía no se conocen todos los detalles sobre qué se puede hacer con los peces capturados.
Cómo interactuar con los animales
Los animales no funcionan únicamente como parte del paisaje. El juego incluye un compendio para registrar especies que se van encontrando, parecido a un catálogo. Asimismo, los animales se organizan en tres categorías: raros, descubribles y legendarios. Queda por conocer qué especies pertenecen a la última categoría y dónde aparecen.
También es posible acariciar al menos a un perro. La recopilación señala que esta interacción puede mejorar la reputación de Jason, aunque no se ha confirmado si el mismo tipo de acción estará disponible con otras especies.
La caza es otra actividad que genera interés. El juego presenta escenas con Jason cerca de ciervos y con un rifle, pero no se han precisado todos los detalles sobre su funcionamiento ni sobre la posibilidad de obtener o vender recursos. Por eso, conviene distinguir lo que ya se puede experimentar en el juego de las características que todavía no han sido explicadas con detalle.
Una fauna que acompaña la exploración
Con más de 170 especies, la vida salvaje es uno de los elementos que amplían la exploración de Leonida. Los jugadores podrán encontrar animales diferentes al cambiar de región y registrar parte de sus descubrimientos en el compendio. La lista disponible reúne mamíferos, aves, reptiles y criaturas marinas, pero podría ampliarse conforme se exploren más zonas.
Caimanes, flamencos, manatíes, delfines y tiburones están entre los animales más llamativos del juego. Su presencia conecta los distintos entornos de Leonida y añade encuentros inesperados durante los recorridos. A medida que los jugadores avancen en GTA 6, podrán descubrir qué otras especies viven en sus ciudades, costas y pantanos.

articles.title: NetWasm 0.10 Speeds Up C# on WebAssembly, Now Faster Than Mono AOT
articles.text:
The team behind NetWasm has published a write-up of its 0.10 optimisation work, spanning releases 0.10.1 to 0.10.8. The changes touch exception handling, array bounds checks, WebAssembly SIMD and integer division. On the project’s own benchmark set, NetWasm now comes out ahead of Mono AOT and gets close to desktop .NET on some workloads.
NetWasm is a compiler and runtime that compiles C# programs ahead of time into small, standalone WebAssembly files. It takes the IL that Roslyn produces and emits Wasm, using its own runtime and a CoreLib ported from .NET. The yardstick is the Mono AOT build for WASI, which runs .NET on the same engine. A new garbage collector had already put NetWasm in front on allocation-heavy code, but plain loops were still slower: a quicksort of 100,000 integers took 77.2 ms, against 58.0 ms for Mono AOT.
Much of the early gain came from exception handling in 0.10.1. Wasmtime adds extra register save-and-restore code around any function that can throw or catch, floating-point registers included. Methods with null, bounds or checked-arithmetic checks paid that price on every call. Throws now go through a shared function and the catching handler releases the frames, which cut UI churn from 17.6 to 7.9 ms.
Version 0.10.2 inlines small straight-line methods in loops, tuple swaps included, and skips checks already performed on the same array and index. The quicksort fell to 54.0 ms. DoomSharp, a C# software renderer for Doom that ships a NetWasm build, served as a second test case. Value-type accessors now compile to plain field loads, and at O3 small branching helpers are inlined inside loops. Together these brought a 120-frame render from 3,595 down to 1,934 ms.
SIMD arrived in 0.10.7. Vector128, Vector<T> and PackedSimd lower to 128-bit Wasm instructions, and element-wise array loops handle four or more elements per iteration, with a scalar fallback. Hoisting loop-invariant Math calls allowed a solver for Burgers’ equation, a fundamental partial differential equation from fluid mechanics, to vectorise: its first test dropped from 497 ms to 71 ms, against 186 ms for Mono AOT and 93 ms for desktop .NET.
Version 0.10.8 targets division and range-checked arithmetic. A remainder that follows a division now reuses the quotient and skips repeated zero-divisor and int.MinValue / -1 checks. A trial-division test fell from 1,376 to 765 ms, while Mono AOT needed 862 ms.
Across the 2,213 cases, 0.10.8 at O3 with NetWasmGC takes 0.41 times Mono AOT’s time as a geometric mean, excluding five cases where Mono’s LLVM removes the work. Against desktop .NET 11 RC3 JIT the ratio is 0.87, down from 2.15 for 0.10.6. By family, the ratio to Mono AOT runs from 0.34 for intrinsics to 0.81 for math. The 120-frame DoomSharp render takes 1,623 ms on NetWasmGC, compared with 2,371 ms for Mono AOT and 1,053 ms for desktop .NET JIT.
Those figures come from Wasmtime 49.0.3 on an Apple M1 Max, using cases from dotnet/performance plus five NetWasm workloads. The authors also found that identical loops at different addresses could differ by up to 15 per cent, so their A/B tests align every function to 4 KiB.
The article is open about what is left. Desktop .NET is about 3.1 times faster on vector benchmarks, because it can use host SIMD directly while Wasm is limited to fixed 128-bit operations. Math.Pow is 1.4 times slower than on Mono AOT, and CopyBlock64 is 3.3 times slower. One workload, NewtR, regressed to 1.9 times slower than in 0.10.6, which the authors blame on Wasmtime’s register allocator keeping a value in a stack slot around the loop.
Since the numbers are self-reported and come from one machine and one runtime, results elsewhere may differ. NetWasm can be tried in the online playground, and local setup is covered in the compile and publish guide. Developers can find the documentation is in the official GitHub repository.

articles.title: Nvidia Responds to Gentlemen Ransomware Claim
articles.text:
Nvidia says it has found no indication that its systems or networks were affected after the Gentlemen ransomware group named the company on its data leak website.
The group’s listing includes Nvidia’s logo and a general description of the chipmaker. It offers no explanation of the alleged attack, with the section about stolen information indicating that details will be provided later.
The company has acknowledged that it is investigating a possible security incident, but its statement points to a third party rather than Nvidia’s own infrastructure.
“Nvidia is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner. We have found no indication that Nvidia systems or networks were affected. We continue to monitor the situation,” an Nvidia spokesperson told SecurityWeek.
The statement does not identify the partner or describe the nature of the incident. It also does not specify whether any Nvidia-related information may have been exposed.
The ransomware group’s listing does not establish that Nvidia was breached or that any of its data was stolen.
The Gentlemen ransomware operation emerged around mid-2025, initially operating as a closed group before launching an affiliate program later that year. Microsoft tracks its operators as Storm-2697.
The group uses a double-extortion model in which attackers steal data and encrypt systems, threatening to publish the stolen information to pressure victims into paying. Its affiliates have targeted organizations in numerous sectors, including manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, and financial services.
The Gentlemen has become increasingly active, with its leak website now listing more than 1,100 alleged victims.
According to Sophos, Gentlemen affiliates have used compromised credentials and legitimate administrative tools during intrusions. In one investigated incident, ransomware was deployed less than 24 hours after the earliest identified post-compromise activity.

articles.title: Opinion: Ottawa wants an investment supercycle. Here’s how to make that happen. | BetaKit
articles.text:
Liam Gill leads the Capital Program at MaRS Discovery District, the largest innovation hub in Canada. In 2024, MaRS-supported companies raised 13 percent of all venture capital deployed in Canada.
Earlier this month, the federal government released Budget 2026, which Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne says will kickstart an “investment supercycle.” 
An investment supercycle is exactly what our startup ecosystem needs, and the measures announced will help. But to guarantee Canadian entrepreneurs thrive for generations, we need to truly make Canada the greatest place for entrepreneurs to build. This means not only providing competitive economic conditions but building a private-sector-led venture capital (VC) industry to fund growth and build procurement pathways for the government to buy new technologies.
“To guarantee the benefits of Canada’s investment supercycle last, our startups need more than a short-term boost; they need changes that make Canada the greatest place for entrepreneurs to build in the world.”
According to some estimates, there are more than 500 US technology companies with a Canadian founder worth a combined $414 billion USD ($590 billion CAD); half were founded in the last three years. Since 2024, US visas for Canadians have increased by 142 percent. The US has arguably provided better economic conditions for entrepreneurs, which has allowed it to attract the most talented Canadians. The new Canada Growth Incentive, a $15-million CAD capital gains exemption modelled on the US Qualified Small Business Stock program, is the biggest change in a generation to the incentives our entrepreneurs have to build in Canada. It will help reverse this trend.
A report earlier this year by the National Angel Capital Organization (NACO) found that Canada has a $322-million USD funding gap from the pre-seed to Series A stages. That has cost our economy 133,000 high-paying jobs and $143 billion in value.
In October, Industry Minister Mélanie Joly announced $1 billion for the Venture and Growth Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI) to provide more capital for our VC ecosystem. While Growth VCCI is a welcome short-term boost, it shouldn’t be mistaken for a long-term solution to Canada’s capital shortage.
This is the fourth iteration of similar initiatives that followed 2013’s Venture Capital Action Plan and two Venture Capital Catalyst Initiatives in 2017 and 2021. In 2012, before the first of these federal programs, Canadian VCs raised $1.78 billion, equivalent to $2.39 billion in 2025 dollars. In 2025, they raised $2.01 billion. Over a similar period, BDC’s average annual direct investing in startups rose from $75 million in inflation-adjusted terms (2009 to 2012) to $354 million in 2025. In other words, real VC fundraising has declined by 12 percent while direct public investment has increased nearly fivefold.
RELATED: Canada sees rebound in angel investments as industry calls for more federal support
If Growth VCCI’s effects are only temporary, how can we leverage the short-term boost to guarantee capital availability for generations to come?
First, we can create new angel investors. A United Kingdom-style innovation tax credit would activate angel investors, steering capital away from passive investments in real estate and GICs into startups.
Second, we can create more VCs. Ten percent of Growth VCCI is already intended to support emerging managers, with the government matching private funds they raise. This should be made permanent by establishing an evergreen fund-of-funds that invests as a limited partner, matching every dollar emerging fund managers raise, up to $10 million per manager.
Third, Canada can become a natural home for global capital. To support our VCs in attracting foreign capital, Canada should create a dedicated legal structure for venture capital funds, combining the tax neutrality of the Cayman Islands with the sub-fund flexibility of Singapore’s Variable Capital Company.
In August 2025, the Canadian government became a customer of two Canadian ventures, signing a $250-million MOU with Cohere and giving a $4.2-million contract to North Vector Dynamics. Last month, both of those companies raised private capital, with Cohere securing $7 billion and North Vector Dynamics securing $29 million. These ventures prove that when the government is willing to be an early customer, it can validate technologies and make ventures a more attractive investment for private markets.
RELATED: Feds reveal breakdown of $750-million VC funding envelope, open Growth VCCI applications
With provincial governments responsible for healthcare, education, infrastructure, transit, and much more, it is vital that they follow the lead of the federal government by creating clear procurement pathways for startups in these industries to sell to the government. Founders won’t build here if they feel they need to sell outside of Canada before our domestic markets will buy their products.
Canada has tremendous potential, and Budget 2026 shows the government wants to match its ambition, but to guarantee the benefits of Canada’s investment supercycle last for generations, our startup ecosystem needs more than a short-term boost; it needs changes that make Canada the greatest place for entrepreneurs to build in the world with strong economic conditions, abundant capital, and clear procurement pathways.
The opinions and analysis expressed in the above article are those of its author, and do not necessarily reflect the position of BetaKit or its editorial staff. It has been edited for clarity, length, and style.

articles.title: UK government forced to disclose secret Apple backdoor order | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information.
The Thursday ruling from the U.K.’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret.
The tribunal’s ruling rejected the Home Office’s claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security.
The ruling comes a year after the U.K. government reportedly demanded that Apple build a backdoor to allow U.K. authorities access to customer data anywhere in the world. Details of the so-called “technical capabilities notice,” which are issued under strict non-disclosure rules, leaked to the media, which drew ire from White House officials and U.S. lawmakers who criticized the effort, arguing that the U.K. order would put Americans’ privacy at risk.
California-based Apple refused the order, and blocked U.K. users from switching on its Advanced Data Protection data-encryption feature for iCloud, rather than comply with the demand. The U.K.’s secret order was later narrowed to allow access to British nationals’ data stored in Apple’s encrypted cloud, and Apple also challenged this second order.
Prior to the ruling, Apple was legally barred from disclosing the order, even after details leaked. When reached for comment, Apple told TechCrunch that it welcomes the decision to make public the fact that the U.K. Home Office issued a technical capability notice.
Apple previously said that it has “never built a backdoor or master key” to any of its products or services and “never will.”
A spokesperson for the U.K. Home Office, which has yet to confirm the existence of a notice, did not respond to a request for comment.
Rights group Liberty International, which brought the legal challenge on behalf of two individuals, said that this is the first known time that the government has been compelled to confirm the existence of a secret technical order.
A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year.
Updated with comment.

articles.title: EUA liberaram quase 900 mil chips de IA para empresas chinesas
articles.text:
O governo de Donald Trump autorizou a exportação de mais de 879 mil chips avançados de inteligência artificial (IA) para empresas chinesas em período de seis meses. Os dados foram divulgados nesta quinta-feira (19) pelo Comitê de Relações Exteriores da Câmara dos Representantes dos Estados Unidos e incluem licenças para companhias que aparecem em lista do Pentágono de organizações supostamente ligadas às Forças Armadas da China.
Entre dezembro de 2025 e maio de 2026, empresas solicitaram autorização para enviar aproximadamente 3,4 milhões de chips ao país asiático. Desse total, mais de 879 mil receberam aprovação do Departamento de Comércio estadunidense, responsável pelo controle das exportações.
Os semicondutores incluem o H200, da Nvidia, e o MI325X, da AMD. Entre as empresas chinesas contempladas nas autorizações estão Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu e BYD.
A divulgação dos números ocorre em meio a debate nos Estados Unidos sobre os riscos de permitir que a China tenha acesso a componentes essenciais para o desenvolvimento de sistemas avançados de IA. Uma preocupação é que essa tecnologia possa contribuir para ampliar as capacidades militares e tecnológicas do país.
Quais empresas chinesas receberam autorização?
Os documentos divulgados pelo comitê mostram que algumas das maiores empresas de tecnologia da China receberam autorização para importar chips avançados de IA.
A Tencent teve o maior número de unidades aprovadas entre as companhias destacadas, com 150 mil chips. A lista inclui:
- Tencent: 150 mil chips;
- Alibaba: 75 mil chips;
- Baidu: 43 mil chips;
- BYD: quatro mil chips.
As quatro empresas aparecem em relação do Pentágono que identifica organizações chinesas supostamente ligadas às Forças Armadas do país.
A divulgação das informações foi autorizada pelo presidente republicano do Comitê de Relações Exteriores da Câmara, Brian Mast. Ele utilizou poderes previstos na Lei de Reforma do Controle de Exportações para tornar públicos dados de solicitações de licenças relacionadas às vendas de chips da Nvidia e da AMD para a China.
O comitê também apontou que os pedidos de exportação incluíam solicitações da Nvidia relacionadas à possível utilização de intermediários envolvidos em contrabando de chips para facilitar as vendas a empresas chinesas.
Quantos chips realmente chegaram à China?
Apesar do número expressivo de autorizações, ainda não está claro quantos dos semicondutores aprovados foram efetivamente enviados para a China.
Os dados divulgados pelo comitê mostram que o governo estadunidense autorizou mais de 879 mil unidades, mas isso não significa que todas tenham sido embarcadas ou entregues às empresas destinatárias.
A diferença é importante porque o processo de exportação envolve etapas posteriores à concessão da licença. Portanto, os números divulgados representam autorizações concedidas pelo governo dos Estados Unidos, e não um balanço confirmado de chips que chegaram ao território chinês.
Leia mais:
- Saída voluntária na Microsoft reflete mudança no trabalho com IA
- Anthropic movimenta mercado em estreia na Nasdaq; veja como foi o primeiro dia
- Alibaba triplica lucro no trimestre com avanço da IA
O que dizem Nvidia e AMD?
A Nvidia afirmou que as autorizações concedidas estavam sujeitas a condições rigorosas e envolviam volumes limitados de semicondutores.
A empresa também declarou que, apesar de ter recebido algumas licenças, interrompeu posteriormente os envios de chips H200 para a China.
A AMD, por sua vez, não se pronunciou.
Governo Trump flexibilizou restrições a chips avançados
A liberação dos dados reacende o debate sobre a política estadunidense de exportação de semicondutores para a China.
O governo de Joe Biden havia imposto restrições ao acesso chinês a chips avançados de IA. A preocupação era que esses componentes pudessem acelerar o desenvolvimento tecnológico e ampliar as capacidades militares de Pequim.
Em dezembro de 2025, Trump autorizou a Nvidia a vender seus chips H200 para empresas chinesas, revertendo parte das restrições anteriores. A decisão provocou críticas de parlamentares e especialistas que defendem postura mais rígida diante da concorrência tecnológica chinesa.
A divulgação das licenças pela Câmara dos Representantes coloca novamente em evidência a tensão entre os interesses comerciais das fabricantes estadunidenses e as preocupações de segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Ubisoft lays off 166 employees in Quebec
articles.text:
Ubisoft has laid off 166 employees at its Montreal and Quebec City studios.
“As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs,” a Ubisoft spokesperson said in a statement to MobileSyrup. “We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect.”
The company added that affected staff are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.
Ubisoft Montreal is the French gaming giant’s flagship studio with around 4,000 employees, leading development on marquee franchises like Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six, Far Cry, Prince of Persia and Watch Dogs. Outside of this year’s Rainbow Six Mobile, though, the studio has largely been supporting development on other Ubisoft titles while working on various other new projects, including an upcoming Assassin’s Creed codenamed “Hexe.”
Ubisoft Quebec, meanwhile, staffs around 600 and was behind last year’s hit Assassin’s Creed Shadows, the latest mainline Assassin’s Creed game, not counting this year’s remake of Black Flag. It’s unclear what the studio has been working on since the release of Shadows outside of various updates to the game.
These layoffs come as Ubisoft has been struggling in recent years, leading to a studio co-ownership venture with Tencent that led to a company restructuring. Amidst all of that, Ubisoft has laid off hundreds of employees, including 70 last month at its Singapore team and 40 in Toronto earlier this year, as well as closed multiple studios, including those in San Francisco, Osaka, Stockholm, Belgrade, and Finland. Here in Canada, it also closed Halifax (following unionization efforts) and Winnipeg. Ubisoft’s next release is Rayman Legends Retold, a Ubisoft Montpellier- and Milan-led remake of 2013’s Rayman Legends that hits consoles and PC on Dec. 3.
It should be noted that the timing of this news is certainly questionable. After all, today is the long-awaited launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which has understandably dominated the news cycle. Therefore, it seems as though Ubisoft is looking to try to bury the latest rounds of layoffs under the shadow of GTA.
The string of cuts and closures in Canada, especially, has garnered renewed scrutiny in recent months due to the significant government subsidies Ubisoft has received. As The Walrus noted earlier this year, Ubisoft has been given as much as $2 billion in Canadian incentives since the ’90s, yet it’s been reducing significant portions of its workforce here.
Update: 19/11/2026 at 3:08 p.m. ET — This news also comes alongside Ubisoft’s announcement of a GenAI subsidiary because AI slop will certainly help cut costs in the long-term.
