articles.title: A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
articles.text:
“We’ve got this,” Colette Kress, interim CEO of Nvidia, said Tuesday night as she closed out the embattled chip company’s third quarter earnings call.
A brief history of Nvidia’s recent stock fluctuations
Tracking the stock price amid Jensen Huang’s extramarital affairs and alleged spy scandal.
By Thursday, the company’s stock price was hovering at around $150 per share, a nearly 40 percent drop from its all-time high on October 6th, and wiping out a brief post-earnings pop on Tuesday night. Meanwhile, Wall Street was paying up for one of Nvidia’s biggest customers as Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected.
Looking at the earnings report numbers alone, Nvidia had a blockbuster quarter. Q3 revenue more than doubled from the same period last year up to total $115.8 billion, driven by data center revenue that was up 110 percent and exceeding Wall Street expectations. Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the highly anticipated Vera Rubin platform, which shipped during the quarter, becoming the “fastest product ramp in company history,” Kress told investors.
“Our momentum is real,” Kress said. “With the market-leading multiyear roadmap, supply agreements extending through to the end of the decade, and sustainable demand, we are well positioned to accelerate Nvidia’s leadership position.”
But investors are stilltrying to reconcile Nvidia’s stellar recent financial performance and position as a central pillar in the AI economy with serious concerns over its future.
The company’s stock has taken a stunning tumble in recent weeks. Fueled first by a broader market sell-off of chip stocks amid concerns about the AI bubble, the stock took another blow following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, according to US intelligence sources cited by The New York Times.
Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s newly appointed chairman of the board, told investors on the call Tuesday that the company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and has already tapped an executive search firm to help find a replacement. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has led the company ever since — famously without a succession plan — has become essentially inseparable from it in the eyes of Wall Street and the media. But while Huang may not be ready to let go, posting on X this week that he’d be “honored” to be reinstated as CEO, Nvidia’s executive suite seems ready to move on.
It has been a tumultuous two and a half weeks for Nvidia.
On October 29th, The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Jensen Huang to be the target of a Chinese espionage plot. The report centered on his “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a Chinese national and an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company and one of Nvidia’s clients. Nvidia initially contested the report, adding that Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang “are not unusual or unexpected.”
Nvidia’s stock seemingly remained unaffected by the reports, at least at first. The share price closed at $213.66 on October 29th, down just 0.8 percent from the previous day. (Julian Barnes, one of the reporters on the story, later commented, “I will confess I was kind of surprised that the world’s initial reaction to our October story was a bit muted.”) The stock closed at a 4 percent drop the next day as the entire Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent, the worst single-day decline since June.
The stock continued to fall through Wednesday, November 4th, the day after the blue wave swept the midterms, stoking fears on Wall Street that the new class of Democratic governors in key states like Texas would slow down data center construction. On Thursday, November 5th, Nvidia’s stock fell 9.2 percent, its largest single-day drop in at least a year. But chip stocks began to recover the next day, and by close on Friday, November 6th, Nvidia was back up 2.8 percent to a share price of $186.64.
Then all hell broke loose. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang sent a company-wide memo to Nvidia staff in which he apologized for engaging in an extramarital affair. The memo coincided with the opening of an independent investigation by Nvidia’s board into Huang’s alleged misconduct and whether company secrets or national security had been compromised. Huang said he would cooperate fully with the investigation. By the opening bell on Monday, November 9th, Nvidia shares had tumbled 7 percent and trading volume surged past its three-month average as investors reacted to the memo. After a brief rebound, the stock continued to oscillate the next day, as more details of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang’s relationship emerged. By the time the market closed on Tuesday, November 10th, Nvidia shares were down to $168.89, nearly 10 percent below the closing price on the last day of 2025.
The stock rebounded slightly on Wednesday, November 11th, as investors prepared for Nvidia’s third quarter earnings call, scheduled for the following Tuesday, November 17th. By Wednesday night, however, shares had plunged yet again as media reports circulated that Nvidia’s board was considering ousting Huang, and other reports emerged detailing a second alleged affair, this time between Huang and an Nvidia employee.
Nvidia announced Huang’s departure on the morning of Thursday, November 12th, sending the company’s shares falling nearly 14 percent at the open. It closed at just a 4.3 percent dip. The intraday low of $148.80 per share was its lowest price in a year.
On December 1st, Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews. Nvidia’s general counsel will do the same on December 2nd.
Retail investors have already seized the opportunity to buy the dip. In the first 30 minutes of trading on Thursday, November 12th, retail investors bought $111 million of Nvidia shares in the largest-ever first half-hour of opening for the stock, Bloomberg reported, citing Vanda Research.
They might be onto something.
Nvidia’s average price target is $232.59, with the lowest estimate at $130 and the highest at $350, according to an analysis of analyst projections over the last three months by Google Finance.
Nearly two-thirds of those analysts issued a “Buy” rating for Nvidia in the last three months. Of those, all 30 reiterated that rating post-earnings.
The stock closed at $145.98 on Thursday, a new 52-week low.
Then again, numbers are the core basis for stock market ratings, and numbers may not be Nvidia’s problem right now. It’s everything else — the leadership vacuum, upcoming congressional testimony, regulatory uncertainty, broader questions about neocloud customer financing and sales to China — that will continue to impact the stock in the coming weeks.

articles.title: What a billion-dollar deal says about the US battery market
articles.text:
What a billion-dollar deal says about the US battery market
The deal between Sila and Panasonic Energy is a bright spot for the industry, and it shows how politics have shifted recently for batteries.
After a tough few years littered with some high-profile failures, there’s some positive news for next-generation batteries in the US.
Sila just signed an agreement with Panasonic Energy, a global battery manufacturer, to supply silicon-carbon anode material, a possible key to smaller, lighter batteries. It’s a deal that Sila says could be worth more than $1 billion over time.
This arrangement also shows how much the politics of batteries have shifted lately. A major part of the financial backing for this factory’s production is a $1.4 billion loan from the Trump administration’s Defense Department. While batteries can be a major tool to help drive the energy transition and cut emissions, right now much of the industry is more focused on geopolitics.
Founded in 2011, Sila makes silicon-based anodes for lithium-ion batteries. The big selling point here is the potential to improve energy density—Sila’s anode weighs a fifth as much as the graphite used in anodes today and cuts the volume in half, according to the company. So using this new material enables batteries to pack more energy into the same weight and volume, allowing longer range for EVs, for example. The material can also deliver more power and recharge faster, compared with conventional chemistry.
We’ve been following Sila (and its competitors) for years. My colleague James Temple covered the company when its battery first appeared in Whoop fitness wearables in 2021.
Things have gotten a lot bigger since then. In 2022, Sila announced plans for a factory in Moses Lake, Washington, and received $100 million from the US Department of Energy, part of a multibillion-dollar round of grants under the Biden administration to support the US battery supply chain.
The company opened its factory in September 2025, and it’s already operating. But the deal with Panasonic will help it scale to at least 10 times more production than current levels, says Gene Berdichevsky, the company’s cofounder and CEO.
Panasonic has committed to buying tens of thousands of tons of material, Berdichevsky says, though Sila isn’t sharing specific numbers on the total commitment or the price Panasonic is paying.
This agreement is Sila’s first mass-market deal and a big one for the United States’ next-generation battery market, which has largely been on the ropes over the past few years. Two billion-dollar battery companies, 24M and ESS Tech, have declared bankruptcy and shut down just in the last year.
The glimmer of hope here is tied up with something I’ve been noticing about this industry: the shifting politics. While batteries used to be firmly considered a climate technology, we’ve seen a lot of companies move away from messaging around the clean energy transition and lean into geopolitics.
China dominates the battery world and particularly the battery anode market, controlling over 90% of graphite production today. For years, the US has been trying to curb reliance on Chinese batteries, battery materials, and other materials used in crucial technologies, like rare earth metals. But the Trump administration has ramped things up, and earlier this year the US Defense Department committed a $1.4 billion loan to Sila aimed at helping the US face a “significant technology sovereignty challenge,” as a press release put it.
Sila’s announcement of the Panasonic deal does mention EVs—but not climate, emissions or the energy transition. Rather, it’s all about American industrialization. (And, of course, a mention that a North American battery supply chain can also help power the AI market.)
I asked Berdichevsky about this shift and whether the company holds decarbonization as a priority.
“I think the politics of it has shifted around us much more than our motivations have shifted,” he said. “It’s really the energy efficiency that motivates engineers like myself and technologists at our company. And I still think that that’s still at the heart of it.”

articles.title: Meet the Shark RazorVac: a sleek, affordable new handheld vacuum built to banish hidden crumbs from your sofa, desk, and car
articles.text:
From makeup spills to dusty car interiors, Shark’s new RazorVac handheld vacuum cuts through mess with cyclonic suction and dirt-illuminating LEDs
Clean for up to 40 minutes on a single charge
- The Shark RazorVac is a handheld vacuum with cyclonic suction and integrated LED
- Its runtime is up to 40 hours in Eco mode
- It's available in the US now for $129.99 (about £100 / AU$190)
I'm not saying I have a vacuum problem but because I have kids and a dog I currently own three cleaners: a Dyson cordless, a USB one for the car and a handheld Shark in the kitchen. And if my credit card wasn't maxed out I'd be getting a fourth: the new Shark RazorVac, a new contender for the best handheld vacuums crown.
The big selling point here is that the RazorVac combines power with portability. SharkNinja says it's twice as powerful as its best-selling competitor, and it weighs a titchy 1.2lbs. And unlike the handheld I have in the car, it doesn't run out of power after dusting half of the dash: in Eco Mode you can expect up to 40 hours of runtime.
RazorVac: a razor with a laser
There are some smart ideas in the RazorVac, including a spotlight LED so you can spot dust and debris that you might otherwise miss. The cyclonic cylinder separates the debris from the airflow to keep the suction strong — solving a problem I've encountered with various handhelds — and there's a one-press button for easy emptying.
There are two included tools. The multi-surface pet tool is designed to lift embedded hair from upholstery, while the duster crevice tool reaches into tight spaces such as between your sofa cushions or down the side of your car seats.
The RazorVac will come in three colors initially: Petal Pink, Matcha and French Gold. And SharkNinja's website will have two more exclusive colors in limited editions: Gold Chrome and Silver Chrome. More colors will arrive in 2027.
The Shark RazorVac is available in the US now, with a list price of $129.99 (about £99 / AU$191). International pricing and availability haven't been announced just yet.

articles.title: Black Friday airfryer : des références Ninja, Philips et Cosori dans notre sélection à prix réduit
articles.text:
Nous avons sélectionné sept appareils couvrant un large spectre d’usages : de l’airfryer compact d’entrée de gamme au modèle double tiroir grande capacité, en passant par un robot-cuiseur et un airfryer vapeur. Les prix fournis par les marchands ont été vérifiés au moment de la publication.
Les offres Black Friday sont soumises aux stocks disponibles chez chaque marchand. Certaines peuvent disparaître rapidement, en particulier sur Amazon où les prix fluctuent fréquemment.
Les meilleures offres airfryers
- Ninja Double Stack XL à 169 euros au lieu de 269 euros
- Philips Airfryer 4000 Vertical Duo à 169 euros au lieu de 249 euros
- Cosori Turbo Tower Pro à 239 euros au lieu de 279 euros
- Ninja Crispi Pro 7-en-1 à 189 euros au lieu de 229 euros
- Xiaomi Mijia Smart Steam à 164 euros au lieu de 179 euros
- Dreame Tasti à 94 euros au lieu de 119 euros
- Moulinex Cookeo+ à 198 euros au lieu de 249 euros
Pour le reste, nos recommandations sont détaillées dans notre guide des meilleurs air fryers.
Ninja Double Stack XL
Vous êtes à la recherche d’un air fryer double tiroir sans sacrifier la moitié de votre plan de travail ? Le Ninja Double Stack XL répond à ce problème avec une architecture verticale : ses deux tiroirs de 4,75 litres sont superposés plutôt que posés côte à côte, ce qui lui permet d’afficher 9,5 litres de capacité totale sur seulement 28 cm de largeur. Avec ses 2 470 W et ses quatre niveaux de cuisson simultanés, il peut rôtir un poulet entier par tiroir et nourrir jusqu’à 8 personnes en une seule fournée.
Les points forts du Ninja Double Stack XL
- 9,5 litres de capacité sur 28 cm de large
- Quatre niveaux de cuisson simultanés
- 6 fonctions dont déshydratation et croustillant max
Le Ninja Double Stack XL est disponible à 169 euros chez Amazon au lieu de 269 euros habituellement, soit une remise de 100 euros.
Philips Airfryer 4000 Vertical Duo
Philips a choisi la même logique verticale que Ninja, mais pousse la capacité un cran plus loin : le Philips Airfryer 4000 Vertical Duo propose deux paniers de 5 litres pour un total de 10 litres, le tout sur une empreinte réduite de 45 % par rapport à un double tiroir horizontal. La puissance de 2 750 W alimente deux résistances indépendantes, une par compartiment, pour des cuissons simultanées à des températures différentes. Chaque panier est équipé d’une fenêtre de visualisation et d’un revêtement céramique sans PFAS.
Les points forts du Philips Airfryer 4000 Vertical Duo
- 10 litres répartis en deux paniers de 5 litres
- Fenêtres de visualisation sur chaque compartiment
- Revêtement céramique sans PFAS
Le Philips Airfryer 4000 Vertical Duo est proposé à 169 euros chez Amazon au lieu de 249 euros, une remise de 80 euros.
Cosori Turbo Tower Pro
La tour plutôt que le tiroir : le Cosori Turbo Tower Pro mise sur un format vertical à double panier superposé pour loger 10,8 litres de capacité (4,3 litres en haut, 6,5 litres en bas) dans un encombrement contenu. Sa puissance de 2 630 W s’appuie sur la technologie Dual Blaze, avec des résistances positionnées en haut et en bas du panier inférieur pour une cuisson homogène. Il embarque aussi le Wi-Fi, avec une connexion à l’application VeSync pour piloter les cuissons à distance. Dans notre test du Cosori Turbo Tower Pro Smart, six semaines d’usage quotidien ont confirmé qu’il tient ses promesses pour les familles de cinq personnes et plus.
Les points forts du Cosori Turbo Tower Pro
- 10,8 litres en format vertical compact
- Technologie Dual Blaze avec résistances haut et bas
- Connectivité Wi-Fi via l’application VeSync
Le Cosori Turbo Tower Pro est disponible à 239 euros chez Amazon au lieu de 279 euros, soit 40 euros d’économie.
Ninja Crispi Pro 7-en-1
En dehors des formats verticaux à double tiroir, le Ninja Crispi Pro 7-en-1 propose une approche différente : ses récipients sont en verre thermorésistant, sans revêtement antiadhésif synthétique. La boîte inclut deux contenants (5,7 litres et 2,3 litres) et une base modulaire ajustable qui s’adapte à l’un ou l’autre selon la quantité à préparer. Les sept modes de cuisson couvrent la friture sans huile, la cuisson au four, la levée de pâte, le rôtissage, la déshydratation et le réchauffage croustillant. En revanche, il n’y a pas de cuisson simultanée en deux zones indépendantes : un seul récipient est actif à la fois.
Les points forts du Ninja Crispi Pro 7-en-1
- Récipients en verre sans PFAS, compatibles lave-vaisselle
- Deux tailles incluses : 5,7 litres et 2,3 litres
- 7 modes dont levée de pâte et déshydratation
Le Ninja Crispi Pro 7-en-1 est affiché à 189 euros à la Fnac au lieu de 229 euros, soit une remise de 40 euros.
Xiaomi Mijia Smart Steam
Soit un air fryer classique, soit un cuiseur vapeur : le Xiaomi Mijia Smart Steam tente de combiner les deux dans un seul appareil. Son réservoir d’eau de 1,5 litre positionné en haut de l’appareil alimente un générateur de vapeur à 900 W capable d’atteindre 130 °C, ce qui permet de cuire à la vapeur, à l’air chaud ou en mode hybride vapeur et friture dans le même panier de 7 litres. Dix modes de cuisson sont disponibles, dont sous-vide, déshydratation et décongélation. La connexion à l’application Xiaomi Home donne accès à plus de 100 recettes. Prenez soin de vérifier la compatibilité avec votre installation avant l’achat : cet appareil est vendu sur le site Mi et peut nécessiter une commande directe auprès de Xiaomi France.
Les points forts du Xiaomi Mijia Smart Steam
- Cuisson hybride vapeur 130 °C et air chaud 360°
- Réservoir de 1,5 litre pour jusqu’à 7 plats par remplissage
- 10 modes dont sous-vide et déshydratation
Le Xiaomi Mijia Smart Steam est disponible à 164 euros sur Mi au lieu de 179 euros, soit 15 euros de remise.
Dreame Tasti
Vous êtes à la recherche d’un air fryer qui tranche avec les cuves en plastique habituelles ? La Dreame Tasti mise sur deux récipients en verre borosilicate de 6 mm, sans revêtement, sans risque de rayures ni d’émanations à haute température. Elle embarque deux contenances (2,5 L et 4,5 L), ce qui la rend aussi bien adaptée à un repas solo qu’à une tablée de famille. Sa technologie à air chaud 3D, couplée à une infusion de vapeur haute température, vise à préserver l’humidité des aliments tout en les grillant en surface.
Les points forts de la Dreame Tasti
- Deux cuves en verre borosilicate sans revêtement chimique
- Double capacité : 2,5 L et 4,5 L interchangeables
- Cuves compatibles lave-vaisselle
La Dreame Tasti est disponible à 94 euros chez Boulanger au lieu de 119 euros, soit 25 euros d’économie.
Moulinex Cookeo+
Le Moulinex Cookeo+ n’est pas, à proprement parler, un air fryer : c’est un multicuiseur haute pression 6 litres, capable de cuire sous pression, mijoter, dorer, cuire à la vapeur ou maintenir au chaud. Son intérêt dans une sélection orientée friteuse sans huile ? Un couvercle Extra Crisp vendu séparément (ou inclus selon les packs) qui bascule l’appareil en mode air fryer en quelques secondes, sans changer de cuve. L’écran LCD guide l’utilisateur pas à pas à travers 150 recettes préprogrammées, et l’application Mon Cookeo en recense plus de 2 500 supplémentaires. La capacité de 6 litres convient à des repas pour 2 à 6 personnes.
Les points forts du Moulinex Cookeo+
- 6 modes de cuisson dont cuisson haute pression
- 150 recettes préprogrammées, plus de 2 500 via l’application
- Cuve antiadhésive de 6 L compatible lave-vaisselle
Le Moulinex Cookeo+ est proposé à 198 euros sur Amazon au lieu de 249 euros, soit 51 euros d’économie.

articles.title: Google ajoute un mode privé à sa recherche IA : voici ce qu’il garde pendant 24 heures
articles.text:
Le Mode IA de Google permet désormais d’ouvrir une conversation qui n’apparaîtra pas dans votre historique et n’influencera pas vos prochaines recherches. Vous en perdez l’accès dès que vous la quittez, mais Google conserve le fil pendant 24 heures.
Toutes les recherches ne sont pas bonnes à partager, et cela vaut aussi pour le Mode IA de Google. Depuis le 17 novembre, Google déploie les fils de discussion temporaires dans le Mode IA de son moteur de recherche. Comme l’indique TechCrunch, un bouton permet de mettre la personnalisation de côté le temps d’une conversation, sans toucher aux réglages de son compte.
Un bouton pour poser une question hors de son historique
Si vous avez déjà utilisé les discussions temporaires de l’application Gemini, le principe est familier. Cette fois, le bouton se trouve dans le Mode IA du moteur de recherche, qui vient d’adopter Gemini 4 Hydrogen. Il suffit de cliquer sur l’icône en haut à droite avant de saisir sa question. Aucun réglage du compte Google n’est à modifier.
Une fois dans le fil, vous pouvez relancer l’IA, joindre une image ou poser une question à l’oral. Google répond sans s’appuyer sur votre activité passée, et ce que vous lui dites ne viendra pas modifier la personnalisation de vos prochaines réponses. En contrepartie, certaines fonctions sont indisponibles, dont les applications reliées à votre compte, le partage d’une réponse et la génération d’images.
Ce qui disparaît tout de suite, et ce qui reste 24 heures
Quand vous quittez la conversation, vous revenez à la recherche habituelle. Même si vous changez d’avis dans la minute, vous ne pourrez plus rouvrir le fil depuis l’historique de Google ou celui du Mode IA. Google précise que la conversation n’est pas enregistrée dans votre compte et qu’elle disparaît au bout de 24 heures.
Google indique que ces échanges ne servent pas à entraîner ses modèles d’IA générative, sauf si vous envoyez des commentaires ou si leur utilisation est nécessaire pour des raisons de sécurité. L’entreprise dit aussi continuer à collecter certaines données dissociées de votre compte pour faire fonctionner ses services et soutenir ses activités commerciales. Elle ne précise pas dans sa documentation si ces données servent au ciblage publicitaire.
Le fil temporaire s’arrête aux portes du moteur de recherche. Dès que vous ouvrez un résultat, le site consulté et les services qu’il utilise peuvent collecter des données, et votre navigateur peut enregistrer la visite. On peut donc demander des idées de cadeaux à Google sans les retrouver dans son historique de recherche, sans gâcher la surprise en laissant le nom de la boutique dans les suggestions de la barre d’adresse.
Autrement dit, le mode protège surtout de vos propres traces et de la personnalisation, pas d’un éventuel regard extérieur. Dans un contexte où Google pousse son IA au cœur de la recherche, ce qui alimente une grogne que le moteur de recherche DuckDuckGo cherche à capitaliser, le geste ressemble à un gage de confiance bienvenu, mais limité.

articles.title: Teilt Metas KI-Agent Muse Informationen aus fremden Chats?
articles.text:
Sicherheitsprobleme bei Metas KI-Agent: Teilt Muse Informationen aus fremden Chats?
Anfang September 2026 hatte Meta mit Muse einen persönlichen KI-Agenten vorgestellt. Der Start erfolgte zunächst nur in den USA. Die App verzeichnet mittlerweile mehr als zehn Millionen Downloads. Intern sorgt der KI-Agent aber für Unruhe.
Muse liest private Nachrichten
Wie von Reuters ausgewertete Berichte von Meta-Mitarbeiter:innen zeigen, soll sich Muse unerlaubt Zugriff auf Nachrichten des Ende-zu-Ende-verschlüsselten Messengers Signal verschafft haben. Außerdem soll der KI-Agent ungefragt Buchungen vorgenommen und – ebenfalls ohne entsprechende Anweisung – angebliche Kontostände der Nutzer:innen genannt haben.
Große Besorgnis ausgelöst haben zudem Muse-Aktionen, in denen der KI-Agent Nutzer:innen Antworten zu Anfragen geschickt haben soll, die sie selbst nicht gestellt hatten. In einem Fall teilte Muse mit, dass eine Anfrage bezüglich der Kontrolle über den Datenschutz eines Kindes nicht übermittelt werden konnte.
Gibt es ein Datenleck bei Metas KI?
Der betroffene Meta-Mitarbeiter zeigte sich laut Reuters überrascht, da er mit dem KI-Agenten nie über das Thema gesprochen und auch nichts getan habe, was diese Nachricht hätte auslösen können. Muse ließ auf eine entsprechende Nachfrage hin wissen: „Ich habe keine wirkliche Erklärung dafür, außer dass es nichts mit unserem Gespräch zu tun hatte“.
In einem anderen Fall soll die Meta-KI einem Mitarbeiter angeboten haben, eine Nachricht bezüglich der Abholung eines Couchtisches zu verfassen. Der Mitarbeiter hatte allerdings weder einen Tisch gekauft noch einen solchen Kauf geplant. Die Erklärung laut KI: „Ich habe Kontextinformationen zur Abholung eines Couchtisches abgerufen, die offenbar gar nicht zu dir gehören“.
KI könnte Kontexte vermischt haben
Und: Es habe sich „nicht um mein Gespräch“ gehandelt, wie der Mitarbeiter aus dem entsprechenden Chat zitiert. Bedenken, dass es zu einer „möglichen Vermischung von Kontexten zwischen verschiedenen Konten“ gekommen sein könnte, versuchte Meta allerdings auszuräumen.
Die KI scheine Nachrichten zu halluzinieren, hieß es intern. Auslöser sei wohl, dass der Agent angehalten sei, auch zwischen den eigentlichen Sitzungen mit den Nutzer:innen zu interagieren.
Meta nennt die Vorfälle Einzelfälle
Demnach seien sowohl das zugrundeliegende KI-Modell als auch die Software von dem Problem betroffen. Das zuständige Meta-Team arbeite schon an der Behebung. Meta-Sprecher Daniel Roberts bezeichnete die von Reuters beschriebenen Beispiele gegenüber der Nachrichtenagentur als „Einzelfälle“. Meta führe interne Tests durch, um seine Produkte zu aktualisieren und den Schutz zu verbessern.
Neben dem befürchteten Datenleck steht auch der oben erwähnte Signal-Zugriff im Fokus externer Beobachter:innen. Signal-Präsidentin Meredith Whittaker forderte von Meta verbindliche technische Barrieren, damit App-Entwickler:innen ihre Programme vor dem Zugriff von KI-Agenten besser schützen könnten.
Apple-Update soll KI-Agenten beschränken
Wie Reuters mit Expert:innen nachvollziehen konnte, ist Muse in der Lage, auf Android-Geräten Nachrichtentexte aus Push-Mitteilungen zu lesen. Auf dem Mac nutzt der KI-Agent Bedienungshilfen und Bildschirmaufnahmen. Auf dem iPhone scheiterte derweil der Versuch, sich Zugriff zu verschaffen. Apple hat mittlerweile ein Update ausgeliefert, das den Zugriff von Agenten beschränken soll.
))) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: Microsoft confirms app installation, launch issues after hotpatch
articles.text:
Microsoft has shared a workaround for installation and launch issues affecting Office and third-party applications after installing this month's Windows 11 hotpatch.
In a service alert seen by BleepingComputer, Microsoft told IT administrators that these problems may appear during installation, launch, or even during normal app use on systems running Windows 11 24H2 and later.
"Devices which installed the November 2026 hotpatch update (the Originating KBs listed above), might experience an error when installing, launching, or running some applications. Resulting from this issue, errors similar to "ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099)" are displayed," Microsoft said.
"Current investigation suggests this issue occurs for applications which load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, found as msi.dll. This can happen more frequently with 32-bit applications, but can also occur for 64-bit applications under certain conditions."
Microsoft added that this known issue should not impact systems that have installed the standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, but only those that have installed the hotpatch updates pushed through the Windows Autopatch, the company's cloud-based enterprise service that automates Windows and Microsoft 365 software and security updates.
Until a fix is available, Microsoft has shared a workaround to help IT admins temporarily mitigate the bug on affected systems.
To do that, they have to edit the Windows Registry to increase the HotPatchTableSize using the following procedure:
- Open the Windows Registry by opening the Start menu, typing "regedit", and selecting Registry Editor from the results.
- Using the folders and address path, navigate to the HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management folder.
- In the right-hand panel, locate the "HotPatchTableSize" registry key, open it, and set the Value to "2000". Click OK.
- Close the registry editor and restart the device.
"Before you modify the registry, back it up and make sure that you know how to restore it if a problem occurs. For more information, see How to back up and restore the registry in Windows," Microsoft said.
Microsoft said in March that it would turn on hotpatch security updates by default for all eligible Windows devices managed through the Microsoft Graph API and Microsoft Intune, after the May 2026 Windows security updates are installed.
One month later, it fixed a Windows Autopatch bug that caused driver updates restricted by administrative policies to deploy on some Autopatch-managed Windows devices belonging to customers in the European Union.
Microsoft first announced Windows Autopatch in April 2002, saying it would be available for free to customers with a Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater starting in July 2022. The feature reached public preview in early June and has been generally available since July 2022.

articles.title: Africa’s AI adoption numbers are only as good as the counting
articles.text:
Kenya came first in a global ranking of ChatGPT use last year. In a survey published by DataReportal in July 2025, 42.1% of Kenyan Internet users aged 16 and above said they had used ChatGPT in the previous month—the highest share among the markets surveyed. South Africa came in at 34.3% and Nigeria at 27.9%.
Microsoft’s ranking put the three countries in the opposite order. In the first quarter of 2026, it estimated that 23.1% of South Africans aged 15 to 64 had used a generative artificial intelligence (AI) tool, followed by 10.1% of Nigerians and 8.7% of Kenyans. The next quarter brought modest gains in all three countries, with South Africa reaching 23.9%, Nigeria 10.4% and Kenya 8.9%.
The reversal can be confusing—and consequential—because AI adoption figures shape how investors size a market or how governments decide to deliver services. Yet if you look at the numbers closely, the two rankings describe different things.
One shows how popular ChatGPT is among people who already use the internet. The other estimates how far a range of generative AI tools has reached across the working-age population. Then there is a third question, which neither headline figure answers: how many people have found a use for AI that brings them back?
The people surveys leave out
DataReportal’s ChatGPT figures come from GlobalWebIndex (GWI), which surveys internet users. Imagine two countries with 100 adults each. In the first, 40 are online, and half of them use ChatGPT. In the second, 80 are online, and a third use it.
The first leads among internet users. The second has more ChatGPT users across the adult population. The ranking changes simply because the share of people who are online differs.
The difference in access between Kenya and South Africa is substantial. In its Digital 2027 country reports, DataReportal puts Internet penetration at 40.6% in Kenya and 79.5% in South Africa. Nigeria sits at 47.5%.
Those figures cover the whole population and come from a different period from the original ChatGPT survey. They show why connectivity matters, but multiplying them by the ChatGPT percentages would mix age groups and timeframes, yielding a misleading national estimate.
The denominator becomes even more important as the definition of AI widens. In its more recent global AI report, DataReportal says 97.3% of Kenyan internet users aged 16 and above reported using some form of AI in the previous month. In Nigeria, the figure was 96.6%.
“It’s critical to stress that these figures represent the share of Internet users,” the report says. This time the survey was asking about AI broadly. The figures cannot be read as evidence that ChatGPT use has doubled, or that almost everyone in either country uses AI.
Who gets online also affects the comparison. DataReportal found that, across the markets surveyed, 93.3% of internet users aged 16 to 24 said they had used AI in the previous month, compared with 52.2% of those aged 65 and above.
If one country’s online population skews younger than another’s, that alone could lift its adoption rate. The published rankings leave open the question of how much of Kenya’s lead reflects the ages of the people surveyed and how much reflects differences in behaviour among people of the same age.
What Microsoft can see
Microsoft starts with a wider population—everyone aged 15 to 64, whether they work, study or have internet access. It also counts activity across generative AI products. However, the data it observes directly are “primarily originating from users on Windows desktop (PC/tablet) platforms,” according to its technical paper.
People can opt out of sending diagnostic data, and Microsoft uses other sources to estimate usage beyond Windows and account for activity on mobile devices. “These assumptions are difficult to validate,” the researchers write of their mobile adjustment.
That matters when someone’s first encounter with generative AI may be through a chatbot on their phone. A survey can capture that person’s experience if they remember and report it; a model anchored in desktop activity has to estimate how much use it misses.
Both approaches make assumptions, and the two headline figures offer little basis for saying exactly how much of the gap comes from internet access, the mix of products counted, or the way each study collects its data.
Microsoft’s tables also give reason to be cautious about drawing fine distinctions between countries. Its technical paper notes that it sometimes pools markets with limited data to produce regional averages. Nigeria shares its 10.4% second-quarter estimate with several countries, including Ghana, Benin, and Togo.
The table alone offers little basis for treating Nigeria’s 1.5 percentage-point lead over Kenya as a precise measure of how differently people in the two countries use AI. South Africa’s much wider lead is the more striking result.
Relying on chatbots
For a startup selling an AI writing tool to small businesses, familiarity with ChatGPT could make it easier to explain what the product does. Pricing it calls for a different kind of evidence. How often do those businesses need help writing? Do they already get enough from a free chatbot? Would a tool that works in the languages they use with customers be worth paying for?
A high adoption rate among internet users tells a founder where to look for customers. It takes more to work out what those customers will buy.
For a government, the cost of getting the denominator wrong is different. If a ministry puts an AI assistant on its website to explain how to apply for a permit, a high rate of ChatGPT use among connected Kenyans may suggest some applicants will find it familiar.
The ministry still needs to know how many applicants can reach the site, whether they can follow the instructions on a phone and how often they manage to complete the application. Even Microsoft’s wider estimate excludes people aged 65 and over, who may also need the service.
A student who asks ChatGPT to summarise one reading and a trader who uses it every week to draft replies to customers both count in a monthly survey. The distinction starts to matter when the trader changes how they handle enquiries because of the tool. Knowing how many people have reached that point would tell us more about what AI is changing in Africa than knowing which country came first.

articles.title: Chrome croule sous les failles : Google déploie la troisième mise à jour de sécurité en huit jours
articles.text:
Google a déployé une nouvelle version de Chrome sur Windows, macOS et Linux. Baptisée Chrome 158, la mise à jour corrige pas moins de 204 failles de sécurité, à savoir six brèches critiques, 62 failles de gravité élevée, 82 failles moyennes et 54 failles mineures.
À lire aussi : Ces 319 extensions Chrome ont espionné des millions d’internautes pendant 10 ans
Six failles critiques dans le cœur de Chrome
Les six failles critiques touchent des composants clés du navigateur. La moitié des failles surviennent quand un logiciel continue d’utiliser une zone de mémoire qu’il a déjà libérée. Un pirate peut alors s’engouffrer dans la brèche pour corrompre des données, ou y exécuter du code malveillant. Les trois autres failles touchent le composant GPU et ANGLE, la couche graphique de Chrome, et le module Media. Dans les deux cas, Chrome écrit au-delà de l’espace mémoire prévu, ce qui peut écraser des informations voisines.
Pour l’instant, Google n’a pas découvert le moindre indice qui laisse penser que les failles ont été exploitées dans des cyberattaques. Comme toujours, le géant de Mountain View reste discret et refuse de communiquer davantage d’informations techniques, pour des raisons de sécurité.
IA et explosion des failles de sécurité
C’est déjà la troisième mise à jour de sécurité en l’espace de huit jours. Le 3 novembre, Chrome 157 est arrivé avec 213 correctifs. Six jours plus tard, Google a colmaté en urgence une faille zero-day déjà exploitée par des pirates. Deux jours après, un nouveau correctif est venu combler 83 failles dans le code du navigateur. Au total, plus de 500 failles ont été comblées en seulement deux semaines.
Ce déluge de vulnérabilités découle évidemment de l’essor de l’IA générative. Les notes de Google indiquent d’ailleurs que Claude, l’IA d’Anthropic, est à l’origine de la découverte de huit failles, dont deux des six failles critiques. Google s’appuie aussi sur ses propres outils pour traquer les failles, dont Big Sleep, un agent d’IA conçu par DeepMind et Project Zero.
L’accélération chez Google ne concerne pas que Chrome. La semaine dernière, Project Zero, l’équipe de sécurité d’élite de Google, a annoncé qu’elle allait divulguer les failles trois fois plus vite, qu’à l’accoutumée, en ramenant son délai de 90 à 30 jours. Selon les chercheurs, l’IA permet désormais aux pirates d’analyser un correctif dès sa sortie pour déduire une faille capable de mener à une attaque.
Le correctif est inclus dans la version 158.0.8127.36/.37 pour Windows et Mac, 158.0.8127.36 pour Linux, et 158.0.8127.42 pour Android. Pour installer la mise à jour, cliquez sur les trois points en haut à droite de Chrome, puis allez dans « Aide » et « À propos de Google Chrome ». Le navigateur télécharge alors tout seul la dernière version. Cliquez ensuite sur « Relancer » pour l’appliquer sur le navigateur. Vu la cadence actuelle des mises à jour de Chrome, on vous conseille d’activer les mises à jour automatiques.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO puts AI's circular financing boom to the test | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Arriving at public markets today, Anthropic’s IPO is poised to raise billions for the company and its investors. But the biggest surprise may be just how much of that money will end up going to supplier-investors.
Amazon and Google, two of Anthropic’s largest infrastructure partners, hold stakes valued around a combined $307.9 billion at the company’s updated IPO price of $83 per share. Amazon, which invested $18 billion into the AI startup, would see its 14.7% stake hit upwards of $159 billion, while Google’s 13.7% stake is valued at nearly $149 billion, according to share ownership figures disclosed in Anthropic’s IPO prospectus.
A handful of other AI infrastructure providers are also positioned to benefit. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Broadcom, Micron, and TSMC have joined Google in committing $26 billion to Anthropic at its IPO price in a private placement.
In total, Google has invested $12.3 billion into Anthropic since 2023, with another promised $30 billion dependent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones. And with the exception of TSMC, Anthropic has announced multibillion-dollar strategic partnerships with its other infrastructure supplier investors — including Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft, and Micron — that would see Anthropic purchasing their products.
This is the circular financing that has made some observers so skeptical of the AI boom. These companies are not just investors; they’re also Anthropic’s biggest suppliers. It might look like Amazon and Google are putting billions into Anthropic, but they get that money right back when Anthropic needs to train a model or serve Claude to users. From afar, it looks like unprecedented revenue growth for cloud companies and unprecedented fundraising from Anthropic — but it’s just the same money passing from one pocket to another.
Today’s IPO marks a critical change in that financing system, the moment it might just become self-sustaining. Those investments appear to have paid off, and are now liquid. Anthropic is still operating at a net loss of tens of billions of dollars each quarter — but it will no longer be suppliers and private investors footing the bill. Now, capital will come from a mix of public-market investors and corporate bonds, neither of which have the conflicts-of-interest that caused concerns before.
And critically, the company’s new bottom line looks pretty good.
Once it debuts, Anthropic is expected to have about $220 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments, including proceeds from its IPO and the $26 billion private placement. Anthropic also has the ability to pay for future commitments in stock.
Joey Brookhart, who leads the Tokenomics team at SemiAnalysis, estimates that Anthropic needs roughly $280 billion in cumulative revenue over the next four years to pay for its compute bill, which Brookhart said is “achievable given where they will be next year from a revenue perspective.”
“The ownership stake is very worthwhile, and those companies no longer need any more support from [suppliers],” Brookhart told TechCrunch. “Amazon doesn’t need to prop them up anymore. The revenue is all coming from other customers.”
That doesn’t mean the server bills are going down, though. Anthropic has already committed to spend $900 billion, primarily for compute and infrastructure, according to a regulatory filing. Certain agreements have termination provisions, but Brookhart thinks the company is in a strong position to pay up.
On the other side, Anthropic generated $17 billion in third-quarter 2026 revenue, putting the company on pace for a $68 billion annualized rate for the year. If Anthropic continues to grow at its current trajectory, Brookhart believes it could easily cover the gap needed to fund its compute.
Gil Luria, head of technology research at D.A. Davidson, agreed.
“By the time the IPO is done, Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had,” Luria told TechCrunch, noting that the firm raised around $141 billion in capital and will take home around $91.7 billion in net proceeds at $83 per share. “And they’re not burning cash. They’re just going to have a war chest.”
A public listing will make Anthropic a more credible borrower, making it easier to raise money outside of public markets, says Brookhart. That’s despite recent reports that creditors might not see Anthropic as “investment-grade” material.
Luria distinguished between Anthropic’s supplier investments and neoclouds like CoreWeave, which he sees as more purely supported by circular financing. “CoreWeave wouldn’t exist if Nvidia didn’t prop them up, and it probably won’t exist if Nvidia doesn’t bail them out,” Luria said.
Brookhart also pushed back on describing Anthropic’s financing as purely circular, saying it was still “additive to the ecosystem.”
For both analysts, the biggest risk to Anthropic is simply that it will lose the AI race. Right now, the company’s growth is fueled by its status at the frontier of generative AI — but if it’s overtaken by OpenAI, Google DeepMind, or even cheap open-weight models, that could change fast. As Luria put it: “If we’re all using other people’s models, then Anthropic’s not worth a trillion and a half dollars. It’s worth nothing.”
But regardless of who wins the frontier, compute suppliers will likely be just fine. Neither Brookhart nor Luria believe Anthropic’s growth is at risk, despite some arguments that cheaper tokens and more competition will directly affect the AI company’s bottom line.
“For Amazon and Google, the risk isn’t actually that high because in that scenario, we’re using other models,” Luria said. “I’m arguing we’re going to use a lot more AI. I don’t know if it’s all Anthropic’s AI…. That’s still going to come from a data center managed by Amazon, Google, and Microsoft.”

articles.title: Meta now sells 3D movies on Quest VR headsets
articles.text:
Meta now offers more than 150 3D movies that you can buy or rent to watch in VR on its Quest 3 and 3S headsets, the company announced today. The movies are available in Meta’s TV app and include titles like Avatar, Spider-Man: Far From Home, Jurassic World Rebirth, Wicked: For Good, and a Billie Eilish concert film co-directed by Eilish and James Cameron.
Meta now sells 3D movies on Quest VR headsets
Use your Quest 3 to catch films like Avatar and Jurassic World Rebirth in 3D.
The company suggests watching movies in a Theater view that’s rolling out with a new Meta Quest update. Theater view “provides a big screen and dims your surroundings to create a cozy, personal cinema experience,” Meta says.
Meta promises that the library will “keep growing, with thousands of titles and international availability coming” when it launches its VR Glasses next spring. If you’re a Disney Plus subscriber, you can also watch 3D movies on Meta Quest hardware in the Disney Plus app thanks to an update rolled out earlier this month.

articles.title: Simulation of Plasma Chambers for Predictive Simulation of Semiconductor Manufacturing
articles.text:
Home >
                                                                    Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials >
                                                                Simulation of Plasma Chambers for Predictive Simulation of Semiconductor Manu...                                                    
Manufacturing, Packaging & Materials
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Linking plasma chamber simulation with feature-scale process modeling to predict etch profiles, evaluate wafer uniformity, and optimize plasma etching processes.
								November 19th, 2026 - 
								By: Silvaco
								
							
Plasma etching and deposition processes increasingly determine the manufacturability of advanced semiconductor devices, where smaller features, more complex geometries, stricter wafer-uniformity requirements, and new chemistries demand predictive control of ion fluxes at the wafer surface. Kinetic plasma simulation provides a physics-based route to this control by resolving sheath dynamics, ion-neutral transport, and ion angular and energy distributions that cannot be captured reliably with bulk fluid approximations alone. VSim Plasma applies Particle-in-Cell modeling with Monte Carlo collisions to compute self-consistent electromagnetic fields, charged-particle motion, collisions, and current deposition. Validation against inductively coupled plasma measurements shows strong agreement for electron temperature and plasma potential, reasonable density agreement, and consistent electron energy probability function behavior. Coupling plasma-derived ion angular and energy distributions into Victory Process enables feature-scale etch simulation, linking chamber conditions and waveform design to process variability and profile evolution.

articles.title: Marre des miles dans GTA 6 ? On peut changer les unités de mesure
articles.text:
GTA 6 est un jeu vidéo qui se déroule dans un monde ouvert immense et garni de détails, se situant à Leonida, un État inspiré de la Floride. Par conséquent, on y retrouve les unités de mesure utilisées aux États-Unis. Les distances sont exprimées selon le système impérial (pouces, pieds, yards et miles), les températures en degrés Fahrenheit, le poids en livres tandis que le système horaire se base sur des cycles de 12 heures.
Quand on habite en France, ces unités de mesure ne sont pas forcément très parlantes. Prenons l’exemple d’une longue distance à parcourir en voiture. Dans GTA 6, elle s’affiche par défaut en miles (un mile équivaut à environ 1,6 kilomètre). Si on n’a pas cette conversion en tête, savoir que notre futur point d’intérêt se trouve à 5 miles (environ 8 kilomètres) n’aidera pas beaucoup à se rendre compte du temps que cela prendra. Heureusement, on peut passer au système métrique.
Comment changer les unités de mesure dans GTA 6 ?
Rien ne vous oblige à vous coltiner des unités de mesure qui ne vous parlent pas dans GTA 6. Dans les paramètres, on peut tout modifier. Depuis le menu pause et l’onglet Paramètres, on se rend dans le sous-onglet Interface (quatre appuis sur le bouton de tranche droit, R1 sur PS5 ou RB sur Xbox) et on descend tout en bas. L’onglet compte 70 réglages et ceux dédiés aux unités sont à la fin. On peut donc facilement passer à côté en parcourant les menus.
On peut indépendamment changer chaque élément :
- Les distances selon le système impérial (États-Unis) ou métrique (France) ;
- Le poids en livres (États-Unis) ou en kilogrammes (France) ;
- La température en degrés Fahrenheit (États-Unis) ou degrés Celsius (France) ;
- Le système horaire au format 12 heures (États-Unis) ou 24 heures (France).
Les changements s’appliquent tout de suite à la partie en cours, sans avoir à relancer le jeu.
Vous pouvez mélanger les différentes unités, si vous le désirez.
Rockstar Games se montre plus souple que dans GTA 5. Sur l’épisode précédent, un seul réglage, rangé dans l’onglet Affichage, faisait passer tout le jeu d’un bloc du système impérial au système métrique.

articles.title: Community-Focused Academic Brings AI Tools to Colorado Farmers
articles.text:
Many farmers and ranchers in eastern Colorado are curious about artificial intelligence, but they don’t have a local tech-savvy person to show them how to use it. Xue “Alice” Dong has made that her job.
Dong, an IEEE senior member, is an extension regional specialist with the Colorado State University Extension, CSU’s outreach arm. She works in Logan County and serves a 10-county farming area in Colorado’s northeast corner. Her job is to turn university research into practical help for the people who live there.
Xue “Alice” Dong
Employer
Colorado State University Extension in Logan County
Title
Extension regional specialist
Member grade
Senior member
Alma maters
Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot; Beijing Normal University; State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse; Colorado State University Global
She built the AI-Powered Agritourism Chatbot (AgriTourismAI.com), which helps farmers and ranchers launch and run “agritourism” businesses. Agritourism is when farmers open their property to visitors for fun, education, or shopping events. Familiar examples include pick-your-own fruit orchards, lessons on how to grow vegetables, and sales of handmade products.
Dong also teaches workshops where she shows farmers and ranchers how they can use AI tools to help grow and manage their business.
She says she sees herself as a link between the university and the countryside.
“We [extension specialists] act as a bridge,” she says. “We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.”
Many farmers and ranchers are older, and they typically have no technical training. Often their children and grandchildren have left the farm to work in a city or otherwise aren’t around to teach them about new tools. Without help, the benefits of AI could pass the farmers by. Dong’s workshops give them a way in.
Dong was named a finalist in the 2026 GenAI for Good Challenge for her AgriPivot AI Agent. The challenge was organized by IEEE Humanitarian Technologies and theU.N.’s International Telecommunication Union, and her project was selected from 318 teams across 79 countries. She also won the 2026 Award for Innovation from the National Extension Technology Community (NETC), and both the 2025 national and Western regional Educational Technology Awards from the National Association of Community Development Extension Professionals (NACDEP).
She has secured seven competitive grants totaling more than US $250,000 as principal investigator or co-principal investigator, including funding supported by the Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture.
An early love of design and problem-solving
Dong was born in Beijing. Both her parents are doctors.
As a child, she liked drawing new and inventive things. Sketching, she says, lets her picture solutions to problems in her head and put them on paper as practical designs.
That habit grew into a way of relating to her surroundings.
“I’ve always had a passion to create something tangible that can solve problems in the real world,” she says.
She doesn’t credit a single mentor for the direction her life has taken. Instead, she says all her teachers helped lay the groundwork for her career.
She attended the Inner Mongolia Normal University, in Hohhot, an institution that trains teachers. She earned two bachelor’s degrees there in 2013—one in geographical science and one in education.
She then earned a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction from Beijing Normal University in 2016.
That year, she moved to the United States to continue her graduate studies at the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry, in Syracuse. She earned a master’s degree in environmental biology in 2020.
From outreach to extension work
After earning her second master’s degree, she joined Paul Smith’s College, in Paul Smiths, N.Y., as an education and outreach coordinator.
She managed several national watershed projects to protect rivers, lakes, and aquifers. Watersheds are areas of land from which water drains into bodies of water.
She also undertook invasive-species-prevention projects, wrote grants to secure project funding, and designed two educational websites and several outreach publications. One website, Maintain the Chain, helps lake residents, boaters, and visitors from around the world keep invasive species out of the Fulton Chain of Lakes in New York’s Adirondack Park.
In 2022, she joined Stewards of the Coast and Redwoods as program manager. The nonprofit, based in Guerneville, Calif., works with California State Parks to protect, restore, and educate the public about the parks along Sonoma County’s coast and the Russian River area. The region is known for its redwood forests, wineries, and resort towns.
She left in 2023 to join the CSU Extension as a regional specialist, a title she still holds.
Her employer is part of the Cooperative Extension System, a nationwide network run by land-grant universities, schools founded with federal grants to teach farming and other practical subjects. Extension faculty and staff share what researchers at their universities learn with the citizens of those states.
The cooperative system operates on three levels. It is overseen federally by the Department of Agriculture’s National Institute of Food and Agriculture, managed statewide through land-grant universities, and delivered locally by county offices and Extension agents across more than 3,000 counties.
The work goes well beyond farming, Dong says, also covering community and economic development, health initiatives, and the 4-H program, which teaches children hands-on skills in agriculture, science, leadership, and citizenship.
Extension faculty members’ performance is judged on their research, teaching, and service to the community, Dong says—similar to the way professors in academia are evaluated. The difference, she says, is the audience: Professors teach students; most extension specialists teach adults, including farmers, ranchers, and community leaders. The setting is different, too. Dong doesn’t commute from the campus to the countryside; she lives and works in it. Her office is in Sterling, a small rural town. But her projects serve the whole state, and many of the people she helps live one to four hours’ drive away. So, most of her work with farmers and ranchers happens by email, phone, and virtual meetings. County fairs, farmers markets, and agricultural events give her chances to meet large groups of them in person.
She can’t just hand Colorado residents research findings and expect them to figure out the information they need, she says.
“We need to translate that research into something more practical, and easier to use, that farmers and ranchers can understand immediately,” she says.
Dong also focuses not on only on whether people use AI, but also on how they use it. In 2026, she and Paul Hill from Utah State University Extension published “From Access to Governance: Generative AI Literacy for Extension Professionals and Small Businesses, and a Governance-Aware Design Framework” in the journal AI. The paper offers a framework for helping Extension professionals and small businesses adopt generative AI responsibly.
How her AI chatbot helps farmers and ranchers
In 2025, Dong earned a third master’s degree, in artificial intelligence and machine learning, from CSU Global.
She immediately put those skills to work on agritourism, she says. She built the chatbot in Python, a popular programming language. It answers typed questions, and its user interface looks much like ChatGPT’s, but it works differently. Under the hood, it uses retrieval-augmented generation, a technique that has the AI look up information in a set of trusted documents before it answers. Dong curated that collection from Extension publications, so the chatbot’s answers rest on authoritative sources and are less likely to be made up. She presented the project at NeurIPS 2025 (Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). The code is openly available on GitHub, so other Extension offices can adapt it.
The bot runs in a web browser rather than as a phone app. Many farmers she works with don’t own a smartphone, Dong says, but nearly all have a computer, tablet, or other gadget that can connect to a website. The bot works on any of them, with no app to download.
Extension specialists “act as a bridge. We bridge our campus to the rural communities we serve.”
Farmers often ask the bot how to attract visitors and how to write a business plan. A farmer thinking about opening a corn maze, for example, can ask how to price admission, what kind of insurance to carry, and which permits to get. The bot also gives advice on managing risk.
One of her test sites was Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch, in eastern Colorado. Dong documented how the ranch put AI to work in a peer-reviewed case study, “Revolutionizing Agritourism with AI and Machine Learning: A Case Study of Prairie Ridge Buffalo Ranch in Colorado,” published in 2025 in CABI Tourism Cases.
Surveys and interviews she conducted with other users showed that people find it’s easy to use the bot, learn from it, and act on its advice, she says. She is preparing the full results for publication.
Her work extends beyond agritourism. In 2026, she contributed an AI assistant to Project Pythia, an open-science program funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation and led by the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR). The AI assistant turns raw airport weather report data into plain-language guidance for farmers and other non-technical users, and it tells users when data is missing rather than guessing.
She also teaches workshops on AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. She has taught her workshop 20 times to more than 200 entrepreneurs and business owners, who came from 32 Colorado counties. In follow-up surveys, 90 percent of participants reported trying at least one new AI task in their business. Some of the workshops take place at a community center run by the Logan County Economic Development Corp., in Sterling. She has also co-hosted the workshops with the Rural Community Assistance Corp., Colorado Startup Week, and Boulder Startup Week. And she occasionally presents them as webinars, so people don’t have to travel.
Her outreach has taught her that many farmers are eager to try new tools, she says. She shows them how simple her chatbot is to use.
She also offers advice to high school students drawn to the field. Extension specialists each have a specialty, such as livestock, natural resources, food systems, or 4-H. Students should pick one based on their passion, she says.
Land-grant universities offer related programs at the bachelor’s and master’s levels. For graduate students, she adds, Extension offers a third career path beyond academia and industry: “You apply advanced skills directly to the communities that need them.”
How IEEE membership supports her career
Dong joined IEEE in 2025 and soon was elevated to senior member. Her professional home is the IEEE Society on Social Implications of Technology. She also serves as vice treasurer of the IEEE Denver Section’s Young Professionals group.
IEEE supports all three parts of her job, she says. For research, she presented “Entrepreneur AI Agent: Empowering Small Businesses and Bridging the Digital Divide through Context-Aware Generative AI” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC). For teaching, she has offered to bring her AI workshop to Denver Section members and local entrepreneurs. For service, she reviews papers for IEEE conferences.
IEEE conferences matter most to her, she says: “Through them, I can present my research and network with other researchers in the field.”
She attended the IEEE World Forum on Public Safety Technology in Boulder, Colo., in September 2026. The event, she says, opened her eyes to many new projects underway across IEEE.
Still, she says, her work always points back to the farms and ranches of eastern Colorado. Its people are curious, she says, but they can’t make the leap to new technology alone.
“They really need this kind of a bridge,” she says.

articles.title: 4.250 neue Millionäre? Der Börsengang macht Anthropic-Mitarbeiter reich
articles.text:
Anthropic: Das sind die großen Gewinner des Rekord-Börsengangs
Wenn die Anthropic-Aktie am 19. November in den Handel startet, gehören neben frühen Investoren und Big-Tech-Konzernen auch viele Mitarbeiter zu den großen Gewinnern. Sie dürfen schon am ersten Handelstag bis zu zehn Prozent ihrer Aktien verkaufen.
Andere Investoren müssen sich länger gedulden. Für sie gelten gestaffelte Lockup-Fristen: Erste Aktienpakete werden 27, 48, 62 und 76 Tage nach dem Börsengang handelbar. Die sieben Gründer verkaufen beim IPO zwar kleine Pakete, dürfen den Großteil ihrer Anteile aber erst nach Veröffentlichung der Zahlen für das erste Quartal 2027 oder spätestens nach 180 Tagen verkaufen.
Anthropic bringt 980 Millionen Aktien zu je 83 Dollar an die Börse und nimmt damit 81,3 Milliarden Dollar ein, mehr als SpaceX mit 75 Milliarden. Voll verwässert wird das Unternehmen mit rund 1,5 Billionen Dollar bewertet. Weitere 26 Milliarden Dollar kommen über eine Privatplatzierung bei Tech- und Chipkonzernen hinzu.
Anthropic-IPO: Big Tech gewinnt
Die größten Gewinner sind zwei Big-Tech-Konzerne, die Anthropic zugleich mit Rechenleistung beliefern. Laut der letzten Fassung des Börsenprospekts hält Amazon nach dem IPO rund 1,92 Milliarden Aktien, Google rund 1,79 Milliarden. Zum Ausgabepreis entspricht das etwa 159 Milliarden Dollar für Amazon und 147 Milliarden für Google. Eingesetzt hat Amazon nach Berechnungen von Reuters rund 18 Milliarden Dollar, Google 33,3 Milliarden.
Anthropic machte zuletzt knapp die Hälfte seines Umsatzes über die Cloud-Plattformen der beiden Konzerne. Umgekehrt hat Anthropic zugesagt, über zehn Jahre mindestens 110 Milliarden Dollar bei AWS auszugeben und bis 2033 mindestens 114 Milliarden Dollar bei Google Cloud.
Über die Privatplatzierung steigen jetzt weitere Lieferanten ein: Neben Google kaufen Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft und TSMC zusammen für 26 Milliarden Dollar Aktien zum Ausgabepreis.
Milliardengewinne auf Raten
Zu den frühen Investoren bei Anthropic gehören außerdem Skype-Mitgründer Jaan Tallinn, Facebook-Mitgründer Dustin Moskovitz und der frühere Google-Chef Eric Schmidt. Forbes schätzt Tallinns Paket zum Ausgabepreis auf rund 15,6 Milliarden Dollar, etwa das 260-Fache seines Einsatzes.
Laut Daten von PitchBook haben seit 2021 mehr als 300 Geldgeber Anteile bei Anthropic investiert. Zuletzt hatten Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks und Sequoia Ende Mai eine Finanzierungsrunde angeführt, bei der Anthropic noch auf eine Bewertung von 965 Milliarden Dollar kam.
Viele dieser Investoren dürfen erst ab dem 15. Dezember verkaufen und zunächst nur bis zu sechs Prozent ihrer Aktien. Großaktionäre mit mehr als 0,5 Prozent müssen noch länger warten, für sie endet die Sperrfrist erst nach einem Jahr.
Ein früher Investor geht dagegen leer aus: Im Jahr 2021 steckte der wegen Betrugs zu 25 Jahren Haft verurteilte Gründer der Kryptobörse FTX Sam Bankman-Fried 500 Millionen Dollar in das damals kaum bekannte Startup.
Der FTX-Insolvenzverwalter verkaufte die Anteile aber bereits 2024 für insgesamt rund 1,3 Milliarden Dollar. Zum IPO-Preis wäre das Paket nun etwa 37 Milliarden Dollar wert gewesen.
Anthropic-Börsengang: Tausende Millionäre auf dem Papier
Nach einer Schätzung der Privatmarkt-Plattform Hill könnten bei der Bewertung von mehr als 1,5 Billionen Dollar rund 4.250 der etwa 5.300 Anthropic-Mitarbeiter jetzt zumindest auf dem Papier zu Millionären werden. Das sind rund 80 Prozent der Belegschaft. Das Analysehaus Sacra kommt auf rund 2.800 aktuelle und frühere Beschäftigte mit mindestens einer Million Dollar.
Anders als bei den meisten Börsengängen dürfen Mitarbeiter schon am ersten Handelstag bis zu zehn Prozent ihrer Aktien verkaufen und weitere 35 Prozent, nachdem die Jahreszahlen für 2026 veröffentlicht wurden.
Die sieben Gründer geben beim IPO jeweils Aktien im Wert von rund 280 Millionen Dollar ab. Der Großteil ihrer verbleibenden Anteile bleibt jedoch bis zu einem Jahr gesperrt.

articles.title: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims
articles.text:
NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group has added the company to its dark web data leak site.
Although the ransomware operation now lists the American multinational tech giant, it has not yet shared any proof of the breach.
On their leak site, the cybercrime gang threatens to release data and has added a countdown that ends in nine days, on November 28.
While the company told BleepingComputer it hasn't found evidence that its systems were compromised, it said it's now looking into a separate incident that may have affected one of its service providers.
"NVIDIA is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner," an NVIDIA spokesperson told BleepingComputer when asked to confirm the cybercrime gang's claims.
"We have found no indication that NVIDIA systems or networks were affected. We continue to monitor the situation."
NVIDIA confirmed a data breach earlier this year, in May, when it told BleepingComputer that some Armenian users' information (including their names, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and usernames) had been exposed after a regional GeForce NOW Alliance partner was hacked.
However, the company added that the May breach did not affect its network or NVIDIA-operated services.
The tech giant also disclosed another data breach in March 2022 (claimed by the Lapsus$ extortion gang) that affected more than 71,000 employees after attackers accessed its network a month earlier.
The Gentlemen surfaced last year as a closed ransomware group and then switched to a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model, offering affiliates up to a 90% cut of ransom proceeds (compared to the typical 70%–80% other ransomware groups offer).
It operates as a double-extortion group, exfiltrating sensitive data from victims' networks before encrypting their systems and pressuring them with the threat of leaking the stolen information online.
Since it emerged, The Gentlemen has claimed more than 1,100 victims from various sectors, spanning manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, energy, education, financial services, and more.

articles.title: InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 crore in Series B led by FMO
articles.text:
InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO
InPrime will use the funding to expand its reach and improve its technology stack, especially in AI use cases.
InPrime Finserv, a tech-led NBFC, has raised Rs 101 crore in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. This round also saw participation from existing investors Z47 and Pravega Ventures.
InPrime will utilise the capital to expand the reach of existing products and diversify into micro-mortgage products, in line with its segment-focused lending approach. The NBFC will also deepen its investments in AI-driven use cases, across agentic AI and co-pilots.
“From the beginning, we have believed that prime customers are not limited to the formal economy. We have been building around the evolving needs of India’s informal prime customers by combining engineering, local presence and relevant financial products.,” said Rajat Singh, Co-founder and CEO, InPrime Finserv.
InPrime operates 46 area offices across Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Uttarakhand and Madhya Pradesh. It has served 27,000+ households and has disbursed Rs 516.92 crore to date. As of September 30, 2026, its assets under management stood at Rs 332.8 crore, with gross non-performing assets of 0.80%.
Founded in 2021 by Sneh Thakur, Manish Raj and Rajat Singh, InPrime is focused on customers who do not fall under the category of formal employment. This NBFC believes that despite the credit worthiness of this segment, they are unable to raise loans due to the traditional practices of lenders.
According to InPrime, its technology stack allows it to effectively do the task of credit underwriting, which requires interpreting unstructured data, understanding customers beyond conventional financial metrics, and delivering services at scale in vernacular languages.
“Expanding access to finance for underserved entrepreneurs and households is closely aligned with FMO’s aim of making finance more inclusive and accessible. InPrime’s combination of technology, data-driven underwriting, and local presence provides an opportunity to reach customers who are often overlooked by traditional lenders,” said Peter Byrde, Director Private Equity at FMO.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.text:
L’iPhone 18, et son petit frère plus abordable, l’iPhone 18e, représentent la future porte d’entrée vers l’écosystème mobile d’Apple, pour l’heure toujours assurée par l’iPhone 17 et l’iPhone 17e. Car oui, lors de sa keynote de rentrée 2026, la marque à la pomme a créé la surprise en faisant l’impasse sur son modèle standard, laissant toute la lumière aux iPhone 18 Pro et à son premier smartphone pliant, l’iPhone Duo. Ces deux modèles devraient finalement débarquer au printemps 2027 aux côtés d’un potentiel iPhone Air 2.
Que nous prépare Apple pour ce début d’année 2027 ? Comme d’habitude, les rumeurs vont bon train et se contredisent parfois sur les réseaux sociaux chinois. Si vous avez du mal à séparer le bon grain de l’ivraie, voici donc un récapitulatif complet et condensé des rumeurs les plus importantes.
Design et écran : le grand flou autour de l’iPhone 18e
Sur le front de l’affichage et du design, Apple semble vouloir jouer la carte de la continuité pour son modèle classique, mais les bruits de couloir s’opposent radicalement concernant la version « e ».
Pour l’iPhone 18 standard, pas de révolution majeure : on retrouverait l’excellente recette de l’iPhone 17 avec une dalle OLED de 6,3 pouces rafraîchie à 120 Hz, accompagnée de Face ID et de la fameuse Dynamic Island, ce petit espace en haut de l’écran qui sert à masquer la caméra selfie et les capteurs infrarouges tout en affichant des raccourcis et des animations.
Et bien, c’est justement là que le bât blesserait pour l’iPhone 18e. Selon les leakers Digital Chat Station et Fixed Focus Digital, le modèle abordable devrait conserver une dalle OLED LTPS de 6,12 pouces bloquée à un taux de rafraîchissement famélique de 60 Hz, ainsi que sa bonne vieille encoche. Un choix conservateur, pour ne pas dire radin, à l’heure où la concurrence Android propose du 120 Hz depuis des années.
Toutefois, un rebondissement récent vient semer le doute. En publiant des images de prétendus prototypes début novembre, Fixed Focus Digital a affirmé que les deux modèles partageraient finalement la même diagonale de 6,3 pouces. Or, Apple n’a jamais proposé d’écran de cette taille avec une encoche. De quoi laisser espérer l’arrivée de la Dynamic Island sur l’iPhone 18e, ce qui gommerait enfin l’impression d’avoir un iPhone au rabais. À prendre avec des pincettes, donc.
Autonomie : une belle hausse de capacité au programme
Sur le front de l’autonomie, Apple ne joue toujours pas la course aux chiffres démesurés avec le silicium-carbone comme ses rivaux chinois, mais la marque compterait tout de même muscler son jeu.
Selon les premières indiscrétions de Digital Chat Station, l’iPhone 18 devait déjà profiter d’une batterie sensiblement agrandie par rapport aux 3 692 mAh de l’iPhone 17, en passant à une valeur autour de 4 056 mAh. Mais la fuite la plus récente de Fixed Focus Digital va encore plus loin : les iPhone 18 et 18e partageraient exactement le même accumulateur d’une capacité de 4 430 mAh.
Ce serait une progression significative, notamment face aux 4 005 mAh de l’iPhone 17e. Combinée à l’efficience énergétique de la nouvelle puce maison, cette batterie permettrait aux deux smartphones d’offrir une endurance nettement supérieure à la génération précédente.
Performances : la puce A20 et la barre des 2 nm pour tout le monde
Concernant les performances, Apple ne ferait pas de jaloux. Les iPhone 18 et 18e devraient tous deux intégrer la nouvelle puce A20 conçue par Apple et gravée en 2 nm par TSMC. Il s’agirait d’une déclinaison légèrement moins puissante (et moins coûteuse) de l’A20 Pro inaugurée sur les iPhone 18 Pro et l’iPhone Duo en septembre 2026.
Ce passage au 2 nm devrait permettre d’engranger des gains énergétiques importants, tout en assurant une solidité à toute épreuve pour les usages liés à l’intelligence artificielle générative en local. Sur l’iPhone 18e, ce processeur serait d’ailleurs épaulé par 9 Go de RAM d’après l’analyste Ming Chi-Kuo, ce qui constituerait une évolution étrange, mais nécessaire pour tenir la charge sur l’IA locale.
Photo : le strict minimum syndical
Pour le sujet de la photographie, les évolutions s’annoncent particulièrement timides, voire inexistantes, confirmant que Apple souhaite avant tout rationaliser ses coûts de production.
Sur l’iPhone 18, on retrouverait le double module dorsal de 48 mégapixels (grand-angle et ultra-grand-angle). Du côté de l’iPhone 18e, n’attendez pas de miracle à l’arrière : il faudrait une nouvelle fois se contenter d’un unique capteur de 48 Mpx, sans ultra-grand-angle ni téléobjectif. La seule bonne surprise viendrait de la face avant, où le capteur selfie grimperait enfin de 12 à 24 mégapixels.
Prix et date de sortie
Pour la première fois depuis plus d’une décennie, Apple a brisé sa routine en n’annonçant aucun iPhone standard en septembre 2026. Une décision stratégique dictée par l’essoufflement des ventes des modèles non-Pro face aux versions Pro (qui pèsent + de 50% du mix), le besoin d’étaler les sorties face au calendrier de Samsung, mais aussi les tensions d’approvisionnement sur les composants.
Les iPhone 18 et 18e devraient donc sortir du bois au premier trimestre 2027, vraisemblablement entre mars et avril, dans la lignée du calendrier inauguré par les iPhone 16e et 17e.
Concernant les prix, aucun montant précis n’a encore fuité, mais la tendance est clairement à la hausse. En septembre 2026, Apple avait déjà relevé l’ensemble de sa grille tarifaire en France en pleine crise des composants : l’iPhone 17 était ainsi passé de 969 à 1 119 euros (+150 euros), tandis que l’iPhone 17e avait grimpé de 719 à 869 euros. Les leakers préviennent que les iPhone 18 et 18e n’échapperont pas à une nouvelle inflation, ce qui laisse craindre des tarifs de lancement particulièrement salés au printemps prochain.
